default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: Today or tomorrow, I plan to go to the embassy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: か connects two nouns to present two possible time choices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction of movement to the embassy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 行こう is the volitional form, and と marks the content of the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 思って connects the verb 思う with います to create a state of thinking or having a plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: ～ています describes a continuing state of thinking or planning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the destination and the content of the plan. The volitional form 行こう combines with とと思っている to express the speaker's plan or intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～つもりだ, the sentence emphasizes a stronger intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～予定だ is used, the sentence suggests a plan that has been arranged or decided in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake と in this pattern for “and,” but と here marks the content of a thought or intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q1.kobun.cn: NかN; V意向形＋と思っている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vi: Speaking in a foreign language is difficult but interesting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means or language used when speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns 話す into the noun “speaking,” while は makes it the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: けれど connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 楽しいです is the main comment at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.why: 話すの turns the action of speaking into a noun to make it the topic with は. けれど connects contrasting comments: this activity is difficult but still interesting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes speaking in a foreign language as the activity being judged difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: けど has a similar meaning to けれど but is more casual in conversation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.tip: To turn a verb into “the act of doing something,” add の after the dictionary form of the verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ けれど
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vi: My younger sister watches TV all day and refuses to study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the younger sister the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: ずっと modifies the action of watching and emphasizes its long duration.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ばかり limits the activity to テレビ and gives the sense of doing only one thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ていて connects the continuing state of watching with the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the intention to 勉強しよう as the target in the pattern ようとする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: しない negates trying or intending to study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.why: テレビばかり makes clear that the younger sister focuses only on watching TV. 見ていて connects the continuing condition with 勉強しようとしない and expresses the contrast between watching and refusing to study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If だけ is used, the sentence states the limit “only TV” more neutrally and does not emphasize focusing on one activity as ばかり does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern at the end of the sentence emphasizes that the person makes no effort or refuses to start the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q11.kobun.tip: ばかり comes after a noun, while to say that someone only does an action, Vてばかりいる is usually used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vi: When you get sick, you should go to the hospital immediately.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the state of becoming in 病気になる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: なった is the past form and combines with とき to indicate the time when the person became sick.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates a time, while は turns the whole situation into the condition for the advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: すぐに modifies 行ったほうがいい and emphasizes that the person should go at once.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: へ indicates the direction of movement for going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: 行った comes before ほうがいい in the pattern used to give advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: ほうが creates the option that is being recommended.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: いい completes the Vたほうがいい pattern, meaning “should do.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.why: 病気になったときは presents the situation that forms the background for the advice. Then, すぐに indicates time, 病院へ indicates direction, and 行ったほうがいい expresses that the person should go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるとき is used, the sentence refers to the time before or while the illness occurs and does not emphasize that the person has already become sick.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means “should do,” but it is stronger and more direct than ほうがいい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.tip: In advice, Vたほうがいい uses the past form even though the meaning points to an action that should be done from now on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q12.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ とき／Nの ＋ とき; Vた ＋ ほうがいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: あたたかくて connects an adjective with 春らしい; the whole phrase modifies 日.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state つづいている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of つづく connects with いる to create the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: いる comes after a verb in the て form and shows a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.why: The adjective phrase is placed before 日 to modify the noun. 春らしい describes a spring-like quality, while つづいている describes the continuing state of those days.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence sounds more conversational and suggests a judgment that something looks like spring.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes a judgment or appearance similar to spring rather than an inherent quality.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that an adjective ending in い must change to ～くて when connecting to a following clause or adjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q13.kobun.cn: N ＋ らしい; Aいくて ＋ Aい・Aな・N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vi: I was invited to the wedding by the head of my department.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person who receives help or a favor.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.1.vi: of the head of the department
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the owner with the noun けっこんしき.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the event or place to which the speaker was invited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: しょうたいしていただきました is the Vていただく pattern and shows the speaker's humility when receiving a favor from another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.why: The person receiving the favor is the topic with は, while the related person is shown in the phrase の. A verb in the て form connects with いただく to humbly express that another person did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is still receiving help, but the humble and polite tone is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the person who performs the action becomes the subject, and the sentence emphasizes gratitude for that person's action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake いただく as meaning only receiving an object; in this pattern, it can also mean having someone do something helpful for you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.vi: According to the news, it seems that a fire occurred near the station yesterday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.sk: Nに＋よると、＋ Time ＋ Nの場所で ＋ Nが ＋ Vたそうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に in によると marks the information source used as the basis.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: によると connects the information source with the message that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: A time phrase placed before an event to show when it happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の connects 駅 with 近く, creating the phrase near the train station.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle で shows the place where the fire happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the event that is said to have happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: そうだ comes after a verb in the plain form to pass on information that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.why: The source of the information is stated at the beginning with によると, followed by the time, place, and event in that order. そうだ at the end of the sentence shows that the speaker is only passing on information they heard and did not witness directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: When it follows a verb stem or adjective to guess from signs, this pattern means about to or seems, not is said to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence still passes on information, but the meaning is that it was heard or is a reasonable guess, so it is less direct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse そうだ, meaning is said to, with そうだ, which shows appearance; they need to look at the form immediately before そうだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q15.kobun.cn: N ＋ によると、; V普通形 ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.vi: I sometimes argue with my older sister.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.sk: Nは ＋ Frequency adverb ＋ Nと ＋ Nを ＋ します
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic as the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The frequency adverb modifies the action けんかをします.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と shows the person who participates in the action or the person involved in the argument.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the noun けんか as the object of the verb します.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.why: けんかする is a way of combining the noun けんか with する, so けんか takes を. The person who participates in the action is marked by と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If the action is changed to 話す, と only shows the person being spoken with and no longer has the opposing meaning of けんかする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 一緒に is added, the sentence emphasizes doing something together, so it is not natural for expressing the relationship between participants in けんか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of と; for a person who participates in the action or is involved in けんか, the correct particle is と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.vi: It seems that Klaus will go to the sea to play from tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.sk: Nは ＋ Timeから ＋ Nへ ＋ Vます without ますに ＋ 行く ＋ ようです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は shows the person who is guessed to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the starting time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle へ shows the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The form without ます of あそびます combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 行く is the main verb of the phrase あそびに行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: ようです comes after a verb in the plain form to express the judgment that something seems to be so.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.cn: Vます without ます ＋ に行く; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の ＋ ようだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.why: 海へ shows the direction toward the sea, while あそびに shows the purpose of going. ようです is placed at the end of the sentence to turn the whole action into the content of a guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence expresses Klaus's intention or plan, not only the speaker's guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence may emphasize something that is about to happen or information that was heard, depending on the form it connects to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out the particle に in the purpose phrase; they must use the verb stem ます＋に行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.vi: Every dish Mr. Kimura cooks is delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person performing the action 作る in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb in the dictionary form comes before 料理 to modify the dish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase 木村さんが作る料理 is stated as the topic with は.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 疑問詞何 combines with でも to refer to the whole group of objects, making the subject described as delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.why: The clause 木村さんが作る comes before 料理 to identify which dishes they are. 何でも expands the range to all the dishes, and おいしい gives the comment as the predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何か is used instead, the meaning becomes something is delicious, without the meaning that every dish is delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If どのNでも is used instead, the sentence still means any, but the noun must be stated directly after the question word.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand 何でも as the question “what is not anything?”; in this structure, it means “any one is.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.vi: I want to live and continue doing only the things I want to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 自分 with the noun こと, creating a possessive relationship or a related content relationship.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: やりたい comes before こと to modify the thing the speaker wants to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: だけ limits the range, while を marks こと as the object of やる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects the action やる with the next action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: 生きていく expresses continuation into the future and combines with たい to express a desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.cn: N ＋ だけ; Vて ＋ いく; V withoutます ＋ たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.why: The phrase やりたい comes before こと to turn the desired action into a noun. だけを limits the object of やる, and then the て form connects that action with the desire to continue living.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことだけを is replaced with ことしか～ない, the sentence means that the speaker does nothing except those things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことばかり is used, the meaning leans toward doing only those things, often with emphasis or complaint.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse だけ and しか～ない: だけ does not require a negative form, while しか always goes with a negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vi: Yesterday, a famous novelist came from England.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A time word placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the event happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 有名な modifies 小説家 and comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject who came.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: から shows the starting point of the movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 来ました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The time comes before the subject, while the place of departure stands directly before the movement verb. The pattern Nから expresses the source or starting point of the action of coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with へ, the sentence only shows the direction toward England and does not say that the person started from England.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: より can also show the starting source, but it is more formal than から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Do not always translate から as “because”; with movement verbs, から usually means “from.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.sk: N が ＋ V removeます ＋ だして ＋ Vてしまった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the baby as the subject experiencing the state of starting to cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: だす follows the remove ます form of a verb and expresses a sudden start; the て form connects with しまう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: てしまった expresses a completed action. In this sentence, it also carries an unwanted or regretful feeling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.cn: V removeます ＋ だす; Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.why: が identifies the baby as the subject, while だす attaches to the verb stem to show that the crying started suddenly. The て form connects the starting pattern with しまった, creating the feeling that the event happened against one's wishes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If なきはじめてしまった is used, the meaning is still “start crying,” but it is more neutral and places less emphasis on suddenness.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If なきつづけている is used, the sentence says that the baby is continuing to cry, without saying when the crying started.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate しまう as simply “finished,” but in a sentence about an unwanted event, it often gives the feeling of “accidentally” or “ended up.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.vi: When my son goes to bed, I often read books to him.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the person performing the main action the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the clause ねる とき.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form ねる comes before とき to modify the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: とき creates a time phrase and sets the point when the action of reading in the main clause happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the book as the object of the action of reading.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: 読んでやる expresses that the speaker reads for someone who is younger, lower in status, or close to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.why: The clause むすこがねる とき is placed first to state when the main action occurs. 本を is the object being read, while やる adds the meaning that the speaker does this for his son.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is added after とき, the time point is marked more clearly, but the basic meaning hardly changes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 読んであげます is used, the tone is more polite and gentle when saying that one does something good for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may incorrectly use てやる with every type of person. This pattern is suitable for young people, family members, or people of lower status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q21.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形 ＋ とき; Vて ＋ やる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.vi: When I got off the bus, it started to rain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vた ＋ とき、 ＋ N が ＋ V removeます ＋ はじめた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place or vehicle that the speaker leaves when performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: おりた comes before とき to modify the time when the speaker got off the bus.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: とき connects the time clause with the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks 雨 as the subject of the action that begins to fall.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: はじめる attaches to the continuative form of ふる to express that the rain started to fall.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.cn: N を ＋ V; Vた ＋ とき; V removeます ＋ はじめる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.why: The phrase バスをおりた とき sets the time for the event that follows. 雨が is the subject of ふりはじめた, and はじめる shows that the action of rain falling has just begun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If バスをおりているとき is used, the sentence refers to the time while getting off the bus, not after getting off.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If バスをおりたあとで is used, it means after getting off the bus and emphasizes the order of events more than simultaneous timing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may leave out を in バスをおりる, but を here marks the vehicle or place that one leaves, not an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.sk: Time point ＋ Nしか ＋ Vていません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 states the time when the state of having money applies.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: しか limits the amount of money the speaker has and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 持って is the て form of 持つ and connects with いる to express the state of having or carrying something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: いません negates います and completes the structure しか～ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.why: 200円しか is the limited part, while いません provides the required negative form of the pattern しか. 持っている expresses the state of having money, not only the action of holding money.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 200円だけ持っています is used, the sentence simply says that there is 200 yen, so the negative feeling of “there is no more than this” is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If 200円ばかり持っています is used, the sentence may suggest keeping only that small amount of money. It is less natural than しか for expressing limitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget the negative form after しか. Saying 200円しか持っています is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q23.kobun.cn: N ＋ しか ＋ Vない; N ＋ しか ＋ Vていない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.vi: On days when there is little work, I try to go home as early as possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of 少ない in the clause that modifies 日.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 少ない comes before 日 to describe days with little work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase 仕事が少ない modifies 日, while は makes those days the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 早く is the adverbial form of 早い and modifies the action of going home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.5.vi: in order to go home early
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: ように connects a goal or habit that should be maintained with する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: して is the て form of する and connects the structure ようにする with います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.7.n: ています shows that this habit or effort is being maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.why: The clause 仕事が少ない modifies 日, and then は turns the whole phrase into a condition or topic. なるべく早く states the desired degree, while 帰るようにしています expresses a habit of trying to maintain it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 早く帰ることにしています is used, the meaning emphasizes a decision or rule that the speaker has made for himself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 早く帰るようになりました is used, the sentence refers to a change into a habit, not an active effort to maintain it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ようにする with ようになる: する means actively trying, while なる means becoming or forming a change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q24.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ようにする; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.vi: This book is difficult to read because it has many Chinese characters and small print.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ Aい remove い＋くて ＋ N が ＋ Aい＋ので、Vます remove ます＋にくい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun 本 that comes after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 本 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject as having the feature of being numerous.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 多い changes into 多くて to connect a cause or feature with the following part.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject as having the feature of being small.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: ので connects a cause with a result and means “because” or “due to.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: にくい attaches to the remove ます form of a verb to express that the action is difficult to perform.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.cn: Aい remove い＋くて; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので; Vます remove ます＋にくい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.why: The two features of the book are connected by て and ので to give the reason for the conclusion that it is difficult to read. にくい comes after the verb stem 読み and creates the meaning “difficult to read.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning is still “difficult to read,” but it emphasizes the feeling of difficulty or discomfort while reading.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the sentence means “easy to read,” which is opposite to the current conclusion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to change 多い into 多くて when connecting the い adjective with て.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.sk: N から + Quoted sentence と + V受身た
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the person who performs the scolding action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the exact words being quoted.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: しかられた is a past passive form. It shows that the speaker was affected by the father’s action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: The scolding is placed inside quotation marks and connected to the verb with と. The passive verb shows that the speaker received the action, while するな is a direct prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ように言われた is used, the sentence reports the instruction indirectly and more gently.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～と言われた is used, the sentence only means “was told that...” and does not emphasize being scolded.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may incorrectly use the active form しかられた; in the passive form, the person being scolded must be the implied subject of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形 + と + V; Vる + な; V受身形
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: I ended up eating as many as five pieces of cake by myself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.sk: Nで + Nを + Quantityも + Vて + しまった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the way or circumstances in which an action is performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being eaten.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: も follows a quantity to emphasize that it is more than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べて connects the action of eating with しまう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ～てしまった expresses that an action has been completed, often with regret or an unintended feeling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The manner comes before the object and verb. も emphasizes the number five, while 食べてしまった shows that the eating has been completed and that the speaker feels some regret or surprise.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: ～てしまう without も can still express completion or regret, but it does not emphasize the quantity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～だけ is used, the sentence only limits the amount to five pieces and does not imply that this is more than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate も in a quantity pattern as “also”; here it emphasizes the amount, like “as many as” or “even.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q4.kobun.cn: N(数量) + も; Vて + しまう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: I looked for books on subjects such as law and economics at the library.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of looking for books takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: や connects examples in an incomplete list of books.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: など adds more examples, while の turns the whole phrase into a modifier for 本.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks books as the object being searched for.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The past polite verb is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: The place comes before the object group, while the example group comes before 本 to modify the type of books. や and など together create an incomplete list.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence usually gives a complete list of two items: law and economics.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: とかNとか has a conversational tone and gives an incomplete list of examples.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may forget の after など when the whole phrase comes before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q5.kobun.cn: NやNなど; Nなどの + N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: It seems that Kawanaka has started learning guitar.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Kawanaka as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks guitar as the object of learning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 習い is the connecting form of the verb 習う. It comes before はじめる to express the beginning of learning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: らしい attaches to a clause in the plain form to express heard information or an inference.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the object of learning and the verb phrase showing the beginning of the action. らしい comes at the end to turn all this information into a statement based on hearsay or inference.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～そうだ is used, the sentence can easily mean “it looks as if the person is about to start learning,” based on visible signs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: ～ようだ expresses a judgment based on the situation or evidence, not necessarily information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: ます must be removed before connecting はじめる: 習います becomes 習いはじめる, and 習いますはじめる is not used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q6.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + はじめる; V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + らしい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: There is a child standing over there with a face that looks as if they are about to cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the child exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.vi: looks as if they are about to cry
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: そうな connects to a verb stem to express an appearance or a sign that something is about to happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 顔 with 子ども and creates a phrase that modifies the child.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject who is standing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 立って connects with います to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ています expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.cn: V without ます + そうだ/そうな
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The phrase なきそうな顔の modifies 子ども, so it comes before the noun 子ども. あそこに gives the location, while 子どもが is the subject of the action 立っている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: When used at the end of a sentence, this pattern expresses a direct prediction and does not modify a following noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means “like doing something” or “having the quality of doing something.” It does not strongly emphasize that something is about to happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use the full dictionary form before そう; remove ます first, then connect it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: My older brother is saying that he wants a new car.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the older brother as the speaker of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the entire quoted statement; が marks the car as the object of desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 言って connects with います to express speaking or continuing to say something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ています indicates a continuing state or action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The words are placed inside 「」, and と connects them to the verb 言う. In the quoted clause, 車が is what is wanted, while ほしい is the adjective expressing desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたい is used, the sentence says that the speaker wants to perform an action themselves, not that they want to have an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is commonly used to say that another person seems to want something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: With ほしい, the desired object usually takes が, not を as when expressing a desire to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q8.kobun.cn: N + が + ほしい/ほしくない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: I went to visit my friend who was in the hospital because of an injury.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause of being hospitalized.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ている creates a continuing state, and the whole phrase modifies 友だち.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 友だち with おみまい and shows that the visit is for the friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.vi: to visit the friend in the hospital
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 行った is the past form and the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: けがで gives the reason for the hospitalization. The clause 入院している comes before 友だち to identify which friend, and then おみまいに indicates the purpose of 行った.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the reason is stated more formally and emphasized more strongly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only points to a place or an object; by itself, it does not state the purpose of visiting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: で in this sentence indicates a cause, not a place or means.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vi: I cannot do it, but let my husband try doing it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the subject being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two contrasting ideas and softens the transition to a suggestion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person who is allowed or made to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: やらせて is the causative form combined with みる to say to let that person try doing it; ましょう creates a suggestion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.why: After saying that they cannot do it, the speaker suggests letting their husband do it instead. に marks the person who performs the action in the causative structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the husband will be the one who actively tries to do it. The meaning that the speaker lets or makes him do it is lost.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes receiving help from the husband rather than letting the husband do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に in the causative form with を. With intransitive verbs or expressions meaning to let someone do something, the person performing the action usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q1.kobun.cn: N に ＋ V使役形 ＋ てみる; Vて ＋ みる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vi: Put a coin in here and press the button, and juice will come out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the operation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being put in.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 入れて is the て form, connecting this operation with the next action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the button being pressed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb おす combines with と to express a natural result that occurs after the operation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the thing that appears as the result of the operation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: 出てくる describes something coming out and moving toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.why: The two operations are connected by the て form in the correct order. After the button-pressing action, と connects the cause with a natural result that occurs immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with たら, the sentence focuses more on a specific condition and does not emphasize an automatic result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 出てきます is replaced with 出ていきます, the movement goes away from the reference point instead of coming out toward it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use たら for every conditional sentence and overlook the natural-result nuance of と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vi: I bought this comic because I intended to have my younger sister read it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who intends to carry out the causative action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who is made or allowed to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 読ませる is the causative form of 読む, while 読ませよう is the volitional form; と marks the content of the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 思って uses the て form to connect the intention with the action of buying the comic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the thing that was bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 買いました is the main predicate in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない・Vます omit ます＋(さ)せる; V意向形＋と思う; Vて＋
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.why: The person carrying out the intention stands at the beginning of the sentence, and the person who is allowed to read goes with に. The intended content is quoted with と, and then 思って connects it to the completed action of buying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 妹に読ませるつもりで is used, the sentence only states an intention with a planning nuance. It does not directly express the speaker's thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means intending to ask the younger sister to read or help do something, not intending to let the younger sister read.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q11.kobun.tip: It is necessary to distinguish に in the causative sentence from を: the person being made to act usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vi: If you keep watching TV for a long time, your eyesight will get worse.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.sk: Aい ＋ N時間 ＋ N を ＋ Vます omit ます ＋ つづけると、＋ N が ＋ Aい omit い ＋ くなる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the action of watching and shows that it lasts for a long time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks what is being watched.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 見つづける consists of the verb stem 見 and つづける, expressing continuing to watch; と connects the condition with a natural result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the body part that undergoes a change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: An i-adjective changes into the form without い and adds く before なる to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます＋つづける; V辞書形＋と; Aい omit い＋くなる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.why: The duration and object are placed before the main verb. つづける emphasizes that the action continues, while と connects that action with a result that usually occurs naturally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見ながら is used, it means watching while doing something else, without emphasizing continuous watching for a long time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見つづけたら is used, the sentence becomes a more specific hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q12.kobun.tip: The stem used before つづける must be the form without ます, such as 見つづける; 見ますつづける is not used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vi: I do not know whether my mother will be happy with this gift.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject who performs the action of being happy in the clause being questioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the gift as the object of 喜ぶ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: かどうか turns the preceding clause into unknown content, meaning whether or not the person does that action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 分かりません is the main predicate and expresses that the speaker has no information about the preceding content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.why: The clause about the mother's feelings is placed before かどうか as the content that needs to be known. The subject in the subordinate clause uses が, while the main predicate 分かりません expresses uncertainty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 母が喜ぶか分かりません is used, the meaning is still not knowing whether she will be happy, but the direct-question nuance is clearer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: でしょうか is used for polite questions or guesses. It does not create a choice clause functioning as the object of 分かりません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.tip: In the subordinate clause before かどうか, do not add です after a verb in the plain form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋かどうか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.vi: This TV often breaks down, and the sound is poor, so I want to buy a new one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 副詞 ＋ Vるし、＋ N も ＋ Aいから、＋ Aい＋のを ＋ Vます omit ます＋たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the TV as the common topic of the comments.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies 故障する and indicates how often the TV breaks down.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: し connects the first reason and shows that another reason follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds the sound to the list of bad features, instead of は or が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: から directly connects the reason to the wish to buy a new television.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: の replaces a known noun, while を marks the item the speaker wants to buy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: 買いたい expresses the speaker's wish and ends the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋し; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋から; Vます omit ます＋たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.why: し lists inconvenient points, then から gives the reason leading to the wish to buy a new one. の replaces the noun “television” that was already mentioned to avoid repetition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 悪いから is replaced with 悪いので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern lists typical actions or states, so it is not suitable for directly joining reasons such as し.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q14.kobun.tip: し can connect several reasons; do not understand it simply as a connector meaning “and.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time から ＋ N が ＋ Vます omit ます＋はじめる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the time reference for the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates when the rain began.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the event that has started.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 降り is the stem of 降る combined with はじめる to express the start of rain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます＋はじめる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.why: The day and starting time are stated before the rain. The verb stem 降り comes before はじめる to create the meaning “begin to happen.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 降りだしました is used, the rain seems to have started suddenly, with a stronger feeling than はじめる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 雨が降っています is used, the sentence only says that it is raining, without stating when it began.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q15.kobun.tip: Before はじめる, use the verb stem without ます: 降ります becomes 降り, not 降るはじめる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.vi: It smells like strawberries. Did you buy them?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun いちご with におい, creating the phrase “strawberry smell.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the smell as the thing producing the sensation being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: する expresses that there is a smell; けど connects to the following question with a softer tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 買った is the past form, while んですか turns the sentence into a confirmation question based on a reason or evidence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.why: The phrase いちごのにおいがする first gives the basis for the speaker's impression, then けど gently changes to a question for the listener. The past form in 買った shows that the buying action has already happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this phrase emphasizes a pleasant fragrance rather than smell in general.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This question directly asks whether the person bought it, with less explanation or confirmation than んですか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate けど as “but” in every case, while here it mainly makes the question softer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q16.kobun.cn: Nの＋においがする; V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nな＋んですか; V・A・N＋けど
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.vi: Please return this book by March 31.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Deadline までに ＋ Vてくださいね
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this book the topic of the reminder.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the book-returning action must be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ください creates a polite request; ね makes the reminder gentle and friendly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.cn: N・Time＋までに; Vて＋ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and the deadline is placed before the verb to set the completion point. The pattern Vてください turns returning the book into a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is used, the action continues up to that point, without emphasizing completion before it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning does not change much, but kanji is used instead of hiragana in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q17.kobun.tip: Do not confuse までに with まで: までに is the deadline for completion, while まで usually only indicates an endpoint.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.vi: This is used to look at distant places.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the object being introduced the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 遠い comes before ところ to modify the place being viewed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the distant place as the object of the verb 見る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: の nominalizes 見る, and then に indicates the purpose of use.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 使います is the main predicate and states what the object is used for.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.why: The object is introduced as the topic, followed by the thing being viewed and the purpose of use. に connects with the nominalized phrase 見るの to express “what something is used for.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this pattern still shows purpose, but the tone is clearer, more formal, and more focused on the goal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that the object is convenient for looking, rather than directly saying how the object is used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q18.kobun.tip: Do not understand のに here as “although”; in this structure, の nominalizes the verb and に indicates purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.vi: What time do you leave home?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.sk: Time に ＋ N を ＋ Vるんですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates when the action of leaving home takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the starting place with the verb 出る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 出る is the main verb; んですか creates a confirmation question about the time of leaving.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.cn: Place＋を＋出る; V普通形＋んですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning to ask “when,” while 家を出る is a fixed phrase meaning leaving a place. The verb is in the dictionary form because the action being asked about is a routine or has no specific time yet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is similar, but から emphasizes the starting point more; 家を出る is the natural way to say leaving home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If the past form is used, the question asks whether the person has left home, not about their usual schedule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q19.kobun.tip: With 出る, the place left is usually marked with を, not を, which marks an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vi: Please contact me whenever you have trouble.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.sk: Question word ＋ でも ＋ Vた ＋ 時 は ＋ Vてください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: でも comes after a question word to expand it to mean every possible time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 時 indicates time; は states the situation that serves as the condition for the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.why: いつでも expands the time to mean any time. The phrase 困った時は puts the situation first, followed by the request to make contact.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with いつか, it means at some time, so the meaning “at any time” is lost.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 困ったら is used, the sentence emphasizes the condition of having trouble and sounds more hypothetical.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.tip: Learners may easily translate でも as “but”; after a question word, でも instead means “any.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q2.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 + でも; Vた + 時
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.vi: I like both cats and dogs, but I do not like cats as much as dogs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: も marks cats as one of the things the speaker likes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: も connects dogs with cats, creating the meaning “both cats and dogs”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: すき is the adjective predicate な; が connects to the opposite idea and makes the transition softer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes cats the topic of comparison in the second clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ほど sets dogs as the standard for comparing the level of liking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: ではありません makes the adjective な negative with すき and completes the pattern ほど～ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.why: The first clause uses も～も to state that both things are liked. The second clause chooses cats as the topic, uses dogs as the standard of comparison, and denies the degree of liking with the pattern ほど～ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this pattern, the sentence directly says which thing is liked more, with a stronger affirmative tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means that the speaker likes cats almost as much as dogs, which is opposite to the negative comparison in the original sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand ほど as “very,” but in ほど～ない it creates a negative comparison: not as much as or not to the same degree as.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q20.kobun.cn: N＋ほど＋Vない／Aいくない／Aなではない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vi: I think I will choose a heater as my mother's birthday present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects mother with the present and shows the recipient or the person related to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the birthday present the topic of the decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the selected result in the structure にする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: しよう is the volitional form of する; と marks the content of the intention being considered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 思う is the main predicate and takes the intended content immediately before と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.why: The present is mentioned first, then にする shows that the specific choice is a heater. The volitional form しよう comes before とと思う to express the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence emphasizes the intention to buy a heater, not the choice to make it a present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern expresses a clearer decision, while しようと思う keeps the meaning of having an intention or having just thought of an idea.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.tip: に in にする does not only indicate a place; it marks the chosen result or option.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q21.kobun.cn: N＋にする; V意向形＋と思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.vi: Huh? It is so hot, but you are still wearing two layers of clothing?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.sk: 程度副詞 ＋ Aい のに ＋ N を ＋ Number も ＋ Vているんですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies 暑い and emphasizes how hot it is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: のに connects a contrasting clause with what is said in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks clothes as the object of the action of wearing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: も comes after a number to emphasize that the amount is more than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: 着ている describes the state of wearing something; んですか creates a question with a sense of surprise.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.cn: Number ＋ も; V普通形・Aい ＋ のに／Aな・N ＋ なのに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.why: Clause 暑いのに gives the contrasting situation, then 服を着ている gives the surprising action. も comes after the number to highlight wearing as many as two layers of clothing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のに with けれども leaves only the meaning “but,” so the surprise and contrast with expectations become weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use ２まいしか着ていない, the meaning becomes “wear only two,” so it no longer emphasizes that the number is large.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that も comes immediately after a number and means “as many as” or “a full.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.vi: The name has been written on the hat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.sk: Place に ＋ N が ＋ Vてあります
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the resulting state exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that is in the written state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: てあります describes a remaining state caused by someone intentionally writing something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.cn: Place に ＋ N が ＋ Vてある
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.why: ぼうしに identifies the location, 名前が marks the thing existing there, and 書いてあります emphasizes that the result of writing is still visible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: 書いています indicates the action of writing or someone writing, without emphasizing the state of something having already been written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: 書かれています also indicates a written state, but it focuses more on the passive meaning and does not emphasize intentional action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use を after a place in this pattern; the location of the state usually uses に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.vi: I do not know how much it costs to go to Hokkaido.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.sk: N まで ＋ Question word ＋ V辞書形 か ＋ わかりません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: まで indicates the endpoint or destination of the journey.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: いくら asks about the amount of money needed and modifies かかる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the question clause into unknown content and makes it part of わかりません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main predicate and expresses that the speaker does not know the content before か.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.cn: Question word ＋ clause in the plain form ＋ か ＋ わかる／知る
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.why: 北海道まで defines the journey's range, いくらかかるか is the content being asked about, and わかりません concludes that this content is unknown.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: 知りません also means “do not know,” but it emphasizes not having information rather than not understanding or not being sure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: でしょうか is a direct question with a guessing tone, not a clause used as the object of わかりません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q24.kobun.tip: When a question word appears in an indirect clause, keep か after the clause and do not change the word order as in English.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.vi: There are few cars around here, and it is dark, so please be careful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the area being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that is few in number in the area.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: し connects one reason with other reasons that follow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the cause with the advice to be careful in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 気をつけてください uses the form てください to make a request or give advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ し／Aい ＋ し／Aな・N ＋ だし; clause ＋ から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.why: は sets the area as the topic, and が marks cars as the thing being described as few. し lists another reason, while から connects the direct cause with the advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ので instead of から still shows a reason, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: または means “or” and is not used to list several reasons like し.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q25.kobun.tip: し does not simply mean “and” in every situation; here it connects reasons that lead to advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vi: Although he himself is at fault, he still does not intend to apologize to everyone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being evaluated in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the adjective 悪い in the subordinate clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: のに connects a fact with a result that is contrary to what would normally be expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person receiving the apology.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: とする expresses an intention or an attempt to do something, while しない negates that intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.why: The clause 自分が悪いのに states the background fact, but the following action is contrary to what is normally expected. に identifies the recipient of the apology, while 意向形＋としない negates the intention to carry it out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with けれども, the sentence only connects two contrasting ideas. It does not stress the sense of “even so” or “contrary to expectations.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is changed to 謝らない, the sentence only says that he does not apologize. It does not stress the lack of intention or refusal to try.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use のに as an independent connector; a complete clause stating the cause or fact must come before のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vi: Because it is easy to catch a cold in autumn, please be careful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ Vます drop ます ＋ やすいですから、＋ N を ＋ Vてくださいね
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that autumn is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object affected by the verb ひく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it is easy to catch
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: やすい follows a verb stem to show that something is easy to do, while から connects a cause with a result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object in the phrase 気をつける, meaning to pay attention or be careful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: てください makes a polite request, while ね makes the tone softer and friendlier.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.cn: Vます drop ます ＋ やすい; cause clause ＋ から; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.why: 秋は sets the topic, then states the object 風邪をひく and changes the stem ひき into ひきやすい to express that catching a cold is easy. から connects the cause with the reminder 気をつけてください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with にくい, the meaning changes to being difficult to catch a cold or difficult to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason stays the same, but the expression sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q4.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily forget that やすい attaches to the verb stem after dropping ます, rather than attaching directly to the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vi: This inn is fully booked because too many people made reservations, so let us choose a hotel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects こちら with 旅館 to modify the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the inn is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the reason why the inn is full.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ですから connects the state of being fully booked with the decision in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the choice in the pattern Nにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form of する, used to suggest making a decision together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.why: The first sentence states the inn’s situation and its reason using で and から. Then, ホテルに marks the chosen option, while しましょう turns that choice into a suggestion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ホテルになりましょう is used, the sentence means becoming a hotel, not deciding to choose a hotel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ホテルを選びましょう, the meaning is similar, but を is used because 選ぶ is a verb that directly means choose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use を with する to mean choose; this pattern must use Nにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.tokens.10.m: let us choose; let us do
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q5.kobun.cn: N ＋ にする; N・Aな ＋ ですから; Vましょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vi: Just as I was about to leave the house, my friend came.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place of departure in the expression 家を出る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: when I was about to leave
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 出よう is the volitional form, とする expresses an intention, and とした時 indicates the exact time when I was about to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject performing the action of coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: やってきた expresses someone coming toward the speaker or the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.cn: Volitional-form V ＋ とする; Vた ＋ 時; Vて ＋ くる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.why: The clause 出ようとした時 sets the time for the main event. The subject of the main event is 友達, while やってきた emphasizes movement toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 出ようとしたら is used, the nuance is that another event is noticed or occurs just as someone is about to leave.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If やってきた is replaced with やっていった, the direction of movement changes to away from the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q6.kobun.tip: English speakers may translate くる simply as come and overlook the meaning of movement toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vi: It took ten years to build this building.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.sk: N を ＋ V辞書形のに ＋ time period N ＋ かかりました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies the noun ビル that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the building action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the action 建てる into a noun, and に indicates a purpose or an activity that takes time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The time phrase adds the amount of time needed for かかる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: かかりました acts as the predicate and states the time needed to complete the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ のに（purpose）; time N・cost ＋ かかる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.why: 建てるのに turns building into a purpose whose time must be measured. １０年 comes before かかる to state the amount of time spent.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 建てるために is used, it emphasizes the purpose of building, but it is less natural than のに when talking about the time needed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used with the meaning “although,” it must have a contrasting clause. This differs from のに in this sentence, which means “in order to do something.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q7.kobun.tip: English speakers may think のに always means “although,” but after a dictionary-form verb and before かかる, it usually indicates purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vi: I have something I would like to ask…
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.sk: ちょっと ＋ お＋Vます drop ます＋したい ＋ Nが ＋ あるんですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: お聞きしたい is a humble expression used to modify こと.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the pattern ことがある.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: んですか creates a question used to confirm something or begin an explanation, while the three dots show that the sentence trails off.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.cn: お＋Vます drop ます＋する; Vます drop ます＋たい; V普通形＋んですか／Aい＋んですか／Aな・N＋な＋んですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.why: The phrase お聞きしたい comes before こと to modify the thing the speaker wants to ask about. ことがある expresses that something exists, while んですか helps the speaker begin softly and politely.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is still that there is something to ask, but the level of humility is lower.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If the sentence ends with でしょうか, the question is more polite and direct, with less of an explanatory or opening tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q8.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily write お聞き incorrectly as お聞した; き must be kept because お＋聞き＋する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vi: I went outside without washing my face.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action of washing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 洗わない is the negative form, while まま shows that this state is kept unchanged while doing another action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the direction of movement of the action 出かける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 出かけました is the main predicate and describes the action of going outside that has already happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.cn: Vない + まま; place noun + へ + 出かける
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.why: 顔を is the object of 洗う, and then 洗わないまま keeps the unwashed state. 外へ shows direction, and 出かけました is the main action that happens in that state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 洗わないで is used, it only says that the person did not wash and then left. It does not emphasize keeping the state unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 洗わずに is used, the meaning is similar to ないで, but it is more common in written and formal language.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t10-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse まま with ないで; まま emphasizes that the state is kept unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vi: Whenever I look at this photo, I remember my elementary school days.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the photo as the object of the action of looking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition with a result that naturally happens whenever the photo is seen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 小学生の modifies ころ to form the time being remembered; を marks the object of 思い出す.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 思い出す is the main verb and takes the remembered content with を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.why: この写真を見ると creates a repeated condition, and then 思い出します states the result that happens naturally. を is used with both the object being seen and the content being remembered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 見たら usually shows a one-time condition or a specific moment. It does not emphasize that the result always happens whenever the photo is seen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 見たなら is based on an assumption or information already known. It does not express a natural relationship like 見ると.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use と when the following clause is a command or expresses intention; this pattern is suitable for natural, repeated results.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vi: I went to the sea to go for a drive.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.0.vi: all the way to the sea
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle まで shows the destination or limit of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The form without ます of ドライブします combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きました is the main verb in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.why: 海まで gives the destination, while ドライブしに gives the purpose of going. The verb 行きました comes at the end to complete the idea of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ために is used, the purpose sounds more formal and it can be used with nouns or plain-form verbs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～へ行く is used, the sentence only says that someone went toward or to the sea. It does not state the purpose of driving.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に after the noun ドライブ instead of using the form without ます ドライブしに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q10.kobun.cn: Vます形語幹 + に + 行く・来る・帰る
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vi: I cannot cut an apple with a knife.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は states who is being talked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle で shows the tool used for cutting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the object affected by the cutting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 切ること turns the action of cutting into a noun, while が marks that action in the ability structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: できません is the main predicate and denies the ability to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, ナイフで shows the tool, and りんごを shows the affected object. The action 切る is nominalized with こと so that it can combine with ことができません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If the potential form such as 切れません is used, the sentence is shorter and focuses directly on the ability to cut.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is added to ことはできない, the sentence emphasizes or contrasts that this particular action cannot be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often put を after こと, but this pattern requires ことができる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q11.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる・できない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle に shows the place where the car is parked.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the car as the object of the action of parking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 止めるな uses the dictionary form of a verb with な to order someone not to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q12.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the action. な at the end of the sentence turns the clause into a direct and strong prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～てはいけない is used, the prohibition remains, but the full expression is usually more neutral.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ないでください is used, the sentence becomes a polite request not to park.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse な in this pattern with な, which is used after the adjective な; here it comes after the dictionary form to show prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vi: If you have a fever, you should not swim.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks ねつ as the state stated in the condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: あるなら creates a conditional clause and sets the situation as the basis for the advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.2.vi: it is better not to swim
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: およがないほうが states the option that is recommended as better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: いいですよ completes the pattern for advising someone to do or not do something and also softens the statement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.why: The clause with あるなら puts the condition first and then gives the advice. The negative form およがない combines with ほうがいい to say that not swimming is the better option.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～たら is used, the condition is usually connected to a situation that occurs or is more clearly identified.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～べきだ is used, the advice is stronger and has a sense of obligation, not just a better choice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use およがないほうがいい as an independent sentence and forget to put the condition あるなら first.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + なら; Vない + ほうがいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify it and identify the newspaper being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the newspaper as the object of reading.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: お読みになりますか uses an honorific pattern to ask politely about the listener's action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q14.kobun.why: この新聞を is the noun phrase serving as the object of reading. お読みになりますか comes at the end to ask the question while showing respect to the person being asked.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If お読みください is used, the sentence becomes a request or invitation to read, not a question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 読みますか is used, the sentence still asks the same question but loses the honorific tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often add です after になりますか, but になりますか is already the complete ending of the honorific pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.vi: You should not ask a woman's age.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle に shows the person whose age is being asked.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the information being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞いちゃ is a shortened form of 聞いては and connects the action to the prohibition pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: いけません completes the pattern ～てはいけません and expresses something that must not be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.why: The person being asked goes with に, while 年 is the content being asked about, so it goes with を. The form 聞いては is shortened to 聞いちゃ before the negative form いけません to create a prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes a polite request not to ask someone's age, with a weaker prohibitive meaning.
