default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence has a stronger and more formal prohibitive meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and を, but the person being asked uses に, while the thing being asked about uses を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.vi: Because my eyesight is poor, I cannot read books without wearing glasses.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: 目が is the subject of the adjective 悪い and describes the condition of the eyes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the result and gives a softer explanatory tone than から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the item being worn.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: かけずに connects an action that is not performed with the main action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object of the reading action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb 読む is turned into a noun with こと and becomes the object judged as possible or impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: できません expresses negated ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.cn: Vない形（ないを remove）＋ずに; V辞書形＋ことができる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.why: The clause 目が悪いので gives the reason before the result. かけずに places the action of not wearing glasses before the reading action, while 読むことができません uses nominalization to talk about the possibility of reading.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If かけずに is replaced with かけないで, the meaning stays almost the same, but the expression is more common and less formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことはできません is used, the sentence emphasizes that reading is completely impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q16.kobun.tip: Do not connect ずに directly to a noun; change the verb to the ない form and then remove ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.vi: Because I want to see my parents, I plan to return to my country once after graduating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object of meeting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I want to meet them
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 会いたいから gives the reason for the plan in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: たら sets the condition or time when the action of returning home will happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 一度 modifies the action 帰ろう and shows how many times it is planned to happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle へ shows the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: と quotes the content of the intention in volitional form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.6.n: 思う is the main predicate and takes the intention as the quoted content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.why: The reason with から comes first, and then たら identifies when the plan will be carried out. The intention comes before 思う and is connected with と as the content being thought about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 帰ろうと思う is replaced with 帰るつもりだ, the sentence states the plan more clearly and firmly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If 帰る予定だ is used, the sentence focuses more on a schedule or an arranged plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.tip: The volitional form must be used with と思う when talking about the speaker's plan; do not use the plain form 帰るとと思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q17.kobun.cn: Vた形＋ら; V意向形＋と＋思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.vi: When leaving the house, say “I’m leaving now.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.sk: N を ＋ V辞書形ときに ＋ 「Quoted sentence」と ＋ 言う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を shows the place one leaves, used with the verb 出る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 出る modifies とき, while に shows the time when the greeting is said.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the exact words being spoken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 言います is the main predicate and takes the sentence in quotation marks as the spoken content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形＋とき; Quoted sentence＋と＋言う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.why: 家を出るときに identifies the time of the speaking action. The greeting stays inside quotation marks and is connected to 言います by と as the spoken content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 家を出たとき is used, the focus is on the time after leaving the house, when the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If 家を出る場合 is used, the sentence means “in the case of leaving the house” rather than pointing to a specific time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.kobun.tip: と in this sentence does not mean “and”; it marks quoted speech.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q18.tokens.6.m: I’m leaving now and will come back
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.vi: Studying while singing is not good.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.sk: Vます（remove ます）＋ながら ＋ V辞書形のは ＋ Aい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: ながら connects two actions happening at the same time, with 歌う as the secondary action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns 勉強する into a noun, while は makes the whole activity of singing while studying the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: よくない is the predicate that judges the action just mentioned as not good.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.cn: Vます（remove ます）＋ながら; V辞書形＋のは＋Aい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.why: The secondary action 歌いながら comes before the main action 勉強する. The whole activity is nominalized with の and made the topic with は, then judged with よくない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 歌っている間に, the sentence emphasizes the period of singing rather than the two actions happening together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If 歌いつつ is used, the meaning is similar, but the style is more written and formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q19.kobun.tip: ながら attaches to the stem ます, so ます of 歌います must be removed, giving 歌いながら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vi: A person named Suzuki came earlier.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N という ＋ N が ＋ Vました ＋ よ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: さっき shows the time when the action happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: という comes after a name and modifies 人, showing that the person is named Suzuki.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who came.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: よ is used to tell the listener new information or to emphasize information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.cn: N ＋ という ＋ N; sentence ＋ よ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.why: すずきという modifies 人 to identify the person's name. 人が is the subject of 来ました, while よ shows that the listener may not know this information yet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: すずきの人 is not natural for saying a person's name; personal names usually combine with という人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression directly states that Suzuki came, without emphasizing the structure “a person called Suzuki”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q2.kobun.tip: という in this pattern does not mean “say that”; it is used to introduce a name or form of address.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.vi: Stay seated on the chair until everyone finishes eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Vます（remove ます）＋終わるまで ＋ N に ＋ Vて＋いなさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the action of finishing eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べ終わる combines the eating action with 終わる to show completion, while まで marks the time limit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the place where the seated state is maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ていなさい asks someone to maintain a seated position during the stated period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.cn: Vます（remove ます）＋終わる; Vて＋いなさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.why: The clause with まで sets the ending point before the main command. 食べ終わる describes eating being completed, while すわっていなさい asks the listener to remain seated until that point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べ終わるまでに is used, it means that something must be finished by that point or no later than then, not that the action continues until then.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べ終わる間 is used, the expression is unnatural here; 間 usually states the whole period during which a state continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q20.kobun.tip: Distinguish まで from までに: まで means “until”, while までに means “before that deadline”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.vi: This curry rice is too spicy to eat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aい remove い ＋ すぎて ＋ negative potential-form V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks this curry dish as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: すぎる is attached to the form of an い-adjective after removing い to show an excessive degree; て connects it to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べられません is the negative potential form, expressing that it cannot be eaten.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ すぎる; Aな ＋ すぎる; V remove ます ＋ すぎる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.why: The noun comes before は, followed by the reason からすぎて and then the result 食べられません. The form て naturally links the two ideas “too spicy” and “cannot eat”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ので, the sentence only states the cause-and-effect relationship “because it is too spicy, so”, without emphasizing the excessive degree as すぎる does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to remove い before すぎる, so they should not say からいすぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.vi: Wow, that fruit cake looks delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.sk: 感嘆 ＋ Aい remove い ＋ そうな ＋ N ですね
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: おいしそうな directly modifies the noun フルーツケーキ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.ch.2.vi: it is a fruit cake, right
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is placed at the end of the sentence to gently confirm or share an opinion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ そうだ; Aな ＋ そうだ; Vます remove ます ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.why: おいしそうな comes before the noun because it describes the cake. ですね at the end of the sentence gives an opinion and invites the listener to agree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: This form is not used to talk about appearance; when you want to say that you heard someone say it is delicious, use おいしいそうだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q22.kobun.tip: With an い-adjective, remove い before そうだ: おいしそうだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.vi: My father told me to study more.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.sk: N に ＋ Adv ＋ imperative V ＋ と ＋ past passive V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who made the statement in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the entire quoted command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 言われた is the past passive form, expressing that the speaker received a request from their father.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.cn: imperative V ＋ と ＋ 言う・言われる; plain-form V ＋ と ＋ 言う・言われる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.why: The command 勉強しろ is placed before と, while 言われた at the end of the sentence shows that the speaker was asked to do this. 父に marks the person who performed the speaking action in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the statement becomes softer and means that the speaker was told to study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q23.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence with 言われる, the speaker uses に, while the content of the statement uses と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q24.kobun.sk: Adv ＋ N に ＋ お＋Vます remove ます＋ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the listener performs the action of sitting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: お＋the form after removing ます＋ください create a polite request to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q24.kobun.cn: お＋Vます remove ます＋ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q24.kobun.why: こちらに indicates a place and comes before the invitation to perform the action. おかけください is placed at the end to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 座ってください, the invitation is still polite but less formal than おかけください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q24.kobun.tip: Do not attach ください directly after the dictionary form of a verb; use the て form or the pattern お＋remove ます＋ください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.vi: I used Japanese incorrectly, so everyone laughed at me, and I felt very embarrassed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vて ＋ N に ＋ passive continuative V ＋ Adv ＋ past Aい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action or the Japanese that was used incorrectly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects an action or reason to the next clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who performed the action of laughing in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: わらわれ is the passive form; the comma connects this situation to the emotion in the next clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: The はずかしい-adjective is put into the past form to express an emotion after an event has occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.cn: Vて; passive V; past Aい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.why: まちがえて states the reason that led to being laughed at. In a passive sentence, the person who performs the action goes with に, and then はずかしかった states the speaker's emotion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with みんながわらって, the sentence only says that everyone laughed, without emphasizing that the speaker was affected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use が for the person who laughs, but a passive sentence needs に to indicate the agent.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vi: The park where children play must be a safe place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子どもたち with the modified noun, which is こうえん.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb あそぶ comes before a noun to modify こうえん.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な comes before 場所 and keeps な to modify this noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: で is the linking form that connects a noun with なければならない in the structure meaning “must be”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern なければならない expresses obligation or necessity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.why: The clause あそぶ modifies こうえん, forming the phrase “the park where children play”. After stating the topic with は, the sentence uses あんぜんな場所で to specify that the park must be a safe kind of place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence changes to mean that it does not need to be safe.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only states the prediction “it should be a safe place”, and no longer expresses obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget な after the な-adjective before the noun and may confuse なければならない with a meaning of prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q3.kobun.cn: Nで ＋ なければならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vi: What time are you coming home today?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets 今日 as the time reference for the question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the action 帰ってくる occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 帰ってくる in the dictionary form combines with の？ to form a casual question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.why: 今日は states the time range, while 何時に asks for a specific time. の？ comes at the end of the sentence to ask the listener for information in a casual way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence still asks for similar information but is more polite and has a clearer explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If か is used, the sentence becomes a neutral or more polite question and is less casual.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で with a time, but a specific time such as 何時 needs to go with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ の？
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vi: My mother made a cake for me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.sk: Agent が ＋ Recipient に ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ くれる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performed the action of making the cake.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who benefits from the action 作ってくれました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 作って is the form of て joined with くれました. It shows that the mother did it for the speaker’s benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.why: 母が is the person who does the action, わたしに is the person who benefits, and ケーキを is the thing made. The form て joins with くれる to show that another person’s action benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the focus shifts to me receiving help from my mother.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the person doing the action is viewed from the side of the person who does it for someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the direction of くれる and もらう when deciding who gives and who receives.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I came to school by taxi.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.sk: Time は + Means of transport で + Nへ + Vました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks きのう as the time topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the means of transport used for travel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action 来ました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ました is the polite past form of 来る and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.why: The sentence is ordered by time, means of transport, destination, and then action. で states how the person travels, while へ directs the action toward school.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 来ました is replaced with に行きました, it means going to school from another place, without using the speaker as the reference point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is used for 学校, it usually indicates the place where the action happens, not the destination.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for means of transport, but transport usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vi: According to the letter, I heard that my grandmother is still well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.sk: Source of information によると + Nは + Nだそうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: によると indicates the source of information supporting the following content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the topic mentioned in the information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: だそうです attaches to a noun or adjective な to pass on information that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.why: 手紙によると gives the source of the information, and then そぼは identifies the person being discussed. 元気だそうです uses the form だ before そうです because 元気 is an adjective な.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: In the appearance pattern, the adjective な usually connects directly to そうです and means “seems,” unlike the hearsay meaning in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ようです, the speaker is making an inference based on signs or evidence, rather than only passing on heard information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit だ before そうです after a noun or adjective な when using the information-reporting pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka seems to want to go home early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.sk: Person が + Vます-removeます + たがっている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who shows the desire being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 早く is an adverb form that modifies the action 帰りたがっています.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.2.vi: showing a desire to go home
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 帰り is the connecting stem of the verb and joins with たがっています to express a desire observed in another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.why: 田中さんが is the person showing the desire, while 早く modifies the time or manner of returning home. たがる is used because the speaker is describing another person’s desire, not their own.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 帰りたい, the sentence expresses the direct desire of the speaker or of a character speaking about themselves.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 帰りたいようだ is used, the nuance is an inference, “seems to want to go home,” with more focus on judgment than on the visible desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use たい to express another person’s desire, while たがる is needed when the speaker observes that desire from outside.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q8.tokens.4.m: want to; seem to want to
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vi: I do not know whether I will meet my partner at Christmas.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the time when the meeting takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と indicates the person who carries out the meeting action with the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase 会うかどうか forms an indirect question clause and serves as the content that is or is not known.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりません is the main predicate and expresses a state of not knowing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.why: The time and the person accompanying the speaker come before the action content. The phrase 会うかどうか changes the question of whether they will meet into the content of わかりません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～か is used, the sentence usually has the nuance of a direct question or question content, while ～かどうか emphasizes the two possibilities of yes or no.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ～かもしれない, the sentence means that they may meet, not that the speaker does not know whether they will meet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle かどうか or use it as a direct question instead of placing it before わかりません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t11-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + かどうか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vi: The teacher’s way of speaking is very similar to my father’s.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.sk: N の + Vます remove ます + 方 は + N に + Adv + Vている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun 先生 with 話し方 to modify it and show possession.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 話し方 is made from the verb stem 話します and 方. It means the way an action is done; は marks the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies 父 and shows that the father belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the object used to compare the degree of similarity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: よく modifies にている and emphasizes the degree of similarity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: にている is a predicate that describes a state of being similar to an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + 方
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.why: 話し方 is the topic. It is made from the verb 話す and 方 to talk about a way of speaking. The pattern NはNに似ている uses に for the object of comparison and places the similar predicate at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 同じだ, the meaning changes from “similar” to “exactly the same or of the same type,” with a stronger nuance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q1.kobun.tip: 方 must attach to the verb stem without ます, so use 話し方, not 話す方, when talking about a way of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vi: Because I do not like singing very much, I plan not to go to karaoke.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic that is judged to be disliked.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: あまり goes with a negative form to reduce the degree and create the meaning “not ... very much.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I do not like it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason before it with the result or intention after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: には marks the place or activity toward which the speaker is going and also adds a mild contrast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 行かない comes before つもり to state the speaker’s negative intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with から, and the speaker’s intention comes after it. The negative form 行かない combines directly with つもり to express the intention not to do that action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予定です is used, the meaning focuses more on a schedule or decided plan and emphasizes personal will less than つもりです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 行きたくないです, the meaning is not wanting to go, which does not necessarily mean that there is already a plan not to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 行かないつもりです for “not planning to go” in the sense of not having decided yet, but this structure usually expresses the intention not to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q10.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形＋つもりです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vi: Which eye sees better, the right eye or the left eye?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the right eye as one of the two objects being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the left eye with the right eye in the pair of choices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: どっち asks about one of the two objects, while が marks the object being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies 見えます and shows the degree of clear vision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 見えますか forms a question about one side's ability to see clearly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.why: The two nouns before と form two choices, and then どっちが asks which side has the quality stated in the predicate. よく comes before 見えます to show the degree of clear vision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If どっち is replaced with どちら, the meaning does not change, but the expression is more polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: どれ is used to choose one item from three or more choices, so it is less suitable than どっち in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use どれ for every “which one” question, but どっち is specifically used when choosing between two objects.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vi: I have just finished work and am about to leave the company.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 identifies the present time of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks work as the task that has just ended.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the completed action with the following action of leaving the company.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the place being left in the use of 会社を出る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: V辞書形＋ところです describes an action that is about to happen at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.why: 終わって connects the task that has just been completed with leaving the company. 出るところです shows that the action of leaving has not happened yet but will happen immediately after the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 出ているところです, it means being in the middle of leaving or going out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 出たところです, it means having just left the company.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the form ている with ところ in every case, but the dictionary form is the one that describes an action that is about to begin.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vている形・Vた形＋ところです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vi: When I cook a tasty dish, I want someone to try eating it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the dish being cooked.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: おいしく is the adverbial form of the adjective おいしい and modifies つくった.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: Vた＋とき indicates the time after the cooking action has been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who performs the action of eating in the structure 食べてもらう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.4.vi: want someone to eat it for me
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べてもらう describes someone else eating it for or on behalf of the speaker, while たくなる shows that a desire arises.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.why: The clause with とき sets the time when the tasty dish is made, and the main clause describes the desire that arises afterward. に identifies the person who will perform the action of eating in the pattern Vてもらう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is replaced with たら, the sentence has the conditional meaning “if it is cooked well,” rather than simply indicating a time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If V辞書形＋とき is used, it refers to the time of preparing to cook or planning to cook, without emphasizing that the cooking has been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 食べてもらう as “be eaten,” but this pattern emphasizes someone else eating it for or on behalf of the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.tokens.2.n: adverbial form of the adjective ending in い
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.tokens.9.m: receive; have someone do something for you
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q13.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形＋とき; Aい＋とき; Aな＋なとき; N＋のとき
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.vi: I did not mean to make her cry, but...
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: かのじょを is the object affected by the causative verb なかせる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: なかせる is the causative form, meaning to make someone cry, and modifies つもり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: つもりは sets the topic as the intention; は creates a negative or contrasting nuance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: なかった is the past negative of つもりだ; のですが softens the sentence and leaves the rest unfinished.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.cn: Vる＋つもりはない／なかった; Vさせる: causative verb
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.why: かのじょを is the object of the causative action, while なかせる describes making her cry. The phrase Vるつもりはなかった shows that there was no intention to do it; のですが creates a hesitant, unfinished tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, it means not wanting to make her cry, emphasizing desire rather than intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced here, the sentence would have the opposite meaning: having intended to make her cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the causative form なかせる with the passive form なかされる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.vi: I am saving money to get married.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: Vる＋ために states the purpose of saving money.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: お金を is the object of ためています and indicates what is being saved.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ためています is the ている form and describes an ongoing saving action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.why: The purpose clause comes before the main action and is connected with ために. お金を is the direct object of ためる, while ています shows that the saving is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるように is used, the sentence focuses more on a goal or something one hopes to achieve, rather than directly emphasizing an intentional purpose like ために.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vたあとで, it means saving money after getting married, which is completely different in time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use ために after a verb in the past form when expressing purpose; use the dictionary form Vる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q15.kobun.cn: Vる＋ために; Nの＋ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.vi: I want to raise this child in a truly childlike way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies 子 and refers to the child near the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 子は makes this child the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 子どもらしく is the adverbial form of 子どもらしい and modifies the way of raising the child.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: そだてたい is the Vたい form and expresses the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.why: 子は is the topic, while 子どもらしく shows the way of raising the child so that it has childlike qualities. たい is attached after the る form of a verb to express desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 子どものように is used, the sentence only says that something is like a child in one aspect, with a weaker sense of being truly or typically childlike.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 子どもみたいに is used, the expression is more conversational and may refer to an outward similarity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.tip: らしく is the form that connects with a verb of らしい; do not use らしい directly to modify a verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q16.kobun.cn: N＋らしい; らしい→らしく＋V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.vi: Because I ate too much, I got a stomachache. So I will take a rest.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.sk: V ＋ たら ＋ Nが ＋ Aい remove い＋くなる ＋ だから ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: たくさん modifies 食べたら and shows the amount eaten.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べたら connects the cause or condition with the result of having a stomachache.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: おなかが is the subject that experiences the painful state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: いたくなる shows the change from not being painful to being painful; なりました is the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: だから connects a result inferred from having a stomachache.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.cn: Vた＋ら; Aい remove い＋くなる; くなる→くなりました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.why: 食べたら states the cause that leads to the new state of having a stomachache. The adjective いたい changes to いたくなる to express becoming painful, and then だから gives resting as the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vると is used, the relationship sounds more like a certain or usual result, rather than a one-time event like 食べたら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If いたくします is used, it means making the stomach hurt, with a clear subject causing the action, rather than the stomach becoming painful by itself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q17.kobun.tip: With adjectives ending in い, remove い and add くなる; do not add くなる directly to the whole adjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.vi: That child is ten years old, yet looks like a baby.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies 子 and refers to a child far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 子は makes that child the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: なのに connects information that goes against the expectation: the child is ten years old but still looks like a baby.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 赤ちゃんの connects a noun with よう and creates a comparison phrase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ようです is placed at the end of a sentence to describe similarity or an appearance like another object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.why: なのに creates a contrast between the actual age and the appearance or state being described. With the noun 赤ちゃん, 赤ちゃんのようです must be used to express looking like a baby.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Nみたいです, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the tone is more casual and conversational.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Nらしいです, the sentence focuses more on typical baby-like characteristics than on simply looking like a baby.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.tip: Before ようです, the noun must have の; do not say 赤ちゃんようです directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q18.kobun.cn: N＋なのに; Nの／V普通形／Aい＋ようです; Aな＋な＋ようです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.vi: Today's test was not as difficult as last week's test.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N ほど ＋ Aい remove い＋くなかった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: きょうの modifies テスト and identifies which test it is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: テストは makes today's test the object being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 先週の modifies テスト and identifies the comparison point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ほど marks last week's test as the standard for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: むずかしくなかった is the adjective むずかしい in the past negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.why: テストは is the object being compared, while 先週のテストほど is the standard. The pattern ほど～ない denies reaching the standard's level, so it expresses “not as ... as.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nより is used, the sentence directly states that today's test is more or less difficult, depending on the adjective chosen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If Nと同じくらい is used, it means equally difficult and no longer has the meaning of being less difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.tip: In the pattern ほど～ない, the noun used as the standard comes before ほど, and the adjective in the following clause must be changed to the negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q19.kobun.cn: Nほど＋Aいくない／Aいくなかった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vi: In the past, I could not speak, but now I have become able to speak a little Japanese.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N は ＋ N が ＋ potential verb ＋ ように ＋ なる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は gives the time point used for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: は shifts the comparison topic to the present situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 少し modifies the degree to which the speaker can speak Japanese.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the object that can be acted on in the potential structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: ように connects the state 話せる with なる and shows a change reaching a new state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and shows that the change has been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.why: The sentence places the two points 前は and 今は side by side to highlight the change. 日本語が comes before 話せる because, in a potential sentence, が marks the object that can be acted on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only states present ability and does not emphasize the change from the past to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to trying or actively making a state happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before 話せる, but potential verbs usually use が to mark the object that can be acted on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の＋ようになる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.vi: I decided to return to my country next year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.sk: N は ＋ time noun ＋ N へ ＋ V辞書形 ＋ ことにした
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who made the decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: This part indicates when the return will happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the return.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 帰る combines with ことにした to express a decision that has been made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.why: は places the topic at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the time and direction before the main action. The dictionary form 帰る comes before ことにした to turn the act of returning into the content of the decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning changes to something being decided or becoming a certain way because of circumstances or another person's decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ことにする with ことになる and miss the difference between deciding for oneself and having something decided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q20.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ ことにする
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.vi: I asked him many times, but he still did not help me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: も emphasizes how many times the asking action was repeated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects the request that was made with the unexpected result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the person expected to help the contrasting topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 手伝って is the て form combined with くれなかった, expressing that another person did not do the action for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.why: The first clause states a repeated effort, while のに signals an unexpected result. てくれなかった presents the act of helping from the speaker's viewpoint, showing that the speaker did not receive help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with けど, the sentence still connects two contrasting ideas, but the tone is milder and more neutral.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand くれる as only meaning “give,” but in this pattern it emphasizes an action by another person that benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q21.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる・くれない・くれた・くれなかった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.vi: This work must be completed today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun 仕事 that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes “work that must be completed” the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 中に marks the time limit by which the work must be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 終わらせる changes into the conditional negative form なければ and combines with ならない to express obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the time limit and finally the obligation to complete the work. 今日中に defines the time range, while なければならない defines the obligatory nature of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: When までに is used, the focus is on the deadline: the action must be completed by or no later than that time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake 中に for “inside” in the sense of location, but here it refers to the whole period of time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q22.kobun.cn: N + 中に; Vなければならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.vi: There is too much luggage, so it seems impossible to fit it into this bag.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.sk: Nが + Aいくて + Nに + Vます形 remove ます + そうもない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the luggage as the thing described as being numerous.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 多い changes into 多くて to connect the condition of having too much luggage with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: この modifies the noun かばん.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place or target into which the luggage is put.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 入ります removes ます to form 入り, then combines with そうもない to judge that entering is almost impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます + そうもない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.why: The condition of having too much luggage is connected with て to give the reason for the judgment at the end of the sentence. に identifies the bag as the destination, while そうもない denies the possibility suggested by the current situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: With そうにない, the sentence still means “seems not to,” but its negative tone is usually weaker than そうもない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may attach そうもない directly to the dictionary form, but it should be attached to the ます stem of the verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.vi: Because I played games every day, my eyesight has gotten worse.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: This part shows how often the action of playing games happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks games as the object of the action する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: したため connects the reason in the first clause with the result in the second clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the eyes as the body part affected by the change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: わるくなる describes the change to a worse condition, while てしまった adds a feeling that the result is regrettable or unintended.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and the result clause comes second, connected by ため. が selects the eyes as the subject of the change, while なってしまった shows that the result is complete and regrettable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ため is replaced with ので, the sentence sounds softer and more conversational, while ため usually gives a clearer and more formal explanation of the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If ようになる is used, the sentence emphasizes the formation of a new state rather than the reason that led to that state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate てしまう only as “finished,” but in this sentence it also shows regret about the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ため
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.vi: When I went to a shop with delicious cakes, all the customers there were women.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ケーキ with おいしい and shows the aspect in which the shop is described as good.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: おいしい modifies 店, forming the phrase “a shop with delicious cakes.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 行ったら connects a condition or point in time with the result noticed afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes the group of customers in the shop the topic of description.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: ばかり comes after the noun to limit the group being discussed to women, while だった ends the sentence in the past tense.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.why: The phrase ケーキのおいしい店 is formed by two modifiers placed one after another before the noun 店. After going to the shop, は introduces the group of customers, while ばかり emphasizes that the group consisted almost entirely of women.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If ばかり is replaced with だけ, the meaning focuses on the simple limit “only women,” with less surprise or personal reaction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If しか～ない is used, the sentence more strongly emphasizes that there were no other groups of customers besides women.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may habitually place ばかり after a verb, but in this sentence it comes after a noun to mean “all women.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q25.kobun.cn: N + ばかりだ・ばかりだった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb わすれる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: てしまいました describes an action that has been completed and also suggests regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q3.kobun.why: しゅくだいを is the object, so it comes before the verb. わすれてしまいました combines the て form with しまう to express that the forgetting was fully completed and that the speaker regrets it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to doing or preparing something in advance, which is opposite to accidentally forgetting it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If only わすれました is used, the sentence simply reports that the speaker forgot, without emphasizing regret.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q3.kobun.tip: Do not connect the past-tense verb directly to しまう; first change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q3.kobun.cn: Vて+しまう/しまいました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vi: This dish may be a little difficult to eat, but it is delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.sk: 程度副詞 + Vます-removeます + にくい + かもしれませんが + Aい + N です
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 少し slightly reduces the degree of difficulty in eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: にくい is added after the verb stem 食べ to create the meaning “difficult to perform the action.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: かもしれません expresses an uncertain guess, while が connects to a contrasting idea.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: おいしい modifies the noun 料理 that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ですよ is used at the end of a sentence to state something and give information to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.why: 食べにくい describes the difficulty of performing the action of eating. Then かもしれませんが softens the statement and connects it with the positive evaluation おいしい料理. おいしい comes before 料理 because the adjective directly modifies the noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 食べやすい, the meaning changes to “easy to eat.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 食べにくそうだ, the sentence only says that it looks difficult to eat and does not confirm that this is its actual quality.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q4.kobun.tip: The stem used with にくい is the ます stem, so remove ます from 食べます before adding にくい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vi: I hear that it will gradually become colder from now on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the starting point of the change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: だんだん modifies the process of change as it happens step by step.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 寒い changes to 寒く before なる, and then て is used to connect it with いく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いく shows that the change continues from the present toward the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: そうだ at the end of the sentence shows information that the speaker heard from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.why: これから sets the time direction toward the future, while だんだん describes a gradual increase. 寒くなっていく combines the change 寒くなる with the future continuation of ていく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 寒くなってくる, the meaning would lean toward a change that started earlier and has continued to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 寒くなりそうだ is used, it means a prediction based on appearance or signs, not on information heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, change い to く before な​​る: 寒い → 寒くなる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q5.kobun.cn: Vて＋いく; Aく＋なって＋いく
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vi: It is already 10 p.m., but Kim is still working.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: もう emphasizes that the time has already reached 10 o’clock.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: なのに connects a situation that should lead to a different result with the actual result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は identifies Kim as the person being discussed in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ shows that the action continues up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the work being done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: しています is the polite form of ている and shows an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.why: なのに creates a contrast between the late time and the continuing action. まだ comes before 仕事をしています to emphasize that the state has not ended.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with まだ仕事をしていません, it would mean that the person still has not started working, unlike the action of working now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If もう仕事をしました is used, it would mean that the work has been completed, without emphasizing continuation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q6.kobun.tip: まだ does not only mean “not yet”; with Vています, it often means “still doing it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vi: No matter how tired I am, I still do not forget to do my homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: どんなに emphasizes the degree, while ても creates a concessive clause, meaning “even if that condition occurs.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents homework as the topic maintained in every situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ないで connects with やっています and describes doing one thing without forgetting another.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: やっています shows that doing homework continues as a habit or an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.why: The clause どんなにつかれても is placed at the beginning to state a concessive condition. Even if that condition occurs, the topic しゅくだいは remains connected to the action わすれないでやっています in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If どんなに is removed, the sentence only means “even if tired,” without emphasizing how tired the person is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, the sentence focuses on a result that is contrary to expectations or on regret, rather than on the idea that the result stays the same no matter what.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.tip: わすれないで here means doing something without forgetting, not the command “do not forget.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q7.kobun.cn: どんなに＋Vて＋も; どんなに＋Aくて＋も; どんなに＋N／Aな＋でも
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vi: An announcement. The next train is the last train of the day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.sk: V without ます ＋ いたします。＋ N が ＋ N、＋ N の ＋ N でございます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: This predicate describes the speaker’s act of making an announcement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object identified as the next train.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: This time phrase states the day on which the last train is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: さいごの modifies the noun 電車, creating the meaning “the last train.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: でございます is the polite, humble form of です at the end of a sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.cn: お＋V without ます＋いたします
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.why: The first sentence announces the speaker’s action, and the second sentence identifies which train is the last one. The particle の connects さいご with 電車 to form a noun phrase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.0.t: お＋V without ます＋します
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If いたします is replaced with します, the sentence remains correct, but the level of humility and politeness decreases.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If でございます is replaced with です, the meaning does not change, but the expression becomes less formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の in さいごの電車 and incorrectly say さいご電車.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vi: Sushi? If it is sushi, that restaurant is a good choice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: ですか creates a question confirming the topic just mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: なら makes sushi the condition or topic for the comment in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the object judged to be suitable or good.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: いい is the evaluative predicate, while よ adds a tone of informing or suggesting something to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.why: The clause with なら makes “sushi” the condition/topic, and then あの店がいい gives a suitable choice. が comes after あの店 because the restaurant is the object being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だったら, the conditional meaning becomes clearer and is usually more hypothetical than なら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with については, it only states the topic “about sushi” and no longer means the condition “if it is sushi.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand なら as only meaning “if,” but in this sentence it also introduces a topic for evaluation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t12-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋なら; N＋なら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vi: I thought the soccer match would be canceled, but unexpectedly it ended up being stopped.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun サッカー with the noun 試合 to modify the match.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the match as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the state or result that follows the verb なる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: と introduces the content of the thought that the match would be canceled.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 思っていた expresses an existing thought, while たら connects it to an unexpected result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies こと, creating the phrase “the act of stopping.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: ことになる expresses a decision or result that has been established.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 中止になる describes a change into a canceled state, and then と marks the content of the thought. たら connects the earlier thought with the actual result, which is contrary to expectations.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it means that the subject decides to stop something personally, without emphasizing a result decided or formed outside the subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that another event happened immediately after the speaker thought of or realized something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ことにする when they want to say that something has become a shared decision or has resulted from circumstances.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ことになる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vi: That ring was shining like a star.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies the noun 指輪 immediately after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents the ring as the object being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: Nのように creates a comparison and modifies how the ring shines.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ひかっていた describes a shining state that was continuing in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.why: 指輪は is the topic, while 星のように describes how it shines through a comparison. ように comes before the verb to modify the manner of the action or state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 星みたいに is used, the meaning is still “like a star,” but the expression is more conversational and familiar.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 星らしく is used, the sentence means “in a way characteristic of a star,” not merely a comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.tip: After a noun, learners often forget の before ように; they need to use 星のように.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q10.kobun.cn: Nの ＋ ように／V普通形 ＋ ように
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vi: I worked for only 3 hours, but I received as much as 10,000 yen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.sk: Nだけ ＋ Nを ＋ Vたら ＋ Quantityも ＋ past potential verb
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: だけ limits the working time to 3 hours.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 仕事 as the object of the action する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: したら connects a hypothetical condition or time with the result of receiving money.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: も follows a quantity to emphasize that the amount of money is more than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: もらえた is the past form of the potential expression for receiving something, and states that the result occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.why: だけ limits the time to a small amount, while も after the amount of money creates a feeling of surprise because the amount received is large. したら connects finishing the work with the result of receiving money.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use ３時間しか仕事をしなかった, the sentence emphasizes “I could work for only 3 hours” and must include a negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use １０,０００円まで, the sentence only states the maximum amount and does not create the surprise expressed by も.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand も here as “also,” but after a quantity it usually emphasizes an amount that is larger than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vi: The car has remained parked in front of the house for 3 days.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Nに ＋ Duration ＋ Nが ＋ Vたままです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 家 with 前 to create the noun phrase “in front of the house.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the location where the car is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The duration phrase adds the length of time that the state continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the car as the subject of the state 止まったままです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: Vた＋ままです describes the state that remains unchanged after stopping.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.why: 前に identifies where the car is, while ３日間 shows how long the state continues. 止まったままです emphasizes that the car stopped and has remained in that state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 止まりっぱなしです, it usually suggests leaving something as it is or continuing it in an inappropriate way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 止まっています, the sentence only describes the car as being parked and does not emphasize that the state has continued unchanged from before.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before まま in this pattern; an established state usually uses Vた＋まま.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.vi: It is already 11 o’clock. You have school tomorrow too, so go to bed early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: も adds the idea that tomorrow is also included in the condition being mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: なんだから connects the noun 学校 with だから to give a reason with emphasis.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: は states that the child is the person being told to sleep.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective い changes to く to modify the verb ねろ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: ねろ is the imperative form of 寝る, used to give a strong command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.why: The first sentence identifies the time. Then なんだから gives the reason for the command. は marks the person being mentioned, while 早く comes before ねろ to show how to sleep.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with ねなさい, the request becomes gentler and usually has the tone of a superior speaking to a subordinate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace it with 寝てください, the sentence becomes more polite and no longer has a strong command tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse the imperative form with the polite form when they want to say “please do something.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.vi: According to the letter, Mr. Tanaka is said to be well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: によると indicates the source of the information on which the following content is based.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that Tanaka is the topic of the information being conveyed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: だそうです is placed after the adjective な 元気 to report information read or heard from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.why: によると puts the source of the information first, and then は identifies the person being discussed. だそうです ends the sentence with the meaning “it is said,” not a direct appearance-based judgment or guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used after the adjective’s stem form い, this pattern expresses “seems” or “is about to,” not information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace it with と言っています, it emphasizes that the person directly said this.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit だ before そうです when it follows the adjective な or a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形＋そうです・Aい＋そうです・Aな＋だそうです・N＋だそうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.vi: Because there is little rain, the vegetables cannot grow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the state of being scarce in the reason clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ため connects the cause 少ない with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that does not grow larger.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to く to connect with なります and express a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: なりません is the polite negative form of なる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and ends with ため; the result is stated afterward. が is used for the subject of each clause, while 大きくなりません is the structure showing that the change does not occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with 少ないので, the reason sounds softer and more naturally explanatory.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace it with 少ないから, the cause sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often connect the adjective な directly to ため and forget な, but the adjective い connects directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形＋ため・Aい＋ため・Aな＋なため・Nの＋ため
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.vi: Whenever I look at this picture, I always remember that person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the picture as the object being viewed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the condition 見る with a natural or repeated result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: の connects 人 with こと to create a phrase referring to that person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: ことを turns the content 人のこと into the object of 思い出す.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.why: The clause 見ると comes first to state a repeated condition, and the natural result of remembering appears afterward. 人のことを is a way to group that person as the object of 思い出す.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with 見たら, the meaning is closer to “if” or “when I look,” and it does not necessarily show a natural repeated reaction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace it with 見るなら, it means “if I have decided to look,” and does not express an automatic result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often translate と as “and,” but in this sentence と connects a condition with a result that happens regularly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.vi: I go to the convenience store about three times a week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.sk: N期間に + Number of timesくらい + Nplaceに + Vます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates a period of time used as a unit for counting frequency.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: くらい comes after the number of times to show an approximate amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of the action 行きます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.why: The period of time and the number of times come before the verb to state frequency. The first に indicates a time unit, while に after コンビニ indicates the destination.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 週に is replaced with 週ごとに, the sentence emphasizes once every week or week by week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 週で does not correctly express the usual frequency in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に, which indicates frequency, with に, which indicates the destination, because both appear in the same sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.vi: I will say it only once, so listen carefully.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.sk: Nだけ + Vますから、 + Adv + Vstemますなさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: だけ limits the number of times the action 言います occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason in the first clause to the request to listen carefully in the second clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: なさい attaches to the verb stem without ます to form a request or a mild command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.why: The first clause states the limit of one time and then uses から to give the reason. The second clause uses よく to modify 聞きなさい, creating a request for the listener to pay attention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 聞いてください, the request becomes more polite and is suitable for peers or people of higher status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 聞け, the command becomes stronger and more forceful than なさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may attach なさい directly to the dictionary-form verb, but they must use the verb stem without ます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.vi: If I do not wear glasses, I cannot see the writing on the blackboard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.sk: N は + N を + Vないと + N の + N が + potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing being worn.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.2.vi: if I do not wear them
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: Vない＋と creates a necessary condition: if this action is not done, the result will follow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の connects 黒板 with 字 and shows that the writing is on the blackboard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the object that is seen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: 見える expresses the ability to see; its polite negative form is 見えません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.why: The sentence puts the condition かけないと first and then states the result 見えません. が marks the thing that cannot be seen, while の connects a place with the noun 字.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this in the sentence still means “if I do not wear glasses,” but the tone is more formal and forceful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ないなら is used, the sentence becomes an assumption based on stated information or an intention, rather than only a natural condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse が with を and say めがねがかけない, but something being worn must be used with を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vi: I may be late tomorrow because of work, so please go ahead.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the prediction and request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 明日 indicates the time when the possible delay may happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the reason why the speaker may be late.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: かもしれない lowers the level of certainty, while から connects the reason to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 先に modifies the action 行って and shows the order of actions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request or suggestion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.why: 仕事で puts the reason before the verb 遅れる, and then かもしれない expresses an uncertain possibility. から turns this whole prediction into a reason for the request 行ってください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the prediction usually sounds more likely to be true than the open possibility expressed by かもしれない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the reason sounds softer and more objective than から, so it suits a gentle explanation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.tip: Do not put だ before and かもしれない after a verb or adjective; connect them directly to the plain form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + かもしれない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.vi: Hana, could you please listen to me for a moment?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.sk: Person's name + N の + N を + Vていただけませんか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: A person's name at the beginning of the sentence is used to call the listener, not as the subject of the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の shows that 話 is the speaker's speech or story.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content that the listener is asked to hear.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞いて connects with いただけませんか to create a polite and gentle request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.why: The person being called comes first, followed by the content 話を聞いて. The pattern Vていただけませんか places the listener's action in a respectful request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means asking someone to do something, but it is less respectful than いただけませんか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with てください, the speech becomes more direct and may sound like a request or command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before いただけませんか; the verb must be changed to the て form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.vi: If you plan to go to the dentist, you should brush your teeth before you go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the destination of 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: 行く＋なら uses going to the dentist as the situation for giving advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the body part being brushed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: Vて＋から shows that brushing the teeth must be completed before going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 行ったほうがいい uses the past form 行った to present the better choice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: いい completes the pattern for advising someone to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.why: なら sets the situation as a condition, てから puts the two actions in order, and たほうがいい gives advice. Therefore, brushing the teeth comes before 行ったほうがいい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行ったら is used, the sentence focuses on a condition that happens after going, so it is less natural than なら when giving advice about a plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that the later action cannot be done until the earlier action is completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 行くほうがいい, but the advice pattern for saying what someone should do usually uses Vた＋ほうがいい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q21.kobun.cn: V普通形＋なら／Aい＋なら／Aな＋なら／N＋なら; Vて＋から; Vた＋ほうがいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q22.kobun.vi: Although it is winter, it is warm, isn't it?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: N＋なのに connects a fact in the first clause with an unexpected result in the second clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ですね adds a feeling and seeks agreement from the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q22.kobun.why: 冬なのに sets the winter background, which usually suggests cold weather. あたたかい at the end shows a result opposite to what was expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 冬なので, the meaning would be “because it is winter, it is warm,” which does not fit the contrast in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: けど also connects two contrasting ideas, but it is softer and more conversational. It does not stress the contrast with the prediction as much as のに.
