default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q22.kobun.tip: For nouns and adjectives な, you must use なのに, rather than directly saying Nのに or Aな のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい＋のに／Aな＋なのに／N＋なのに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.vi: Hana just came back. Only about five minutes ago.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は shows that Hana is the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: さっき modifies the action 帰った and shows a time close to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: Vた＋ところです describes an action that ended immediately before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: くらい shows an estimated amount of time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 前 points to a time before the present; よ emphasizes information the speaker is adding.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.why: The first clause uses Vたところです to stress that Hana has just finished returning. The second clause gives a specific time to make clear how close that time was.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means “have just done,” but ばかり is subjective and does not have to be as close to the speaking time as ところです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If this form is used, the meaning changes to being in the middle of an action, which is not finished yet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ところ as only a place, but in this pattern it refers to a stage of an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.vi: I am about to eat. Would you like to eat with me?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: これから shows that an action is about to begin.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: V辞書形＋ところです describes an action that is about to begin at the moment of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: いっしょに adds the manner or the person who performs the action with someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: どうですか is used to make a gentle invitation or ask for someone's opinion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.why: これから signals that the action has not started, so 食べるところです uses the dictionary form. The next sentence connects the invitation to eat together with どうですか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 食べているところです, it means that the person is eating and the action has already begun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 食べたところです, it means that the person has just finished eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q24.kobun.tip: 食べるところ, 食べているところ, and 食べたところ must be distinguished by the three times: about to do, doing, and just finished doing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.vi: Micchan is laughing and looks happy, doesn't she?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.sk: N、＋ Aい remove い ＋ そうに ＋ Vている ＋ ね
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The name of the person being called directly appears at the beginning of the sentence and is separated by a comma.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: うれしい removes い and connects to そうに to modify the verb わらっています.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ね is used to seek agreement from the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ そうに・Aな remove な ＋ そうに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.why: うれしそうに comes before わらっています to describe the manner or outward state shown while laughing. ています shows that the action is happening, while ね adds a gentle confirming tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with うれしく, it means “happily,” focusing more on how the action is done than on the appearance being observed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうに with そうな; そうに modifies a verb, while そうな modifies a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vi: I watch five movies each month.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q3.kobun.sk: Time period に ＋ Quantity ＋ N を ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the time period used as the unit for measuring frequency.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ５本 shows the number of films watched during the earlier time period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks films as the object of watching.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q3.kobun.why: The time period with に creates the unit, and the quantity that follows shows how many times or how many items occur during that period. 映画を is the direct object of 見ます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 毎月, the meaning is still “each month,” but the time period is not stated as clearly with the particle に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use を after a time period when talking about frequency. The basic pattern is time period ＋ に ＋ quantity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vi: Because he did not help me, I could not finish my homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the helping action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 手伝って connects with くれる to express doing something to help the speaker; くれなかった is the past negative form, and から states the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks homework as the subject said not to have been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 終わらなかった is the main predicate in the past negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and ends with から, followed by the result. くれる shows that the helping action was intended to benefit the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, it emphasizes that the speaker did not receive help; the viewpoint belongs to the receiver.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If くれる is removed, the sentence only says that he did not help. It no longer has the nuance of an action that should have been done for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse くれる with あげる; くれる is used when someone does something beneficial for the speaker or the speaker's side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.tokens.6.m: did not end; was not finished
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q4.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くれる・くれない・くれた・くれなかった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vi: I did my homework, but the teacher did not come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks homework as the object of doing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects having done the homework with the unexpected result in the next clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the teacher as the subject of coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 来なかった is the main predicate in the past negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.why: The first clause creates a premise that makes the listener expect a different result, while のに signals that the actual result goes against that expectation. The subject of the second clause is marked by が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ても, the sentence means “even if” or “although,” focusing more on a condition than on regret about an unexpected result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If けど is used, the contrast is softer and more conversational. It does not stress surprise as much as のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.tip: With nouns and adjectives な, なのに must be used. They cannot be connected directly with のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vi: My child does not study and only plays all the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with 子ども to modify it and show所属.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the child in the household the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ないで connects a negative action with the following action. It means not doing the first action but doing the next one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてばかりいる describes an action that keeps repeating, often with a feeling of dissatisfaction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.why: ないで connects not studying with the replacement action of playing. ばかりいる puts emphasis on playing too much and repeatedly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it only means continuing to remain in the state of not doing something. It does not have the meaning of doing another action all the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it only says that someone is doing or only doing one thing. Its critical feeling is weaker than ばかりいる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.kobun.tip: ばかり comes after the て form in this pattern. It cannot be used directly after the dictionary-form verb, such as 勉強するばかりいる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.tokens.5.m: do (the continuative form of する)
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q6.tokens.10.m: be doing; remain in a state
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vi: Yamada is also tall, but he is not as tall as Tanaka.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle も adds the meaning “also” and makes 山田さん the topic being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 背が is the subject of the adjective 高い and describes how tall or short someone's body is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 高い in the present form connects with が to move to a contrasting idea.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ほど comes after the object of comparison and creates the standard in a negative sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 高い changes to 高くない to negate the い-ending adjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.why: The first clause states Yamada's feature, while が connects it to a contrasting idea. 田中さんほど sets the comparison standard, and then 高くない makes it negative to say that Yamada does not reach that level.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 田中さんより is used, the sentence directly emphasizes that Yamada is shorter than Tanaka.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 田中さんくらい高くない is used, it still means being below Tanaka's level, but this expression is less natural.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that ほど in a negative pattern must be followed by a negative form in the second clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q7.kobun.cn: N ＋ ほど ＋ Aいくない／Aなではない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vi: If I receive 10 million yen, I want to travel to many countries.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.sk: もし ＋ N ＋ Vたら ＋ Nは ＋ Aな ＋ Nを ＋ Vます remove ます＋たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: もし signals the hypothetical situation stated in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: This amount of money is the object received by the verb もらう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: もらったら uses the た＋ら form to connect a hypothetical condition with its result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は identifies the person who has the desire in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: いろいろな modifies the noun 国.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the range or places to be visited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: 旅行する changes to 旅行したい to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます ＋ たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.why: The もし～もらったら clause gives the condition first, and then は states the speaker's desire. 国を旅行する uses を to show the countries included in the trip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 旅行するつもりだ, the sentence expresses a firmer plan instead of a desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: ほしい is used when the speaker wants to have another person or thing do something. It does not directly replace the desire to travel oneself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ほしい instead of たい when talking about wanting to perform an action themselves.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vi: Today, I went out without eating anything.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は limits the time being discussed to today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 何も goes with a negative verb to show that absolutely nothing was eaten.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べないで is the Vない＋で form and connects an action that was not done with the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main action. It is in the polite past form to show that it happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.why: 何も食べないで is the omitted action, while 出かけました is the main action that happens afterward. The form ないで connects two actions with the meaning “not doing A but doing B.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べずに is used, the meaning is almost the same, but the expression is more formal and difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べなくて is used, the sentence can shift toward a cause or a state. It is less natural than ないで for an action that the speaker chooses not to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t13-q9.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ないで with ないと, because ないと usually means “if one does not do it...” or “must do it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vi: Ah, the button looks like it is about to come off.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.sk: 感嘆、＋ N が ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ そうです ＋ よ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: あ is an interjection at the beginning of the sentence. It shows that the speaker has just noticed the situation in front of them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that is in the predicted state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.2.vi: looks like it is about to come off
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: とれる uses the form without ます, which is とれ, and connects with そうです to predict an event about to happen from present signs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: よ emphasizes information that the speaker wants to tell the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.why: ボタンが is the object showing signs of change, so が is used as the subject of the state. とれそうです comes after the subject to predict an event about to happen, while よ turns the sentence into a warning or announcement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with とれるでしょう, the sentence is only a prediction or inference. It does not emphasize signs of something about to happen right before one's eyes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.tip: そうな is not used in this sentence because the position before です requires the verb prediction pattern Vます without ます＋そうです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q1.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vi: The children's picture has been put up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: 子どもの comes before and modifies 絵, showing ownership or origin.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that is in the state of having been put up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてある describes the remaining result of an intentional action, with an object that has been prepared or arranged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q10.kobun.why: 子どもの絵 creates the noun phrase “the children's picture,” and 絵が makes it the subject of the state. はってあります focuses on the result—the picture is already put up—without saying who put it up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If はっています is used, the sentence usually describes an action in progress or something being in a pasted state. It does not emphasize intentional preparation as Vてある does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If はられています is used, the sentence emphasizes the passive meaning “is pasted,” while Vてある emphasizes the remaining result state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q10.kobun.tip: Vてある usually goes with an arranged object and uses が. Do not mechanically confuse it with Vている just because both describe a state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vi: The rice has already been prepared. Go ahead and eat quickly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the food as already prepared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 作ってあります shows that the rice was made and the result still remains; よ adds a tone of informing or reminding the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 早く is an adverb that modifies the action of eating and urges someone to do it quickly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べなさい is an instruction or a mild command, often used with younger people or subordinates.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.why: ごはんが is the subject of the prepared state, while 早く comes before 食べなさい to show the manner and urgent tone. The two sentences together mean “It has already been prepared, so eat it now.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ごはんができています is used, the sentence only informs us that the rice is in a completed state. It does not stress that someone intentionally prepared it in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 早く食べてください is used, the speech is more polite and has the tone of a request instead of a direct command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q11.kobun.tip: なさい is a request from a superior to a subordinate, so avoid using it with older people or in situations that require politeness.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vi: I always study before going to bed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the action 勉強しています and shows repeated frequency.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb ねる modifies 前 and creates the phrase “before going to bed.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the time when the following action takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 勉強しています uses the ている form to describe a repeated habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.why: ねる前に sets “sleeping” as the time reference, while 勉強しています is the action that is regularly continued. いつも makes it clear that this is a habit, not only something happening at the moment of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～てから, the meaning becomes “after sleeping,” reversing the time relationship.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: ～間に emphasizes an action that happens during the time period of another action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 前に for “after,” but 前に always refers to a time before an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.vi: I am sorry that the children are so noisy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Aい remove い ＋ くて、＋ evaluation or emotion
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that has the noisy state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: うるさい changes to うるさくて to connect the reason to the apology that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: すみません is an apology at the end of the sentence, based on the reason just given.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ くて
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.why: The clause 子どもがうるさくて gives the reason, and then すみません expresses emotion and an apology. The particle が identifies the children as the subject of the state うるさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: ～ので also gives a reason, but creates a clearer and more polite explanatory feeling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: ～のに means “although,” so it creates a contrast instead of a cause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q13.kobun.tip: Do not keep the い-ending adjective unchanged before くて; remove い and add くて.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.vi: This pen is expensive but very easy to write with.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aい ですが ＋ とても ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ やすいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the pen the topic for stating two contrasting features.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ですが connects two contrasting ideas: the price is high, but it is easy to write with.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies 書きやすい and shows the degree of ease in writing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: 書きやすい is formed from the verb stem 書きます and やすい. It describes writing as easy to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ やすい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.why: ですが creates a contrast between the high price and the pen’s easy-writing feature. The stem 書き combines with やすい to turn the action “write” into the feature “easy to write with.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: ～にくい changes the meaning to “difficult to write with,” describing an action that is hard to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: ～そうです describes an appearance that seems easy to write with, without stating it directly like ～やすい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q14.kobun.tip: With ～やすい, use the verb stem by removing ます. Do not use the て form like 書いてやすい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.vi: These clothes are too large. Do you have size M or S?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aい remove い ＋ すぎます。Nか Nは ＋ ありますか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は introduces the clothes as the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きい removes い and adds すぎます to express a state that exceeds the suitable level.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes size S and the choice between M or S the thing being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: ありますか asks whether that size exists or is still in stock.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます・Aい remove い・Aな remove な・N ＋ すぎる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.why: 大きすぎます comments that the clothes exceed the suitable size. Then MかS gives the size choices, while ありますか asks whether the store has those sizes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: ～たい expresses the speaker’s desire, not an excessively large degree like ～すぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: ～ほど is used for comparison or degree. It does not directly mean “too.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q15.kobun.tip: The い-ending adjective must remove い before すぎる: 大きい becomes 大きすぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.vi: Because she is good at cooking and made this dish, it must be delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the area in which she is skilled in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 上手な modifies かのじょ and creates the meaning “she is good at cooking.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who performs the action 作った.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 作ったんですから gives a supported reason for the guess that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: おいしい is the content guessed in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: はずです expresses a confident guess based on the information before it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.why: 料理が上手な is the clause modifying かのじょ, while かのじょが作ったんですから gives the reason for the guess. はずです comes at the end to conclude “it must be delicious” based on that evidence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: ～でしょう also expresses a guess, but it is usually less certain and based on weaker evidence than はずです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: ～かもしれません shows possibility, so it is less certain than はずです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.tip: Before はず, an な-ending adjective needs な, and a noun needs の: 元気なはず, 学生のはず.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ な・N ＋ の ＋ はずです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.vi: My dog does not want to go for a walk in winter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.sk: N は + 時点 は + Nに + Vます remove ます + たがらない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with 犬 and shows only possession.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は sets my dog as the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks winter as the time being limited and emphasized.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the purpose of going and combines with 行く to mean “go for a walk.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きたがらない describes another person's unwillingness to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + たがる・たがらない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.why: 冬は limits the situation by season, while 散歩に行く is the phrase meaning going for a walk. Since the subject is the dog, not the speaker, ～たがらない is used to describe its unwillingness to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: ～たい usually expresses the speaker's own wish or the wish of the person currently being addressed directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: ～たくない directly says “do not want to,” while ～たがらない emphasizes observing another person's behavior.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use ～たい to state another person's wish directly; use ～たがる or ～たがらない instead.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.vi: There is a test tomorrow, so I want everyone to be quiet. I cannot study at all.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates when the test will take place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 静かに is the adverbial form of 静かな and modifies して.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてほしい expresses the wish for someone else to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ぜんぜん modifies the negative predicate すすまない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks studying as the subject that is not progressing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb in the negative form says that the studying is not progressing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before the request and is connected by だから. 静かに comes before して to show how the action is done, while してほしい comes at the end to express a wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, it becomes a more direct and polite request, without emphasizing a personal wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it means wanting someone not to do a certain action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ほしい with wanting to do something themselves, but Vてほしい means wanting someone else to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.vi: I want to become a singer someday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who has the wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: いつか indicates an unspecified time in the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the status or result achieved after なります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: なりたい is formed by removing なります from ます and adding たい to express the speaker's wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, and いつか shows when the wish may happen. With a verb showing a change of status, such as なります, に marks the result, which is 歌手.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning focuses on a plan or intention to become a singer, not only a wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence describes another person's wish based on their outward behavior.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use たい directly after the dictionary form; remove ます first, then add たい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vi: Since the rain does not seem likely to stop, I will go home by taxi.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.sk: N が + Vます remove ます + そうもない + ので + N で + Vます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the natural phenomenon mentioned in the reason clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it seems unlikely to stop
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: やむ becomes やみ after removing ます, and connects with そうもない to show that something is very unlikely to happen. Then ので connects the reason to the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the means used to go home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.why: Clause やみそうもないので comes first to give the reason, followed by the main action 帰ります. Particle で identifies the taxi as the means of travel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with やみそうにないので, the meaning is still “seems unlikely to stop,” but the tone is weaker than そうもない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with やまないので, it states that the rain will not stop, without the judgment based on the situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget も in そうもない, losing the meaning that it is “very unlikely.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q2.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + そうもない + ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.vi: Micchan used to want to become a singer, right?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose wish is mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 昔 indicates when the wish existed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the result or status aimed for after なります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: なりたがっていた describes another person's past wish, while ね seeks agreement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.why: The topic is Micchan, and 昔 comes before the predicate to limit the time. Since the speaker is mentioning another person's wish, たがる is used, followed by the past progressive form to describe a state that existed in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, it directly states the speaker's wish, so it is not suitable for describing Micchan's wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it means Micchan had a plan, which is more certain than simply showing a wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.tip: When the subject is someone else, avoid using たい unless you are quoting that person's exact words or thoughts.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q20.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + たがる・たがっている・たがっていた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.vi: He refuses to go home. I want him to go home soon…
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: なかなか is used with a negative predicate to emphasize that something is difficult to happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 自分 with 家 to form the noun phrase “his own home.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: へ shows the direction of the action 帰る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 帰らない is the negative form of 帰る and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: そろそろ modifies the action that is expected to happen soon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: 帰ってほしい uses the て form to connect with ほしい and express the wish for someone else to go home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.why: なかなか combines with 帰らない to say that he still has not gone home. In the next sentence, そろそろ comes before 帰ってほしい to show that the time when the speaker wants the action to happen has arrived.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, it becomes a direct request for him to go home instead of expressing the speaker's wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it emphasizes that the speaker wants the other person to perform the action for them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q21.kobun.tip: へ shows direction, while を is not used to mark the destination in 帰る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.vi: Nao can speak as many as four languages. That is amazing, isn't it?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.sk: N は + Quantity も + potential V。Aなです + ね
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose ability is being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: も is added after a quantity to emphasize that the number is larger than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 話せます is the potential form and expresses the ability to speak.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the predicate evaluating the ability just mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: ね invites the listener to agree with the comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.why: なおさんは is the topic, while ４か国語も is the object whose quantity is emphasized before the verb 話せます. The next sentence uses ね to share the speaker's impression with the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だけ, the sentence only states the limit of four languages and does not emphasize that this number is large.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning becomes that the person can speak only four languages, implying that they cannot speak any more.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q22.kobun.tip: も after a quantity can mean “as many as” or “also,” and does not always mean “also.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.vi: I can speak only Japanese. I cannot speak English or Chinese either.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.sk: N は + N しか + negative potential V。N も + N も + negative V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose language ability is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: しか limits the object to 日本語 and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 話せません is the negative form of the potential form 話せます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds 英語 to the group of languages that cannot be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: も continues listing 中国語 with the same negative relationship.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: できません negates the ability to use the previously mentioned English and Chinese.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.why: しか limits the languages that can be spoken, so the predicate must be negative. In the next clause, も is repeated to list English and Chinese as also being within the range of languages the speaker cannot use.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だけ, the meaning is still “only Japanese,” but a negative predicate is not required and the emphasis on limitation is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only lists two objects that share the same condition or are considered together, while the current sentence uses it with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use しか with an affirmative predicate; use a negative form such as 話せない or できない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q23.kobun.cn: N + しか + Vない; N も + N も + Vない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q24.kobun.vi: Last night, I could sleep for only three hours.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates the time when the action happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: しか follows a quantity to limit it to three hours and must be used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past negative form and combines with しか to express sleeping for only three hours.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q24.kobun.why: ゆうべ states the time, while ３時間しか limits the duration to three hours. The following clause uses a negative form to complete the pattern しか～ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だけ, the sentence only states the limit of three hours, without requiring a negative form, and the sense of “only a small amount” is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If ばかり is used, the sentence can mean almost the whole time or doing only one thing, so it is less suitable than しか～ない for emphasizing the small quantity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that しか must be used with a negative form such as ない or ません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.vi: Thank you very much for coming today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.sk: Nは + Vてくれて + adverb + ありがとう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic or time being mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 来てくれて uses Vてくれる in a connecting form to show that the listener did something beneficial for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 本当に modifies the thanks and emphasizes the speaker’s gratitude.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ありがとう is an expression at the end of a sentence that shows thanks.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.why: 今日は states the time setting, 来てくれて describes an action someone did for the speaker. 本当に adds emphasis, and ありがとう expresses thanks at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 来てもらって, the focus shifts to the speaker having asked the other person to come or having received help from them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If 来てあげて is used, the speaker shows that they did something for someone else, which is the opposite direction of benefit from this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q25.kobun.tip: Learners may confuse the direction of benefit: くれる means that another person does or gives something for the speaker, while あげる means that the speaker does or gives something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vi: Because I have eaten too much recently, I will not eat lunch today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.sk: Time + Vます remove ます + すぎる + なので、 + Time は + N を + Vません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression modifying the state of eating too much.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I have eaten too much
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べる removes ます to become 食べ, connects with すぎる to become 食べすぎる, and then uses なので to state the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes today the time reference used for comparison with the main action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks lunch as the object of the verb 食べません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + すぎる・Aい remove い + すぎる・Aな語幹 + すぎる + なので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.why: 食べすぎなので is the reason clause placed before the result 食べません. 今日は は limits the decision not to eat to today only, while を connects lunch with the action of eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 食べすぎたので, the reason is viewed as a completed action, while 食べすぎなので emphasizes the current state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q3.kobun.tip: With a verb, remove ます before connecting すぎる; do not say 食べますすぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vi: My handwriting is too poor, so I feel embarrassed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed and makes them the topic of the feeling at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that has the characteristic 下手すぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 下手 is an adjective な, connects directly to すぎる, and changes to the て form to connect the reason with the feeling that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + すぎる・Aい remove い + すぎる・Aな語幹 + すぎる; すぎる → すぎて
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, while 字が identifies what has the excessively poor characteristic. 下手すぎて forms the reason clause, leading to the feeling はずかしいです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 下手なので, it only states that the reason is poor writing and does not emphasize an excessive degree like 下手すぎて.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 下手で, it simply connects two states or reasons, with a weaker tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q4.kobun.tip: The adjective な keeps its stem and connects to すぎる; do not add な before すぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vi: My husband is too busy. He is hardly ever at home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.sk: N は + Aい remove い + すぎます。 + あまり + N に + いません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the husband the topic of the sentence describing his level of busyness.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: いそがしい removes い to become いそがし, then connects with すぎます to express a level beyond normal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: あまり is used with a negative sentence to reduce the degree, meaning “not often” or “hardly ever.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the person being discussed exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: いません is the polite negative form of います, used for people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + すぎる・Aい remove い + すぎる・Aな語幹 + すぎる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.why: The first sentence states the husband’s level of busyness, and the subject is omitted in the second sentence because it still refers to him. あまり combines with いません to express a very low frequency of being at home, while に indicates the place of existence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with とてもいそがしいです, it only means “very busy” and does not necessarily imply a level beyond normal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: あまり家にいません is natural in a negative sentence; using あまり with an affirmative sentence would make the structure and meaning unsuitable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q5.kobun.tip: Learners may use いそがしいすぎます incorrectly; with the adjective い, remove い before connecting すぎます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vi: It is hard to talk when everyone is listening. Let us talk just the two of us.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the action of listening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vていると connects a condition or situation with the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 話しにくい combines the verb stem 話す with にくい to express that an action is difficult to perform.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: で marks the range or members performing the action together; だけ limits the number of people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The form ましょう is used to invite or suggest doing an action together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.why: The clause 聞いていると presents the situation first, while 話しにくい states the result that occurs in that situation. 二人だけで uses で to mark the people carrying out the invitation together 話しましょう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If にくい is replaced with づらい, the meaning is still that talking is difficult, but it focuses more on the speaker’s feeling of difficulty or discomfort.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If みんなが聞いているとき is used, the sentence only states when everyone is listening; it does not emphasize that talking is difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate と as “and,” but in this sentence と connects a situation with a result: “when... then...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形＋と; Vます形の語幹＋にくい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vi: I gain weight easily. Therefore, I do not eat sweet things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb stem 太る combines with やすい to express a state that is likely to occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: だから connects a conclusion or result with the information stated before it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: あまい modifies もの, while は makes sweet things the topic of the action of not eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The form 食べません negates the action of eating in the present or as a habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.why: わたしは sets the topic, 太りやすい states the feature of gaining weight easily, and then だから leads to the result 食べません. は in あまいものは contrasts or gives special emphasis to sweet things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 太りがちだ is used, the sentence emphasizes a frequent tendency to gain weight rather than how easily weight is gained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 太りそうだ is used, the meaning changes to “seem likely to gain weight,” expressing a prediction in a specific situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q7.kobun.tip: Do not attach やすい directly to the complete ます form; remove ます first, and then add やすい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vi: I want a wallet that is easy to use and cute.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 使いやすい changes to the form て, which is 使いやすくて, to connect with the following quality.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: かわいい comes before and directly modifies the noun さいふ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the desired object in the pattern ほしい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ほしいです expresses the desire to have an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹＋やすい; connecting form: Vます形の語幹＋やすくて
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.why: 使いやすくて connects two qualities that both modify さいふ. The noun さいふ goes with が because it is the desired object in the sentence with ほしい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 使いやすくて is replaced with 使いにくくて, the wallet is described as difficult to use.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 使いやすいながら is used, the structure is unnatural here because ながら usually connects two actions or contrasting ideas, not two simple qualities.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q8.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, when connecting with て, change い to くて; do not say やすいて.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.sk: Frequency ＋ Time に ＋ Place に ＋ Vている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎週 indicates how often an action is repeated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the fixed time when the person goes to karaoke.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the action 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 行っている expresses a repeated habit; it does not necessarily mean that the person is going at the moment of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.why: 毎週 and 木よう日に state the frequency and time, respectively; カラオケに states the destination, and then 行っています expresses a repeated habit. The particle に is used for both time and destination, but it has different roles.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 毎週木よう日にカラオケに行きます is used, the sentence is still correct, but it only states the habit neutrally and does not emphasize an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern can also indicate an action in progress, but with the time adverb 毎週, it is naturally understood as a habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t14-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand ています as meaning only “be doing”; look at the time adverb to recognize the habitual meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vi: I was very happy because I received a letter from my father.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person who gives the object in the receiving structure with もらう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that the speaker receives.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: もらって is the connecting form of もらう. It connects a preceding cause or event with the emotion in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to the polite past form to express the emotion after receiving the letter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.why: 父に identifies the giver, 手紙を identifies the received object, and then もらって connects that event with the happiness in the following clause. The order に＋を clearly shows the relationship between the giver and the received object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, it still means receiving a letter from my father, but it emphasizes the source of the object more than the giver’s role.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If くれて is used, the direction of giving is reversed and the giver is usually someone else, so it does not correctly express that I received the letter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を for the giver as well; with もらう, the giver usually goes with に or から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q1.kobun.cn: Nを ＋ もらう／もらって; Nに ＋ Nを ＋ もらう; Vて ＋ もらう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vi: It rained heavily on my way home. Even so, I had not brought an umbrella...
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time or circumstances when an event occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates a natural cause that negatively affects the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 降られました is the passive form of 降る and expresses that the speaker suffered from rain falling on them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object carried in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: のに connects to an idea contrary to what was expected and leaves a feeling of regret or complaint.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.why: 帰りに sets the time background, 雨に is the cause of the negative effect, and the passive verb expresses an unwanted experience. The following clause uses のに to show regret about not bringing an umbrella.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 雨が降りました is used, the sentence only reports that it rained and does not show that the speaker was directly affected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If けれども is used, the sentence still expresses contrast, but its complaining and unfinished tone is weaker than のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 雨を降られました, but the cause of the negative effect in this pattern must go with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q10.kobun.cn: 受身: 五段V 語尾う段→あ段＋れる・一段V る→られる・する→される・来る→こられる; のに: V普通形・Aい・Aなな＋のに・Nな＋のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vi: Because my daughter wanted to attend university, I let her go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject who wants to attend university.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction of the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the result and follows a clause in the plain form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 行かせた is the past causative form, showing that the subject let his or her daughter go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before ので, and the main action comes after the comma. 行かせた shows that the speaker caused the daughter to perform the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～てもらう, it means that the speaker asked the daughter for help or received help from her, rather than allowing her to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.tip: Learners from Vietnam may easily confuse the subject of the causative form because the person who performs the action of going is 娘, while the person who allows or causes it is the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q11.kobun.cn: V使役形：Vる→Vさせる・Vない→Vさせない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: どろぼう is the person speaking after the colon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 止まれ is the imperative form of 止まる, used to give a direct command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: な follows a verb in the dictionary form to create a strong prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q12.kobun.why: The two commands appear one after the other to show an urgent threat. 止まれ is a command to do something, while 動くな is a command not to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, the speech would be more polite and gentler, without the strong prohibitive tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q12.kobun.tip: Learners from Vietnam may easily use 動かないな, but a direct prohibition must use a verb in the dictionary form plus な.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.vi: There is a car parked in front of my house. Someone is sleeping inside it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with 前 to modify the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the car exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that is in a parked state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes a state that continues or exists after the action of parking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the place where the action of sleeping occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: か follows a question word to create the indefinite meaning “someone.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: ている shows that the action of sleeping is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.why: に is used for the place where the car exists, while で is used for the place where the action of sleeping occurs. ている is used in both clauses, but it expresses the parked state in one and the ongoing action of sleeping in the other.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてある were used, the sentence would emphasize a state intentionally arranged by someone, which does not fit a car that is naturally parked.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q13.kobun.tip: Learners from Vietnam may easily use に for every location, but the place where an action occurs must use で.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.vi: The doctor told me to sleep more.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who gives the advice in the passive sentence 言われた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: もっと modifies ねる, showing that more or additional sleep is needed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ように states the content of the advice or request being conveyed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 言われた is the past passive form, meaning that the speaker received advice from the doctor.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.why: The content of the advice comes before ように, while the person giving the advice goes with に. The passive form emphasizes that the speaker is the person who received the advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～と言われた, the speech would be more direct or specific; ように emphasizes a request or piece of advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.tip: Learners from Vietnam may easily translate に as “give,” but in the passive sentence 言われた, に indicates the speaker or the person giving the advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q14.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない＋ように言われる／言われた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.vi: According to the news, it sounds like this summer will become hot.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: によると indicates the information source used as the basis for the statement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 今年 with 夏 to modify “summer.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes this summer the topic of the prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: あつくなる uses the adjective ending in い in the く form to connect it with なる and describe a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: そうだ follows a plain-form clause to convey information heard or read from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.why: The information source is given at the beginning with によると. The predicted content comes before そうだ, while ですよ adds an informing tone and gives slight emphasis to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If the form for guessing from appearance is used, そうだ means “looks like,” not information passed on from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.tip: Learners from Vietnam may easily confuse そうだ, which conveys 聞, with そうだ, which describes appearance; check whether the preceding information was heard or directly observed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.tokens.8.m: seems; I hear that it is
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ＋そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.vi: I hear that Tokyo is a frightening place. Therefore, do not let your daughter go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Tokyo the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: こわい modifies ところ, creating the phrase “a frightening place.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: だ connects the noun phrase ところ with the preceding description before it goes with そうだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: そうだ conveys an opinion about Tokyo from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: だから connects the conclusion in the next sentence with the reason or information in the previous sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the person affected by the causative action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: 行かせる is the causative form, while な changes the whole expression into a prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.why: The first sentence gives information passed on from another source, and the second uses だから to draw a conclusion. 娘を is the person affected, while 行かせるな prohibits the listener from letting the daughter go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行くな is used, it means that the daughter herself must not go; 行かせるな prohibits the listener from allowing or causing the daughter to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If そうだ is replaced by らしい, the sentence has a meaning based on inference from information, but it sounds less like direct transmission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.tip: Learners from Vietnam may easily overlook the difference between 行くな and 行かせるな; the causative form shows that another person performs the action of “going” because someone lets or makes them do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ＋そうだ；V使役形＋な
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.vi: I hear that my daughter received your help. Thank you very much.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.sk: N が ＋ お世話 に ＋ Vた ＋ そうで、 ＋ thanks
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle が marks the subject being mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: に goes with お世話になる to indicate receiving help from someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: なった is the past form of なる, while そうで connects the information heard with the thanks that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: A polite phrase used to end a thank-you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ／そうです; when connecting sentences, use そうで
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.why: 娘が is the subject that received help, while お世話になる is a fixed phrase expressing receiving help. そうで conveys information that the speaker heard and then connects naturally to the thank-you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If the appearance-based guess meaning is used, the sentence means “it looks like someone was helped,” which does not fit information heard from another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうだ in this sentence with そうだ, meaning “looks like,” but here it must be understood as “I hear that.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q17.tokens.6.m: I hear that; it seems that
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.vi: This cake looks delicious, doesn’t it? I really want to eat it!
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.sk: Aい remove い ＋ そうな ＋ N です ね。 Vます remove ます ＋ たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: おいしい remove い, then add そうな to modify the noun ケーキ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.ch.1.vi: it is a cake, isn’t it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: ですね is used to express an impression and seek agreement from the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べたい uses the form たい to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.cn: Aい remove い・Aな remove な ＋ そうだ／そうな ＋ N; Vます remove ます ＋ たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.why: おいしそうな comes before ケーキ to describe an impression seen from the outside. After this comment, 食べたい expresses the speaker’s direct desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with おいしいケーキ, the meaning is “a delicious cake,” which confirms the quality rather than guessing from its appearance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This is incorrect because the adjective い must remove い before connecting with そうな.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q18.kobun.tip: Do not say おいしいそうな; change おいしい to おいしそうな.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.vi: According to Yamada, I hear that the movie theater is not very far away.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 山田さん with 話 and shows whose words they are.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: によると only indicates the source of information supporting the content being conveyed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 映画館 the topic of the information that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: あまり is used with a negative form to reduce the degree, meaning “not ... very much.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.4.vi: I hear that it is not far away
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: とおくない is a negative adjective, そうです passes on information, and よ emphasizes the announcement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.cn: Nの話によると ＋ clause; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ／そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.why: 山田さんの話によると identifies the source of information, and then 映画館は states the topic. あまり combines with the negative とおくない to express “not very far.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is understood as an appearance-based guess, it becomes “the movie theater looks like it is not far away,” while this sentence reports information from Yamada.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: らしい also expresses inferred or heard information, but its feeling is less directly connected to a specific source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q19.kobun.tip: あまり must be used with a negative form; do not use あまりとおいない to say “not very far.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vi: I am having trouble. Could you give me some advice?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: ～ています describes an ongoing difficult situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 何か modifies アドバイス and indicates one unspecified thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being given in the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: くれませんか is a polite negative question used to ask someone to do something beneficial for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.why: The first sentence states the current situation as a background for the request. アドバイスを is the thing being requested, while くれませんか makes the request more polite and softer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If もらえませんか is used, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker wants to receive help or an action from the other person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If くださいませんか is used, the request is more formal and is usually directly connected to the requested noun or action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate くれませんか mechanically as “won’t you give it to me?” It is a polite way to make a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q2.kobun.cn: Nを ＋ くれる／くれませんか; Vて ＋ くれる／くれませんか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.vi: While we were talking, it suddenly became dark outside.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of する in the phrase 話をする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: している indicates an ongoing state, while うちに connects that period with an event that occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that changes to a dark state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 暗くなって expresses a change into a dark state, while しまった adds a sense of unintended or regrettable completion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.why: 話をしているうちに sets the event as a time reference. During that period, outside changed from light to dark, and しまった shows that the change was completed unexpectedly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: 間に indicates a period of time and an event that occurs during it, while うちに emphasizes that the event occurs while the initial state is still continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 間 is used, the two actions are emphasized as continuing in parallel, without emphasizing a sudden change like in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.tip: うちに is usually used with an ongoing state; do not translate it mechanically as “inside the house.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q20.kobun.cn: Vている・V辞書形・Vない形・Vた形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ うちに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.vi: If I were a bird, I would like to fly back to my homeland.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.sk: もし ＋ N だったら ＋ Vて ＋ N へ ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: もし signals a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun 鳥 combines with だったら to create a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the action of flying with the action of returning, showing the manner or an accompanying action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction of movement toward 国.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 帰りたい uses the form たい to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった ＋ ら; for a noun condition, Nだったら is usually used
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.why: もし and 鳥だったら create an unreal condition in the present. とんで connects the action of flying with the direction toward 国へ and the desire 帰りたい in the result clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 鳥なら is used, the feeling is lighter and it can be based on a topic already mentioned, without emphasizing the assumption as strongly as だったら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: としたら makes the assumption stronger, close to “suppose that...,” so the sentence sounds more thoughtful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q21.kobun.tip: With a noun, だったら must be used; do not say 鳥たら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.vi: If you take a day off, you must contact them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.sk: V辞書形 ＋ 場合 は ＋ かならず ＋ N を Vない remove ない ＋ ければ ＋ ならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: 休む in the dictionary form modifies 場合, creating the meaning “the case of taking a day off.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the case of taking a day off the condition or scope in which the rule applies.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: かならず modifies the action of contacting them and emphasizes that it must not be skipped.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.3.vi: if one does not contact them
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: しなければ is the conditional form of a negative, and it combines with ならない to create the meaning “must do.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: ならない completes the pattern ～なければならない and expresses an obligation or requirement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.cn: Vない形 remove い ＋ ければならない; the polite form usually uses Vなければなりません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.why: 休む場合は states the condition in which the rule applies, while かならず emphasizes the action that must be done. ～なければならない has a hypothetical negative structure, but the whole pattern means “must.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～なくてもいい is used, the meaning changes to “it is okay not to do it,” which is opposite to the obligation in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: べきだ also advises or asks someone to do something, but it sounds more like advice and is weaker than a compulsory rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q22.kobun.tip: Do not understand しなければ alone as “if one does”; only the whole phrase しなければならない means “must do.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.vi: Today, I am not going to school; I plan to stay home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は shows that today is the time reference and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative form 行かないで connects an action that is not done with the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle で shows where the action of resting takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 休む comes before つもりです to state the plan to rest.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.why: The sentence first sets the time reference, then marks the destination as an action not taken with に行かないで. The place where the following action happens uses で, while 休むつもりです expresses the speaker's plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence becomes a request not to do something and no longer expresses a plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is still not doing the first action, but the expression is more formal and more common in written language.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and で; に marks the destination, while で marks the place where an action happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q23.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + つもりです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.vi: According to the weather forecast, it is said that tomorrow will be hot.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: によると shows the source of the information used as the basis for the content that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes tomorrow the topic and the time reference of the prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い describes the weather condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: そうです comes at the end of the sentence to report information from the weather forecast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.why: The source of the information is given first with によると, followed by the topic, tomorrow, and the forecast content. The adjective あつい keeps the form い before そうです when そうです has the meaning of reporting information聞.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern can mean that something looks hot when the speaker observes it directly, instead of hearing it from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If でしょう is used instead, the sentence becomes the speaker's judgment or prediction and does not emphasize the source of the information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.tip: Do not omit だ before そうです with nouns and な adjectives; however, an い adjective such as あつい keeps the form い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.vi: It is said that many car accidents have occurred because of the snow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: Nのため gives the reason for the event in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 車の modifies 事故 and shows what kind of accident is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies the degree or number of accidents that occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.4.vi: it is said that they are occurring
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 起きている expresses an ongoing state, while そうです reports information that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.why: The reason 雪のため comes first to set the context for the whole sentence. Then the subject 車の事故 combines with たくさん and 起きている to express that many accidents are occurring, and そうです shows that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the reason has a more negative tone and places stronger blame.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If なので is used, the expression is softer and more conversational, and it often connects directly to a conclusion or explanation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で after a reason because of Vietnamese habits; with a noun in this pattern, のため must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q25.kobun.cn: Nのため・V普通形ため・Aい + ため・Aな + なため
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vi: I do not understand this problem. I will ask the teacher to explain it to me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify a lesson or problem near the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that the speaker does not understand in the structure わからない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: わからない is a negative predicate that states the condition of not understanding.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person from whom the speaker wants to receive the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 教えて is the て form. It connects the verb 教える with もらう to create a structure for receiving help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: もらおう is the volitional form of もらう and shows the speaker's decision or intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.why: The first clause states the problem that is not understood, with 問題が as the object of わからない. The second clause uses 先生に to show the person who helps and 教えてもらおう to express the intention to receive an explanation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the focus is on the teacher actively explaining it to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the speaker directly asks the teacher to explain it and does not emphasize the speaker's own intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.tip: With わかる, the thing being understood usually goes with が, while the helper in てもらう goes with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + もらう/もらおう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vi: I became ill from working too hard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: はたらきすぎて consists of the verb stem はたらき and すぎる, then uses て to connect the reason with the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the state or result that the subject becomes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました describes a change that has happened and combines with 病気に to create the meaning of becoming ill.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.cn: Vます-stem・Aい omit い・Aな omit な・N + すぎる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.why: わたしは states the subject, はたらきすぎて shows a cause that exceeds the necessary level, and 病気になりました expresses the result of becoming ill.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If はたらきすぎたので is used instead, the reason is stated directly with ので, without emphasizing the softer connection made by て.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If はたらきすぎてしまって is used, the sentence adds a feeling of regret or having accidentally done too much.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q4.kobun.tip: When すぎる is combined with a verb, the stem without ます, such as はたらきすぎる, must be used, not はたらきますすぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vi: Let us finish the homework within this year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: のうちに shows the time period by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: やってしまおう combines the てしまう aspect with the volitional form and shows the intention to finish the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q5.kobun.why: The topic is given first with は, followed by the time period with のうちに, and then the action that needs to be completed. てしまおう emphasizes the intention to finish the task.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 間に is used instead, the sentence only focuses on doing something during a period and has less of the meaning “while still within that period.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget の after a noun when using the pattern Nのうちに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q5.kobun.cn: Nの + うちに・V普通形 + うちに・Aい + うちに・Aなな + うちに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vi: Even after you graduate, please do not forget me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: Vて+も creates a concessive clause, meaning that even if graduation happens, the following result does not change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb 忘れる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 忘れないで is a shortened negative form of てください, used to make a gentle request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q6.kobun.why: The clause 卒業しても puts the concessive condition at the beginning of the sentence. The forgotten object is marked by を, while the gentle reminder is placed at the end with ないでね.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If てもらいたい is used, the sentence expresses a wish for the listener to perform the action, rather than a direct reminder to “not forget”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use ないも to say “even if someone does not do it”; the correct form is Vないで＋も.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q6.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も・Aくて ＋ も・Aなで ＋ も・Nで ＋ も
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vi: Tanaka appeared in that film and then became famous.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: あの modifies the noun 映画 that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the work or place where a character appears or takes part.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 出て connects the appearance with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The noun 有名 combines with になる to express a change into the state of being famous.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.cn: N ＋ に なる・Aな ＋ に なる・Aい omit い ＋ くなる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.why: 田中さんは is the topic, while 映画に indicates the work in which the person appears. The two actions are connected by て, with the appearance leading to the result of becoming famous.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 有名である is used, the sentence only describes the state of being famous and does not emphasize the process of change.
