default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q7.kobun.tip: With the adjective い, い must be changed to く before なる; do not use Aい＋になる directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vi: My computer was broken by a child.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that was broken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: こわされました is the polite past passive form, showing that the speaker was affected by the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q8.kobun.why: In an affected passive sentence, the person who performs the action goes with に, the affected object goes with を, and the verb is changed into the passive form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If the causative form is used, the meaning becomes “make or let the child break it,” completely changing the relationship between the people involved.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に for the person causing the action with を for the object affected by the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q8.kobun.cn: 五段V: 語尾う段→あ段＋れる・一段V: る→られる・する→される・来る→こられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vi: Officer! My wallet has been stolen!
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This expression is used to call the listener, not as the subject of the passive action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that was taken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ぬすまれました is the polite past passive form, describing an event that caused loss or damage to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q9.kobun.why: The subject is omitted because the affected person is the speaker. The wallet is marked by を, while the passive verb shows that it was taken against the speaker’s wishes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence only presents the wallet as the thing that was stolen; the current expression emphasizes the loss suffered by the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q9.kobun.tip: Do not translate the passive form mechanically as “the wallet was stolen”; understand it as an event that caused trouble or loss for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t15-q9.kobun.cn: 五段V: 語尾う段→あ段＋れる・一段V: る→られる・する→される・来る→こられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vi: Yesterday, when I went to her house, I bought a souvenir to take with me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう indicates the time when the whole action took place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the owner with 家, forming the phrase “her house.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: V辞書形＋とき creates a time clause that sets the background for the action of buying a souvenir.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the souvenir as the object being bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: 買って connects the action of buying with 行った, expressing that the speaker bought it and took it along while going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.why: The clause 行くとき comes first to identify the time of the main action. に indicates the destination, を indicates the object bought, and 買って行った shows that the speaker bought it first and then took it along while traveling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the action of buying the souvenir is understood to happen before going, emphasizing the order of events.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたとき is used, the time is understood as after the action of going has been completed, which is different from 行くとき.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often translate とき as an independent verb; in fact, it follows a clause to create a time phrase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ とき; Vて＋いく／Vて＋いった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.vi: When I was sick, I asked a friend to buy medicine and bring it to me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person experiencing the state of being sick in the subordinate clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: のとき creates a time phrase meaning “when in the state of being sick.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who performs an action that benefits the speaker in the pattern Vて＋もらう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.4.vi: asked someone to buy and bring it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 買ってくる connects with もらった to express that the speaker received help from a friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.why: The time clause comes first to give the situation. Then に indicates the helper and を indicates the thing bought. Vて＋もらう presents another person’s action from the speaker’s viewpoint as the receiver of help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてくれる is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the friend actively did the action for me, rather than my experience as the person receiving the benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern does not simply describe buying medicine; it shows that the speaker received help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に and を, but に identifies the person who performs the helpful action, while を identifies the object affected by the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.vi: As soon as my son came home from school, he went out to play without doing any of his homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies my son as the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point of the action of returning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a natural condition or time, showing that the next action happens as soon as he comes home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: も replaces を and emphasizes that even the homework was not done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: せずに is a special form of する＋ずに, connecting an action that was not done with the next action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the purpose of going, namely, going to play.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: てしまった describes a completed action, with a feeling of regret or something happening against expectations.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.cn: Vない形 omit ない＋ずに; する→せずに; 来る→こずに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.why: と connects coming home with the result that happens immediately afterward. ずに places the action of not doing homework before going out to play, while に in 遊びに行く indicates the purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vないで is used, the basic meaning is still “do the next action without doing V,” but the written-language nuance of ずに is lost.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: Vなくて usually connects a cause or state, so using it here is less natural than ずに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use しないずに, but ずに must connect to the form that omits ない, and する alone changes to せずに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.vi: Because there has been an accident, you cannot pass through that road now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the event that happened in the cause clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause to the result and creates a soft, natural expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: いま indicates the time of the current situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes that road the topic and creates a contrast with other roads.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 通れません is the negative potential form, while よ is used to announce and emphasize information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.cn: Potential-form verb＋ます・ません・る・ない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.why: ので places the cause before the result. は makes the road the topic, while the negative potential form shows that passing through it is impossible in the current situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vことができない, the meaning that it is impossible to do remains the same, but the expression becomes longer and more explanatory.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Vられない can mean cannot, but with some verbs it can also easily be understood as the passive form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often form the potential form of group 1 verbs incorrectly; 通る changes the final sound る to れ to form 通れる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.vi: If you are full, it is okay not to finish all the food.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that has the described condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: なら changes the condition いっぱい into a hypothetical condition for the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 全部 modifies 食べる and shows the scope of the food that needs to be eaten.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.3.vi: even if you do not eat
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べない changes into 食べなくて and then connects to も to express the meaning “even if you do not eat.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: かまいません ends the sentence by giving permission or saying that the action is not a problem.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.cn: Vない形 remove ない＋くてもかまいません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.why: なら puts the condition of being full first. The phrase 食べなくてもかまいません expresses that not eating everything is acceptable, while 全部 defines the scope of the eating action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vなくてもいい is used, the meaning “it is okay not to do it” is almost the same, but the conversational tone is more direct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vなくてはいけない, the meaning changes to “you must do it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often connect 食べないても directly, but they must change ない to なくて before adding も.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q13.tokens.3.m: if it is, if it is in a state
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vi: We have the day off tomorrow, so let’s go hiking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ Nなので ＋ N に ＋ Vましょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents tomorrow as the time and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.1.vi: because we have the day off
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 休み is a noun, so な is added before ので to connect the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or activity toward which 行く is directed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.why: The sentence gives the time and reason first, then makes an invitation in the main clause. に in ハイキングに行く indicates the destination or purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still means “because..., so...,” but the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行きましょうか is used, the sentence changes from a firm invitation to a lighter suggestion or request for the listener’s opinion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget な before ので after a noun or な adjective; they must say 休みなので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい＋ので／Aな＋なので／N＋なので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.vi: Because I have a headache and also have a fever, it seems that I will not be able to attend today’s meeting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 痛い changes into 痛くて to connect the painful condition with the following health information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: も adds another symptom besides the headache.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the health condition as the reason to the conclusion in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: きょうの modifies 会議 and identifies the meeting as taking place today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: に indicates the event that the speaker will attend, while は adds emphasis and a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.7.n: 出られ is the potential form, which connects with そうもない to predict that the possibility of attending is almost nonexistent.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます＋そうもない; Aい remove い＋そうもない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.why: The two symptoms are connected by て, and then ので turns the whole health condition into a reason. に marks the meeting as the object of attendance, while the potential form combined with そうもない expresses the prediction that attendance is impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vそうにない is used, it also means that something seems unlikely to happen, but it emphasizes the low possibility without も.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning does not change, but the sentence becomes longer and more clearly emphasizes ability or the possibility of carrying out the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse 出られる with 出れる; in standard writing, they should use 出られる and then connect it as 出られそうもない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.vi: As soon as I left the house, it suddenly started snowing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vたら ＋ Adv ＋ N が ＋ Vます-removeます ＋ はじめる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place of departure in the phrase 家を出る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a preceding condition or time with the following event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes the adjective な 急 into an adverb modifying 降りはじめた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks snow as the subject of the phenomenon that begins to occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The continuative form 降り of 降る connects with はじめる to express “begin to fall.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ はじめる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.why: The 出たら clause sets the time as a basis, and the new event is then stated in the following clause. 雪が is the subject of the phenomenon, while はじめる follows the continuative form of 降る to show the beginning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 降り出した, the nuance is that the snow suddenly starts falling, with emphasis on the sudden beginning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use the complete past form of the verb before はじめる; use the shortened form ます, such as 降りはじめる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.vi: Not now. Let’s talk after we finish eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.sk: N ではなく ＋ N を ＋ Vます-removeます ＋ おわってから ＋ Vましょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: ではなく negates 今 and connects it with the alternative or time stated afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks ごはん as the object of the action 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べ is the shortened form of ます connected to おわる; てから indicates the time after the action is completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do the action together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ おわる; Vて ＋ から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.why: ではなく excludes the present time, while 食べおわってから specifies that the talking will happen only after eating is finished. から connects the completion point with the action suggested at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べてから is used, it only says that the action happens after eating, without emphasizing that the eating has been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.kobun.tip: Do not attach おわる directly after the dictionary form; use the verb stem without ます, such as 食べおわる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q17.tokens.3.n: adjective ending in い (なく form)
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.vi: That runner kept running for as long as three hours.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.sk: N は + duration も + Vます-without ます + つづける
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies ランナー and identifies the runner being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks ランナー as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: も follows a duration to emphasize that it is longer than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 走り is the form of ます joined to つづける to express a continuous action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.cn: Vます-without ます + つづける
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.why: は limits the topic to the runner, while 3時間も states the duration and emphasizes how long it was. 走りつづけた places the continuation pattern in the predicate to show that the action did not stop during that period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 走っていた is used, it only describes the state of running in the past and does not emphasize continuous continuation like つづける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q18.kobun.tip: も after a duration has the meaning “as long as…” or “as many as…,” so it should not simply be translated as “also.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.vi: It has been three years since I started learning Japanese.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.sk: N を + Vます-without ます + はじめてから + duration です
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks 日本語 as the object of learning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: 習い joins with はじめる to mean starting to learn; てから uses that time as the starting point for counting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: もう adds the meaning that time has passed up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 3年です states the period that has passed since the starting point of learning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.cn: Vます-without ます + はじめる; Vて + から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.why: 日本語を is the object of 習う, while 習いはじめてから creates the point “since starting to learn.” After that point, もう3年です shows how much time has passed up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 日本語を習ってから is used, it means “since learning Japanese,” but does not emphasize the starting time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q19.kobun.tip: はじめる must be attached to the verb stem without ます; do not use the dictionary form 習うはじめる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vi: It will rain from the afternoon, so you should take an umbrella with you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle から marks the time when the rain starts.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects the reason before it with the advice after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the umbrella as the thing being carried.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.3.vi: it is better to take it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 持っていった is the past form of Vていく and comes before ほうがいい to give advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ほうがいいですよ expresses gentle, friendly advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.why: The reason comes first with ですから, followed by the thing to carry with を. 持っていった combines with ほうがいい to advise taking the umbrella along.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If only Vていく is used, the sentence only describes taking the umbrella along and no longer has the meaning of advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also gives advice, but it does not emphasize carrying something while moving as Vていったほうがいい does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit い in 持っていった; いく here keeps the meaning of moving away after doing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q2.kobun.cn: Vて+いく／Vて+いった; Vた+ほうがいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.vi: The number of foreigners coming to Japan has gradually increased.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the destination of the verb 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 来る in the dictionary form comes before 外国人 to modify “foreigners.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase 日本に来る modifies 外国人; が marks this group as the subject of ふえてきました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ふえて is the て form joined to くる, showing an increasing trend that has continued from the past to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.why: 日本に来る is a clause modifying 外国人, so the whole phrase acts as the subject of the sentence. てくる shows that the change started in the past and has progressed to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ふえていきます is used, it emphasizes that the trend will continue to increase from the present onward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.tip: Do not understand くる here as meaning only “come”; after Vて, it can show a change gradually progressing toward the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q20.kobun.cn: Vて + くる; Vて + きた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.vi: Tomorrow is a day off, so it is okay to sleep late.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the time and topic of the permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is a day off
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the reason with the result and explains why sleeping late is allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: まで marks the time limit up to which the sleeping continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.3.vi: it is okay to keep sleeping
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 寝ている expresses the state of continuing to sleep, while ても puts that state into a permission pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: いい completes the てもいい pattern, showing that doing it is allowed or not a problem.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.cn: Vて + もいい; Aい-without い + くてもいい; Aな + でもいい; N + でもいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.why: だから gives the reason, and then 遅くまで sets the limit of the sleeping time. The phrase 寝ていてもいい combines the continuing state with てもいい to express permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 寝なくてもいい is used, it means that not sleeping is also okay, which is the opposite of allowing sleep in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q21.kobun.tip: てもいい does not mean that doing it is required; it only says that doing it is allowed or not a problem.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.vi: It is okay for you to come to the party with your friends.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle に indicates the place or event being headed to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle と indicates the person doing the action together with someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: いっしょに modifies 来て and shows how the person comes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ても is the て form + も, creating the condition under which the action is allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: かまいませんよ ends the sentence with permission and a friendly tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.why: N に states the place or event being headed to, while N と and いっしょに add the person coming along and the manner. Vてもかまいません shows that the action 来る is accepted.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead still means that coming is allowed, but the tone is more direct and common.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this replaces the pattern in the sentence, the meaning changes to “you are not allowed to come.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake と in 友だちと for “and,” but here it only indicates the person coming along.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q22.kobun.cn: Vて＋もかまいません・Aい＋くてもかまいません・Aな＋でもかまいません・N＋でもかまいません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.vi: Since I also have to go to school tomorrow, I have to go to sleep.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: も emphasizes that there is also a school schedule tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: Nだ＋から connects the reason to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: もう modifies 寝なければならない and shows the time when action is needed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 寝ない changes to 寝なければ to create a condition in the obligation pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: ならない completes the pattern なければならない, expressing that something must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.cn: Vない remove い ＋ ければならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.why: The clause 学校だから gives the reason first, and then もう emphasizes the urgent need to go to sleep. 寝なければならない has a hypothetical negative structure combined with ならない to express obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this still means "have to sleep". The meaning is almost unchanged, but the way the clauses are connected is different.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, it only gives advice to sleep, which is weaker than an obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q23.kobun.tip: Do not connect the dictionary-form verb directly to ければならない; first change it to the ない form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.vi: On Sunday, I did nothing and rested comfortably.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Sunday the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 何も goes with the negative form せず to mean doing absolutely nothing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: せずに is a special form of する＋ずに. It connects the action that is not done with the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ゆっくり modifies 休みました and shows how the resting is done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 休みました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.cn: Vない remove ない ＋ ずに; する → せずに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.why: は sets Sunday as the topic range, while 何も＋せずに negates the preceding action. The main action at the end of the sentence isゆっくり休みました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing せずに with しないで still means "without doing", but it is more common and less formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the written or more formal form of Vないで.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q24.kobun.tip: With する, do not use しずに; change it to せずに instead.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.vi: Since my fever has gone down, it is okay not to take medicine.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: 熱が is the subject of the state 下がった.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: Vた＋ので connects a cause that has already happened with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks medicine as the object of 飲む.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲まなくても is ない＋くても. It creates the condition "even without taking it".
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: いいです completes the pattern なくてもいい, showing that the action is not necessary.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.why: The clause 熱が下がったので gives the reason first, followed by the object 薬を and the action 飲む. The negative form combined with てもいい makes it clear that taking the medicine is no longer necessary.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to an obligation to take the medicine.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, it becomes advice not to take the medicine. This is stronger and does not simply mean that it is unnecessary.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form 飲む with なくてもいい; change it to the ない form, which is 飲まない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q25.kobun.cn: Vない＋なくてもいい・Aい＋くなくてもいい・Aな＋でなくてもいい・N＋でなくてもいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vi: No matter how difficult it is, I will keep trying until the end.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: どんなに emphasizes the high degree of the situation in the preceding clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な 大変 connects with ても through the 大変でも form to create a concessive condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle まで shows the limit or endpoint of the effort.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: がんばります is the main predicate. It states a result that does not change, no matter what the preceding condition is like.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.why: どんなに～ても creates a concessive clause and comes before the result to emphasize that the level of difficulty does not change the speaker's determination. 最後まで shows the time limit or endpoint of the action がんばります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the emphasis shifts toward quantity or degree: no matter how much, the result does not change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If たとえ is used, the sentence emphasizes the assumption "even if" and usually has a clearer sense of determination or hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.tip: With an adjective な such as 大変, remove な and connect directly to でも: 大変でも.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q3.kobun.cn: どんなに＋Vても・Aい＋くても・Aな＋でも・N＋でも
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vi: If you smoke, please smoke in the seats over there.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action of smoking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: なら turns the situation "smoking" into a condition for the request that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects あちら with 席 to create the phrase "the seats over there".
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the place where the action of smoking takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: ください completes the polite way of making a request or asking someone to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, followed by the place and the requested action. で identifies where the action takes place, while Vてください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used instead, the sentence has a more specific sense of condition or time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If ば is used instead, the sentence focuses more on a rule-based or hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で when talking about the place where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ なら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vi: Please write your address and name on this sheet of paper.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects こちら with 紙 and modifies the sheet of paper.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows where the content is written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects 住所 with 名前 in the same object group.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks all the content that needs to be written, including the address and name.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: お＋the verb's form with ます removed＋ください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.why: The place receiving the content goes with に, while the information to be written is joined by と and marked by を. The pattern お～ください comes before ください to politely ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: With Vてください, the request is still polite but less formal than お～ください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ていただけますか is used instead, the sentence becomes a softer request in question form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q5.kobun.tip: Do not add お to every verb; this pattern is used only with suitable verbs and the form with ます removed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vi: Do you remember how much you paid for that painting ten years ago?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the painting was bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: その modifies 絵 and identifies the painting that has already been specified.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the painting as the object that was bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.3.vi: how much it was bought for
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: いくらで asks about the purchase price, while か closes the small question included in the information to remember.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 覚えている describes the state of remembering information from the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: か turns the whole sentence into a polite question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.why: The information being asked about—the purchase price—is placed before か, and this whole clause becomes the object of 覚えている. で indicates the price, while か marks the small question inside the main sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～かどうか, the content becomes only “whether or not”; it does not ask for the specific amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: With ～のを覚えている, the event is turned into a noun with の instead of keeping the form of a small question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q6.kobun.tip: Do not put か at the end of the whole sentence when asking for specific information inside the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vi: Because I was lonely by myself, I was very happy that my friend came.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.sk: Stateで ＋ Aいので ＋ Nが ＋ Vてくれて ＋ Aいかった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the state or situation when the speaker felt sad.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason before it with the feeling and event after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who carries out the action of coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 来てくれて consists of Vて＋くれる, showing that the friend came and that this action benefited the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective in the past form describes the speaker’s feeling after the event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.why: ので states the reason first. Then, the friend’s coming is connected to the feeling with the て form. くれる shows that another person’s action benefits the speaker or makes the speaker grateful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vてもらう, the focus shifts to the speaker receiving help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vてあげる, the speaker is the person who performs an action for someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the subject of くれる; with くれる, another person does something beneficial for the speaker or the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vi: There is a strange sound outside. Please go out and check it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the sound comes from or where the speaker notices it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective な to 音 to modify the sound.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the sound perceived through hearing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: Nがする describes perceiving a sound, smell, taste, or sensation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: ちょっと softens the degree of the requested action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: 見てきてください asks the listener to go, check, and return.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.why: The sound is treated as the object of perception and goes with がする, rather than being a sound actively produced by a person. The next sentence uses Vてくる to describe going somewhere else to check and then returning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is used, the sentence only says that an object or event exists; it does not emphasize the feeling of hearing it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 聞こえます is used, the focus is on the sound reaching the ears and being heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q8.kobun.tip: Do not translate がする as “make a sound”; this pattern describes sensations such as sounds, smells, or tastes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vi: I can hear the sound of a television from the next room. It seems that someone is there.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates where the sound comes from.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the sound that is heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞こえる describes a sound naturally reaching the ears and being heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: だれか refers to an unidentified person who is the subject of いる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ようだ usually follows a clause and expresses an guess based on a sign just noticed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.why: から identifies the source of the sound, while 聞こえる expresses the natural possibility of hearing it. Hearing the television provides the basis for the guess だれかいるようだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～そうだ is used, the nuance is that something looks a certain way based more directly on its appearance, without emphasizing an inference from information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～らしい is used, the sentence focuses more on information or signs showing that something seems true.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use ような before the predicate; before ようだ, use a plain-form clause or Nの.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t16-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ ようだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vi: When I am tired, I sometimes leave the television on and fall asleep.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects a condition or situation that usually leads to the action that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks テレビ as the object of つける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: Vた＋まま indicates that the television remains on while the next action happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ことがあります turns the event into something that can happen, while しまう adds the meaning of accidentally or completely.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.why: と states a situation that usually leads to a result, while つけたまま describes the television remaining unchanged. The phrase 寝てしまうことがあります describes sometimes falling asleep in that state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it emphasizes two actions happening at the same time, without emphasizing a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, it means turning on the television beforehand or leaving it on intentionally, which differs from accidentally leaving it unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.tip: まま must express a continuing state; do not translate it mechanically as “after” like あとで.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q1.kobun.cn: Vた＋まま・Vない＋まま・Aい＋まま・Aな＋なまま・Nの＋まま
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vi: Because there are many Chinese characters, I cannot read Japanese newspapers.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks what is said to be numerous and creates the reason for the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason clause with the result; 多い keeps the polite form before から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 日本語 with 新聞, while を marks the object of the reading action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb 読む combines with こと to turn the action into a noun phrase, which becomes the subject of できません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: できません expresses the inability to perform the action that was previously turned into a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and ends with から. The action 読む is changed into the noun phrase 読むこと, and then ができません is used to say that the action cannot be performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 読めません is used, the meaning is still “cannot read,” but it directly uses the verb’s potential form and is shorter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put を before できる, but in this pattern the action must go with ことができる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q10.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vi: Because I also have a part-time job in the evening, I cannot get up easily in the morning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the part-time job as existing in the evening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: も adds the evening to the times when the part-time job exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the cause with the result of being unable to get up in the morning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 朝 indicates the time when the action 起きられません takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: なかなか is used with a negative sentence to express that something is difficult to happen or is not achieved for a long time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 起きられません is the negative potential form of 起きる, meaning that the person is unable to get up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.cn: 一段V: remove る + られる; 五段V: change the final sound to the え row + る; する → できる; くる → こられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.why: The reason for having a part-time job is stated first with から. 朝 comes before the verb to indicate the time, while なかなか combines with the negative form 起きられません to emphasize being unable to get up for a long time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning of ability does not change, but the expression is longer and more formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 起きられません for the passive voice; in this sentence, it is the negative potential form, meaning “cannot get up.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vi: Because my friends will come to visit, I will clean the room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the people who will come to visit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the purpose of coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason for the visit with the action of preparing the room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the room as the object whose state is changed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the new state that the room is made to have.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: します combines with きれいに to express that the subject actively makes the room clean.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and connects to the main clause with から. 部屋を is the object affected by the action, while きれいにします expresses actively changing the room into a clean state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If きれいになる is used instead, the sentence only says that the room becomes clean, without emphasizing who performs the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use きれいくする, but きれい is an な adjective, so きれいにする must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q12.kobun.cn: N + にする; Aな + にする; Aい + くする
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.vi: The department manager is making a scary face and seems to be angry about something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the department manager as the person described through the facial expression and state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the expression created in the phrase 顔をして.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the visible expression with the judgment in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 何か indicates an unspecified thing and adds meaning to the state of being angry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ようです comes after the Vている clause to make an inference based on the visible facial expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.why: The facial expression is presented first as an observed sign, and then て connects it to a conclusion. おこっているようです expresses the state of being angry, and this judgment is based on the visible expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうです is used instead, the sentence focuses more on the direct impression that the person looks angry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If みたいです is used instead, the meaning is close to ようです, but the expression is more casual and conversational.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ようです directly after a noun or adjective and forget the connecting form, but before ようです, Nの or Aなな must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ようです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.vi: Because they are always together, those two may be a couple.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of frequency that modifies the state of being together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects the reason in the first clause with the guess in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: A demonstrative word that modifies 二人 and identifies the two people being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: は presents those two people as the topic for the speaker’s guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: かもしれません comes after a noun to express an uncertain possibility.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and connects with ですから. After the topic is stated with は, the noun 恋人 combines with かもしれません to create an uncertain guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence is still a guess, but it has more of a predictive or evidence-based judgment tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand かもしれません as a mild statement, but this pattern always keeps an uncertain tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + かもしれません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.vi: I do not want to go, but it has been decided that I will go on a business trip abroad from next month.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being discussed and makes them the general topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.1.vi: do not want to go, but
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 行きたい changes to the negative form 行きたくない, while が connects the two contrasting ideas.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the starting point for the business trip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination of the business trip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The plain-form verb comes before こと to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: ことになった expresses a decision or situation that has already been settled.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.why: The idea of not wanting to go is stated first with が to create contrast. Then, the time and destination come before the action, and the action is nominalized with こと and combined with になった to express a decision that has been made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence says that the speaker personally decides to go on the business trip, rather than the decision being made externally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse ことになった with personal intention; this pattern usually emphasizes a result that has already been decided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形（辞書形・ない形・た形など）＋ ことになる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.vi: I am planning to start my own company in the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ V意向形 と ＋ 思っています
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: A time phrase that sets the time for the plan being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 自分 with 会社, showing that the company belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the company as the object of the action of starting it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 作ろう is the volitional form, and と marks it as the content of the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 思っています expresses an intention formed earlier that is still held now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.why: The time phrase しょうらい comes first to show when the plan will be carried out. The phrase 自分の会社を is the object, while 作ろうと 思っています combines the volitional form with と to state the content of the plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence states the plan more directly and firmly, without emphasizing the process of continuing to hold the thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced here, the sentence has more of a planned schedule or expected timetable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before と 思っています, but when expressing their own intention, they need to use the volitional form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q17.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と ＋ 思っています
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.vi: I like meat too, but I am trying to eat a lot of vegetables.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: も replaces は and adds meat to the group of foods the speaker likes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 好き is a な adjective used as the predicate, while が connects it to the mildly contrasting idea in the next clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: も marks vegetables as the object being eaten and also means that they are added.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb of degree that modifies 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べるように states the action or state that the speaker is trying to maintain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: しています combines with ように to express the effort to turn the action into a habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.why: The first clause admits the speaker's preference using が, then shifts to a habit the speaker wants to maintain. も is used twice to show that both meat and vegetables are included in what is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence emphasizes a decision or effort made at the time of speaking, while しています emphasizes a habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced here, the sentence shows a clearer rule or personal decision rather than simply an effort to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 食べるようにしています as trying to eat something once, but this pattern usually refers to maintaining the action regularly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q18.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ようにしています
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.vi: This morning, because of the typhoon, the train was delayed by as much as one hour.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ Nのために ＋ N が ＋ Duration も ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets this morning as the time reference for the event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: Nのために shows the cause of the train's delay.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the train as the subject that falls into the state of being delayed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: も emphasizes that the delay lasted longer than usual.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: 遅れました is a polite past-tense predicate that states the result that occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.why: The time is stated first, followed by the cause using のために. The subject 電車が comes before the duration of the delay, and then 遅れました ends the sentence with the result that occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence still states the cause, but the explanation sounds softer and more conversational.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced here, the sentence sounds as if it blames the cause or complains negatively about it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out の after a noun, but with a noun it must be connected in the form Nのために.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.tokens.8.m: as much as, as long as
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vi: After eating, please take this medicine.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks ごはん as the object of 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: Vた＋あとで connects a completed action with an action that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the medicine as the object of 飲んでください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to ask or instruct the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.why: 食べたあとで sets the time after eating has finished. The main clause that follows is a request to take medicine, so 飲む changes to て＋ください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it here still means “after eating,” but it emphasizes finishing the first action before doing the next one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced here, the meaning changes to “before eating,” which is the opposite of the current order.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q2.kobun.tip: With あとで, the earlier action usually uses た to show that it has been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.vi: I will make a note so that I do not forget my appointment with my friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: との connects 友だち with 約束, showing an appointment or promise with a friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the appointment as the thing that needs to be remembered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: Vないように states the purpose of avoiding forgetting the appointment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.ch.3.vi: will make a note in advance
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: しておきます expresses making a note beforehand to prepare for something later.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.why: The thing to remember comes before を, while わすれないように states the negative purpose. The action メモしておきます is done beforehand as preparation and to avoid forgetting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence can state the purpose more directly, but ように sounds more natural when aiming to avoid a state such as forgetting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced here, the sentence emphasizes trying to create a habit or taking deliberate action, rather than preparing something in advance as in ておく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use わすれないために in every situation, but ように is suitable when the goal is to maintain or avoid a state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ように
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q21.kobun.vi: After I started my part-time job, I have been very busy every day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q21.kobun.sk: Nを ＋ Vて、 ＋ Time ＋ Adv ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action of starting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the earlier action with the state that occurs afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q21.kobun.why: The phrase アルバイトをはじめて comes first to state the background event or cause. Then, 毎日とても modifies the state いそがしいです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes the time after completing the action more than the connection leading to the later state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ～て as only meaning “and,” but here it also connects a cause or event to its result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.vi: In Japanese, which is more difficult: pronunciation or kanji?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the two nouns being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 漢字 is the second item in the pair of choices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks which of the two choices is being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective むずかしい acts as the predicate, and か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.why: は limits the topic to Japanese, then と lists the two things being compared. どちらが is the subject being asked about, while むずかしい is the quality being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with どれが, the sentence usually asks about one item among three or more choices, so it does not fit the two items here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with どのNが, the speaker must state the noun immediately after the question word, such as どの科目が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use どれ in every case, but どちら is usually used when choosing between two sides.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.vi: I went to watch a soccer match and shouted loudly, “Go for it!”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects サッカー with the noun 試合 to form the phrase “soccer match.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the match as the object of going to watch it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The form without ます 見に combines with 行く to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the action of going to watch the match with the following action of shouting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the quoted words exactly as spoken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: 大きい modifies 声 to form the phrase “loud voice.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks 声 as the object being produced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.why: 見に行って describes going to watch the match, then connects to the action of shouting encouragement. The shout is placed in quotation marks and connected with と to show what was uttered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with がんばって, the encouragement becomes softer and more polite than the strong command がんばれ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 見に行く with 見て行く; に here shows purpose, not the action of watching before going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q23.kobun.cn: V命令形＋と＋言う・叫ぶ・声を出す
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.vi: Compared with my older sister, I cook better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: より states the reference point for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: のほうが marks the side judged to be better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the area in which someone is judged to be skilled.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.why: 姉より sets the comparison point, while わたしのほうが identifies the side that is better. 料理が shows the area in which じょうず ability is being judged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would mean that both sides are equally skilled instead of saying that I am better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If used with a negative form such as 姉ほどじょうずではありません, it means not as skilled as my older sister.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out の in わたしのほうが, but のほうが is a fixed phrase in this comparison pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q24.kobun.cn: N1より＋N2のほうが＋Aい／Aなです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.vi: At night, I was woken up by a loud noise from the room next door.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.sk: Time ＋ NのNのAなNで ＋ V受身ました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects となり with 部屋 to identify the room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 部屋 with the phrase 大きな音 to modify the sound.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 大きな directly modifies 音.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: で shows the cause or agent that made the speaker wake up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: The passive form shows that the speaker was affected by the outside noise.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.why: The phrase となりの部屋の大きな音で combines the modifying parts into the cause of the event. おこされました uses the passive form because the speaker is the person affected by being woken up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with the active form, the meaning would be “woke someone up,” with the speaker as the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with おきました, the meaning would only be “woke up,” without saying that the noise caused it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the active form おこしました, but when the person is affected, they must use おこされました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q25.kobun.cn: V受身形：五段Vあ＋れる・一段V＋られる・する→される・来る→こられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vi: I have climbed Mount Fuji as many as three times.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.sk: N に ＋ Vた ＋ ことが ＋ Number of times も ＋ あります
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object or destination of the climbing action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense verb modifies こと, creating the meaning “the act of having climbed.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns the previous action into a noun meaning an experience; が marks the subject being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: も emphasizes that the number of times is more than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: あります describes the existence of the experience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.why: The action is changed into a noun with こと, and then あります is used to say that the experience exists. The phrase showing the number of times comes before あります, and も emphasizes the number.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence describes something that happens sometimes or an action that one sometimes does, not an experience one has had.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistakenly use Vる before ことがある when they want to say “have ever done,” but experience must use Vた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q3.tokens.5.n: noun showing the number of times
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vi: According to the news, a large typhoon is expected to arrive next week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.sk: N によると ＋ Time ＋ Aな ＋ N が ＋ V普通形 ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: によると shows the source of the information being reported.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase is placed before the event to identify when it will happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな directly modifies the noun 台風 that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject of the action 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです is attached to the plain form to report information heard or read.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.why: The source of the information is stated first with によると, followed by the time and the subject of the event. 来るそうです uses the plain form of 来る before そうです because this is reported information, not a direct guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, そうです means “looks like it is about to,” based on visible signs, not information heard from the news.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse そうですreported information聞 with そうですspeculation; check whether the information comes from something heard or from signs in front of you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vi: I do not know whether I can run 10 km.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.sk: Distance も ＋ potential V か ＋ negative potential V か ＋ わかりません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: も emphasizes that the distance is large or significant.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: か is placed after the first clause to create one of two possibilities that need to be determined.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative clause is repeated after か to create the structure “whether ... or not”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりません is the main predicate and takes the whole question content before it as something that is unclear.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.why: The two opposite possibilities are placed in parallel and connected by か. The whole phrase is the question content of わかりません, while も emphasizes the distance of 10 km.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning of “whether or not” remains the same, but the negative clause is not repeated separately.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place か only at the end; this structure requires か after both the affirmative and negative possibilities.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形＋か ＋ Vない形＋か
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vi: I will go out next Sunday because my friend has a wedding.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this time the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the polite form is the predicate of the first sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 友だち with 結婚式 and shows possession or a related connection.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks an existing event and gives the reason being explained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: んです adds an explanatory meaning or gives background for the previous sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.why: The first sentence states a plan, and the second explains the background. あるんです uses んです after the plain form of a verb to connect the reason with the information just mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If からです is used instead, the sentence gives the reason more directly and clearly, with less of the gentle explanatory tone of んです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.tip: Before んです, the verb must be in the plain form; the polite form ありますんです cannot be used directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ んです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vi: Both her way of speaking and her way of eating are truly feminine.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes her the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: も marks the first element in the list “both ... and ...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: も is parallel with 話し方も, and both are the objects being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb that modifies the quality 女性らしい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: らしい is attached to a noun to describe a characteristic that matches the image of that noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.why: The two characteristics are listed with the pattern も...も, and together they support the comment about her. 女性らしい describes a style with characteristics that match the image of “feminine.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence focuses on the comparison “like a woman” and does not emphasize feminine characteristics.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 女性だ is used instead, the sentence only states that she is a woman and does not describe her style or characteristics.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand らしい as “I hear that”; in this sentence, it comes after a noun and means “typical of” or “fitting the image of.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vi: Because I really like cake, I always end up eating too much.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Aなで ＋ Adv ＋ Vます-removeます ＋ すぎる ＋ てしまいます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that is liked with 大好き.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: で is the connecting form of the adjective な 大好きだ, connecting the reason to the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: すぎる attaches to the verb stem 食べ, while て connects the excessive action with しまいます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいます describes an action that happened unintentionally or caused the speaker regret.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます・Aい remove い・Aな/N ＋ すぎる; Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.why: 大好きで gives the reason, and then いつも shows how often the action happens. 食べすぎてしまいます combines the meaning of “excessively” from すぎる with the regretful or unintended meaning of てしまう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 食べすぎます is used, the sentence only says that the person eats too much and does not clearly show that it is accidental or regrettable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If only 食べてしまいます is used, the sentence shows that the person accidentally eats, but does not say that the amount is excessive.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily attach すぎる after the dictionary form; with verbs, ます must be removed before connecting, as in 食べ＋すぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vi: This cookbook is easy to understand, and it looks like the dishes can be made simply.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: わかりやすい changes to わかりやすくて to connect the two characteristics.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes the adjective な かんたん into an adverb modifying できそうです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.3.vi: looks like it can be done
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: できそうです expresses the judgment that making the dish seems possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, and then the two characteristics are connected with て. かんたんに modifies the ability to carry out the action, while そうです comes at the end to give a judgment based on appearance or the current condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ようです is used instead, the sentence focuses on an inference based on signs or information, rather than only a direct impression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use そうです after the dictionary form of a verb, but with verbs the stem of the ます form must be used, as in できそうです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q9.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹・Aい（いを取る）・Aな ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vi: Because my older sister will come from my hometown, may I take tomorrow off?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the person who is coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who performs the action 来ます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason clause to the request for permission that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes tomorrow the emphasized point in time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.4.vi: let me take a day off
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 使役て形 combines with いただく to ask a superior for permission to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The negative question form creates a polite and humble request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.why: The clause 来ますから gives the reason before the request for permission. 休ませていただけませんか expresses asking an authorized person to allow the speaker to take a day off, using very polite language.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence still asks for permission but is more casual and direct, without clearly showing humility.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the request for permission sounds more direct than the soft request of いただけませんか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 休ませる as “make someone take a day off,” but in this pattern it means “allow me to take a day off.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q1.kobun.cn: V使役て＋いただけませんか（五段: a段＋せる・一段: させる・する: させる・来る: こさせる）
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vi: You can reach that restaurant in a three-minute walk from the station.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N から ＋ Vて ＋ Time duration で ＋ potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the restaurant is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point for going to the restaurant.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 歩いて shows the means of travel and connects naturally with 行けます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the time needed to complete the journey.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 行けます is the potential form of 行く and expresses that one can reach that place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.why: から identifies the starting point, 歩いて states the means of travel, and three minutesで shows the time required. 行けます ends the sentence with the meaning that one can get there.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with に, the sentence may be understood as referring to a specific time when one must arrive, not the time needed to travel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If かかって is used, the focus changes to the fact that it takes three minutes, without directly emphasizing the ability to get there.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q10.kobun.tip: The particle で in this pattern shows the required duration, not a place or means of travel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vi: The place where I was born is a small town called Yamanaka.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the action of being born.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.1.vi: the place where I was born
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the clause into a noun, while は makes the whole content the topic to be explained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: という introduces the name 山中 for the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective phrase 小さい modifies 町, and then です serves as the polite predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.why: The clause 生まれた is nominalized by のは so that it can be the topic. という connects the place name with the noun 町, and then です identifies it as the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning becomes “be called” or “be known as,” which sounds more formal and objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence explains the name N itself instead of introducing the town’s name.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q11.kobun.tip: という comes between a name and the noun it names; do not translate it as the word と used to connect two equal nouns.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vi: Because I was hungry, I ended up eating as many as five bananas.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Vていたので、＋ N を ＋ Quantity も ＋ Vてしまいました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the hungry state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result; すいていた expresses that the hungry state was continuing at that time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks bananas as what was eaten.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: も is added after a quantity to emphasize that the number is larger than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べて connects the action of eating with しまう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: てしまいました expresses that the action was completed and often carries a feeling of regret or that it was unintended.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.why: The hungry clause comes before ので to give the reason. The quantity five本 is used with も to emphasize eating a large amount, while てしまう shows that the action was completed unexpectedly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it would mean doing something in advance or preparing it, without the unintended meaning of eating too much.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence would only describe an ongoing state or action, without emphasizing completion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q12.kobun.tip: Do not translate も after a quantity as “also”; in this structure, it adds emphasis, like “as many as” or “even.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vi: I intend to commute to the company by car.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction or destination of travel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before つもりだ to express the speaker’s intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.why: 車で states the means of transportation, 会社へ states the destination, and 通う shows regular travel. つもりだ comes after the dictionary form to turn the action into an intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would only express a desire to go to the company, without necessarily showing a decided plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence would focus more on a schedule or arranged plan and sound more objective than a personal intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.tip: つもりだ connects directly with the dictionary form or ない form, but not with the ます form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形（辞書形・ない形）＋ つもりだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q14.kobun.vi: If you study, turn off the TV.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: なら comes after a clause to state a condition or assumption.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb けす.
