default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: なさい connects with the verb stem after removing ます to form a request or mild command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q14.kobun.why: The conditional clause 勉強するなら comes first to state an assumed situation. テレビを is the object of the action けす, while なさい comes at the end to make a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the request becomes more polite and does not sound like a superior speaking to a subordinate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern changes the sentence into advice, which is softer and does not directly require the listener to act.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use なさい as a polite expression with everyone, but this pattern is usually used when a superior speaks to a subordinate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vi: While the fish is cooking, I will make a salad.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks fish as the object of cooking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 間に shows the period when the action in the following clause occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks salad as the object of the verb 作ります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 作ります at the end of the sentence states the main action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.why: The phrase やいている間に sets the time for the action 作ります. Since cooking is in progress, use the ている form before 間に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 間は is used, the period is presented as the topic, without emphasizing an event that happens during it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: うちに emphasizes that something should be completed before the current state or period changes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit ている, but when saying that one action is done while another is happening, Vている間に must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q15.kobun.cn: Vている・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の ＋ 間に
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.vi: Because it is quiet, it seems that I will sleep well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective なしずか needs な before ので to connect a clause expressing a reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the state of sleeping and means sleeping well or soundly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.2.vi: seems likely to be able to sleep
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: そうだ follows the potential form ねられる to express a prediction that something seems possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.why: しずかなので gives the reason first, then よくねられそうだ gives the predicted result. With the adjective な, な is required before ので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and conversational, and the soft tone is reduced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: ようだ expresses a judgment based on a situation or information, not only an outward impression like そうだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say しずかので, but the adjective な must keep な: しずかなので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので; Vます語幹 ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vi: You must not touch this computer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the object or the place of contact for the verb さわる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: Vてはいけません is placed at the end of a sentence to show that something is forbidden.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q17.kobun.why: このコンピューターに is the object affected by さわる. The て form combines with はいけません to turn the action into something forbidden.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes a polite and softer request not to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning is also that something must not be done, but this expression is more conversational and direct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q17.kobun.tip: The verb さわる usually goes with に, so を should not be used mechanically as with many other transitive verbs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.vi: My younger brother does nothing but play and does not do his homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 弟 the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: Vてばかりいる describes repeatedly doing an action, while いて connects it to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks homework as the object of the verb しません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative form しません states that the action is not performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.why: 弟は is the topic, and あそんでばかりいて then shows an action that is repeated excessively. The final clause states what is being neglected: しゅくだいをしません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that the younger brother is playing, without criticizing him for playing too much.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes doing only one thing, but it does not necessarily imply continuing or repeated action like ばかりいる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ばかり as simply “only,” but Vてばかりいる often implies dissatisfaction because the action continues or is repeated too much.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.vi: This is the ring my mother gave me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the item being introduced the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the mother as the subject of the giving action in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the recipient in the structure くれる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause 母がわたしにくれた comes before and modifies the noun ゆびわ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: です connects the noun to the topic to complete the introductory sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.why: The clause 母がわたしにくれた is placed directly before ゆびわ to identify which ring it is. くれる shows that the item was given by someone to the speaker or to someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If あげる is used, the giver gives the item to someone else, without showing that it is given toward the speaker as くれる does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If もらう is used, the recipient becomes the subject and the sentence focuses on receiving.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse が and に in くれる: the giver goes with が, and the recipient goes with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q19.kobun.cn: Nが Nに Nを ＋ くれる／Vて ＋ くれる; Vた ＋ N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vi: That movie is a very good story, and it made many people cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the movie is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: で connects the description of the movie to the result clause that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the people affected by the action that made them cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 泣かされました is the causative-passive form, expressing that someone was affected so strongly that they had to cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.why: The movie is introduced as the topic, and its description is connected by いい話で to the result experienced by many people. が marks the people affected, while 泣かされました emphasizes that they were made to cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence only says that many people cried, without stating what caused them to cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the subject will be the person who makes others cry, not the person affected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 泣かされる with 泣かせる because they do not distinguish the affected person from the person causing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q2.kobun.cn: Aい・Nな ＋ で、V使役受身
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q20.kobun.sk: N は ＋ question word＋でも ＋ potential verb
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 何でも marks the unlimited object of 食べられる, meaning “anything.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べられる is the potential form and expresses the ability to eat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q20.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, then 何でも becomes the unlimited object of the verb. 食べられる expresses the subject’s ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何か is used instead, the meaning becomes “eat something,” without the sense that anything is acceptable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 何も is used instead, it usually goes with a negative sentence and means “not eat anything.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse でも with the meaning “but,” but in 何でも it creates the unlimited meaning “anything... also...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vi: Dear guest, I will carry your luggage for you. Your room is this way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.sk: N を ＋ お＋V remove ます＋します。N は ＋ こちらでございます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: This is a form of address used for someone being served.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being carried for someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.2.vi: I will carry it for you
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: お＋the verb’s stem form ます＋します creates a humble expression for the speaker’s action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes おへや the topic of the following sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: こちら indicates a location near the speaker, while でございます is the polite form of です.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.cn: お＋verb stem ます＋する／します
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.why: The item being handled for the guest is marked with を, while the staff member’s action uses the humble form お持ちします. In the next sentence, おへやは introduces the topic and こちらでございます indicates the location politely.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If お持ちになります is used, it is respectful language for the guest’s or another respected person’s action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 持ってきます is used, it is only an ordinary polite expression and does not clearly show the staff member’s humility.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use お＋V＋します with every verb; remember that the verb must change to the stem form ます before adding します.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.vi: Mr. Kimura is eating tempura, and it looks very delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.sk: N は + N を + Aい remove い＋そうに + Vて + います
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person performing the eating action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food being eaten.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: そうに changes an adjective into a state or manner that modifies the verb 食べています.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects 食べる with います to create an ongoing-action structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: ています expresses an action that is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.cn: Aい remove い＋そうに／Aな＋そうに／V remove ます＋そうに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.why: おいしそうに comes before the verb to describe how the person looks while eating. 食べています combines form て with います to show that the action is ongoing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If おいしく is used, it confirms that the person is eating deliciously, without emphasizing that the food looks delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: This form is incorrect because an adjective ending in い must remove い before そうに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep い in おいしいそうに; with the pattern そうだ, the adjective い usually removes い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vi: Teacher, do you know Mr. Shimura's phone number?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being asked whether they know the information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 志村さん with 電話番号 and shows ownership or a related connection.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the information known in ごぞんじです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ごぞんじですか is a respectful way to ask whether someone knows some information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.why: The known information is the object, so it takes を. The phrase 志村さんの電話番号 comes before を to clearly identify which phone number it is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 知っていますか is used, it still means “do you know?”, but it is a normal expression and does not show as much respect as ごぞんじですか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If 分かりますか is used, the question asks whether the listener understands or knows how to handle something, rather than focusing on knowing information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use が with ごぞんじです, but the known information must be marked with を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q23.kobun.cn: N + を + ごぞんじです（か）
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.vi: I received this gift from him on my birthday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + Person に + もらいました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies プレゼント and must be used with a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the gift as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time when the gift was received.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: に identifies the person giving the gift in a structure meaning receiving something from someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: もらいました is the polite past form of もらう and shows that the speaker received something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.cn: Person に／から + N を + もらう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.why: The gift is made the topic with は. The time comes before the giver, while に identifies the source of the gift in the structure もらう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of に, it still means receiving something from him, but it clearly emphasizes where the gift came from.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with あげました, the meaning reverses and becomes “gave it to him.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the direction of giving and receiving; with もらう, the receiver is the subject, while the giver usually takes に or から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vi: The teacher told the student that there would be a test next week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.sk: N は + Person に + 「Sentence」 + と + 言いました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person performing the speaking action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に identifies the listener or the person receiving the spoken message.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 来週 indicates when the content of the message will take place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of します in the quotation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: します is the predicate of the directly quoted speech.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks all the content inside the quotation marks as quoted speech.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: 言いました is the main verb in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.cn: Quoted sentence + と + 言う／言います／言いました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.why: The speaker comes first with は, and the listener takes に. The spoken content is placed in quotation marks and connected to the verb 言う by と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If ある is used, the meaning becomes “there will be a test next week,” focusing on the existence of the test.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If 伝えました is used, it means “communicated,” and does not necessarily quote the exact words spoken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget と after the quoted content; in this pattern, と must come immediately before 言いました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vi: If you do not eat breakfast, it is not good for your body.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks breakfast as the object of eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べないと creates a negative condition, meaning that if one does not eat, it leads to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に identifies the thing affected by not eating breakfast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: よくないです is the predicate evaluating the result of the preceding condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.why: The action of not eating breakfast comes before と to form the condition, while 体によくない is the natural result for the body. に attaches to the affected object, not to a place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning becomes that even if one does not eat breakfast, it is still not good, emphasizing concession.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence has a clearer hypothetical conditional meaning and less of a natural-consequence meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand と here as “and,” but in this sentence と connects a condition with an inevitable result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vi: Because work is busy now, I am working even on days off.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 indicates when the work situation is occurring.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks work as the subject that has the busy state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ですから connects the reason with the action explained in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: でも attaches to days off to present a case that still occurs despite being unexpected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: てい​​ます expresses an action that is continuing or a current state of working.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason, and then 休みの日でも highlights the case of continuing to work even on a day off. ています shows that this work is continuing or is a current state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes “even N,” and is suitable when N is a case that normally should not occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 休みの日も is used, the sentence only says “also on a day off,” which is weaker and does not emphasize that it is unexpected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand でも here as “but,” while it comes after a noun and means “even...also.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vi: If you put money in here and press the button, delicious coffee comes out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the money is put.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks money as the object of the action of putting it in.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of putting in money with the action of pressing the button in sequence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the button as the object of the action of pressing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: と connects pressing the button with the result that naturally happens immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks coffee as what appears after the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: 出てきます describes the coffee appearing and coming toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.why: The two actions are connected in sequence by the て form. Then, pressing the button comes before と to show a condition that naturally produces a result. が marks coffee as the thing that appears.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If おすと is used instead of おしたら, the sentence focuses more on the condition “after pressing is finished” than on an automatic rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If おせば is used, the sentence only states a hypothetical condition and does not emphasize that the result always occurs through the mechanism.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use と for every “if” sentence, but と is usually suitable for natural results or results that happen automatically in a machine.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I did not have an umbrella, so I asked a friend to lend me one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう indicates the time when the situation occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the umbrella as the thing being carried.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 持っていなくて connects the state of not having an umbrella with asking a friend to lend one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who performs the action for the speaker in the Vてもらう pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: かしてもらいました describes the speaker receiving the action of lending from a friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.why: The state of not having an umbrella is stated first with ていなくて as the reason. The friend, marked by に, performs the action, while the speaker receives the benefit, so てもらいました is used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If かしてくれました is used, the focus is that the friend actively lent the umbrella to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If かしてあげました is used, the subject is the person who performs an action for someone else, so it does not fit the meaning that the speaker received help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に in Vてもらう for the receiver, but に indicates the person who performs the helpful action for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q6.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もらう／もらいます／もらいました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vi: When I graduated, Mr. Tanaka sent me a congratulatory message.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 卒業 with 時 to create a time phrase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that Mr. Tanaka is the person who performs the action of giving.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the message as the thing given or sent to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: くださいました is a respectful expression used when a superior gives or does something for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning to state the situation. The giver is then marked with は, the thing given with を, and くださる shows respect toward the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with くれました, the meaning of giving to me is still correct, but the respectful feeling toward the teacher is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If いただきました is used, the subject is the speaker receiving a gift or an action from a superior.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use もらいました for every case of “being given something,” but when the subject is a superior doing something for the speaker, くださいました should be used to show respect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q7.kobun.cn: N1 は (わたしに) N2 を くださる／くださいました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vi: I want to cook food from my country for Teacher Ishikawa.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person for whom the action is performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 国 with 料理 to create a noun phrase that modifies another noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the food being cooked.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 作る changes to the て form to connect with さしあげる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.5.vi: want to do something for someone
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: さしあげる shows that the speaker humbly performs an action for a superior; たい expresses desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.why: The receiver comes first, followed by the food and the action of cooking. Vて connects the cooking action with さしあげる, while たい adds the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is still doing something for another person, but the humble feeling toward a superior is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the meaning becomes wanting to receive an action done by someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use さしあげる with people of equal status; this pattern is suitable when the receiver is someone deserving respect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka likes anime, so he knows everything about anime.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of both clauses.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: With 好き, が marks the object of liking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 好きで connects the state of liking with the following clause, creating a cause or background-information relationship.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: のこと turns アニメ into the content that is known; は states that content as the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 何でも shows an unlimited range: he knows anything about anime.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: 知っています describes a state of knowing, not only a one-time action of learning something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.why: The clause 好きで states Tanaka’s characteristic and then connects it to the result of knowing a lot about anime. 何でも is placed before 知っています to emphasize the entire range of content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning becomes knowing something, without the idea of knowing everything.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, it usually goes with a negative sentence and means not knowing anything at all.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 何でも with 何も; 何でも usually goes with an affirmative sentence, while 何も usually goes with a negative sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t18-q9.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or a respectful title
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vi: Because smoking is harmful to my health, I plan to quit smoking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object affected by the adjective 悪い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a reason clause to the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of quitting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun つもり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: つもりです expresses the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with ので, followed by the object を and the intended action. The verb やめる in dictionary form connects directly to つもりです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means that the speaker intends not to do the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the ます form before つもりですが, but this pattern requires the dictionary form or the ない form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ つもりです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vi: Although the child has a test tomorrow, they do not study at all.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ N が ＋ あるのに ＋ Adverb ＋ N を ＋ Vません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents 子ども as the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: あした indicates when the test will take place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks 試験 as the subject of ある, that is, something that exists tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: のに connects the fact that there is a test with the unexpected result of not studying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ぜんぜん modifies the negative predicate 勉強しません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: しません is a negative predicate that describes an action contrary to what the listener would normally expect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.why: The clause about the test is stated first as background for the surprising result that follows. のに creates a contrast between the fact that the child should study and the fact that they actually do not study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: けど also connects two contrasting ideas, but its conversational tone is lighter and more neutral than のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: ても means that the result still occurs even under that condition; it does not necessarily show surprise or blame.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.tip: ぜんぜん usually goes with a negative predicate, so it is not used with 勉強します in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vi: I ate with a friend while talking about the movie I watched yesterday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.sk: N と ＋ N を ＋ Vます leave ます ＋ ながら ＋ Time ＋ Vた ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who performs the eating activity together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 食事 as the content of する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ながら follows the ます form of する to connect two simultaneous actions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: きのう indicates when the action 見た took place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 見た modifies えいが, identifying it as the movie watched yesterday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: の connects えいが with 話, showing that the conversation was about the movie.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks 話 as the content of 話をする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: しました is the polite past predicate form of する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.cn: Vます leave ます ＋ ながら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.why: ながら connects two actions with the same subject: eating is the background action, and talking is the main action. The phrase きのう見た comes before えいが to modify the movie, and えいがの話をしました states the content of the conversation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is used instead, the sentence means that the speaker talked only after finishing the meal, so the actions are no longer simultaneous.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: あいだに emphasizes that one action occurs during the time of another action; the subjects do not have to be the same.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q11.kobun.tip: ながら attaches to the ます form of the verb, so します changes to しながら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vi: I will graduate from university next year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 来年 indicates the expected time of graduation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the place or organization that the subject leaves upon graduation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: そつぎょうします is the main predicate and describes the expected graduation in the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q12.kobun.why: 来年 places the time reference at the beginning of the sentence. With 卒業する, を does not mark an ordinary object; it marks the university that the speaker leaves after completing their studies.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: で usually indicates the place where an action occurs, so it is not suitable for expressing the university that one graduates from.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: 出る also uses を for a place one leaves, but it only means leaving and does not mean completing one's studies.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q12.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate を as an object; with 卒業する, を marks the place or organization that is left.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vi: It is okay not to come to the company tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the time reference being mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.2.vi: even if one does not come
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 来る changes to 来なくても to connect the negative form with a pattern that permits not doing something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: かまいません completes the pattern meaning that it is acceptable not to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.cn: Vない形（leave ない）＋くてもかまいません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.why: Tomorrow is a time reference, so は is used. The destination is connected to 来る with へ, while 来なくてもかまいません expresses permission not to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to “must come to the company.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning is almost the same, but this expression is more common and informal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q14.kobun.tip: Do not connect なくても with the plain verb form; before てもかまいません, the negative form ない must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q15.kobun.vi: You are very busy, aren't you? Shall I help with something?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: ですね ends a light comment and seeks agreement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 何か is an interrogative word combined with か to refer to an unspecified object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょうか is used at the end of a sentence to offer help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q15.kobun.why: The first sentence comments on the listener's condition, and the second sentence makes an offer. 何か comes before the verb and refers to an unspecified object of the help, while ましょうか expresses the wish to provide support.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何を is used, the speaker asks about or refers to something more specific: what to help with.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 何でも is used, it means helping with anything, emphasizing that there are no limits.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q15.kobun.tip: 何か means something, unlike 何を, which means what or which thing and refers to a more specific object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vi: It took me three days to write the report.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.sk: N を ＋ V辞書形＋のに ＋ Time ＋ かかる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks レポート as the thing that was written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 書くのに turns the action of writing into a noun, and に indicates an action that takes time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 三日 indicates the time needed for the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: かかりました is the predicate showing that time was spent; よ emphasizes the information being conveyed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.why: レポート is the object of 書く. The action 書く is changed into a noun using の, then に connects it with a period of time to say how long it takes; かかる is a verb showing the time or cost involved.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書くために is used, the focus is the purpose of writing, so it is less natural than のに when talking about the time needed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書くのは is used, this part becomes a topic or an object being commented on, and no longer directly indicates an action that takes time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.tip: Do not translate のに here as “although”; in the structure with かかる, it means “in order to do something.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q16.kobun.cn: V辞書形＋のに＋時間・お金・労力＋がかかる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.vi: Tanaka probably did not go to the party yesterday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Tanaka as the person whose action is being guessed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects きのう with パーティー to modify “party.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the event toward which the act of going is directed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 行く changes into 行かなかった to express not going in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: だろう follows the plain form to show the speaker's guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.why: The phrase きのうのパーティー forms a noun phrase meaning “yesterday's party,” then に connects the event with 行く. 行かなかった shows that the event did not happen, while だろう adds the meaning of guessing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with かもしれない, the level of certainty is lower and it only means “it may be.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If でしょう is used, the tone is more polite than だろう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.tip: だろう must follow the plain form, so 行きませんでしただろう is not used in this structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N＋だろう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vi: When I was a child, my mother always said to me, “Study.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: 子どものとき indicates the time or period when the event occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the main speaker in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: いつも modifies いいました and shows repeated frequency.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who receives the words or order.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the exact words spoken by the mother; なさい attaches to the verb stem after removing ます to give a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: いいました is the past-tense predicate, reporting speech that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます＋なさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning to set the background. The speaker and listener are marked by は and に, respectively; the spoken content is inside quotation marks and is connected to 言う by と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with べんきょうしてください, the request is more polite and can be used widely with people of equal status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If べんきょうしろ is used, the command is stronger and ruder than なさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q18.kobun.tip: なさい connects to the verb stem after removing ます, so use べんきょうしなさい instead of べんきょうするなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.vi: If you do something like that, everyone will laugh at you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vたら ＋ N に ＋ passive V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the action being performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb する changes to the past form した and then connects to ら to create a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive sentence, に identifies the person who performs the action affecting the subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: わらわれます is the polite passive form, expressing that someone else laughs at the person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.why: The conditional phrase comes first, followed by the result affecting the subject. Because the result is being laughed at by others, the performer is marked by に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with と, the sentence has a stronger sense of an inevitable or automatic result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with なら, the sentence is based on information or an assumption mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that the passive uses に to identify the person who causes the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vi: From now on, our lives seem likely to become more convenient.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the starting point of a change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: わたしたちの modifies the noun 生活.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は identifies life as the topic being predicted.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: もっと modifies the degree of convenience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 便利な changes to 便利に to indicate the state achieved after the change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: なりそうだ predicts a change that seems likely to happen soon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.cn: Vます語幹・Aい remove い・Aな remove な ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.why: 生活は is the topic, while 便利に indicates the state into which life will change. なり connects with そうだ to make a prediction based on the current situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ようだ is used, the meaning is a guess based on signs or received information, without emphasizing that it seems likely to happen soon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q2.kobun.tip: With Aな, learners may easily keep な before そうだ, but they must remove な and use 便利そうだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.vi: My younger sister always wants my things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 副詞 ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Aい remove い ＋ がる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the younger sister as the person showing desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the action and shows frequent repetition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects the owner with the noun もの.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the thing that the younger sister wants.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ほしがる expresses another person's desire through their outward behavior and is conjugated in the polite form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ がる; ほしい → ほしがる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.why: The topic is the younger sister, while the desired thing is marked by を. Because the speaker describes another person's desire, ほしがる is used instead of ほしい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほしい is used, the sentence usually expresses the speaker's own desire or a desire being asked about directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～たい is used, the focus is on wanting to perform an action, not on wanting to possess an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ほしい directly for another person, but they should use ほしがる when observing that person's desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.vi: Yesterday, my friend made me drink alcohol that I dislike, so I have a headache today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N に ＋ Aな な ＋ N を ＋ causative-passive Vて ＋ Time は ＋ N が ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: A time phrase placed at the beginning of the sentence to show when the event happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: In the causative-passive form, に indicates the person who forces the subject to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 嫌いな comes before and modifies the noun お酒.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the drink that the person is forced to drink.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 飲まされる is the causative-passive form of 飲む, while て connects yesterday's event with today's result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle は states that today is the time reference for the condition being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle が marks the body part that is in a painful condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.7.n: 痛い is the adjective い used as the predicate to describe a headache.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.cn: Vる: group 1 changes to the あ sound + される; group 2 drops る + させられる; する → させられる; 来る → こさせられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.why: The forced drinking happened first, so it appears in the first clause and connects with て to today's headache. The person who forced the action takes に, while the alcohol is the object of drinking and therefore takes を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～させる is used, it means making or allowing someone else to do something. It does not stress that the subject was forced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～てもらう is used, the sentence means having someone do something as a favor or receiving help, not being forced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に for the object in the causative-passive form, but here に indicates the person who forced the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.vi: I am planning to give flowers to my mother on her birthday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.sk: N は + N の + Time に + N を + volitional V と + 思っている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は indicates the person who intends to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects mother with the noun 誕生日, creating the meaning "mother's birthday."
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the time when the flowers are planned to be given.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the thing being given.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: あげよう is the volitional form, and と quotes the content of the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: 思って connects the verb 思う with います to express an intention that is still being maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: 思っています expresses an intention formed earlier that is still being kept.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.cn: volitional V + と + 思っている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.why: The object and time of giving the flowers are stated before the content of the intention. The volitional form combines with と 思っています to turn giving the flowers into a plan that is still being kept in mind.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～つもりだ is used, the sentence states the intention more clearly and directly, while ～と思っています focuses on the current thought or plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～予定だ is used, the sentence focuses more on a schedule or an arranged plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate と as "and," but in this pattern と marks the content of the thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.vi: I ended up drinking as many as five bottles of beer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.sk: N を + Quantity も + Vて + しまいました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the drink being consumed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: も comes after the quantity to stress that the amount is greater than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 飲んで is the て form of 飲む, connecting the action of drinking with しまいました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてしまいました describes an action that has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.why: The quantity is placed immediately before the verb and も is added to stress the large amount. Vてしまいました is placed at the end of the sentence to close the completed action and express regret.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～だけ is used, the sentence only limits the quantity to five bottles and does not stress that this is a large amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ておく is used, the sentence means doing something in advance or keeping a state for a later purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand も as only meaning "also," but after a quantity it often means "as many as" or "as much as."
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.vi: This is the house where Mr. Tanaka lives.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は indicates the place being introduced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the clause that modifies 家.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 住んでいる comes before 家 to modify it and identify which house it is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 家です is the main predicate, confirming that this place is the house described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.why: The clause has 田中さんが before the noun 家, so the whole clause identifies the house. ている describes the ongoing state of living and connects directly to the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vる, the sentence can describe a regular action or an intention, without stressing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with Vた, the meaning changes to the house where Tanaka lived or used to live.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places this clause before the noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q25.kobun.vi: There is a handkerchief lying here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the handkerchief exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks an object that appears or exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes the present state resulting from an event that has happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q25.kobun.why: The place is stated first with に. Then the object is introduced with が, and its present state is described with Vています. This structure focuses on where the handkerchief is now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is used instead, the sentence only says that the handkerchief exists here, without stressing that it has fallen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: で usually indicates the place where an action occurs, so it is not suitable for saying where an object exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で for every meaning of "at," but the existence or location of an object usually takes に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vi: When I got home, I found that a letter from my mother in the countryside had arrived.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action 帰る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the conditional action with the event that happens immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: くにの modifies はは and shows that the mother is in the countryside.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle から indicates the source or sender of the letter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks an object that appears or arrives at a place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects 来る with いる to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: いた is the past form of いる and shows that the state already existed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.why: 帰ると sets the time condition, and then the result that was noticed is described. から indicates the source of the letter, while 来ていた expresses that the letter had arrived and was there at that time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used instead, it means "after getting home..." and has less of the rule-like or immediate-discovery feeling of と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate と as "and," but in this sentence と connects the time condition "just as... then...."
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vi: Today is Monday, so that library is probably closed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes today the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the reason to the statement in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: あの modifies the noun 図書館.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は marks the library as the subject of the judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The noun やすみ connects with の to modify はず.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: はずだ shows a well-supported guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.why: The reason 月曜日だから comes before the conclusion about the library. With the noun やすみ, use の before はずだ to connect the two nouns.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with でしょう, it is only a softer guess and does not stress the logical basis as はずだ does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out の after a noun, but they must say やすみのはずだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ はずだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vi: The air in the room is bad, so may I open the window?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: へやの modifies くうき and means the air in the room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject that has a bad condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause to the request for permission in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object being opened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 開けても creates the condition in the permission pattern てもいいですか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: てもいいですか is used to ask permission to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.why: The cause is stated first with ので, followed by the action for which permission is requested. 窓を is the object of 開ける, and the ても form combines with いいですか to ask for permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it still asks for permission, but sounds more formal and stiff.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the て form, but they must say 窓を開けてもいいですか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vi: Excuse me, could you help me for a moment?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.sk: Opening phrase ＋ 副詞 ＋ Vて ＋ いただけませんか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: すみません is a polite opening before asking for a favor.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと softens the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action 手伝う with the request pattern いただけませんか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: いただけませんか is a very polite way to ask someone to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.why: すみません and ちょっと soften the request, while the て verb form connects directly to いただけませんか. This expression puts the listener in the position of kindly helping the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, it is still a request but is less formal and more familiar.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand いただけませんか as simple negation, but the whole phrase is a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q6.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いただけませんか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vi: At the swimming pool, you must take a shower before swimming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: では sets the location as the context for the rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time before which the following action must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb あびる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.3.vi: if I do not take a shower
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: あびる changes to the あびなければ form to connect with なりません and create a meaning of obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: なりません completes the double-negative pattern なければなりません, meaning must.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.cn: Vない remove い ＋ ければならない／なければならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.why: The location is stated first with では, followed by the time point およぐ前に. The required action is placed before なりません in the あびなければ form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the sentence means that taking a shower is not necessary.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that something is forbidden, not only that it is required.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake なければなりません for negation, but the whole pattern means must do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q7.tokens.9.m: must; required in the pattern ～なければなりません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vi: You cannot take photos in this concert hall.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies コンサート会場 and identifies the specific location.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: では sets the location as the area where taking photos is not possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the action とる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns とる into a noun, while が marks taking photos as the thing whose possibility is being considered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: できません is a negative predicate that completes the meaning that the action cannot be performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.why: The location comes first with では to limit the rule. The action とる is nominalized with こと and then made the subject with が of the possibility pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence directly says that taking photos is forbidden.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern uses the verb's potential form and focuses more on the person being unable to take photos than on the rule at the location.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use を before ことができません; a nominalized action must go with が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことができる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vi: I am saving money to buy a new house.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 新しい directly modifies うち.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the house as the object intended for purchase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 買うために states the purpose of saving money.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks せつやく as the content of the action する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: して is the て form of する, connecting the saving action with います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: ています describes an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.why: The goal of buying a house is placed first with 買うために, followed by the main action of saving money. 買う uses the dictionary form because it comes before ために to show an intentional purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ように, the sentence may suggest doing something to achieve a goal or ability, rather than directly stating the purpose of buying a house.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: ので would show a cause, making the sentence mean saving money for some reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.tip: For a purpose that the subject actively carries out, use Vるために; do not change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ために／Nの ＋ ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vi: I plan to have my daughter study abroad.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates that I am the person with the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person affected by the causative action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates where the studying takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: させる changes 勉強する into the causative form, meaning to let or make the daughter study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: つもりです turns the preceding action into the content of the plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: The person who plans to do the action is marked by は, while the daughter is the person being made to study, so she goes with を. The place uses で, and then the causative form combines with つもりです to express the plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it means that I plan to study by myself or that the studying will take place, without emphasizing having my daughter study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence expresses a wish for the daughter to study, not necessarily the speaker's plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse the person who performs the action with the person who is made to do it; in this pattern, the person who is allowed or forced to act usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q1.kobun.cn: V使役形＋つもりです; Nを＋V使役形
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vi: When I was young, my parents made me study English.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with ころ to form a phrase meaning when I was young.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ころ indicates the past time when the event happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive causative sentence, に indicates the person who forced or made the subject do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: させられました combines the causative and passive forms to express that the subject was forced by someone else to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to set the context. 両親に is the person who caused the force, 英語を is the content of the study, and 勉強させられました forms the predicate showing that the speaker was affected by it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～させる is used, it means that the parents made or allowed someone to study, without emphasizing the learner's feeling of being forced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～てもらう is used, it means that someone helped or arranged for the person to study, not that the person was forced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse the subject before に; in a passive causative sentence, the person being forced is the implied subject, while the person doing the forcing goes with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q10.kobun.cn: V使役形（Vさせる）＋られる（五段動詞では Vない形＋せられる／される）
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vi: Ali will probably come to school by train.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents Ali as the topic being predicted.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of the action 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before はずだ to make a well-supported prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.why: は introduces the person being predicted, で states the means of transportation, and へ states the destination. はずだ comes at the end because everything before it is the basis for predicting that Ali will come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～べきだ is used, it means that Ali should or must come to school, expressing advice or obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～予定だ is used, it only states a schedule or fixed plan, not necessarily the speaker's prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.tip: English learners may translate はずだ as absolute certainty; this pattern usually expresses a well-supported prediction that could still be wrong.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の＋はずだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.vi: I decided to learn guitar starting this month.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being learned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before こと to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ことに combines with する to form a pattern expressing a decision to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する, completing the pattern ことにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.why: 今月から sets the starting point, followed by the object ギターを and the action 習う. 習うことにしました turns the action of learning into the content of the decision and uses the past form to say that the decision has been made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning shifts to something being decided or becoming a decision because of circumstances or another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means making an effort to build a habit or actively continue learning guitar.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.tip: English learners may forget that the verb before こと must be in the dictionary form, not directly in the ます form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ ことにする
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.vi: My daughter wanted to go to the United States during New Year's, but she could not go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Time に ＋ N へ ＋ Vます-stem ＋ たがっていた ＋ けれど、negative past potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person showing the desire to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the planned time of departure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きたがっていた expresses a desire shown by a third person, while けれど connects to the contrasting idea.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 行けませんでした is the negative past potential form and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 ＋ たがる; main clause ＋ けれど(も)
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.why: The person who has the desire is the daughter, so むすめが and the expression たがる are used. The destination goes with へ, while けれど connects the desire in the first clause with the result that she could not go in the second clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it directly states the desire of the speaker or the person being addressed, without emphasizing a third person's outward expression of desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the pattern is for wanting to have an object or something, not for wanting to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q13.kobun.tip: English learners may use たい for a third person, while this sentence needs たがる to say that the person appears to want to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vi: Everyone here is a group of students who gathered to study literature.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the group of students exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: いるの turns the clause into a noun, while は states that clause as the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ために indicates the purpose of gathering.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The past clause comes before 学生たち to modify the group of students.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: です identifies the people mentioned in the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.why: The clause ここにいる is nominalized with のは to ask or identify who the people here are. 研究するために states the purpose, while 集まった comes before 学生たち to modify the group of students.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is replaced with ように, the purpose is usually more related to ability, a state, or a result to be achieved than to an intentional action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is replaced with ので, the preceding part becomes a cause and no longer means the purpose of studying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.tip: English learners may translate ために as “because,” but in this sentence it only means “in order to study.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q14.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.vi: Mr. Morikawa took time off work because he was ill.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N で ＋ N を ＋ past Vます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the reason for taking time off.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を is used with 休む to indicate the place or organization from which someone takes time off.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みました is the main predicate, in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.why: は makes Morikawa the topic, 病気で gives the reason, and 会社を休む is the natural combination for saying that someone is absent from school or work at an organization. The predicate 休みました comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with に is unnatural for the meaning of taking time off work; a place or organization used with 休む usually takes を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If だから is used, the reason is expressed as a clearer clause with a more direct explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に with 休む because of the influence of Vietnamese, but to say that someone is absent from school or work, use を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.vi: My mother wakes me up at 6 o’clock every day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Frequency ＋ N に ＋ Time に ＋ passive V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person affected by the passive action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎日 modifies an action that happens regularly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the time when I am woken up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 起こされます is the polite passive form of 起こす, expressing that I receive the action from my mother.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: change the う sound to the あ sound ＋ れる; Group 2: remove る ＋ られる; する → される; 来る → こられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.why: The affected person is marked by は, the person who causes the action uses に, and the time uses に. The passive form comes at the end to show that I am the person being woken up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that my mother helps wake me up, giving a sense of receiving help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, my mother becomes the subject, and the sentence only describes her waking me up, without making me the affected person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に, which marks the person causing the action, with に, which indicates time; in this sentence, there are two に with different roles.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q16.tokens.8.m: be done to, be made to
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.vi: I will buy toys and sweets for the children, then go home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person receiving the item or the person the item is bought for.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: や connects nouns to list some examples, while を marks the things being bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 買って is the て form, connecting the earlier action of buying with the later action of returning home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 帰ろう is the volitional form, expressing an intention or an invitation to go home together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.cn: N ＋ や ＋ N; Vて ＋ V; for Group 1 verbs, change the final sound to the お row ＋う, for Group 2 remove る＋よう, する→しよう, 来る→こよう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.why: 子どもに indicates who the items are bought for, while おもちゃやおかしを is a list of some objects serving as the object. The て form connects the sequence of buying first and then going home, and 帰ろう ends with an intention or invitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If や is replaced with と, the sentence lists all the toys and sweets, without the meaning of “such as” or “and so on”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If とか is used, the listing sounds more casual and emphasizes that these are only examples.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand や as an absolute “and,” but や usually lists only some items, and there may be others.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.vi: I do not know whether this answer is correct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun 答え, meaning “this answer.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 答え the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the clause 正しい into the point that must be judged as correct or incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: どうか combines with か to create the meaning “whether ... or not.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: わからない is the main predicate, expressing that the speaker does not know that content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.why: The phrase 正しいかどうか comes before わからない because it is the content that the speaker does not know. は gives the topic, while かどうか turns the whole clause into an indirect question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If only か is used, the sentence can directly ask “Is it correct?”, while かどうか emphasizes that both possibilities are unknown.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: Using this instead means “it may be correct,” so the speaker is guessing rather than saying that they do not know.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often translate and use かどうか as a direct question; in fact, this pattern usually appears inside a larger sentence such as わからない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ かどうか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.vi: I had my teacher eat the sandwich I made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Vた ＋ Nを ＋ Person に ＋ Vて ＋ いただきました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の indicates possession or a connection with the clause 作った.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The plain-form verb 作った comes before a noun to modify サンドイッチ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food as the object of eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who performs the helpful action or the person toward whom the action is directed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: めしあがって is the て form, connecting the action of eating with いただきました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: ていただきました expresses that the speaker received help and shows gratitude and humility.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.why: The clause わたしの作った modifies サンドイッチ, so it is placed directly before that noun. 先生に is the person who performs the action, while めしあがっていただきました shows that the speaker received that help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with ～てもらう still means “have someone do something for you,” but it is less polite and humble.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern makes the person performing the action the subject and emphasizes gratitude for the teacher eating the sandwich as a favor.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often confuse に with the receiver; in ～ていただく, に usually indicates the person who performs the action from which the speaker receives help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: The suitcase placed over there belongs to Billy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location of the suitcase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: てある describes the state of an object having been placed there by someone, and the whole phrase modifies スーツケース.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the suitcase the topic whose owner is being identified.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: の replaces an omitted noun and expresses possession before です.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: The phrase おいてある comes before スーツケース to describe which suitcase it is. に indicates the location, while のです confirms that the suitcase belongs to Billy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the person or thing currently placing the suitcase, rather than the state of the suitcase having already been placed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence would say that the suitcase is Billy, so the possession relationship would be incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for location, but the location or state of an object usually uses に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.vi: This is a photo taken just as the small bird was about to fly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the item being introduced the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing the action of flying in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: ちょうど modifies ところ and emphasizes the moment just before the action happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.3.vi: when it was about to fly
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: Vようとする expresses an intention or the time just before doing something, while ところ turns that moment into the object being photographed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: とった comes before 写真 to modify the photo.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends the sentence and identifies これは as the photo being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.why: The clause とぼうとしているところ modifies the moment when the photo was taken, and then を marks that whole moment as the object of とった. とった comes before 写真 to create the phrase “the photo taken ...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vているところ, it means that the photo was taken while the bird was flying or performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with Vたところ, the meaning changes to taking the photo just after the bird has flown.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often understand ところ as meaning only “place”; in this sentence, it refers to the time of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.tokens.4.m: exactly, just at the right time
