default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q20.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ とする; V辞書形 ＋ ところ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.vi: As for the department manager's address, Mr. Aota knows it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 部長 with 住所, creating the meaning “the department manager's address”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the address the topic and separates it from the person who knows the information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who knows the address.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 知っている describes a state of knowing and having that information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.why: 住所は is the topic stated first, while 青田さんが is the person who has the state of knowing that information. 知っている uses the ている form to describe the state of “knowing,” not an action in progress.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 住所が is used, the address becomes the subject or new information, without the topic-setting meaning of は.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If わかっている is used, the meaning is closer to “understand clearly,” while 知っている emphasizes having information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often translate 知っている as “be knowing”; in many cases, it describes the state of knowing, not an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.vi: Both my father and mother come home late every day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.sk: Nも ＋ Nも ＋ Time ＋ Vてくるのが ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: も marks the father as one of the subjects who share the stated characteristic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: も is repeated after 母 to create the structure “both father and mother”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 毎日 indicates the repeated time of coming home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the phrase 帰ってくる into a noun, and が marks returning as the thing described as late.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: おそいです is the predicate and comments that the time of coming home is late.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.why: も is repeated after two nouns to connect them with the meaning “both ... and ...”. The phrase 帰ってくるのが is the subject of おそい because the sentence evaluates the act of returning as late.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is replaced with は, the sentence presents only the father or the mother as the topic and no longer includes both people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing の with こと still nominalizes the verb, but the tone is more formal and general.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often omit も after the second noun; to say “both A and B,” use Aも Bも.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q22.kobun.cn: N ＋ も; V普通形 ＋ のが ＋ Aい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.vi: Mr. Akiyama said to me, “Keep going.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Nに ＋ 「Clause」 と ＋ Vた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the person who says the sentence the topic of the reported sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who receives the words.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the exact words being quoted.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 言った is the main predicate and indicates that the act of speaking happened in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.cn: Plain-form clause ＋ と ＋ 言う・思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.why: The speaker is marked by は, the listener goes with に, and the exact words are placed in quotation marks and end with と. 言った comes at the end of the sentence to show a past speaking action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ように言う is used, the sentence reports the content of a command or request indirectly rather than keeping the exact words.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～そうだ is used, the sentence usually means “I hear that” or “it seems,” not an exact quotation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use に instead of と before the spoken content; in a quotation structure, と is what marks the words being said.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.vi: Because the curtains are still closed, it seems that Kou is still sleeping.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the state being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the て form connects with いる to describe a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it is still that way
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the cause clause with the result clause that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: は states the topic being guessed about in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: まだ modifies the sleeping state and shows that it is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: ている describes a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: ようだ is placed at the end of the sentence to give a guess based on an observed sign.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.cn: Vて＋いる; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの＋ようだ; Cause clause ＋ から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.why: The clause with から comes first to state the basis, and then the main sentence uses ようだ to make a guess. まだ comes before ねている to emphasize that the sleeping state has not ended yet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with らしい, the sentence focuses more on information heard from someone or a general judgment than on a direct sign.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If そうだ is used, the sentence can more easily mean that something appears to be about to happen or appears to be happening from its outward appearance, which differs from the guess expressed by ようだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often understand ている as meaning only “be doing,” but with states such as しまっている or ねている, it can also indicate a state that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.vi: This is the grammar book that the teacher gave me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the item being presented.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who performs the giving action in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the receiver of the giving action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: くださった is the past form and comes before the noun to modify the book.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects the content with 本 and shows that this is a book about grammar.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends the sentence politely and identifies this as a book.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.why: The clause 先生がわたしにくださった comes before 本 to modify 本. の connects ぶんぽう with 本, while です turns the whole noun phrase into a polite introduction sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If もらった is used, the subject is usually the receiver, and the viewpoint shifts to the receiver.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If いただいた is used, the receiver speaks humbly about receiving something from the teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.tip: 先生がわたしに should not be translated mechanically as “the teacher on my side”; in this sentence, the phrase is part of the clause modifying 本.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q25.kobun.cn: N1が＋N2に＋くださる／くださった; V普通形＋N; N1の＋N2
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: I still have not decided what to do on Sunday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the action will be performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content of the action する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns a question into indirect-question content serving as the object of 決める.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ modifies the negative phrase that follows and indicates that something has not happened up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ていない expresses an unfinished state or the absence of a result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: The question 何をするか is placed before the sentence as the content of the decision. まだ combines with ていない to say that the decision has not been completed up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it makes the explanatory or emphatic tone of the question clearer and often feels more direct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, it means deciding whether to do it, not deciding what to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may easily place か at the end of the whole sentence; in an indirect question, か comes immediately after the question content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q3.kobun.cn: V疑問詞＋V普通形＋か; まだ＋Vていない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: It seems that as many as five people are still at the company.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates both the place of existence and makes that place the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies the state of continued existence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: も emphasizes that the number is greater than expected; this phrase is the subject of いる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects のこる with the existence verb いる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: いる describes people who still exist or remain at a place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: ようだ is placed at the end of a sentence to express an inference based on the situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: The place phrase comes first to state where the condition occurs. も emphasizes the number of five people, while のこっている describes the state of still remaining; ようだ turns the whole statement into an inference.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with そうだ, the sentence focuses more on heard information or direct signs, not only on a situational inference.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: らしい also expresses an inference or reported information, but its basis in an external source or evidence is clearer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget that いる is used for people and animals, while ある is used for things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ ようだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: The sky has become much brighter. Morning is coming soon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.sk: N が ＋ だいぶ ＋ Aい remove い＋く ＋ なって ＋ きた。もうすぐ ＋ N だ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject whose state changes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: だいぶ modifies the degree of becoming brighter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 明るい changes to 明るく to connect with なる and describe the change into a bright state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects なる with くる in a structure showing a change progressing toward the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: てくる shows that the change has gradually progressed toward the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: もうすぐ modifies the time 朝 and indicates that it is approaching soon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: だ ends a noun sentence and confirms that the approaching time is morning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.cn: Aい remove い＋く＋なる; Vて＋くる; N＋だ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The adjective 明るい changes to the state form 明るく to combine with なる. てくる emphasizes the gradual brightening up to the present, while the next sentence states the approaching time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the change is viewed from the present and continues toward the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that it became bright, without emphasizing the gradual process toward the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may easily connect 明るいなる directly; the adjective い must change to 明るく before なる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: My younger brother has been sleeping continuously since noon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N から ＋ 副詞 ＋ Vます形 remove ます＋つづける ＋ Vて＋いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the younger brother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the time when the action began.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ずっと modifies the prolonged state of sleeping.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The remove form ます of 眠る connects with つづける to express continuing to sleep; the form て connects with いる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ている describes a state that has continued from before until the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます＋つづける; Vて＋いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The phrase indicating the starting time comes before the continuing state. The verb without ます connects with つづける to emphasize that the action continues, and then connects with ている to show that the state is still maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If only ～ている is used, it only says that someone is sleeping and does not emphasize continuous sleep over a period of time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ～っぱなしだ, the meaning is to leave the state unchanged, often implying that it has not been dealt with or is undesirable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may translate つづける simply as continue and forget to put the preceding verb into the form without ます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vi: Because a foreigner asked me for directions, I showed them the way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.sk: N に ＋ N を ＋ past passive verb＋ので、Vて＋あげる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who performed the asking action in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞かれた is the past passive form, while ので connects this clause to the reason that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て of 教える connects with あげる to create a structure meaning to do something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: あげました shows that the speaker did something helpful for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.cn: Vて＋あげる; V普通形 past＋ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.why: The passive clause comes first to state the situation and reason. After ので comes the speaker's action, where Vて＋あげる shows that the action was done for another person's benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～てくれる is used, another person does something beneficial for the speaker or the speaker's side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～てもらう is used, the speaker emphasizes receiving help from another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may use あげる for every giving-and-receiving direction without considering who performs the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vi: The book that I will take to school tomorrow has already been put in the bag.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time related to the action of taking the book.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction of movement for the action 持っていく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb clause comes before 本 to modify the book that will be taken along.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The phrase 持っていく本 modifies 本, while は makes the book the main topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the place where the object is put.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て of 入れる connects with ある to express a prepared result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: ～てある describes an object that someone has already prepared, and that state still remains.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.why: The clause 持っていく comes directly before 本 because it describes the book. After stating the topic, に shows where the book is, while 入れてある shows that the preparation is complete and the result still remains.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～てある is replaced with ～ている, it only describes the state of the book being in the bag, without emphasizing that someone prepared it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ～ておく emphasizes an action done in advance for a future purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse ～てある with ～ている; ～てある usually focuses on a result prepared by a person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q8.kobun.cn: Vて＋いく; Vて＋ある; V普通形＋N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vi: When I passed in front of the embassy, I met Ben.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 大使館 with 前 to form the phrase “in front of the embassy.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the place or route that someone passes through.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The past form of 通る connects with ら to create the condition or time when the following event happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person whom the speaker meets.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 会った is the main predicate in the past form and describes an event that happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.why: 大使館の前 forms a specific place, and を goes with 通る to show the place passed through. The clause 通ったら comes first to state the time or condition, followed by the main event 会った.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～と is used, the result usually happens naturally or automatically whenever the condition occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～なら is used, it means “if that is really the case” or “if we are talking about that condition.” It is less natural than ～たら for describing an event that already happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t2-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit を before 通る, but を here marks a route or place that someone passes through, not an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vi: It is said that the lion drops its young from a high place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the lion the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 高い modifies the noun ところ that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: から shows the starting point of the action of dropping something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 自分 with 子ども to show possession.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object affected by 落とす.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the main verb in the reported content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: そうです follows the plain form to report information that the speaker heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.why: The topic is stated first, followed by the starting place, the object of the action, and the verb 落とす. そうです connects with the whole plain-form clause to show reported information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ようです is used, the meaning changes to “it seems,” based on a guess or sign.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: らしいです also means “it is said,” but it has a clearer nuance of guessing or indirect information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse そうです, which reports information, with そうです after omitting ます, which describes appearance or a prediction about what will happen soon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vi: Because the number of vehicles has increased, traffic accidents have also become more common.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Vたので ＋ N が ＋ Aい-omitい＋くなる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the thing whose amount has increased.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result in a soft explanatory way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that becomes more numerous.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 多くなりました describes a change from fewer to more.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.why: The first clause gives the cause using ので, and the second clause gives the result. The adjective 多い changes to 多く and then connects with なる to describe a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 多くする is used, it means that someone actively makes the amount become larger.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is replaced with から, the cause keeps the same meaning, but the tone becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep the ending い before なる, but they must omit い and add く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vi: If the weather is good tomorrow, I will climb the mountain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: あした shows the time of the condition and the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: なら changes the noun phrase いい天気 into a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the destination of the climbing action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.why: The condition いい天気なら comes before the comma, followed by the action planned if the condition is true. に marks the mountain as the destination of 登ります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, the sentence usually describes a more specific condition. It can mean that, after finding out that the weather is good, the speaker will climb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If と is used, the sentence can mean that whenever the condition occurs, the result will inevitably occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use なら directly after the adjective い and forget to keep the form いい unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない・Vた・Aい・Aな・N ＋ なら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.vi: Because it has started to rain, you should go home early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks a phenomenon that is happening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the verb 降る with 来る to express that the rain has started.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the cause clause with the advice that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb modifies the action 帰る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: Vたほうがいい is used to give advice that someone should do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: です makes the sentence polite, while よ emphasizes the advice to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first with から, followed by the recommended action. 早く modifies 帰る, while ほうがいい follows the past form of the verb to create advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with べきだ, the sentence has a stronger tone, close to “you really should go home.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 帰るほうがいい, but advice meaning “should do” usually uses the form た before ほうがいい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.vi: This skirt has a nice color and a nice design. In addition, the price is cheap.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to clearly identify the skirt being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the skirt the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: も marks an additional feature alongside the design.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: も connects the design and the color in parallel as the subjects of いい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: それに adds another advantage to the content just mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: も shows that the price is an additional advantage.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.why: は limits the topic to the skirt, while も is repeated to list several equal advantages. それに stands at the beginning of the next sentence to add another advantage about the price.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If そして is used, the sentence only continues the information in order, so the sense of adding an advantage is weaker than with それに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If また is used, it means “in addition,” and the listing sounds more neutral.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit も from the later features after using は, but も clearly expresses the meaning “also... also...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.vi: I try to keep the habit of eating many vegetables.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks vegetables as the object of the action of eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb of quantity that modifies 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ように changes the action 食べる into a goal that is maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: している describes an effort or habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.why: を marks the object of 食べる, while たくさん modifies the amount eaten. ようにしている connects the target action with する to express an effort to maintain a habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ようになる, the sentence describes a change that has become a habit, without emphasizing the conscious effort to maintain it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ようにしている with ようになる; the first pattern describes the subject's effort, while the second describes a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ようにしている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.vi: My older brother went abroad to study design.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the older brother as the subject who carries out the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects デザイン with 勉強, creating the phrase “studying design”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ために connects the purpose with the main action 行きました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction toward the mentioned place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: ました marks an action that happened in the past, using polite language.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.why: The purpose phrase comes before the main action, so the listener knows the reason for going. へ marks the direction toward a foreign country, while の connects the noun デザイン with 勉強.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ように, the purpose is usually connected with an ability or a state that needs to be achieved, so it is less natural than ために with an intentional action such as studying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget の in デザインの勉強; when one noun modifies another noun, の is usually needed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ために・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.vi: Although I am waiting for his phone call, no call has come yet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: からの modifies 電話 and indicates the source of the call.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the phone call as the object being waited for.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: のに connects the situation of waiting with the unexpected result that the call does not come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: かかってくる describes a call coming to the speaker, while ません gives a polite negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.why: The phrase 彼からの電話を is the object of 待っている. のに comes after the clause about waiting to create a contrast with the result that the call does not come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If ても is used, it means “even if I wait...,” so it focuses more on a concessive condition and shows less disappointment than のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If けど is used, the contrast is softer and more conversational, and the unexpected result is less emphasized than with のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate のに as “in order to,” but in this sentence it is a pattern showing contrast: “although... nevertheless...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Vている・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.vi: These shoes are too big, so they are difficult to walk in.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aいすぎて、＋ Vwithoutます ＋ にくいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before くつ to indicate the shoes being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the shoes the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: すぎる attaches to an adjective to show an excessive degree, while て connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: にくい attaches to the stem of a verb to express that an action is difficult to perform.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.cn: Vwithoutます ＋ にくい; Aいwithoutい・Aな ＋ すぎる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.why: 大きすぎて gives the cause related to size, and then て connects it to the result that walking is difficult. にくい comes after the verb stem あるき to change the action of walking into “difficult to perform.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If にくい is replaced with やすい, the sentence has the opposite meaning: the shoes are easy to walk in.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: すぎる indicates an excessive degree, while にくい indicates that an action is difficult to perform.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily attach にくい directly to the dictionary form, but the verb stem without ます must be used: あるき＋にくい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person affected, meaning the people who have to worry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks what is caused in the phrase 心配をかける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb かける is in the polite past form and describes having caused worry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.kobun.why: The people made to worry come first with に, while 心配を is what is caused and goes with を. かけました ends the sentence and shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence still means making someone worry, but it directly emphasizes causing that person to worry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after a person's name, but the affected person in 心配をかける must go with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.kobun.cn: N ＋ に ＋ 心配をかける
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.vi: Because my senior taught me many things, I became better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person who does the teaching in a structure for receiving help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: いろいろ modifies the content being taught, meaning many different things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 教えて uses the て form to connect the verb 教える with いただく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: いただいた expresses that the speaker humbly received teaching; ので connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に marks the state achieved after the change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: なる is in the polite past form and expresses an achieved result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.why: The first clause gives the helper, the content, and the action of receiving teaching, and then ので connects it to the result. 上手に comes before なりました because it describes a change into a better state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If いただいた is replaced with もらった, the meaning is still that the speaker was taught, but the level of humility is lower.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な before ので with the adjective な and nouns, but the correct forms are Aななので and Nなので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; Vて ＋ いただく
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vi: Because I was taught many things by my senior, I became skillful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 甘い modifies もの, forming the phrase “sweet food”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: もの is the object of 食べる, while ばかり emphasizes eating only this type.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the condition 食べる with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 太ります is the result; よ is used to tell the listener information or emphasize it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.why: The phrase 甘いものばかり is the object limited by ばかり. The clause 食べると comes first to state a condition that normally leads to a result, followed by the result 太ります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, it only states a specific condition. It does not emphasize a certain or usual result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: なら is based on information or an assumption that has already been given, so its meaning is different from the natural condition expressed by と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate と as “and,” but in this sentence と connects a condition with a result that usually occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の ＋ と
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.vi: I just traveled to Japan last month.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.sk: Time に ＋ N へ ＋ N に ＋ Vた ＋ ばかりです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to show when the trip happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle へ shows the destination of the trip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 旅行に combines with 行く to show going for the purpose of traveling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 行った is the past form before ばかり and describes an action that has just been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.why: The destination takes へ, while 旅行に attaches to 行く to state the content of the trip. ばかり follows the た form to emphasize that the action happened recently.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vたところです, it emphasizes more strongly that the action ended just now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vている, the sentence describes an ongoing or present state and no longer emphasizes that it just happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ばかり after the dictionary form, but this pattern must use Vたばかり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.vi: Because this tape recorder is light and convenient, I always use it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies テープレコーダー and points to one specific thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the tape recorder the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 軽い changes to 軽くて to connect the first feature with the next one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: べんり is an な adjective, so な is added before ので to state the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: いつも modifies the action of using and shows frequent repetition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: 使って combines with います to create a structure that describes using something continuously or regularly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: ています describes a state or habit that continues to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.why: The two features, light and convenient, are connected. Then ので connects the reason with the habit of using it. は marks the topic, while ています shows a continuing habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with だから, the reason is stated more directly and conversationally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 使っています is replaced with 使います, the sentence only describes a habit or plan and does not emphasize continuity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect the adjectives な and ので while leaving out な, but they must say べんりなので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.kobun.cn: Aいくて ＋ Aなな ＋ ので; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.vi: I went to see a movie yesterday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ N を ＋ Vwithoutます に ＋ 行きました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the time point the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the movie as the object of watching.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 見 is the ます-less form of 見る and combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main predicate and describes going for the purpose of watching a movie.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.cn: Vます-withoutます ＋ に ＋ 行く・来る・帰る
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.why: 映画を is the object of 見る, while 見に attaches to 行く to state the purpose. The purpose verb uses the form without ます, not the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ために, the purpose is emphasized more clearly and the expression is more formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If the whole phrase 見に行きました is replaced with 見ました, the sentence only means that the speaker watched a movie, without saying that they went there.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place を after 見に, but に marks purpose here, so they must say 見に行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.vi: Last summer was not as hot as this summer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: 去年の modifies なつ and identifies it as last year's summer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes last summer the object being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ほど shows the degree used as the standard for comparison with this year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 暑い changes to 暑く to connect with the negative form of ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: なかったです creates the polite past negative form of the adjective 暑い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.why: Last summer is the topic, while this yearほど is the comparison standard. The negative form follows ほど and means that it does not reach the same degree as the item being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with より, the sentence directly states which object is hotter instead of emphasizing that last year was not as hot as this year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 同じくらい, the meaning changes to equally hot, which is opposite to the negative meaning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate ほど mechanically as “as,” forgetting that with a negative form, this pattern means “not as ... as.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.kobun.cn: N ＋ ほど ＋ Aいくない; N ＋ ほど ＋ Aなではない; N ＋ ほど ＋ Vない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.vi: I got up early to catch the 5 o'clock train.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the time phrase with the noun 電車, forming the meaning “the train at 5 o'clock.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object that must be caught in the pattern 間に合う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ように connects the goal clause with the main action 起きました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 早く is the adverbial form of the adjective 早い and modifies 起きました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 起きる changes to the polite past form to serve as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.why: The phrase 5時の電車 identifies the train that must be caught, while まにあうように states the goal of getting up early. The verb in the preceding clause ように uses the plain form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ために, the sentence emphasizes a more intentional purpose and usually goes with an action that the speaker can choose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: ような must come before a noun to modify it, so it cannot end a goal clause like ように.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ために mechanically; when the goal is a desired state or result, ように is more natural.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Vない形 + ように
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.vi: This hot pot dish uses both fish and meat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the dish being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: も replaces を and marks fish as an ingredient that is also used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: も continues to attach the same feature, “being used,” to meat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 使います is the predicate and takes the two objects listed with も.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.why: は sets the dish as the topic, while も is repeated to show that fish and meat both serve as ingredients. The same predicate applies to both nouns.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with やなど would mean listing a few examples, without emphasizing both objects completely.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means “not only N but also N” and emphasizes the additional second object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may place も only on the last noun, but the “both...and...” pattern requires も to be attached to each noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vi: After you finish reading that book, could you lend it to me?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.sk: N + Vます-remove ます + 終わる + たら + Vて + くれませんか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies 本 and identifies the book known to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 本 is the object mentioned first; the comma shows that the following part continues to refer to it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: よみおわる means finishing reading, and たら connects the condition to the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: かして is the て form and connects the verb “lend” with くれませんか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: くれませんか creates a polite request, asking whether the listener can do something to help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます + 終わる; Vた形 + ら; Vて + くれませんか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.why: よみおわったら sets the time condition first, while かしてくれませんか is the main request. The form Vます-remove ます + 終わる expresses completing the reading action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 読み終わると would make the sentence sound more like a rule or a natural result, so it is less natural for making a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: 読んだら only means “after reading” and does not emphasize that the reading is finished as 読み終わったら does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form directly before 終わる; remove ます from the verb before connecting it with 終わる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.vi: Because this machine sometimes breaks down, it is very troublesome.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies きかい and identifies the machine being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the machine the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ときどき modifies the event of breaking down and shows how often it happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause 壊れる is nominalized with こと and serves as the subject with が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: あるから connects the reason before it with the conclusion 困る after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 困る is the main predicate and states the speaker’s result or feeling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.why: 壊れることがある turns the machine breaking down into an event that sometimes happens. The reason clause comes before から, while 困る is the conclusion explained by that reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using こともある means “it also sometimes happens,” emphasizing that this is one possibility among other cases.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ので presents the reason more gently and objectively than から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.tip: Do not understand ことがある here as “have experienced.” With V辞書形, it means that the event sometimes happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことがある; 普通形 + から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.vi: I bought fruit juice, sandwiches, and some other things for the party.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects パーティー with ために to identify the purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ために indicates the purpose of the buying action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: や lists one example among the things bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: など adds the meaning “and so on,” while を marks the whole group of things as the object of 買いました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 買いました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.why: ために places the purpose before the buying action. や lists examples, while など shows that there are other items on the list; を covers the whole group as the object of 買いました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ように usually describes a goal or a state to be achieved, rather than the direct purpose of buying things in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: と is used between nouns to fully connect “A and B,” while や only gives examples and usually goes with など.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may always translate や as “and,” but や only lists a few examples, not a complete list.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.kobun.cn: Nの・V辞書形 + ために; NやNなど
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the thing being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the original material used to make the object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 作られます is the polite passive form, meaning “is made.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.kobun.why: The sentence makes the produced object the topic, then states the material with から. The verb uses the passive form to express the meaning “is made.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with で作られる, the focus would shift toward the material or means used to make the product.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse から with で, but から emphasizes the original material.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose desire is being observed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person involved in the marriage relationship.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: たがって is the connecting form of たがる and expresses a desire observed in another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ています expresses an ongoing state of desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.why: The person with the desire is stated at the beginning with は, while the marriage partner goes with と. たがっている is used because the speaker is commenting on another person’s desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If たい is used, the sentence directly expresses the speaker’s own desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If たがる is used, the sentence only states an outward sign of wanting to do something and does not emphasize an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may use たい for other people, although another person’s desire usually uses たがっている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + たがっている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vi: Mr. Kobayashi was laughing when he suddenly became angry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: まで indicates a time period continuing up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 笑っていた modifies 小林さん.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who performs the action of becoming angry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: とつぜん modifies the action that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: だした means starting an action or state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.why: The clause 笑っていた comes before the noun to describe Kobayashi's earlier state. After that state, とつぜん and 出す together emphasize that the anger started suddenly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 始める, the sentence only says that the action starts in a neutral way, without stressing its suddenness.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 続ける, the meaning changes to continuing an action that is already in progress.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand 出す as meaning only “to take out,” but after a verb stem it also means “to start suddenly.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vi: After graduating from high school, I plan not to go to university.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who has the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action of graduating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 後 connects graduating with what happens afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: には makes university the topic being considered and adds a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 行かない modifies つもり and shows that the intended action is not going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: つもりです ends the sentence by expressing the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.why: 後 comes after the action of graduating to identify the time. The sentence then presents university as the topic with には. 行かない comes before つもり to show the content of the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予定だ is used, the sentence focuses more on a planned schedule than on personal intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If と思う is used, the sentence only expresses a thought or prediction, which is weaker than a clear intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that the verb must come before つもり, not after つもり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ つもりだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vi: I take English conversation lessons twice a week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time period に ＋ Number of times ＋ Nを ＋ Vている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who does the learning activity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に connects a time period with a number of times and shows repeated frequency.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks what is being learned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects 習う with いる to create a continuing-action or maintained-state pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: いる completes the Vている pattern and shows that the learning activity continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.cn: Time period ＋ に ＋ Number of times; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.why: The phrase １週間に２回 shows frequency and comes before the object and action. Vている shows that learning is an ongoing activity, not something that happens only once.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If １週間ごとに is used, it means “every one week” and does not directly state the number of times like ２回.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 間に emphasizes an event that happens within a period, not regular frequency.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place に after the number of times. The correct structure is time period に number of times.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vi: I arrange the books neatly on the shelf so they are easy to find.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the books being arranged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: さがしやすい modifies ように and describes the favorable condition that should be achieved.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ように connects the purpose with the arranging action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the place where the books are put or arranged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: きちんと modifies ならべる and shows how the arranging is done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.why: The phrase さがしやすいように states the purpose of the action ならべる. に indicates the place of arranging, while きちんと describes how the action is performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is used, the purpose is stated directly and is usually connected with a subject who has a clearer intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If ような is used, the following part must be a modified noun, so the structure before the verb ならべる cannot remain unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.tip: Do not translate ように as an independent goal. Connect it with the main action that follows to understand it as “so that.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形・Aい ＋ ように; Vます-stem ＋ やすい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vi: My husband works late every night.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は ＋ time ＋ N まで ＋ N を ＋ V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with 主人 to create the noun phrase “my household's husband.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 主人 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The time phrase comes before the predicate to show when the repeated action happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: まで marks the endpoint of the time period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks work as the object of する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.why: The time phrase まいばん shows frequency, while おそくまで indicates the ending limit of working. 仕事をする is a verb phrase in which 仕事を is the object of する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with までに, the meaning is to finish the work by or before a deadline, not to continue working until that time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use までに when they want to express an action continuing until a time point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.vi: Recently, it has become uncommon to see birds flying in the sky.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.sk: N が ＋ N を ＋ Vのが ＋ time ＋ あまり ＋ Vなくなる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the action 飛ぶ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を refers here to the space that the object flies through, not to an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 飛ぶの turns the action of birds flying into a noun phrase; が marks it as what is seen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The time phrase adds a time range for the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: あまり is used with a negative form to express a low degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: 見られない changes into the form なく and then connects with なった, expressing a change into a state in which something is no longer easy to see.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.why: そらを飛ぶ describes the path or space that the bird flies through. The whole 飛ぶのが becomes the subject of 見られなくなった, meaning that seeing birds flying has become less common.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the focus is on the place where the flying happens, without stressing the space being flown through.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may assume that を only marks an object, so they may avoid using を with motion verbs such as 飛ぶ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.tokens.11.m: be able to; be affected by
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.vi: He has returned to his country but still has not gone back to the company.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks かれ as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of returning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 帰った in the た form connects to まま to keep the state after returning unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ modifies the negative predicate 戻っていない, emphasizing that it has not happened up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the place the person has not returned to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: 戻って is the て form that connects the verb to いない to create a negative progressive form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: いない negates the state of being at the company now or having been there.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.why: 帰ったまま sets the state of "having returned to his country" as the background, and then the main clause says that the state of not returning to the company is still continuing. 会社に indicates the destination of the action 戻る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 帰ったあとで, the sentence only talks about an action after returning to the country and does not emphasize that the state remains unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand まま as simply "still," but it is always connected to a state that continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.vi: Around what time will your husband return?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ time ごろ ＋ お ＋ Vます-stem ＋ になります ＋ か
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being asked about as the topic; ご主人 is a polite way to refer to someone else's husband.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ごろ is attached after a time to show an approximate time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: お comes before the verb stem 帰り and connects to になります to honor the action of the person being mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: か changes a statement into a polite question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.why: 何時ごろ comes before the predicate to ask about an approximate time. お帰りになります is an honorific predicate used to show respect for the person being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If お帰りですか is used, the sentence is still polite but uses a nominalized expression and does not emphasize the action of returning as お帰りになりますか does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place になります after the entire dictionary-form verb; the verb stem without ます must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q14.kobun.cn: お ＋ Vます-stem ＋ になる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.vi: If you want to sing better, you should study with Teacher Tanaka, the music teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object or ability being evaluated as 上手.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: に changes 上手 into the target state after なりたければ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: なりたい changes to the conditional form ければ to state the condition for the advice that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 音楽教師 with 先生 and shows Teacher Tanaka's profession or role.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the person the speaker recommends studying with.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: ならえば is the conditional form of 習う and directly creates the condition for いい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: いい combines with the conditional form to give suitable advice or an option.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.7.n: よ emphasizes information or advice for the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.why: なりたければ states the goal and condition, while ならえばいい gives a suitable way to achieve it. に marks the teacher whom the speaker recommends studying with.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vたほうがいい, the advice becomes more direct and stronger, with the meaning "you had better do it."
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vるといい is used, the advice is softer and closer to the meaning "it would be good to do it."
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ばいい as "if good," but in this pattern it means "should do it" or "it is fine to do it."
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.vi: If it is Sunday, you can come at any time because I will be at home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: なら takes the noun 日曜日 to state a condition or hypothetical topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: いつでも indicates any unlimited time and modifies the invitation to come to the house.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the speaker exists with the verb いる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: います expresses the speaker's existence at 家.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: から connects the reason います with the request 来てください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: 来て is the て form used to connect with ください in a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: ください creates a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.why: なら limits the condition to Sunday, and then いつでも expands the possible time of arrival. から puts the reason before the invitation, while 来てください is a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with いつか, the meaning becomes "sometime" and no longer means that any time is acceptable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If いつも is used, it means "always" and usually modifies a habit or state, not an optional time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse いつでも with いつも; いつでも refers to any acceptable time, while いつも means always.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q17.kobun.vi: I became very tired from walking continuously for as much as 30 kilometers.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q17.kobun.sk: Quantity ＋ も ＋ Vて ＋ 副詞 ＋ Vた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: も is attached after a quantity to emphasize that it is a large amount beyond expectation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the continuing action with the tired result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main predicate, stating the result of walking a long distance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q17.kobun.why: The quantity phrase comes before も to highlight the long distance. The clause 歩き続けて states the reason or situation leading to the result 疲れました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is replaced with まで, the sentence emphasizes reaching a more specific limit rather than exceeding expectations.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may leave out も because they think the quantity already gives enough meaning, but も creates the meaning "as much as" or "such a large amount."
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q18.kobun.vi: How about having some coffee and then going out?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: でも comes after a noun to suggest one option in a gentle way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: てから connects the action that must happen first with the action that happens later.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q18.kobun.why: コーヒーでも gives a suitable example of what to do first. 飲んでから sets a clear order: drink first, then go out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used instead of でも, the sentence only directly says to drink coffee. It no longer has the suggestion “how about/for example.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand でも here as “but,” while it actually means giving an example of a choice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.vi: The water here cannot be used for drinking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: ここの modifies 水 and identifies the source or location of the water.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 水 the topic evaluated in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before のに to create a phrase showing the purpose of use.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: のに turns the action 飲む into a noun, and に shows the purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: 使えません is the negative potential form, while よ emphasizes the information being told to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.why: 水は is the object whose use is being discussed. 飲むのに turns drinking into a purpose, and then 使えません denies the possibility of using the water for that purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with ために, the sentence becomes more formal and focuses more clearly on the purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used to mean “although,” the sentence needs a contrasting clause, so it does not fit this purpose structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may think のに only means “although,” but in this pattern it means “for/to do.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vi: I have been to Africa once.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Number of times ＋ Nへ ＋ Vたことが ＋ あります
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose experience is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 一度 adds the number of times the experience occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the direction of the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたこと turns “having gone” into a noun phrase, and が makes it the subject of あります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: あります completes the pattern for expressing that someone has had an experience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.why: The verb 行く changes to the past form 行った before こと to turn a completed action into an experience. あります shows that this experience existed in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vることがある, the sentence usually means doing something occasionally, not having done it before.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If ない is used, the sentence becomes negative: the person has never had that experience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use the present form before こと, but an experience that happened before must use Vた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.vi: Because tomorrow is a day off, he is probably free.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the topic of the clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is a day off
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the reason to the conclusion in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 彼 the object being guessed about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な needs な before はず because it modifies the noun はず.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: はずです expresses a conclusion based on known information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.why: The clause with だから gives the basis first, and then 彼はひまなはずです gives the conclusion. With the adjective な, な is required before はず.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If はずです is replaced with でしょう, the sentence becomes a softer guess and does not strongly emphasize logical evidence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If に違いない is used, the level of certainty is stronger, and the speaker almost confirms the statement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget な in ひまなはずです because they think the adjective な connects directly to はず.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ な ＋ はずだ; N ＋ の ＋ はずだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.vi: Because this washing machine is old, repairing it is impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the washing machine the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects a characteristic or reason to the comment in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 修理する comes before の to create the content of the action being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: の turns the action 修理する into a noun, while は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: むりです comments on whether repairing it is possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.why: 古くて connects the machine's condition to the conclusion. 修理するのは turns repairing into the topic, and then むりです evaluates that action as impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is replaced with ことは, the sentence becomes more formal and general, but it can still introduce an action as the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If のが is used, repairing becomes the subject of the comment instead of the topic introduced with a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate のは as a separate word, but they need to understand the whole phrase 修理するのは as “as for repairing.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.vi: I felt relieved when the stolen car was found by the police.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: 盗まれた is a past passive verb that modifies 車.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: だ connects the noun 車 with an affirmative statement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the agent performing the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: によって indicates an agent or method and is often used in formal expressions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: 見つけられて is a passive form connected by て to the emotional result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the main predicate, expressing relief after the event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.why: 盗まれた modifies 車 to describe the car's condition. 警察によって marks the police as the agent in the passive sentence, while 見つけられて connects the finding of the car with the feeling of relief.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 警察が見つけて is used, the police become the active subject that finds the car, so the focus is not on the car being found.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見つかって is used, the sentence uses an intransitive form meaning “be found/found” and does not clearly state that the police found it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse によって with に, which indicate only a place or time; in a passive sentence, it often indicates the agent.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.sk: N は ＋ adverb ＋ Vて ＋ いく
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the fire as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: This word modifies a change that happens slowly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the て form connects with いく to express a process of change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: いった is the past form of いく and shows that the change happened over time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.why: 火は places the topic at the beginning of the sentence, and then だんだん shows the degree of change. 消えていった combines the て form with いく to express the fire gradually becoming weaker and going out in a direction away from the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～てくる, the change is viewed as moving toward the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ている is used, the sentence only describes an ongoing state and does not emphasize the direction of change over time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand いく only as “go,” but in ～ていく it also expresses a change that gradually continues later.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.vi: This book is useful for learning about Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the book being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the book the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 日本 with こと, forming a phrase meaning things about Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the content being learned into a noun, while を marks the content of 知る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary form 知る comes before の to turn the action into a noun that expresses purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: のに shows purpose or use, and is equivalent to “to” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: 役に立つ is a fixed phrase meaning useful for a purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.7.n: 立ちます is the main predicate in the phrase 役に立ちます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.why: 日本のことを知るのに is a purpose phrase. It comes before 役に立ちます to say what the book is useful for. The dictionary form 知る is used before のに because learning is the purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～ために, the sentence becomes more formal and emphasizes the purpose of carrying out the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～のに便利だ is used, the focus changes to convenience rather than general usefulness.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.kobun.tip: Do not confuse のに, which shows purpose, with のに, which means “although”; look at the following clause to determine the meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.vi: It is time to go to bed. Please do not watch TV anymore.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: もう shows that the present time has reached the point when something needs to be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary form 寝る comes before 時間 to modify the time for sleeping.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 時間 shows a point in time, while よ is used to announce or emphasize information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks TV as the object of watching.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 見ないで is the negative form ない combined with で to ask someone not to do an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.why: 寝る modifies 時間 to identify this as bedtime. In the next sentence, テレビを is the object that someone is asked to stop watching, while 見ないでください is the polite pattern for asking someone not to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～てはいけない, the sentence becomes a stronger prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～なくてもいい is used, it means “it is okay not to do it,” not a request not to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out で in ～ないでください, but ないでください must be kept as a complete phrase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vi: According to my older brother's letter, the whole family is well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows possession and modifies 手紙.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: によると introduces the source of information supporting the following content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は states the topic of the information being communicated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: みんな modifies 家族, showing that all members are included.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 元気だ is the predicate of the reported clause; the adjective な keeps だ before そうです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです at the end of the sentence shows information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.why: によると places the source of information before the reported clause. Then, 家族は states the topic, 元気だ gives the content, and そうです marks it as hearsay.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: In the form Vます, with ます omitted, or Aい, そうです can express appearance or a prediction, and does not necessarily show heard information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: によれば also introduces a source of information and is close in meaning to によると, but it is more formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out だ before そうです, but nouns and adjectives な need だ when using そうです to mean hearsay.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q3.kobun.cn: N + によると; N・Aな + だ + そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vi: Even if my parents object, I intend to study abroad.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: たとえ announces a concessive condition in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject carrying out the action of objecting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: Vて＋も connects the concessive clause with the unchanged result in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: は states the person whose intention is being presented.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies つもり, creating the meaning “intend to study abroad.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: つもりです ends the sentence and shows the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.cn: Vて＋も／Aい omits い＋くても／Aな＋でも／N＋でも; V辞書形＋つもりだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.why: The clause たとえ...ても states an obstacle but does not change the decision in the main clause. The dictionary form 留学する comes before つもり to show an intended action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with なら, the sentence becomes a hypothetical condition and no longer has the sense that the decision stays unchanged even if something happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: 予定です focuses on a planned schedule, while つもりです emphasizes a personal intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ても with an unconjugated verb て; change 反対する to 反対して before adding も.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vi: Because I have to get up early tomorrow morning, I intend to go to bed early tonight.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 明日 with 朝, forming a phrase that indicates a point in time.
