default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that tomorrow morning is the time reference for the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I have to get up early
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects a reason with a result and comes after the plain form of an adjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: は changes the topic to the action planned for tonight.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 早く is the adverbial form and modifies 寝よう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: 寝よう is the volitional form, quoted by と as the content of 思います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: 思います ends the sentence and expresses the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.why: A time phrase comes first to make clear when the event happens. ので gives the reason, while the volitional form + と 思います expresses the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason but sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If つもりです is used, the sentence emphasizes an existing plan rather than an intention formed while speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that と in ～ようと思う must come after the volitional form, not after the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので; V意向形 + と思います
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: ながら connects a secondary action 飲み with the main action that follows; 飲み is the shortened form of ます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being sung.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q6.kobun.why: The action used with ながら is the secondary action, while the final verb 歌います is the main action. Both actions have the same subject and happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: When て is used, the sentence usually expresses sequential actions or a cause-and-effect relationship, without emphasizing that they happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: When 間に is used, the focus is on one action happening during the time of another action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ながら; remove ます first, then add ながら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vi: The Japanese-Language Proficiency Test is held every year in July and December.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the test is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎年 modifies the time when the event is held.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the times when the event is held.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 行われます is the passive form, used when the test receives the action of being held.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.why: The topic is the test. The two months are joined by と and marked by に. The passive form is suitable because the sentence focuses on the event being held, without stating who organizes it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 開催されます is used, the meaning is still “is held,” but the expression is more formal and is often used for events.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行います is used, the test becomes the performer of the action, so the sentence needs a clearer organizer as its subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に in the month phrase for a place marker; here, に marks a time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vi: Kim is good at Japanese like a Japanese person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Kim is the person being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a noun with ように to create a phrase comparing manner or degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object evaluated as 上手.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 上手です is the adjective predicate な in polite form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.why: は states who is being evaluated, while が marks the ability being evaluated. The phrase のように comes before 上手 to compare Kim’s Japanese ability with that of a Japanese person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ような is used, the comparison phrase must modify the noun that follows; it cannot directly modify 上手です.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If みたいに is used, the meaning is similar, but the expression is more casual than ように.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.tip: Do not omit の after the noun before ように; say Nのように, not Nように directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q8.kobun.cn: N ＋ のように; Aな ＋ です
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vi: Because I am very busy, I do not have much time to sleep.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: とても modifies the adjective that follows and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes い to くて to connect with the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: あまり usually goes with a negative sentence to express a small amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause 寝る modifies 時間, while が marks this phrase as something that does not exist.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.why: くて connects the state of being busy with the result of not having time to sleep. 寝る comes before 時間 to modify the noun, while あまり combines with ありません to express a small amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause is clearer and softer; くて directly connects two states or events.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ないで is used, the meaning changes to doing one thing without doing another, so it is no longer a cause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.kobun.tip: The adjective い does not connect with で; い must change to くて.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vi: If you want to buy cheap electrical products, you should go to the Akihabara district.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective 安い comes before 電気製品 to modify the electrical products.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the electrical products as the object of 買う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form 買う comes before なら to state a condition or hypothetical topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: なら connects the condition with the advice in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the name as the content of いう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: いう connects the place name with 街 to create the phrase “a district called Akihabara.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: へ shows the direction of movement to a place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: 行けば is the conditional form of 行く and connects with いい to create advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.8.n: 行けばいい is a pattern expressing a recommended suitable way to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.why: The phrase “buy cheap electrical products” is placed before なら to make the condition. Then, 秋葉原という街へ identifies the place to go, while 行けばいい gives advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～たら, the condition is presented as something that may happen or be completed first.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: ～ばいい only gives advice; if なら is omitted, the condition “if you want to buy” is lost.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.tip: なら follows a verb in the plain form, an adjective, or a noun; it does not connect directly with a verb in the ます form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ なら; N ＋ なら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.vi: Since each person gets three notebooks, please take them yourself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Quantity ＋ ずつ ＋ ですから ＋ N で ＋ Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic being divided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ずつ comes after a quantity to show that the quantity is divided equally among each person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ですから connects the reason before it with the request after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the method or the person who directly performs the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the verb 取る with the request pattern that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.why: The topic is stated first, followed by the quantity divided among each person. ですから turns this information into a reason, while Vてください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If それぞれ is used, it means each individual person or thing, but it does not emphasize equal division as ずつ does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget to place ずつ immediately after the quantity to be divided equally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.vi: Even though the exam was near, that person did not study at all.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the person being discussed the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 試験 with 前 to form a phrase that modifies a time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the time when a state or change begins.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ても connects a concessive clause, meaning that even if the preceding condition occurs, the following result does not change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 全然 is usually used with a negative form to emphasize that something does not happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: The past negative polite verb form, serving as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.cn: Vて + も; Aい remove い + くても; Aな + でも; N + でも
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.why: The phrase 試験の前に indicates a time, while なっても turns that time into a concessive condition. The main clause uses 全然 with a negative form to emphasize that the person did not study at all.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern expresses a contrast between the preceding condition and the unchanged result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, a feeling of regret or reproach becomes clearer, instead of simply expressing concession.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ても as an independent connector and forget to put the verb or adjective before it in the correct form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.vi: I repaired the department manager's car for him.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person performing the action as the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: のために indicates the person who benefits from the car repair.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the direct object of 修理する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the action of repairing the car with the helping action that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: さしあげる follows Vて and shows that the speaker did the action for someone of higher status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.why: The person performing the action is the topic, the beneficiary goes with のために, and the car is the object of 修理する. 修理してさしあげました combines the repair action with the respectful meaning of doing it as a favor.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If のために is replaced with に, the sentence only states the target of the action, and the meaning of doing it for that person's benefit becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If てあげました is used, the meaning of doing something as a favor remains, but the level of respect is lower than with てさしあげました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse のために with に and lose the meaning of the beneficiary.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q12.kobun.cn: N + のために; V辞書形 + ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.vi: I was sent abroad for four years because of work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.sk: N は + N で + N へ + Time period + V使役受身
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person affected by being sent away.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the reason or circumstances that led to the person being sent away.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ４年間 indicates the length of time the person was sent away.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 行かされました is the causative-passive form, expressing that someone was made or forced to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.why: 仕事で gives the reason, 海外へ gives the destination, and ４年間 gives the duration; these parts add information one by one to the predicate 行かされました. The causative-passive form shows that the speaker did not go willingly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If によって is used, the cause or agent is emphasized in a more formal way, and it is less natural than で in this work-related context.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行かれました is used, the sentence is only the passive form of go and does not clearly show that the person was forced or ordered to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 行かされました for the simple past, although it is the causative-passive form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.vi: If you keep sitting in front of a computer, your back will hurt.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects パソコン with 前 to identify the front of that object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the action of sitting takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてばかり emphasizes repeatedly doing only one action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: いると connects a continuing state with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the body part whose state changes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending in い changes to く to connect with なる, expressing becoming painful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: なります expresses a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the action of sitting, while ばかりいる shows that the action continues and is repeated too much. と connects a general condition with the result that the body changes into a painful state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If only Vている is used, the sentence simply says that someone is sitting, without the meaning of continuing to sit or doing only one thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Vると expresses a general condition, while てばかりいると emphasizes a continuing state before it leads to a result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change 痛い to 痛く before なる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.vi: Because even I do not clearly understand the meaning of this word, explaining it is difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 言葉 with 意味 to form the phrase “the meaning of this word.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the meaning of the word the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: にも marks the person who knows or understands something and adds the meaning “even I do not know.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: から connects the reason in front with the conclusion that explaining it is difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: の turns the verb 説明する into a noun, and then は makes explaining the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.7.n: 難しい is the predicate stating how difficult the explanation is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.why: The clause before から gives the reason, while 説明するのは難しい is the conclusion. の nominalizes the action 説明する, making the whole act of explaining the topic evaluated with 難しい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If のが is used, the sentence focuses directly on the difficulty of explaining; のは gives the feeling of presenting that action as a topic for contrast or comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: ことは also nominalizes a verb, but it sounds stiffer and more formal than のは in ordinary speech.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit の and say 説明するは難しい, but a dictionary-form verb needs の to become the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q15.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のは + Aい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.vi: If you do something bad, you must apologize.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: 悪い modifies こと, forming the phrase “bad thing”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ことを is the object of した.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb formた combines with ら to express the condition “if/when someone does it”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 謝らなければ is the negative conditional form, which prepares for the obligation pattern that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ～なければならない expresses an obligation: having to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ら。Aい remove い ＋ かったら。Aな ＋ だったら。N ＋ だったら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, followed by the conclusion about the obligation. The pattern ～なければならない uses a negative conditional form to express something that must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～なら is used, the sentence has a hypothetical nuance based on information or a condition that has been stated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ～ても, the meaning changes to “even if someone does something bad, they still have to apologize”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake ～なければならない for “if not,” but the whole phrase means “must”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.vi: Because of the earthquake, the newly built house was damaged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: Nのため states the cause that leads to the event in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 建てた modifies 家, while ばかり shows that the action has just been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 家が is the subject affected by the damage.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 壊れた is a past-tense predicate, showing that the house was damaged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.why: The cause phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to explain the reason. The phrase 建てたばかりの comes before 家 because a modifying clause must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～ので, the sentence still expresses a cause-and-effect relationship, but the tone is softer and more naturally explanatory.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ～から, the reason is stated more directly and conversationally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place the modifying phrase after the noun, as in Vietnamese, but Japanese places 建てたばかりの before 家.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.vi: It can be said that computers are one of the greatest inventions of the twentieth century.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that computers are the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ２０世紀 with the noun 発明, showing the scope or period of the invention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 最大の modifies 発明, showing the highest degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 発明 with 一つ, forming the phrase “one of the inventions”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.4.vi: even if it is called one
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 言っても is the form て＋も, creating a concessive meaning before いい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: ～てもいい expresses permission or an acceptable possibility.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.why: The topic コンピューター is stated first, followed by a series of phrases の that narrow the meaning of 一つ. The sentence ends with ～てもいい to show that this judgment is acceptable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～てもかまわない, the meaning of permission is almost unchanged, but the tone is more formal and definite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～と言える is used, the sentence emphasizes the ability to state or evaluate something rather than permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that てもいい must follow a verb in the て form and cannot directly follow a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.vi: This country has a strange smell. I wonder if it has gone bad.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies 国, identifying the country being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that this country is the topic of the speaker’s impression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 変な modifies におい, forming the phrase “strange smell”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing sensed in the pattern Nがする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: します combines with におい to express the perception of a smell; ね adds a confirming nuance for the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective 悪い changes to the continuative form 悪く to connect with なった.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: なる in the past form expresses a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.7.n: かな expresses the speaker’s wondering or mild guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.why: In the pattern がする, a noun for a sensation, such as におい, comes before が and acts as the thing being sensed. The next sentence uses 悪くなった to ask whether the state has changed for the worse.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～がある, the sentence only says that a smell exists, without emphasizing the sensed feeling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～そうだ is used, the sentence makes a prediction based on appearance or signs, rather than directly expressing the sense of smell.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with におい, but this perception pattern uses においがする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vi: It is best not to drink a beverage when you do not even know its name.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: も emphasizes that even the name of the beverage is unknown.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 分からない comes before 飲み物 to modify the type of beverage.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The whole modified phrase becomes the topic, while は states which beverage is being discussed in the advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative form ない comes before ほう to create the action that is advised against.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ほうがいい expresses advice; here, it advises the listener not to drink.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: いいですよ ends the advice with a gentle, friendly tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.why: 名前も分からない is a clause modifying 飲み物, helping identify which beverage it is. The clause 飲まないほうがいい uses the negative form before ほうがいい to give advice not to drink.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～ないでください, the sentence directly tells the listener not to drink.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～たほうがいい is used, the sentence advises doing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.kobun.tip: For negative advice, use Vないほうがいい; do not use Vるほうがいい to say “should not.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.vi: Even though I said I did not want to, the doctor forced me to be hospitalized.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.1.vi: that I did not want to
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content said to be いやだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 言って is the て form, connecting 言う with いる to show a continuing state or action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ～ても creates a concessive relationship: even in that state or situation, the following result still occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: は states the person affected in the passive clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: に marks the person who performs the forcing action in the causative-passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.6.vi: was forced to enter the hospital
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.6.n: させられた is the past causative-passive form, expressing that someone was forced to enter the hospital.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.why: The content of the speech comes before と, followed by ても to create a concessive meaning. In the main clause, the person who is forced to act is the topic, while the person doing the forcing is marked by に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: ～ても only expresses the meaning “even though,” while させられる shows that the speaker was forced to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ～させる, the meaning changes to “make someone else do something,” so it no longer means that the speaker was forced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake に for a place, but in a causative-passive sentence, に usually refers to the person doing the forcing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q20.kobun.cn: Vて + も。V使役受身: Vさせる + られる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.vi: I heard that Hanako’s mobile phone was stolen by a pickpocket.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Hanako is the person affected by the event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that was stolen in a passive sentence showing harm.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who carried out the action of taking the phone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 取られた is the past passive form, showing that Hanako suffered because her phone was taken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです usually follows a clause to convey information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.why: The passive construction showing harm makes the affected person the topic, the lost object the object, and the person who caused the action follow に. そうです at the end of the sentence shows that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～らしい is used, the sentence has a meaning of supposition or evidence-based information, rather than simply reporting what was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: そうだ indicates an outward sign and must follow a connective form such as 取られそうだ. It means “looks likely to be stolen,” which differs from そうです reported聞.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use が for a lost object, but the passive construction showing harm usually uses Nは Nを Nに Vられる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q21.kobun.cn: Nは + Nを + Nに + V受身。V普通形 + そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.vi: As of today, it has been exactly one year since I came to Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.sk: N に + Vてから + Time で + Adverb + Time に + なりました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place connected with 来て, creating the starting point “come to Japan.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: てから connects the earlier action with the period that began after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: で uses today as the point from which to count the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates that the result reached is a period of one year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, expressing that the time has reached a new point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.why: 来てから sets the starting point, while 今日で sets the ending point for calculating the period. 一年に なりました expresses the change from not yet having reached one year to having reached one full year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of で at 今日で, the sentence only says that something starts today, and no longer means that today is the point used for calculation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に after 今日, but when saying “as of a certain time,” で must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.vi: Now I can read simple Japanese passages.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.sk: Time point は + Aな な + N の + N が + Potential V ように + なりました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the present time as the topic, in contrast with the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective ending in な with the following noun 文章.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 日本語 with 文章, showing the type of text being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object that can be read.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 読める is the potential form, while ように connects the achieved ability with なる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: なりました expresses a change in ability over time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.cn: Potential V + ように + なる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.why: 文章が is the object being read, so が is used with the potential verb 読める. ように なりました connects the newly achieved ability with なる to express the change from the past to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes the change and the result achieved, while ～ようにする expresses actively trying to make something happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 読める in this pattern; the object takes が when the verb is in the potential form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.vi: Wait quietly in the car, okay? Do not go outside.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.sk: N の N で + Adverb + Vている のよ。Vて + は → ちゃ + だめよ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 車 with 中, creating the phrase “inside the car.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the action 待ってる takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: おとなしく is an adverbial form that modifies the action of waiting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 待ってる is a shortened form of 待っている, while のよ gives the reminder a friendly, informal tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects 出る with the next verb to create the action sequence “go outside.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: いっちゃ is a shortened form of いっては, creating the first part of the prohibition pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: だめよ ends the prohibition, and よ is used to emphasize the statement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.why: 中で identifies the place to wait, while おとなしく modifies the manner of waiting. 出ていっちゃだめ combines the verb 出ていく with the shortened form ちゃだめ to create an informal prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～てはいけない, the prohibition keeps the same meaning but sounds more formal and firm.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 出ていかないで is used, the sentence becomes a softer request meaning “please do not go out,” without the clear prohibition tone of だめ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.tip: ちゃ in いっちゃ is not a separate particle. It is a shortened form of ては in the pattern ～てはだめ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q24.kobun.cn: Vて + はだめだ → Vちゃだめだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.vi: The teacher goes to the swimming pool every day. The teacher seems to like swimming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.sk: N は + Frequency + N へ + Vている。N は + N が + ナA語幹 + らしいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the teacher as the topic of the action and comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎日 indicates how often the action of going swimming occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement of 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ている expresses an ongoing action or a repeated habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: は shifts to a comment about the same person, the teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the object of the preference 好き.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: らしい expresses a judgment based on information or signs, while です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.why: へ attaches to the destination of 行く, while ている shows that going to the swimming pool happens every day. With 好き, the object of preference takes が, and then らしい adds a sense of supposition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 好きそうです is used, it means that someone appears to like something based on outward appearance, not necessarily on reported information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If 好きなようです is used, the supposition is more cautious and is usually based on a situation or signs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.tip: With 好き, do not use を to indicate something that someone likes; the noun for the object usually takes が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹・N ＋ らしいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the electric light as the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: によって indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 考え出された is the past passive form, describing the electric light as having been invented by someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: what kind of thing is it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ものですか creates a question that asks who performed the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.why: 電灯は is the passive object moved up as the topic. だれによって asks about the agent, while 考え出されたものですか uses the passive form to ask who invented it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～に作られた, the question changes to ask who made it, without emphasizing the idea of invention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If だれが～ましたか is used, the question is more direct and active, with the person who acts as the subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the affected object usually goes with は, while the person who performs the action goes with によって.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.kobun.cn: N ＋ によって; V受身た形 ＋ ものですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vi: These shoes are made of thick paper.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the shoes are the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the material used to make an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 作られて is the passive form て, combined with いる to describe the resulting state of being made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: いる combines with the て form of a verb to indicate a resulting state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: ものです concludes the sentence and explains the nature of the shoes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.cn: N for material ＋ で ＋ V受身形; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.why: The topic 靴は is described by the clause 厚い紙で作られている. The particle で states the material, while the passive form emphasizes that the shoes are made from that material.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with から, the sentence emphasizes that the original material has changed into the product.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If によって is used, the sentence may emphasize the person or method used to make the product.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に instead of で when talking about materials, but materials require で.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vi: Vegetable dishes are what I like more than anything else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 野菜料理 the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の indicates possession or a connection with the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: より gives the standard of comparison; 何より is an expression that emphasizes the highest degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 好きな modifies もの and shows that it is something the speaker likes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ものです turns the preceding part into a noun phrase and concludes the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.cn: N ＋ より; 何より is a fixed phrase used to emphasize the highest degree of comparison
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.why: 野菜料理は is the topic, while 私の何より好きなもの is the noun phrase that gives the comment. 何より comes before 好きな to set the standard of comparison, meaning more than all other things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 一番好きな, the meaning is still “like the most,” but the tone is more direct and common.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 誰より好きな, the objects being compared change from all things to all people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.kobun.tip: Learners may easily translate 何より word for word, but this phrase usually means “more than anything else” or “more than anything.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vi: On a day off, I did housework for that friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 休み with 日 to form the phrase “day off.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に goes with なった to indicate a result or a state of becoming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: なった is the past form of なる in the clause that modifies 友だち.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 友だち with ために to identify the person being addressed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: ために indicates the person who benefits from the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks 家事 as the object of やる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: やって is the て form of やる, combined with あげた to describe doing something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ あげる; past: Vて ＋ あげた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the person helped through 友だちのために. 家事を is the object, while やってあげた shows that the speaker performs an action for the friend's benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vてくれた, the friend or another person will do the housework for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vてもらった, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker received help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q6.kobun.tip: Learners may easily confuse the direction of benefit in あげる, くれる, and もらう; identify who does the action and who receives the benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.vi: I hear that the number of unmarried women in Japan has been gradually increasing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: では limits the area or context being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The plain-form clause modifies 女性.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the increase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the entire idea 増えてきた as the content being reported.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: いう connects the quoted content with ことだ to create the pattern ということだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ということだ is placed at the end of the sentence to report heard information or a conclusion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる; past: Vて ＋ きた. Plain-form clause ＋ と ＋ いう ＋ ことだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.why: 結婚しない comes before 女性 to modify this noun. 女性が増えてきた is the main clause, while と言うことだ turns that content into reported information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with という話だ, the sentence leans more toward “there is a story or information that...”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If そうだ is used after 増えてきた, the sentence still reports heard information but is shorter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q7.kobun.tip: Learners may easily forget that the clause before ということだ must be in the plain form, not the polite form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.vi: At this moment, her face looked lonely.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.sk: NのNは ＋ 時間 ＋ Aい removeい ＋ そうに ＋ V見える
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の modifies 顔, identifying the face as belonging to her.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the face is the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 今 indicates the time of the observed state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: そうに turns 寂しい into an adverb that modifies 見えた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 見えた is the predicate, describing the impression created by the face.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ そうに; Aな ＋ そうに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.why: 彼女の顔は is the topic, and 今 states when it was observed. 寂しそうに comes before 見えた because it describes the appearance perceived by the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ように見える is used, the sentence means “like” or “seems,” based on a broader judgment rather than only on the immediate appearance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If らしく見える is used, the sentence emphasizes that the appearance matches the characteristic of being lonely.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, い must be removed before そうに: 寂しい becomes 寂しそうに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q8.tokens.7.m: fill in the linking form く
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vi: I almost arrived late for the appointment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で combines with 少し to indicate the point just before something happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies 時間, forming the phrase “the time of the appointment.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the time at which being late is considered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 遅れる in the dictionary form comes before ところだった.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: Vるところだった describes something that almost happened but ultimately did not happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.why: もう少しで is placed first to show that something almost happened. 遅れるところだった uses the dictionary form because it refers to an action that was about to happen but was avoided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vるところだ, it means that the action is about to happen, without the meaning of “almost.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with Vたところだ, it means that the action has just been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vs.2.d: If it is replaced with Vているところだ, it means that the action is currently being performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use 遅れるを, but 遅れる goes with a time point through the particle に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ところだった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vi: The dollar goes up and down, so it is unstable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the dollar as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 高い changes into 高かったり to state one of the changing states.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 安かったり states the contrasting condition, while で connects the series of conditions to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 不安定だ is the summary comment about the rises and falls just mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.why: The two forms of かったり are placed together to list changing, non-fixed states. で connects this list to the conclusion 不安定だ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～たり～たりする is used, the sentence lists typical actions or states without directly connecting them to a conclusion with で.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～し～し is used, the sentence emphasizes several reasons or characteristics, rather than changes between different states.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い must change い to かった before り; it cannot be directly attached to 高いり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q1.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ り、Vた形 ＋ りで／Aい → かったり／ナA・N ＋ だったり
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.vi: I dislike that he always leaves the door open and goes outside.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the action 出て行く and indicates frequency.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks ドア as the object kept in an open state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたままで describes keeping the state unchanged after an action and then performing the next action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 出て is the て form, connected with 行く to describe going out of the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: ので connects a reason to the result or feeling stated afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: いやだ is the sentence ending, expressing the speaker’s dislike.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.why: 開けたままで comes before 出て行く to show that the door remains open while he leaves. ので connects this repeated action to the feeling いやだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Vたまま also indicates that a state remains unchanged, but it does not directly suggest a connection to a following action like ままで.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vないで is used, it means going out without doing a certain action, not keeping the state unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q10.kobun.tip: ままで should not be translated as “while”; the main meaning of the pattern is that the previous state remains unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.vi: There is a good hotel near the station.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 駅 with 近く, forming the phrase “the area near the station.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the location where the hotel exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: いい directly modifies ホテル.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate indicating that an object or place exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.why: 駅の近くに forms a place phrase and comes before あります. In existence sentences, the location goes with に, while the existing thing is marked by が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: そばに also means “beside or very near the station,” with a closer feeling than 近くに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q11.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with places, but in an existence sentence with あります, they need to use に for the location and が for the existing thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.vi: Please come here before 9 a.m. tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.sk: N の N は ＋ Time までに ＋ N へ ＋ Vてください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with 朝, identifying which morning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that tomorrow morning is the time reference for the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: までに indicates the latest deadline by which arriving must be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: へ marks the direction of movement for the action 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 来て is the て form, connected with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.why: 朝は sets the time reference, while 9時までに states the deadline for arriving. ここへ indicates the direction, and 来てください turns the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is used instead of までに, the meaning focuses on “up to 9 o’clock” or a continuing period, without emphasizing a completion deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: 9時前に also means before 9 o’clock, but it usually focuses more on the time before that point than on the deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use までに for an action that continues over time; this pattern is suitable for something that must be completed before a deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.vi: Although this apartment is old and cramped, it is very convenient because it is near the school.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies アパート and must come directly before the noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the apartment the topic of two contrasting comments.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 古い changes to 古くて to connect the adjective い with the next feature.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: it is old and cramped, but it is close to the school.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: から marks the reference point used to judge the distance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: 近い changes to 近くて to connect with the adjective 便利.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: 便利だ is the predicate that ends the second clause and states a positive conclusion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ くて; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ が
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.why: 古くて and 近くて connect adjectives that both describe the apartment. が comes between the two parts to create a contrast between the inconvenient points and the convenient point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: けれども also means “but,” but it is fuller and more formal than が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: のに emphasizes a result that is contrary to a prediction or expectation, more strongly than the neutral contrast expressed by が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q13.kobun.tip: The adjective い must change to くて when connecting clauses; it cannot use the form いくて directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.vi: I chose a sweater as a birthday present for my mother.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 母 with 誕生日, showing the relationship “my mother’s birthday.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 誕生日 with プレゼント and identifies the type of present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: は states which present is being decided on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the result of the choice in the pattern Nにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する and expresses a choice that has been decided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.why: プレゼントは is the item selected, while セーターに is the result of the decision. しました shows that the decision to choose a sweater has been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nを選ぶ is used, the sentence emphasizes the action of “choosing N,” while Nにする shows the decision to choose that option.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Nになる expresses “become” or “be decided as,” and does not directly state the person who made the decision like Nにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q14.kobun.tip: In the pattern Nにする, に comes after the chosen option; do not use を as when simply saying that you choose an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.vi: Do you remember where you bought that book?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the book as the object that was bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle で indicates the place where the buying took place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The question clause uses the past form 買った and ends with か to make it the content being remembered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the verb 覚える with the auxiliary verb いる in 覚えています.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: いますか creates a polite question about whether someone remembers.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.why: The phrase 本を is the object of 買う, while どこで asks where it was bought. The whole clause 買ったか comes before 覚えていますか to make it the content to remember.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If のか is used, the explanatory or emphatic feeling of the question is clearer, while か is more neutral.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If かどうか is used, it asks whether the book was bought there, not the specific place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place か at the end of the whole sentence, but in an indirect question か comes immediately after the clause being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q15.tokens.8.m: be in a state of, be doing
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は identifies the person asking for advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 何を asks about the task or object that the speaker should help with.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The form たら connects a hypothetical condition with いいですか to ask what should be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたらいいですか is used to ask about a suitable way to act or to ask for advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q16.kobun.why: 何を comes before 手伝う because it is the object of the helping action. The pattern Vたらいいですか turns the question into a request for instructions: what should I do?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with Vばいいですか still asks what should be done, but the feeling focuses more on the condition or the correct way to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This sentence only asks whether someone will help with something or what they will help with. It does not clearly ask for advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q16.kobun.tip: Do not translate たら mechanically as only “if”; in Vたらいいですか, the whole pattern means “what should I do?”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.vi: I wonder what kind of voice that bird makes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle は makes the bird the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: どんな comes before 声 to ask about the type or quality of the bird’s call.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle で indicates the method or voice used to make the call.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.4.vi: I wonder what it sounds like
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 鳴くのかな expresses a gentle wondering feeling when the answer is not known.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.why: どんな must come directly before the noun 声 to modify the type of voice. 声で expresses the method of calling, while のかな turns the whole sentence into a statement of wonder.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is close to どんな声で, but it is more formal and stiff.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: どの声で asks which voice to choose from known voices, not what the voice is like.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q17.kobun.tip: どんな always comes before a noun and cannot be used alone as a question word for a place or a person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.vi: I wanted to travel, but I could not go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N に ＋ V removeます＋たかった が ＋ negative past potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は identifies the person who has the desire and faces the opposite result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に marks the destination of the verb 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きたかった is the past form of the desire 行きたい; が connects it to the opposite result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 行けなかった uses the negative past potential form to express being unable to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.cn: V removeます＋たい／たくない／たかった／たくなかった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.why: 旅行に adds a destination to 行く. The first part states a past desire, and が connects it to the second part to emphasize that the desire was not fulfilled.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: 行きたいが expresses a present desire, not a desire that existed in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: けれども also connects two contrasting ideas, but is more polite and complete than が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q18.kobun.tip: When たい is changed to the past, change たい to たかった; do not use 行きましたたい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.vi: I started playing tennis last month.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.sk: Time から ＋ N を ＋ V removeます＋始めました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle から indicates the starting point of a habit or activity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the activity that was started.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 始めました is the polite past form of 始める. It combines with テニスを to say that someone started playing this sport.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.cn: V removeます＋始める／始めた／始めます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.why: 先月から identifies the starting point, while テニスを is the content of the activity. The verb 始める comes after the ます-removed form of the verb to show that an action has begun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence only says that the person started playing. Adding 先月から clearly states that they started in the previous month.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: し始めました emphasizes that the action of playing began, while テニスを始めました sounds more natural when talking about starting a sport or habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q19.kobun.tip: With this pattern, the verb before 始める must remove ます. For example, use 読み始める, not 読みます始める.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vi: It seems that this work cannot be finished even by tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Deadline までに ＋ Vremoveます ＋ そうもありません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before 仕事 to identify the work being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the work the topic of the prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action is expected to be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 終わりそうもない expresses a negative prediction that completion is unlikely.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません completes the polite negative form of the pattern そうもない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.cn: Vremoveます ＋ そうもない／そうにもない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.why: までに sets the deadline for completion. 終わりそうもありません combines the prediction marker そう with the negative form to emphasize that completion is almost impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 終わりそうです is used, the meaning changes to “it seems almost finished,” which is the opposite of the negative prediction in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 終わらなさそうです is used, it also means that the work does not seem finished, but the tone is usually softer than そうもありません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q2.kobun.tip: With a verb, remove ます and then add そうもない; do not use the dictionary form 終わるそうもない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.vi: If you meet a neighbor on the street, say hello.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where the meeting occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 近所の modifies 人 and identifies the person as someone from the nearby area.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the person being met.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The past form 会った combines with ら to create the condition “when or if you meet someone.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do the action together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.cn: Vた形＋ら；Aい removeい＋かったら；Aな＋だったら；N＋だったら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.why: 道で indicates the place, while 近所の人に is the object of 会う. The clause 会ったら comes first to state the condition, followed by the suggestion あいさつしましょう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: 会うと usually expresses a natural result or something that happens every time, so it is less suitable than たら for a reminder in a specific situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: 会えば also states a condition, but it has a more hypothetical or rule-like tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse に and で: で indicates the place where the meeting happens, while に indicates the person being met.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.vi: That restaurant is crowded whenever you go there.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the restaurant the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: いつ indicates the time assumed in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: Vて＋も creates a concessive clause, meaning that the result stays the same no matter what you do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 込んで connects with いる to create the ている form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: いる shows that the restaurant is in a crowded state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.why: いつ行っても is the concessive clause that comes first and covers every assumed time. Then, ても leads to the unchanged result that the restaurant is always crowded.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it means “when you go,” the sentence changes into a condition or natural-result relationship. It no longer means “whenever you go.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning changes to “you may go at any time,” expressing permission rather than an unchanged result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may easily mistake ても for a simple condition and forget that this pattern emphasizes that the result remains the same.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q21.kobun.cn: Vて・Aいくて・Aな/Nで ＋ も
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.vi: It is fine if you call late, so please call.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い changes to the くても form to create a concessive meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: かまわない expresses acceptance, while ので connects this reason to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb 電話する with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.why: おそくてもかまわない shows that calling late is still acceptable. ので connects this acceptance as the reason for the request 電話してください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is almost “it is fine to be late,” but it is shorter and places less emphasis on the idea that there is no problem.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: It also means “it is fine to be late,” but it focuses more on a satisfactory condition than on permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.tip: Do not use おそいもかまわない directly; first change the adjective い to く before ても.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q22.kobun.cn: Vて・Aいくて・Aな/Nで ＋ も ＋ かまわない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.vi: Because I kept talking for about an hour, my throat became dry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.sk: Duration ぐらい ＋ Vます-stem ＋ 続けた ＋ ので、N が ＋ Vた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: ぐらい comes after a period of time to indicate an approximate duration.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 話し is the stem with ます removed. It connects with つづけた to express an action that continued until before the result occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the body part that enters the state described by the predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.why: The duration comes first to add information about how long the speaking continued. 話しつづけたので connects the cause to the result のどがかわいた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is substituted, the meaning becomes “finished speaking,” focusing on the endpoint rather than continuous duration.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning changes to “started speaking,” showing the starting point of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.tip: When using 続ける, remove ます from the preceding verb, so say 話し続ける, not 話します続ける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q23.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ 続ける／続けた／続けている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.vi: The wind is not as strong today as it was yesterday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the item being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: ほど comes after the comparison point to set the standard for a lower degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the wind as the subject whose strength is being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 強い changes to 強くない to make the strength negative.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.why: きのうほど is the comparison standard, while 強くない denies that today reaches the same level of strength as that standard. The particle が marks the subject of the adjective 強い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression is less natural for a negative comparison of degree; ほど is more suitable for the meaning “not as strong as.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning changes to “the wind is stronger today than yesterday.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.tip: The pattern ほど～ない requires ほど after the comparison standard and a negative predicate. It does not make the preceding noun negative.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q24.kobun.cn: N ＋ ほど ＋ Vない／Aいくない／Aなではない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.vi: Because I forgot my mobile phone, I could not contact anyone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vた ＋ ために、V past negative potential form
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object related to the action of forgetting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense verb comes before ために to state the cause leading to the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: できませんでした expresses past inability and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.why: The forgotten object is marked with を, and then わすれたために turns this event into the cause. The following clause states the result: being unable to make contact in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: It also states a cause, but it has a lighter and more natural conversational tone than ために.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: It emphasizes the responsibility or negative result caused by forgetting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.tip: Before ために, a noun must be followed by の, and an adjective な must be followed by な; do not connect Nために or Aなために directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形 + ために/Aい + ために/Aな + な + ために/N + の + ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vi: I hope you get better soon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the illness as the subject of getting better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the clause expressing a wish with いい, creating the meaning “I hope that...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: いいですね expresses a gentle wish or hope.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q3.kobun.why: 早く modifies 治る to state the desired time. The clause 治ると comes before いいですね, so the whole sentence expresses hope that it will happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It states a wish more directly and is less friendly and sympathetic in tone than いいですね.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use は after 病気 in this pattern if you want to emphasize that the illness is the subject that gets better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + といい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vi: I always make sure that the students practice hard every day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.sk: Nに + Time + Adverb + Nを + V使役形 + ようにしている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person who is made to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks what the students are asked to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: させる is the causative form, while ように connects the goal of maintaining the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: して is the て form of する, and it connects with います to express a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: している expresses actively maintaining something as a habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.why: 学生に is the person performing the action, while 練習を is what that person is made to do. ようにしている comes after させる to express the speaker’s effort to maintain this practice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses an effort or decision to form a habit, but it does not emphasize an already maintained state as ようにしている does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 学生に with 練習を: に refers only to the person being made to act, while を refers to the action being performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.tokens.6.m: make someone do; allow someone to do
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.tokens.8.m: do; the て form of する
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q4.kobun.cn: Vる/Vない + ようにする（文中は ようにしている）
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vi: The coffee made by my father is very good.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の appears in the modifying clause and shows that the father performs the action of making the coffee.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 入れた is a past-tense verb that directly modifies コーヒー.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the coffee made by the father the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: おいしい is an adjective that な describes the coffee.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.why: おとうさんの入れた forms a modifying clause for コーヒー, in which the father is the person who made it. After stating the topic with は, the sentence ends with an adjective describing its good taste.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The subject of the action can also be stated in a modifying clause, but が shows the subject more clearly than の.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It only expresses possession or connection; it does not necessarily say that the father made the coffee.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q5.kobun.tip: Do not understand おとうさんの as simple possession; in a modifying clause, の can refer to the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vi: You do not need to hurry so much, because there is still a whole hour left.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.sk: Degree + Vない+くてもいい。 + まだ + Nも + あるから
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: そんなに modifies 急がなくてもいい and indicates the degree to which there is no need to hurry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 急がなくてもいい expresses that it is not necessary to perform the action in a hurry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: も after a quantity emphasizes that more time remains than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: から connects the reason to the previous sentence and explains why there is no need to hurry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.why: The first sentence gives advice not to hurry. The second sentence uses から to state the reason, while も emphasizes that plenty of time remains.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It means that something must be done, which is the opposite of the meaning “do not need to” in なくてもいい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It also means that something does not need to be done, but it is usually more neutral and formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.tip: Do not change 急ぐ into 急がない and attach ても directly; it must be changed to 急がなくてもいい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q6.kobun.cn: Vない形（いを取る）+くてもいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vi: I almost crashed into the car driving in front of me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.sk: Degree + Nを + Vて + いる + Nに + Vます語幹 + そうだった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: もう少しで refers to the very short distance or time before an event could happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を here refers to the route or area where the car is driving.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 走って connects with いる to form the progressive form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: いる completes the 走っている form and modifies 車 that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the object toward which the action ぶつかる is directed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ぶつかりそうだった expresses an event that almost happened but did not actually happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.why: 走っている is a modifying clause for 車 and identifies which car. 車に combines with ぶつかる to indicate the object of the collision, while そうだった shows the risk that almost occurred in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It also expresses something that almost happened and often emphasizes the moment just before the action began.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses that something seems about to happen in the present or future, without the sense that it almost happened in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.tip: Do not understand そうだった as simply the past tense of a guess; in this pattern, it emphasizes an event that almost happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q7.kobun.cn: Vます語幹 + そうだった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vi: Everyone is waiting for contact from her, who lives in City A, where the earthquake occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the earthquake as the event that occurred in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 起こった creates a modifying clause for A市 and identifies the city where the earthquake occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where 彼女 lives.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 住んで connects with いる to form the progressive form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 住んでいる modifies 彼女 and shows that she lives in City A.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: からの indicates the sender of 連絡 and modifies this noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: が marks the message as the thing that is being awaited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: 待たれる is the passive form of 待つ, expressing that the message is being awaited by everyone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.why: The two clauses before it modify A市 and 彼女 in that order, identifying the place and the person being discussed. 連絡が is the grammatical subject of the main sentence, while 待たれる uses the passive form to emphasize that the message is being awaited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used instead, it would mean that the message is waiting, not that people are waiting for the message.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: It also means “is expected,” but it sounds more formal and focuses more on expectation than on the specific act of waiting for a message.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in A市に as “toward”; with 住む, に usually refers to the place where someone lives.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q8.kobun.cn: V五段: う段→あ段＋れる／V一段: るを取る＋られる／する→される／来る→こられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.vi: I want to become a person with lots of money like you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: みたいに turns a noun phrase into an adverbial comparison phrase that modifies なりたい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks お金 as the thing possessed in 持っている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: たくさん modifies 持っている and shows the amount of money.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 持って is the て form. It connects the main verb with いる to create the pattern 持っている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 持っている creates a modifying clause for 人, meaning “a person who currently has money.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: に marks the result or status that someone wants to become after なりたい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: なりたい expresses a desire, while なあ shows emotion or a wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.why: The phrase あなたみたいに comes first to state the person being compared with. The clause 持っている modifies 人, and then 人に なりたい expresses the wish to become such a person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with ように makes the expression more formal and stiff than みたいに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: のような must come before a noun, so say あなたのような人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put みたいに after the whole sentence, but this pattern must come before the thing being compared or the action being modified.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t23-q9.kobun.cn: N・V普通形 ＋ みたいに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vi: There are many umbrellas, aren't there? Which one is yours?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks umbrellas as things that exist in a large quantity.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: いっぱい modifies あります and shows the number of umbrellas.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: あります expresses existence, while ね adds a tone of confirmation or shared observation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing being asked about as the subject of です.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: の turns あなた into a possessive phrase that modifies the omitted noun after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: ですか creates a question asking which one belongs to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.why: The first sentence states the existence and number of umbrellas. In the second sentence, どれが is the selected item, while あなたの replaces あなたのかさ to avoid repeating the noun かさ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: The full expression means “is it your umbrella?”, while あなたのですか omits the noun because it is clear from the context.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This means “which one are you?”, so it asks about the wrong object because あなた must be the owner.
