default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q1.kobun.tip: の at the end of a phrase does not always mean のだ; here, it replaces a known noun and means “yours.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.vi: It seems that the library was closed last week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ N が ＋ N だったようだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the closed status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 休み is a noun used as the predicate, stating the library's status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: だった is the past form of noun＋だ. It combines with ようだ to make a guess about a past state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.why: The time is made the topic with は, while the library is the subject of the state, so が is used. Because 休み is a noun and the event belongs to the past, だった must be used before ようだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used instead, it would mean that someone told the speaker that the library was closed, not that the speaker is making a guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If this were used instead, the sentence would also mean that the speaker heard or had evidence that the library was closed, with a less direct tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.tip: With a noun before ようだ, you must use の or だった; do not connect Nようだ directly when you want to describe a past state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の／だった ＋ ようだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vi: I will give you the ticket later.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 時間 に ＋ お＋Vます omitます＋いたします
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the ticket is the object being mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows when the ticket will be given.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: お＋verb stem＋いたします is a humble way to describe the speaker's action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.cn: お＋Vます omitます＋いたします
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.why: The ticket is stated with は, and the time of giving it is marked with で. The phrase お渡しいたします uses a humble form to lower the speaker's action of giving the ticket and show politeness toward the receiver.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vs.0.t: お＋Vます omitます＋します
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used instead, the sentence would still be polite, but it would be less humble than いたします.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If this were used instead, the sentence would only have ordinary politeness and would not emphasize lowering the speaker's status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use おいたします directly with a verb; put お before the verb stem, and then add いたします.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vi: The way to read this kanji is very difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.sk: この N は ＋ Vます omitます＋方 が ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that this kanji is the object being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 読み方 is formed from the verb stem 読み＋方, while が marks this phrase as the subject of the adjective むずかしい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective むずかしい acts as the predicate, and です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.why: この漢字は sets the topic, while 読み方が is what is judged to be difficult. The verb 読む, with ます omitted, becomes 読み and joins with 方 to form a noun meaning “way of reading.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used instead, the sentence would say that performing the action is difficult, without emphasizing the method or way of reading.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If this were used instead, the pattern would mean that something should be done in a certain way, not that it is difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.kobun.tip: 方 in 読み方 must connect to the verb stem with ます omitted, not to the dictionary form 読む.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.vi: I showed my friend a photo of the mountain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Receiver に ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Vた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states who performs the action of showing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person affected, that is, the person shown the photo.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 山 with 写真 and shows that the photo is about the mountain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object that is shown.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 見せた is the past form of 見せる and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.why: The person performing the action is marked by は, the person shown the object uses に, and the object shown uses を. 山の modifies 写真, creating the phrase “a picture of the mountain” before it is placed as the object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with と, the meaning becomes that I looked at the picture with my friend, not that I showed it to my friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 山の is replaced with 友だちの, the picture belongs to your friend or is related to your friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.kobun.tip: With 見せる, the person shown the object uses に, while the object shown uses を; do not reverse these two particles.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vi: The day Mr./Ms. Tanaka comes is Tuesday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person performing the action 来る in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 来る comes before 日 to modify it, creating the meaning “the day when Mr./Ms. Tanaka comes.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the specified time the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the sentence that identifies the specific day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.why: 来る comes before 日 and modifies 日, so the whole phrase means “the day when Tanaka comes.” は marks that time phrase, and then です gives the identifying information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: のは turns the whole clause into a noun phrase and emphasizes that it is Tanaka’s coming that happens on Tuesday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: 来た refers to the day when Tanaka came in the past, while 来る refers to the day when Tanaka will come or usually comes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.kobun.tip: The clause 来る must come before 日; do not put 日 before 来る following English word order.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vi: Only people who made a reservation can enter that restaurant.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.sk: N は + Vた + N しか + negative potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the restaurant being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.2.vi: only people who made a reservation
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause よやくした modifies 人, while しか limits the subject and always goes with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 入れません is the negative potential form and completes the structure しか～ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.why: よやくした modifies 人 to form the group “people who made a reservation.” しか marks the only allowed range, so the predicate must be the negative form 入れません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: だけ also means “only,” but it does not require a negative predicate like しか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This sentence only says that people who made a reservation can enter; it does not emphasize that other people cannot enter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.tip: A common mistake is to use しか with an affirmative predicate; remember that しか always goes with the negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.kobun.cn: N・V普通形・Aい・Aなな + しか + Vない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vi: I went to buy a bag, but they were all expensive, so I could not buy one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.sk: N を + Vます omit ます に + 行ったが、 + 疑問詞 も + Aくて + negative past potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The form ます of 買います combines with に to show purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: どれ combines with も to include all the choices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective 高い changes to 高くて to connect a reason or condition to the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: 買えなかった is the negative past potential form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 + も; Aい → Aくて; negative past potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.why: 買いに行った shows the purpose of going. Then が creates a contrast, どれも shows that all the choices are expensive, and 高くて connects the reason to the result of being unable to buy one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: どれか means one of them, without including all the choices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: どれでも means any one is acceptable and emphasizes free choice, not that all of them share the same feature.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.kobun.tip: Do not translate どれも as “one of them”; in an affirmative sentence, どれも usually means “all of them.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.vi: I cannot go out because I have neither money nor time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.sk: Nも + Vないし、 + Nも + Vないから、 + N に + negative potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: も adds money to the list of things that are not available.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: し connects one reason to another and shows that there is an additional reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: も marks time as the second reason belonging to the same state of not having something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the reason to the result 行けない in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: に shows the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: 行けない is the negative potential form and states the result that I cannot go out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.why: The two reasons are listed with し and both use も to emphasize that they are unavailable. から connects the reason to the result 行けない, while 遊びに行く shows the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also shows a reason, but its tone is softer and more objective than から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: たり～たり is used to list representative actions or states, not to give several reasons like し.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit し from the first reason; when several reasons are listed, each reason is usually connected with し.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + し; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.vi: Which do you like better, playing sports or watching sports?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of both playing and watching sports.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns する into a noun, while と marks the first choice being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns 見る into a noun, and と marks the second choice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: どちらが asks which of the two choices has more of the feature 好き.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 好き is the adjective な, used to express preference and ending with the question form ですか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.why: の turns the two actions する and 見る into nouns so they can be placed side by side. The two choices are marked with と, and then どちらが asks which one suits 好き better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: どちらも means both, so it no longer asks which choice is preferred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern directly states that B is more than A, instead of asking an open question with どちらが.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use a verb directly before どちらが; turn it into a noun with の, then connect the two choices with と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.kobun.cn: Vるの + と + Vるの + と + どちらが + Aなですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.vi: I made the child do homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.sk: Causer は + person being made to act に + N を + past V使役
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who makes someone do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who is asked or made to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the action of doing homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: させた is the past form of the causative form, showing that someone made another person do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.cn: V1 ない → Vさせる; for V2, remove る ＋ させる; V3 する → させる・来る → 来させる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.why: わたしは is the person who causes or requests the action, while 子どもに is the person who directly does the homework. しゅくだいを keeps the particle を because the homework is the object of the action, and then させた expresses that the person was made to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: It means that I asked the child to do it or had the child help me. The meaning is softer and does not strongly emphasize force.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: It only says that the child did the homework independently. It does not show that I caused the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.kobun.tip: In the causative form, do not confuse the person who is made to act with the subjectが; with a transitive action, this person usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.tokens.6.m: made someone do; let someone do
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vi: That teacher's speech is too difficult for international students.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: あの and の both modify 話, identifying which teacher the speech belongs to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 話 the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に only indicates the person who experiences the quality, while は emphasizes the range used for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: すぎる follows an adjective to express a degree beyond what is suitable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.cn: Vます・Aい remove い・Aな remove な・N ＋ すぎる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.why: The sentence first presents the content being evaluated, then identifies the people who find that content difficult. に indicates the person being considered, while すぎる adds the meaning of exceeding the normal level.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence means “from the viewpoint of or for international students,” focusing more on the standpoint of the evaluation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If the adjective is used without すぎる, the sentence only means “difficult” and no longer has the meaning “too difficult.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that に in this pattern marks the person who experiences the quality, not the person who performs an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.vi: I am studying Japanese to work in Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where 働く takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: Vる＋ために connects the purpose to the main action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of 勉強する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb 勉強する with いる to form the progressive form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: いる shows that an action is in progress.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.why: The purpose phrase 働くために comes before the main action 日本語を勉強している. で identifies the place of work, while を marks Japanese as the object of study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ように, the sentence usually emphasizes a goal or a state to be reached rather than a direct purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put ために after the main action, but the purpose phrase must come before the action being performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.tokens.8.m: the て form of する
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.vi: I still have never read this manga.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: まだ modifies the whole sentence and shows that, up to the present, the experience has still not occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks マンガ as the object of 読む.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 読んだこと expresses an experience; the given sentence has 「だ」 in the position where 「が」 is normally used in a negative pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません denies the existence of that experience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.why: まだ is placed at the beginning of the sentence to limit the time up to the present. Vたことがありません turns the action of reading into a noun expressing experience, and then denies that the experience exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ことが with ことは emphasizes or contrasts the fact that this particular experience has never happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form in a pattern expressing past experience; use Vた before こと.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ことがある／ない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.vi: My mother was happy like a child because it was her first time flying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that mother is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: はじめて modifies the action of flying and shows that it was the first time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the vehicle or object that mother boards.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 乗って uses the て form to connect flying with the action of being happy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: Nの modifies ように, creating the object used for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: ように indicates a way of being happy that is like a child.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: よろこんだ is the main predicate in the past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.why: 乗って、 connects the earlier action with the emotion that follows. 子どものように comes before よろこんだ to describe how mother was happy through a comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ような is used, it must modify a noun and cannot directly modify the verb よろこんだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.kobun.tip: ように usually modifies a verb or adjective; do not use ような before a verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.vi: Because the shirt is dirty, I will wash it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the shirt as the subject that is in a dirty state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: よごれて is the て form of よごれる, connected to いる to express a resulting state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ている describes the current state, while から connects the reason to the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 洗います is the main action performed because the shirt is dirty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.why: シャツがよごれている states the condition that gives the reason. から connects that reason with the result or decision 洗います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので makes the reason softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.tip: With verbs showing a change of state, such as よごれる, ている usually describes a state that has already occurred, not necessarily one that is still happening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる; 普通形 ＋ から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.vi: I plan to quit smoking from tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.sk: Time から ＋ N を ＋ Vるつもりです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks cigarettes as the object of やめる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: Vる＋つもりです expresses the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.why: あしたから is placed before the action to identify the starting point. やめるつもりです turns quitting smoking into the speaker's plan or intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: 予定です focuses on a fixed schedule or plan, while つもりです emphasizes one's own intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.tip: つもり follows the plain form of a verb; it does not connect directly with やめます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ つもりだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.vi: If you have free time, please come and visit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks free time as the assumed condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: あったら is the たら form, connecting a condition to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the purpose of 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 来て is the て form. It combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes an invitation or request polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.cn: Vた＋ら; Aい removeい＋かったら; Aな＋だったら; N＋だったら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.why: The conditional clause あったら comes first and provides the basis for the invitation. あそびに来る with に shows the purpose, while 来てください is the polite invitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence has a more natural or necessary conditional meaning and is less suitable for an invitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.kobun.tip: たら is made from the past form, so あったら must be used instead of あるら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vi: My father has a very loud voice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the part or feature being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きい is an adjective describing the feature of 声.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q3.kobun.why: 父は is the main topic, while 声が is the specific feature belonging to the father. Therefore, が comes after the part that has the feature, and the adjective ends the description.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If の is used to show possession, the sentence focuses directly on “my father’s voice” instead of describing my father through that feature.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If を and する are used, the meaning becomes “my father makes his voice louder,” showing an active action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use を before 声 when saying that a person has a feature such as a loud voice, beautiful eyes, or long arms.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vi: You must not forget your promise to your friends.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects 友だち to the following noun, while の turns the whole phrase into a modifier for 約束.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the promise as the object of the action of forgetting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ては creates a prohibited condition when combined with いけません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: いけません completes the prohibition pattern わすれてはいけません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.why: The phrase describing the relationship with friends comes before 約束 to modify the promise. 約束を is the object of わすれる, and the form てはいけません turns that action into something prohibited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes a request saying “please do not forget,” with a softer meaning than a prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning is “it is okay to forget,” which is completely opposite to the original sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may incorrectly separate と and の; in a noun phrase, と connects the relationship, while の connects the whole phrase to the main noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q4.kobun.cn: N と ＋ の ＋ N; Vて ＋ は ＋ いけません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vi: Piano music is coming from the neighboring house.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows where the sound comes from.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の modifies 音 and shows that the sound belongs to the piano.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the sound being perceived in the pattern 音がする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: している describes sound that continues to be produced at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.why: The place where the sound comes from uses で, while the type of sound is identified by the phrase ピアノの音. 音がする describes the existence of a sound, and ている shows that the sound is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the focus is on the listener being able to hear the sound, without emphasizing that the sound is being produced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence clearly says that someone is playing the piano instead of only describing the sound.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.tip: Do not translate する mechanically as “do”; in 音がする, する means to produce or perceive a sound.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q5.kobun.cn: N が ＋ する; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vi: I study judo once a week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time period に ＋ Number of times ＋ N を ＋ Vている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who studies judo.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に connects a time period with a number of times to create a frequency expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 一回 shows how many times the action happens during the stated time period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the subject being studied as the object of 習う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 習っている describes an activity that has started and is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.cn: Time period ＋ に ＋ Number of times; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.why: The frequency phrase comes before the verb to show the repeated schedule of the action. Then judo is the object of 習う, while ている emphasizes the state of currently studying it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that I practice judo once a week, without emphasizing studying with a teacher or following a program.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is replaced with で, the expression becomes unnatural when describing a regular frequency.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q6.kobun.tip: In the frequency pattern, に comes after the time period; do not put に after the number of times.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vi: Please wash the vegetables well before cutting them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the vegetables as the object being washed and cut.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies 洗って and shows the degree of washing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: てから connects the completed action of washing with the action that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: てください turns 切る into a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.why: The vegetables are the shared object of both actions. てから requires a specific order: wash them first, and only then cut them; てください expresses the polite request at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is omitted, the sentence only connects the two actions without clearly emphasizing that the first action must be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with あとで, the meaning is still “after,” but it focuses more on the time after the action than on a smooth sequence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.tip: てから must attach to a verb in the て form; do not use the dictionary form directly, such as 洗うから, to say “after washing.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q7.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ から; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.vi: It says: “Do not throw rubbish here!”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the place where the prohibited action happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing being thrown away.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: Vる＋な creates a strong negative command; と marks the whole quoted prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て combines with ある to describe the remaining state created by the writing action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: ある combines with Vて and shows that the content has already been written and remains there.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.why: A place is used with に, and the affected object is used with を. Then the dictionary-form verb＋な creates a prohibition. The whole prohibition is put in quotation marks and connected with 書いてある to say that the content has already been written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the tone becomes more like a rule or a polite reminder, not as strong as Vる＋な.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes a request not to do something, which is softer than the prohibition on the sign.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse な here with な used for exclamation; in this pattern, な comes after Vる and means that the action is forbidden.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q8.kobun.cn: Vる ＋ な; Vて ＋ ある
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.vi: What do you plan to do after leaving the company?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of leaving or quitting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects leaving the job with the next action or plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: どう modifies する and asks how or what will be done next.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Vる＋つもりですか asks about the listener's plans; する is the dictionary form before つもり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.why: やめて connects leaving the company with the plan afterward. どう comes before する to ask specifically what the listener plans to do, while つもりですか turns the preceding action into a question about intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes a scheduled time or fixed plan more than personal intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the tone is softer and shows a current thought or plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use the ます form directly before つもり; use Vる or Vない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q9.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ つもりだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.vi: That art museum is always crowded, no matter when you go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 疑問 from ＋ Vて ＋ も ＋ N が ＋ Adv ＋ Vいる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies びじゅつかん to identify the museum being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the museum the general topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: いつ states the assumed time in the concessive clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 行っても uses the て form plus も to connect the idea that the following result occurs at any time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the people who are present in the museum.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: たくさん modifies the number of people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: います is an existence predicate used for people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.why: いつ goes with 行っても to form the clause "no matter when you go." This clause comes before the result 人がたくさんいます to emphasize that the result does not change with the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that the result is the same no matter which time you choose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 行くたびに, it means that the place is crowded every time you go, with more emphasis on repetition than concession.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 行くても, but the verb must change to the て form before adding も.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も; Aくて ＋ も; Aな・N ＋ でも
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.vi: Because I had a stomachache, I went to the hospital and was made to wait for a whole hour.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Aくて、 ＋ N へ ＋ Vたら、 ＋ Time も ＋ Vさせられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is painful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective いたい changes to いたくて to connect the cause with the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of travel to the hospital.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 行ったら connects a condition or time with the event in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: も follows a time period and emphasizes that the duration was longer than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 待たされた is the passive causative form, showing that the speaker was forced by someone else to wait.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.cn: Vない omitない ＋ させられる; V五段 can be shortened to the ない form omitない ＋ される
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.why: いたくて states the cause first, followed by へ marking the direction to the hospital. 行ったら sets the time point, while 待たされた at the end states the speaker's experience of being forced to wait.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 待たせた is used, the subject is the person who makes someone else wait, which is the opposite of the meaning that the speaker was forced to wait.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 待っていた is used, it only says that the person was waiting, without the sense of being forced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.vs.2.d: Adding そうだ changes the forced waiting into reported information or an inferred appearance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 待たせる and 待たされる; させられる shows the subject who experiences the force.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.vi: If you press here, the door will open.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the point that is pressed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb おす connects with と to state a natural result that occurs immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the object that undergoes the change naturally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 開く is an intransitive verb, describing the door opening by itself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.why: The phrase ここを identifies the point being pressed, and then おすと connects the action with a natural result. Because ドア opens by itself, が and the intransitive verb 開く are used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vると is used in an ordinary conditional sentence, the sense of a rule or certain result remains.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 開ける is used, the sentence means that someone opens the door because it is a transitive verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 開く for opening something; in this sentence, the door opens by itself, so 開く must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.vi: The teacher has already gone home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the teacher the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: もう modifies the action and shows that leaving has been completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: お＋the verb's plain form without ます＋になる creates respectful language for the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.why: 先生は is the topic, while もう identifies the time when the action was completed. The structure お帰りになる is used because the person performing the action is the teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 帰りました is used, the sentence is only normally polite and does not show respect for the subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 帰られました is used, the sentence is still honorific, but its tone is simpler than お帰りになりました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use お帰りしました when talking about an action by a respected person; しました can easily become humble language.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.kobun.cn: お＋Vます語幹＋になる／ご＋Nサ変＋になる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.vi: This time, it has been decided that I will return to my country.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: 今度 indicates the time or occasion about to be mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the destination of 帰る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 帰る in the dictionary form modifies こと and turns the whole action of returning home into a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ことに is the connecting part in the pattern Vることになる, expressing a decision or an established result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました shows that a new decision or situation has been formed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.why: 帰ること turns returning to one's country into the content of the decision. ことになる emphasizes that the decision or result was formed because of circumstances, not only personal desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ことにする, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker made the decision personally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 予定だ is used, the sentence only states a plan or intention and does not emphasize that it has been decided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.tip: Do not simply translate ことになる as “will”; this pattern often implies that a decision or result has already been arranged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形＋ことになる／Vない＋ことになる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.vi: I tried every possible way, but I still cannot find it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: いろいろ modifies さがした and shows that the search was done in many ways.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects an action that was done with a result contrary to expectations.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 見つからない is the negative form of the intransitive verb 見つかる, while んです adds an explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.why: The clause さがしたのに creates the expectation that the item will be found, but 見つからない states the opposite result. んです is used to explain this situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced by ので, the sentence expresses the causal relationship “because I searched in many ways...,” and no longer has a contrasting meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If ても is used, the sentence emphasizes “even if one does...,” as a concessive condition, with a different tone from disappointment about the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse のに with ので because both follow a clause; remember that のに means “even so,” while ので means “because.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Naな・Nな＋のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.vi: My room is not as wide as my older sister's room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase わたしのへや is the topic, and は is used to compare it with my room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ほど marks the object used as the comparison standard in a negative degree pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 広い changes to 広くない to express a negative degree of width.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.why: The object being compared is placed before は, while the standard is placed before ほど. The negative predicate means “not reaching the same level as” that standard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If より is used, the sentence directly says “wider than...,” while ほど～ない emphasizes being unequal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 同じくらい is used, the sentence means nearly the same or at the same level, which is opposite to the negative meaning in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.tip: Do not place ほど after the topic; ほど must come after the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.kobun.cn: N＋ほど＋Aいくない／N＋ほど＋Naではない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.vi: He read the same novel as many as five times.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ Number ＋ も ＋ Vた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks him as the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 同じ modifies 小説, showing that it is the same novel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the novel that was read.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The number ５回 combines with も to emphasize a surprisingly high number of times.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 読んだ is the casual past form of 読む, showing that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.why: 小説を is the object of the reading action, while ５回も comes before the verb and modifies its frequency. も replaces the usual way of marking a number and adds emphasis.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is omitted, the sentence simply states the number of readings in a neutral way, without emphasizing that it is many.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If ５回しか読まなかった is used, the sentence means that it was read only five times, suggesting that this is a small number.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand も as “also,” but after a number it usually emphasizes the meaning “as many as” or “as much as.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who caused the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing taken in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb とる changes to the passive form とられる and then to the past form とられた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.kobun.why: The affected person is understood to be me, while だれかに marks the person who caused the action. さいふを is the affected object and comes before the passive verb とられた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning becomes that someone took it for me or helped me, so it no longer expresses harm.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern usually expresses indirect passive meaning and emphasizes that the speaker is affected by another person's action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the particles に and を, but に marks the person who caused the action, while を marks the affected object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.kobun.cn: N1 は ＋ N2 に ＋ N3 を ＋ V受身形
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.vi: It is okay not to bring a camera.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the camera the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of 持つ connects with 来る to create the compound verb 持って来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.2.vi: even if one does not bring it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 来る changes to the negative form 来なく, then connects with ても to mean that it is okay not to do the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: かまいません is the final part of a pattern expressing permission not to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.why: The topic is the camera, and the unnecessary action is placed before なくてもかまいません. 持って来る is divided into 持って and 来なくても to negate the entire action of bringing it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the basic meaning is still “it is not necessary to do it,” but the tone is usually shorter and more casual.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence changes to mean that one must bring the camera.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that the negative form of 来る is 来なく, not 来ない, when connecting with ても.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ なくても ＋ かまわない／かまいません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.vi: This restaurant always has many people waiting in line, doesn't it?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies レストラン to identify the restaurant being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the restaurant the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: いつも modifies the state of waiting in line and shows frequent occurrence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies 人 and shows the number of people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the people who are in the state of waiting in line.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: ならぶ is used with ている to express the continuing state of waiting in line.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.6.n: ね is used at the end of a sentence to seek agreement or confirmation from the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.why: レストランは is the topic, while 人が is the subject of the state of waiting in line. いつも and たくさん modify frequency and quantity respectively, and then ならんでいます states the current condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is that someone is lining up or arranging objects, because it is a transitive verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence only describes the action or habit of lining up and does not emphasize that it is continuing now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ならべる instead of ならぶ, but ならぶ means lining up by oneself, while ならべる means arranging something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.vi: Can Japanese money be used at this store?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies 店 to identify the store being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で marks the place where the money is used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects 日本 with お金 to create the phrase “Japanese money.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the object that can possibly be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 使う changes to the potential form 使える and then takes the polite form 使えます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: か changes a statement into a question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.why: この店で identifies the location, while 日本のお金が is the object that can be used. The potential form 使えます comes before か to ask whether the action is possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence only asks whether someone uses it, not whether its use is possible or allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence asks for permission to use it, which is different from asking whether it can be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate が as “yes,” but here が marks the object in a sentence using the potential form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.kobun.cn: Vる → Vえる／Vられる; V可能形 ＋ か
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.vi: I hear that there will be a festival near my house next week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の ＋ Location で ＋ N が ＋ V普通形 ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: らいしゅう indicates when the festival will take place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects うち with 近く to create the phrase “the area near my house.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で marks the location where the event will take place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks an existing or occurring event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: ある is an existence verb used for lifeless things or events.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです comes after the plain form to pass on information that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.why: The time and place come before the event おまつりがある. そうです follows ある to show that this is reported information, not the speaker's direct judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the meaning is that something seems about to happen or looks that way, not that the speaker heard it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence still means that the information was heard, but the tone is less direct and more speculative.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the two types of そうだ, so remember that あるそうです means “I hear that it will happen,” while ありそうです means “it seems that it will happen.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうだ／そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.vi: Because I practiced every day, I became able to swim.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Vたので、＋ V可能形 ＋ ように ＋ なる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 shows the frequency of the practice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause clause to the result, and れんしゅうした is the past form of the practice action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.2.vi: to the point of being able to swim
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ように with the potential form およげる shows the ability state aimed for after the change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました describes a change that was achieved before now and continues to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.why: The clause with ので states the cause, while およげるようになりました states the result: the ability has changed. ように connects the target state with なる to express the process of becoming able to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were replaced, the sentence would describe a decision or result that has been arranged, without emphasizing a change in the speaker's ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were replaced, the sentence would express the intention to try to create that state, without confirming that it has been achieved.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use およぐようになりました, but when saying that someone has become able to swim, they need to use the potential form およげる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形・可能形 ＋ ように ＋ なる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.vi: Even if you study a foreign language, you will forget it if you do not speak it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of studying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: て form ＋ も creates a concessive condition, meaning even if someone does something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The form ない changes to なければ to create a condition meaning if someone does not do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: て form connects the verb わすれる with しまいます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: しまう expresses completion, often with a feeling of regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.why: The phrase 勉強しても states a concessive situation, while 話さなければ states a negative condition. The result わすれてしまいます is placed at the end of the sentence to emphasize completely forgetting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were used here, the sentence would mean that it is okay even if someone does not speak, instead of meaning that they will forget if they do not speak.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ないと is used, the conditional meaning is more natural and conversational, and less formal than なければ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake なければ for a simple negative form, but it means if someone does not do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.vi: My son does nothing but play every day and does not study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ Vて ＋ ばかりで ＋ N を ＋ Vない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎日 shows the frequency of the action 遊ぶ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: あそんで is the て form, which connects with ばかりで to express doing only one thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ばかり limits the action, while で connects it to an opposite result or comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object of しない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: しない is the negative form of する, stating that the action is not performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ばかりいる／ばかりで ＋ clause; N ＋ ばかり
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.why: 毎日 comes before the verb to state frequency, while あそんでばかりで emphasizes doing only one thing. The following clause uses しない to state the action that is neglected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It only describes a state of doing something now or regularly, without the meaning of “doing nothing but” in ばかり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It can mean “just need to do,” and usually does not have a strong complaining tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ばかりで as “because,” but here it means “doing nothing but.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.vi: Do you know who wrote this book?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the unknown subject in an embedded question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of 書いた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 書いた is the past form and serves as the predicate of the question clause before か.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: か changes the question clause into information that is known or unknown.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: 知って is the て form of 知る, connecting with います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: 知っていますか creates a polite question about whether the information is known.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.why: The question of who wrote the book is placed inside a clause ending with か. Then 知っていますか asks whether the listener knows this unknown information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used for yes-or-no questions, not directly with question words such as だれ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses the speaker's thought or guess instead of asking whether the listener knows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put か at the end of the whole sentence, but in this pattern か comes immediately after the embedded question clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 ＋ 普通形 ＋ か ＋ 知っている／分かる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.vi: The airplane flew across the sky from east to west.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を indicates the space that the subject flies through.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: から marks the starting point of the movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the action of flying with 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: 行く expresses continued movement in the stated direction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.why: 空を combines with verbs of movement to state the space flown through. から and へ arrange the starting point and destination direction, while とんで connects with 行きました to create a sequence of actions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 空で飛ぶ were used, it would emphasize the place where the action happens and would be less natural than 空を飛ぶ when talking about flying across the sky.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If まで were used, it would emphasize the range extending to the west, while へ only indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で with 空, but movement through a space usually uses を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.vi: K's apartment is near the station.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects K with the following noun to show possession.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the apartment the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the place used as the reference point for judging distance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 近い is an adjective ending in い and serves as the predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.why: The structure は ... に近い takes the apartment as the thing being described and the station as the distance reference point. The adjective 近い comes at the end to finish the statement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 駅の近く were used, it would mean the area near the station, not directly say that the apartment is near the station.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 駅から近い were used, it would also mean near the station, but would emphasize the distance measured from the station.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say 駅を近い, but 近い needs a place as the reference point together with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.vi: My child likes listening to scary stories.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.sk: N の + N は + Aい + N を + Vwithoutます + たがる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の modifies こども, giving the meaning of children belonging to the speaker's family.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the child as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective こわい comes before 話 to modify the story.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content being heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞き is the verb stem and connects to たがる to express an observable desire in another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.cn: Vます withoutます + たがる/たがっている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.why: こわい directly modifies 話, so it comes before the noun. 聞きたがる places the child's desire in the predicate and uses たがる because the subject is someone other than the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 聞きたい, it usually expresses the speaker's desire or the desire of the person being addressed directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 聞きそうだ is used, it means that the person seems about to listen, not that they want to listen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use たい for every subject, but when expressing another person's desire, たがる is usually used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.tokens.8.m: want to; show a desire to
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.vi: I hear that those two people will get married next year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Vる + らしいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the two people as the topic of the information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The time expression comes before the action to state when the marriage will take place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form する comes before らしい to make the content that is guessed or reported.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: らしいです ends the sentence with a tone of heard information or a well-supported guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.why: らいねん adds the time to けっこんする. The verb in the plain form comes directly before らしい because the whole marriage information is being reported.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with そうです, the meaning clearly leans more toward information heard directly from some source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If しそうです is used, it means that the people seem likely to get married soon based on current signs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.tip: Learners may easily place らしい after a time noun, but this pattern must come after the whole content that is heard or guessed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + らしいです; N + らしいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vi: My father often says interesting things that make everyone laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies my father as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: こと is modified by おもしろい, and the whole phrase is the object of 言う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the action of speaking with the result of making everyone laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the person affected by the causative action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: わらう changes to the causative form わらわせる, meaning to make or cause someone to laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.cn: 五段V: sound う → sound あ + せる・一段V: remove る + させる・する → させる・来る → こさせる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.why: The sentence makes my father the subject, then connects the speaking action with て. The causative verb at the end shows that my father's words cause everyone to perform the action of laughing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～てもらう, it would mean that the father receives help or permission for someone to laugh, without emphasizing making the other person laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ようにする is used, the sentence describes trying to make something happen, not directly making another person act.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.kobun.tip: Learners may easily understand みんなを as the person who laughs, but in the causative form that person is marked by を because they are affected by the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.vi: You must not enter this room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies へや.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place that the subject enters.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 入って is the て form and combines with は to create a prohibition pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: いけません in this pattern means that the previous action is not allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.why: The place へやに comes before the action 入って. The て form combines with はいけません to turn entering the room into a prohibited action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning changes to must do it, which is the opposite of not being allowed to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also asks someone not to do something, but it sounds more like a polite request than a prohibition rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.tip: Learners may easily mistake 入ってはいけません for meaning that entering is bad, but the whole phrase has the fixed meaning of must not enter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.kobun.cn: Vて + は + いけない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.vi: Walk straight, following the person in front.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.sk: Nの + Nに + Vて + Adv + Vwithoutます + なさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 前 with 人 to indicate the person in front.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person whom the speaker follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: つづいて is the て form and connects the action of following with the command to walk straight.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: まっすぐ modifies 歩き and shows how to walk.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 歩き is the verb stem without ます and combines with なさい to create an instruction or a mild command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.cn: Vて +; Vwithoutます + なさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.why: The person being followed goes with に, then つづいて connects to the main action. まっすぐ modifies 歩き, while なさい comes at the end to turn the sentence into an instruction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If てください is used, the speech is more polite and more like a request than the direct instruction with なさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern expresses an obligation to do something, not a direct request to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.kobun.tip: Learners may easily attach なさい to the dictionary form, but they must use the verb stem without ます: 歩きなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.vi: Today, I was praised by my teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates when the action happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は identifies the person affected and makes the speaker the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ほめる changes to the passive form ほめられる and takes the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.why: The person affected is marked with は, while the person performing the action goes with に. The verb uses the passive form to express that I received the action of being praised.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it means to make or force someone to praise, so it no longer means to be praised.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This form is still passive but removes the polite tone of ほめられました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.tip: Learners may easily mistake に in a passive sentence for the object, but here に indicates the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.kobun.cn: Vる → Vられる; Vない → Vられない; Vた → Vられた; Vなかった → Vられなかった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.vi: I think continuing the work is impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of つづける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the action つづける into a noun, while は makes the whole action the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the quoted judgment before 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 思う is the main verb and expresses the speaker's thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.why: The action つづける is nominalized with の so that it can be the topic with は. The content of the thought is むりだ, which comes before と, and then 思う expresses the speaker's thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 思う is replaced with 言う, the sentence changes from an opinion in the mind to words spoken aloud.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: むりで cannot connect directly to と 思う because the plain form むりだ is needed before と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.tip: Learners may easily omit だ after the adjective な or the noun before と 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ と 思う; Aな・N ＋ だと 思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.vi: Smoking too much is not good.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects タバコ to the noun that follows, forming a phrase about smoking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: すいすぎ means smoking beyond a suitable level, while は makes it the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: よくない gives the main judgment, while よ emphasizes information that the listener should remember.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.cn: Vます語幹・Aい語幹・Aな語幹 ＋ すぎる; when used as a noun, ＋ すぎ can be used
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.why: すいすぎ shows that the amount of smoking is over the limit. Then は makes this situation the topic, which is judged with よくない. の connects タバコ to the action of smoking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If すいすぎる is used, it directly describes the action of smoking too much, not a noun used as the topic like すいすぎは.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with すっては, the sentence can change to a prohibition or warning meaning that smoking is not allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the plain form すう before すぎる, but they must use the form without ます, which is すい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.vi: I will throw it away later, so please gather the trash in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates when the trash will be thrown away.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I will throw it away
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason clause to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the object being gathered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 集めて connects with おく and shows that the trash is gathered beforehand to prepare for a later action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.why: Clause すてるから gives the reason first, followed by the request to gather the trash. ておく shows that the gathering is done beforehand to prepare for throwing it away later.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If おいて is removed, only the request to gather the trash remains, without the meaning of doing it in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If てあります is used, it emphasizes that the trash has already been gathered, not that it is a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change おく to おいて before ください in the pattern for asking someone to do something in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ おく; Vて ＋ おいて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.vi: Please return this book by the day after tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.sk: N は ＋ time noun ＋ までに ＋ Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before 本 to modify it and indicate the book near the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the book the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action of returning it must be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the verb 返す with ください to create a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.why: The book is stated as the topic, while the deadline comes before the action of returning it. 返して ください express a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If までに is replaced with まで, it means returning it up to the day after tomorrow, without emphasizing that it must be completed before the deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This is still a request to return the book, but it does not state a completion deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse までに with まで and leave out に when they want to express a deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 疑問詞 ＋ でも ＋ potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who can perform the action of sleeping.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: どこ combines with でも to indicate every place without limitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ねる changes to the potential form ねられる and is conjugated politely as ねられます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.why: どこでも works as an unlimited place adverb, while ねられます shows the ability to sleep. は identifies the person with this ability as わたし.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with どこか, it means sleeping somewhere, not anywhere.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it means not being anywhere at all.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse どこでも, meaning anywhere, with どこか, meaning somewhere.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 ＋ でも ＋ V; N ＋ でも ＋ V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: もっと modifies the degree of 大きい and means “even larger.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 大きい is an adjective that modifies 字, while もっと increases the degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the method or form used to perform the action of writing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 書いて is the て form, which connects the verb 書く with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください is used to politely ask the listener to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.why: もっと大きい modifies 字 to state a request about the size of the letters. 字で indicates the form used for writing, while Vてください comes at the end to express a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with を, 字 becomes the object being written and no longer means “in letters” as it does in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If 字で is replaced with ペンで, the writing tool is stated as a pen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse で with を because both can come after a noun, but で here indicates the method, while を indicates the object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the helpful action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the task that the friend helps you do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: てつだって is the て form of てつだう, and it connects with くれた to create a structure for receiving help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてくれた shows that someone did the action for the speaker or someone in the speaker’s group.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.why: 友だちが is the person who performs the action, while そうじを is the task being helped with. The て form connects てつだう with くれた and shows the benefit that the speaker receives from the friend’s action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてもらった is used, the focus shifts to the speaker receiving help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてあげた is used, the speaker or someone in the speaker’s group is the person who helps someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand くれた only as “give,” but in Vてくれた it describes another person doing something beneficial for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くれる・くれます・くれた・くれました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.vi: Teacher Yamada always reads books that look difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Adv ＋ Aい without い ＋ そうな ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states Teacher Yamada as the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: むずかしい removes い and adds そうな to modify the noun 本.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the book as the object of reading.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: て is the connecting form of 読む and connects it with います to express an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: います combines with Vて to express an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.cn: Aい without い ＋ そうだ・Aな ＋ そうだ・Vます without ます ＋ そうだ; before a noun, use そうな
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.why: むずかしそうな comes directly before 本 because it is a clause modifying the book. The phrase 読んでいます at the end of the sentence shows that the reading is continuing and happens regularly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If the hearsay form is used, the sentence means that the book is said to be difficult, not that it looks difficult from seeing it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ～ような, the nuance becomes “like” or “seems,” and is less direct than the outward impression expressed by ～そうな.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use むずかしいそうな to say that something seems difficult; with the adjective い, remove い before そうな.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.vi: There are only 5 minutes left. Let's hurry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: あと modifies the remaining period of time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: しか limits the remaining amount and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: ありません is the negative form of ある, completing the pattern しか～ない with the meaning “only ... left.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 急ぎましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite or urge someone to act together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.why: あと ５分 states the remaining amount of time, while しか emphasizes that this amount is small and that there is no more. Because しか requires a negative form, the predicate uses ありません; the next sentence uses ましょう to suggest that we hurry together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If だけ is used, it only states the limit “only five minutes,” and the required negative meaning is lost.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If ごろ is used, it means “about five minutes,” so it no longer means “only five minutes left.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that しか must always be used with a negative predicate such as ない or ありません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.vi: I will personally deliver the luggage next Monday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ N の ＋ Time に ＋ お ＋ Vます語幹 ＋ いたします
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 荷物 the topic of the announcement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who directly delivers the luggage.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects らいしゅう with 月曜日, forming the noun phrase “next Monday.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates when the delivery will take place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: おとどけいたします is a humble expression that lowers the speaker's action when serving the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.cn: お＋Vます語幹＋いたす・いたします; Sino-Japanese nouns usually use ご＋N＋いたす
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.why: は states that the luggage is the topic, while が identifies the person responsible for delivery. The phrase らいしゅうの月曜日に clearly states the time, and お～いたします is used to speak humbly about the speaker's action.
