default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If おとどけします is used, it is still polite, but it is less humble than いたします.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If おとどけになります is used, the respected action belongs to the listener or another person, not the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use お～いたします with every verb, but this pattern is used only when the subject is the speaker or someone on the speaker's side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.ch.0.vi: in a way suitable for a student
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: らしく turns 学生 into an adverb, modifying a way of studying that suits the role of a student.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: もっと modifies 勉強しなさい, asking someone to study more or work harder.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: しなさい is used to give an order or reminder, often to a younger person or a subordinate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.why: 学生らしく sets the standard for the action based on the learner's role. もっと comes before the verb to increase the degree, while しなさい ends the sentence with a reminder that has an imperative tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 学生として is used, it means “as a student,” which is more neutral and does not emphasize being suitable for the image of a student.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If 学生のように is used, it means “like a student,” focusing on comparison rather than asking for behavior suitable for the role.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate らしく as “like,” but in this sentence it emphasizes behavior that suits the person's nature or role.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.kobun.cn: N ＋ らしく・らしい・らしくない; Vます語幹 ＋ らしい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.vi: If Mr. or Ms. Kobayashi comes, be sure to let me know.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action of coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 来たら is the た form of 来る, connected with ら to create the condition “if or when someone comes.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: かならず modifies 知らせてください, emphasizing that the message must not be missed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who receives the information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 知らせて is the て form of 知らせる, connected with ください to create a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてください expresses a polite request to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first to state the time or condition for the main action. に marks the person who receives the information, while Vてください at the end of the sentence turns the request to give information into a polite favor.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 来ると is used, it means that whenever Kobayashi comes, the result naturally follows, so it is less suitable for a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If 来るなら is used, it means something close to “if he plans to come or if he is indeed going to come,” based on information already known.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand 来たら as past tense, but in a conditional pattern it often refers to something that will happen first or sets a condition for a later action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ら; Aいかったら; Aなだったら・なら; Nだったら・なら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.kobun.vi: They are international students from Asia.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the people being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: からの connects アジア with the noun that follows to describe its origin.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence and states the identity of the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.kobun.why: かれらは is the topic, and アジアからの modifies りゅうがくせい. The structure からの turns the origin アジア into a modifier for the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes the people who came from Asia through the action 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate からの as a separate verb, but here it only forms a modifying phrase for the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.vi: Could someone please close the window for me?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: か comes after an interrogative word and turns だれ into an indefinite person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object affected by the action of closing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb uses the て form to connect with ください and create a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ください makes the statement a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.why: だれか is the unidentified subject of the request, while まどを is the object of 閉める. The て form connects with ください to express a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, だれも is usually used with a negative form and means no one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use だれも with an affirmative sentence to mean someone; the indefinite form must use だれか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 ＋ か；Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka was late for the meeting, so the director reprimanded him.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.sk: N1 は ＋ N に ＋ Vて ＋ N2 に ＋ passive V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Mr. Tanaka is the person affected in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the event for which the person was late.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the situation of being late with what happened afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 注意する changes 注意された into the passive form, showing that Tanaka was reprimanded by the director.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.cn: 五段V: sound う → sound あ ＋ れる・一段V: remove る ＋ られる・する → される・来る → こられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.why: Tanaka is the affected person, so he is the topic marked with は. The person performing the passive action is the director, so he is marked with に; おくれて connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～てもらう is used, it means that Tanaka had someone remind him, emphasizing receiving the action rather than experiencing a passive action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～させられる is used, it means being forced to perform an action, not being reprimanded by someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person performing the action usually uses に, not を as in an active sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vi: I do not know where Mr. Kobayashi went.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: か changes the question どこへ行った into an indirect question clause that gives the content being known.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりません is the main predicate and takes the preceding question clause as its content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.why: どこへ行ったか is a question embedded in a larger sentence, so it does not end with a question mark. か comes after the whole clause to mark the unknown content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～かどうか is used, the sentence asks whether something is true or not. It is used for yes-or-no questions, not for asking about a place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～とわかる is used, the preceding part is usually information or a conclusion that has already been established, not a question containing a question word.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.tip: In an indirect question, keep the question word such as どこ and add か at the end of the clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 + V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + か + わかる/知る
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vi: Please write the report with a pen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the report as the object that is requested to be written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the tool or means used to carry out the action of writing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: て is the connecting form that links 書く with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ください is placed after Vて to ask the listener to carry out the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.why: レポートは is the topic, ペンで indicates the tool, and 書いてください is the complete request phrase. The particle で is suitable because a pen is the means used for writing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ペンで is replaced with ペンに, the sentence will no longer correctly express the tool used for writing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書きなさい is used, the sentence has a stronger command-like tone and is usually spoken by someone in a higher position.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.2.d: If 書いていただけませんか is used, the request will be more polite and softer than てください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に with the meaning “by,” but the tool used to carry out an action must go with で.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.vi: If you keep watching TV all day, your eyesight will get worse.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action of watching.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 見て is the て form, which connects the verb to ばかりいる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ばかり emphasizes that the subject keeps repeating only one action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes an ongoing state, and と connects the condition with a result that usually occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject whose condition changes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the く form to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: なります expresses a change; よ is used to emphasize the reminder.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.why: The object テレビを comes before the action 見て. The pattern てばかりいると expresses repeatedly doing one action, and then と connects it to the natural result that the eyes get worse.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with だけ, the sentence only limits the meaning to watching TV, so the critical tone about repeatedly doing it becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If ばかり is removed, the sentence only means that the eyes will get worse while watching TV; it does not emphasize watching TV all the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget that ばかり must come after the て form and before いる. In this pattern, do not say Vるばかりいる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + ばかり + いると
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.vi: Which bus goes past the library?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects としょかん with まえ to create a noun phrase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the place that the bus passes, not an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 通る comes before and modifies バス.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: は states that the bus is the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: どれ asks which choice; ですか creates a polite question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.why: The phrase としょかんのまえを通る is a clause that modifies バス, so 通る comes directly before the noun バス. The particle を indicates the route or place that the bus passes through.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Nで通る usually emphasizes the vehicle or method used to pass through, not only the route location.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Nに行く means going to a place, unlike を通る, which means passing through that place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に with a place that is passed, but を is used to indicate the route or place passed through.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.vi: The camera I bought yesterday was stolen from me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう indicates the time of the action of buying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The past clause 買った modifies カメラ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing stolen in a passive sentence showing harm.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ぬすまれて is the て passive form, which connects with しまいました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいました expresses something that happened unwillingly and caused regret.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.why: 買った comes before カメラ to identify which camera it is. The passive construction showing harm uses カメラをぬすまれて and shows that the speaker suffers trouble even though they are not the direct object of the stealing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence only reports that the camera was stolen and places less emphasis on the harm to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This sentence means that the subject stole the camera, making the subject the person who carried out the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate and use the passive as if the camera must be the subject, but the passive construction showing harm often uses Nを to state the thing that causes trouble for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Vられる + てしまう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.vi: I drank as many as ten bottles of beer last night, so I have a headache.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.sk: Time は + N を + Quantity も + Vたので、N が + Aい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that last night is the time frame for the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the drink that was consumed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: も comes after a quantity to emphasize an unexpectedly large amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲んだ is the past form; ので connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: いたい is the predicate describing pain in the head.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.cn: Quantity + も; V普通形 + ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.why: The quantity 10本 is placed before も to emphasize drinking an unusually large amount. The cause clause comes before 飲んだので, while the result, a headache, comes after the comma.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If だけ is used, the sentence only limits the amount to ten bottles and may imply that it was not more than that.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes drinking only ten bottles and often carries the feeling that the amount was less than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may understand も as “also,” but after a quantity it can emphasize the meaning “as many as” or “as much as.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.kobun.vi: As for the gift, let’s choose flowers.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the gift as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the result of the choice in the pattern Nにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form of する, used to invite someone or suggest making a decision together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.kobun.cn: N + にする; remove ます from Vます + ましょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.kobun.why: プレゼントは sets the range of choices, while 花に states the chosen option. しましょう turns that decision into a suggestion to do it together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this, it means making a direct decision, with less of an inviting tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.kobun.tip: When choosing an option, Vietnamese learners may easily confuse にする with をする; this pattern uses Nにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.tokens.4.m: let’s do it; let’s do it together
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.kobun.vi: Because it is convenient, I often use a computer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: With the adjective な, べんり must add な before ので to connect the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies 使います and shows the frequency of use.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the tool or thing being used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first, followed by the frequency, the object, and the main verb. べんり is an な adjective, so な is needed before ので, creating a soft and objective way to state the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with から, the sentence still means “because,” but the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget な in べんりなので; the adjective な always needs な before ので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい + ので; Aな・N + な + ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.vi: The wind will probably be strong tomorrow too.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing the speaker’s guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: も is placed after a time point to include tomorrow in the range of the prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has the state 強い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: An adjective ending in い keeps its original form and combines with だろう to express a guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.why: たぶん is placed at the beginning to signal a guess. 風が is the subject with the state 強い, while だろう comes at the end to turn the statement into a prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with かもしれない, the sentence is still a prediction, but the level of uncertainty is usually higher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners easily change 強い to 強く before だろう, but an adjective ending in い must keep its original form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだろう・Nだろう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.vi: You must brush your teeth before going to bed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The dictionary form of a verb comes before まえに to show that the action happens first.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: まえに connects with the verb before it and creates a time point before another action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb that emphasizes that the action is required.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of brushing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb みがく changes to the ない form, and then ない changes into なくては to connect with the obligation pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: いけません completes the pattern なくてはいけません, expressing that something must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.why: 寝るまえに sets the time point for the main action. 歯をみがかなくてはいけません uses a negative form together with いけません to express the obligation to brush one’s teeth.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with てはいけません, the sentence means that one must not brush one’s teeth.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with なければなりません, the obligation keeps almost the same meaning but sounds more formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake なくてはいけません for meaning that something must not be done, but this pattern actually means that it must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.kobun.cn: Vない形のない → なくては + いけない／いけません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.vi: The house burned down, and there were also injured people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.sk: N も + linking V + Vた + N も + Vました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: も marks the house as an event added alongside another event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 焼け is the linking form of 焼ける, used to connect two consecutive events.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause けがをした comes before 人 to modify the person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds the injured people to the list of events that occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 出ました is the main predicate, showing that the injured people appeared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.why: 焼け connects two events in the same sentence. も is repeated after 家 and 人 to emphasize that, in addition to the house burning, injured people also appeared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is replaced with は, the sentence only states that injured people are the topic and loses the added-event nuance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used, 人が出ました only identifies the subject and does not emphasize “also” or “in addition.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically translate も as “also,” but in this sentence it also suggests an additional noteworthy event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.vi: Because Dad seems angry, please stay quiet while doing it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Dad is the topic of the prediction clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: そうです expresses appearance or an imminent prediction, while から connects this clause to the reason for the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects a manner or accompanying action with the action at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: お＋なさいます creates a respectful expression for the action of the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.why: The first clause states a condition that seems about to happen, and から shows the reason. 黙って connects the manner with the following action, while おなさいます uses honorific language to elevate the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with お～になります, this is also honorific, but it emphasizes the higher-status person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with いたします, the speaker lowers their own action instead of showing respect to someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use なさる for their own action, while this honorific is mainly used for the action of the respected person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q14.kobun.cn: Vます語幹 + そうだ／そうです; お＋Vます語幹＋なさる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.vi: I hear that this river is as deep as 10 meters.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.sk: N は + N が + quantity も + ある + そうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the river being described the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 深さ is a noun meaning depth, and が marks the stated measurement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: も emphasizes the large size of the number 10 meters.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: ある expresses the existence of a quantity or level.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです comes after the plain form to report information that the speaker has heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.why: は states the river, while 深さが shows the measured quantity. １０メートルもある emphasizes the great depth; そうです adds that the information was heard from someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: ようです shows that the speaker is making a guess based on signs, not necessarily reporting information they heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: らしいです can also report information that was heard, but it usually keeps some distance from the information’s certainty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.tip: そうです means “I hear that” and must come after the plain form; it is not used directly after a noun or a polite-conjugated verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.vi: I have also read the book that the teacher wrote.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the writing action in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern お～になった is honorific, and the entire clause before 本 modifies the book.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 本 is the noun modified by the preceding clause, and は presents it as the topic of the main sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: も replaces は to add the speaker to the group of people who performed the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 拝見いたしました is humble language, lowering the speaker's reading action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.why: 先生がお書きになった comes before 本 to identify which book. The main sentence takes 本 as its topic, adds 私も as the person who performed the action, and uses 拝見いたしました to speak humbly about the speaker's action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern honors another person's action, as in お書きになった in the clause about the teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern humbles the speaker's action, with the same function as 拝見いたしました in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use honorifics for both sides, but they must distinguish お～になる, which honors another person, from 拝見いたす, which lowers the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.kobun.cn: お + Vます語幹 + になる; 拝見する → 拝見いたす
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.vi: Even an elementary school student can solve a problem this simple.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.sk: こんな + Aな な + N は + N でも + potential V よ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective ending in な to the noun 問題.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: は states the problem being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: でも presents 小学生 as an extreme example, meaning “even”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: できる expresses ability, while よ emphasizes the information the speaker wants to convey.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.why: The phrase 問題は places the topic first, and then 小学生でも presents the subject used as an emphasized example. The predicate できる shows that the problem is within that subject's ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If でも is replaced with だけ, the meaning becomes “only elementary school students,” which is opposite to the emphasis “even.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse でも in this sentence with the meaning “but,” although it means “even.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.kobun.cn: Aな + な + N; N + でも
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.vi: While I am in Japan, I want to visit an old friend once.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.sk: N に + Vている + あいだに + Nの + N を + number of times + Vたい + と + 思います
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place of the state いる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: いる modifies あいだ and indicates a state continuing over a period of time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: あいだに limits the time when the action occurs while the previous state is still continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 昔 with 友だち, creating the noun phrase “old friend.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object of the action たずねる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: たい is attached to the continuative form of a verb to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.7.n: と marks the quoted content of the desire before 思います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.8.n: と思います softens the expression and conveys the speaker's intention or thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.why: 日本にいるあいだに creates a time frame in which the visit takes place. The object comes before たずねたい, and the entire desire is introduced by と and ends with 思います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If あいだ is used without に, the sentence may mean that the action continues throughout the whole period, instead of happening within that period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: うちに emphasizes taking the chance before the state changes, so its nuance differs from simply saying “while in Japan.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate あいだに as “the whole time,” but this pattern usually focuses on an action that happens during that period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.kobun.cn: Vている + あいだに; Nの + あいだに; Vたい + と + 思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.vi: If the weather is bad tomorrow, it is okay not to come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: もし signals that a hypothetical situation will be stated in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: 明日 identifies the time of the weather situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has the quality 悪い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective 悪い changes to 悪ければ to form the conditional clause “if bad.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: 来なくても combines the negative form with ても to introduce the meaning “it is okay not to do it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: なくてもいいです expresses permission or that an action is not required.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + ければ; Vない remove い + くてもいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.why: The conditional clause with 天気が悪ければ comes first and states the hypothetical situation. The following clause uses 来なくてもいい to say that, in that situation, not coming is still acceptable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 悪ければ is changed to 悪くても, the meaning becomes “even if the weather is bad,” so it is no longer the condition “if bad.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If なくてもいい is replaced with なければならない, the meaning changes to “must come,” which is opposite to being allowed not to come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily divide 悪い into 悪いば, but the conditional form of an adjective ending in い must be 悪ければ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vi: I keep remembering things from that enjoyable trip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.sk: Aい past + N の + N ばかり + Vている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective in the past form comes before the noun and modifies the trip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 旅行 with こと, showing that こと belongs to the trip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: こと is the object being remembered, while ばかり emphasizes that they are the only things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects 思い出す with います to create a state that is continuing or keeps happening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている and expresses a repeated action or continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.why: 楽しかった旅行 modifies こと and forms the object of 思い出す. ばかり limits what is remembered, while 思い出している shows that the state is still continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, it limits the object neutrally, without emphasizing the feeling of repeatedly doing or thinking about it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the focus is on repeatedly doing one action, not simply limiting a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.tip: ばかり does not always mean a large quantity; in this sentence, it emphasizes focusing only on one subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.kobun.cn: N ＋ ばかり; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.vi: The meeting will end in five minutes, so please wait a moment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.sk: Time ＋ で ＋ N が ＋ Vます ＋ ので ＋ ちょっと ＋ おVください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: で refers only to the time needed for the meeting to reach the result of ending.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the state 終わります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the request in the following clause, creating a soft and polite tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: お待ちください is a polite way to request the action of waiting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.cn: Time ＋ で; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; お ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.why: あと５分で defines the remaining time before the meeting ends. ので turns this clause into a reason, and then お待ちください gives a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If あと５分まで is used, the meaning focuses on “until the five-minute point” and does not express the time needed for the ending.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: から only indicates the starting point of a time or a reason, so it does not fit the meaning “it will end in five minutes.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に after a period of time, but when talking about the time needed to reach a result, they must use で.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.vi: When I opened the built-in closet, I saw a cat sleeping.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object opened by the action 開ける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the action of opening with the result or event discovered immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that is in the state 寝ていた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: ていた describes a state that was continuing at the past time being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.why: 開けると creates the point “when it was opened,” and the sentence then shifts to what was seen at that point. 寝ていた emphasizes that the cat was sleeping when the speaker opened the closet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 寝ていた is replaced with 寝た, the meaning becomes “slept,” referring only to a completed action and not emphasizing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 開けたら is used, the sentence has a stronger conditional or specific-time meaning, while 開けると suggests a natural result that happens immediately upon opening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 寝た to translate “be sleeping,” but an ongoing state in the past requires 寝ていた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と; Vている → Vていた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.vi: If it were me, I would probably collapse after walking continuously like that for three whole hours.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.sk: N なら ＋ そう ＋ Time も ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ 続ける ＋ ては ＋ Vてしまう ＋ でしょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: なら sets ぼく as the hypothetical subject for considering a separate situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: も emphasizes the unusually long duration of three hours.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 歩き続ける expresses continuing to walk, while ては connects the prolonged situation with an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: しまう emphasizes a result that happens against one's wishes or is regrettable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: でしょう expresses a gentle guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.cn: N ＋ なら; Vます remove ます ＋ 続ける; Vて ＋ は; Vて ＋ しまう; V普通形 ＋ でしょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.why: ぼくなら sets the assumption “if it were me,” then そう３時間も adds the manner and duration. ては connects continuing to walk with a bad result, while しまう and でしょう add regret and a guess, respectively.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 歩き続けては is changed to 歩き続けても, the meaning becomes “even if I continued walking,” without emphasizing the bad result caused by continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: ながら only describes two actions happening at the same time, so it does not clearly show that continuing leads to an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand ては as “and then,” but in this sentence it has the warning-like meaning “if one keeps doing it, then...”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.vi: Wherever she goes, she takes her pet dog with her.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed throughout the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 行っても connects a concessive condition, meaning that wherever she goes, the result is the same.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects a noun that modifies 犬.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the dog as the object being taken along.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects 連れて with the verb 行く to express going together or taking someone along.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: 行く is the main predicate, combining with 連れて to form 連れて行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.why: The clause どこへ行っても comes first to state a situation that does not change. 連れて行く uses the て form to show that the action of taking someone along is performed together with 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with どこへ行ったら, the sentence becomes a supposition about going somewhere, and no longer means doing the same thing wherever one goes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that the result does not change even when the condition changes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse へ, the direction of movement, with を, the object being taken along, so どこを is not used in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も; 疑問詞 ＋ Vて ＋ も
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.vi: If you only look from behind, sometimes you cannot tell whether the person is male or female.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: だけ limits the object being viewed to only the view from behind.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The conditional form ば connects the condition with the result stated afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: なのか creates one possibility in the question of whether the person is male or female.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: なのか presents the second possibility and works together with 男なのか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The negative form なく connects the state of not knowing with なる and expresses a change into that state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: なる describes a change into a state where one cannot distinguish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: こと turns the entire preceding event into a noun, while が marks it as something that occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.7.n: ある completes the pattern ことがある and describes something that happens occasionally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.why: The phrase 男なのか女なのか comes before 分からなくなる to make the content something that cannot be determined. ことがある turns this entire state into a noun and then says that it sometimes occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 男とか女とか is used, the sentence only lists possibilities and does not emphasize uncertainty or not knowing which possibility to choose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is used when there is only one issue of whether something is true, so it is less suitable than のか～のか when there are two choices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit な before のか with nouns, but they must say 男なのか and 女なのか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.kobun.cn: Nなのか ＋ Nなのか; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋なのか; V普通形 ＋ ことがある
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.vi: It is already spring, but it is still cold.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: もう shows that spring had already arrived before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the state or result that なる changes into.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: のに connects two clauses that conflict with what the speaker expected or hoped for.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ modifies 寒い and shows that the cold state has not ended.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 寒い is the predicate stating the result that conflicts with expectations after spring has arrived.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.why: なったのに creates a contrast between spring having arrived and the fact that it is still cold. まだ is placed directly before 寒い to emphasize that the cold state continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with ので, the sentence means that it is cold because spring has arrived, which removes the unexpected contrast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If なっても is used, the sentence means that even if spring has arrived, it is still cold, emphasizing the condition rather than the surprise.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate のに as “because,” but in this sentence のに must be understood as “even though” or “despite that.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vi: I do not want to do anything that makes my mother cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ V使役形 ＋ ような ＋ N は ＋ Vたい negative
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は names the person whose wish is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person who is made to perform the action of crying in the causative clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: なかせる is the predicate of the clause modifying こと, expressing making one's mother cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ような connects the preceding clause to the noun こと, creating a phrase meaning “a thing like that.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: こと turns the preceding action into a noun, while は makes that thing the object of negation and adds a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: したくない is the negative form of wanting to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.cn: Nを＋V使役形；V辞書形＋ような＋N；Vます omit ます＋たい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.why: 母をなかせるようなこと is the clause modifying こと, referring to things that may make one's mother cry. ことは turns all of those things into something the speaker does not want to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ような is replaced with ように, the phrase changes to mean doing something in a way or for a purpose, and no longer directly modifies a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means having one's mother cry or being affected by her crying. It is different from actively making one's mother cry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を after the person being made to do something, but with a directly transitive verb such as 泣かせる, 母を marks the person who is made to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.vi: You can see birds flying in the sky.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the space or flight path through which the bird moves.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing the action of flying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects 飛ぶ with いる to create an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the clause 鳥が飛んでいる into a noun, while が marks what is seen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 見えます describes something or a state that naturally comes into the viewer's sight.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.why: 空を indicates the flight path, while 鳥が is the subject of 飛んでいる. The whole clause is turned into a noun by の, then made the subject of 見えます to express what is seen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見える is replaced with 見る, the sentence emphasizes that the viewer actively watches the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見られる is used, the nuance is that one can see or is allowed to see something, not simply that it naturally comes into view.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before the thing seen, but the pattern 見える uses が to mark something that naturally comes into view.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ のが ＋ 見える
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.kobun.vi: Because my stomach hurts, I will eat only half.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state of being in pain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects a cause to a result and means “because.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: だけ comes after a noun to limit the amount and means “only.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first, followed by the limited quantity and then the main action. だけ modifies 半分 to emphasize that the amount eaten stops at half.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, a negative form is required, with the emphasis “I will eat nothing other than half.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put だけ at the end of the sentence, but だけ must come directly after the word or phrase being limited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.vi: Because a guest is coming, I will set the plates on the table in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the verb 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason for preparing with the action done afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects テーブル with 上, creating the phrase “the top of the table.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the plates are put.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the item being arranged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: ならべて is the て form of ならべる, and connects with おきます to express doing something beforehand as preparation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.why: The reason is stated first, followed by the place and the item affected, and finally the preparatory action. おく follows the て form to show that the plates are set out before the guest arrives.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence focuses on the state of the plates already being set out, without emphasizing that the speaker actively prepared them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the dictionary form before おく, but this pattern requires the verb in the て form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.vi: My son has become able to put on his shoes by himself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose ability has changed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the way an action is performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the object that can be acted on in a potential construction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: はける is the potential form and connects with ようになりました to express gaining a new ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました shows that a state or ability has changed from before.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.why: The topic is the person whose ability has changed, followed by the method and the ability gained. The potential form はける combines with ようになる to express the process of becoming able to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means actively trying or arranging to do something, rather than describing an ability that has developed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ようになる with “become” in general; after a potential form, it usually refers to the development of an ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q7.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない・V可能形 ＋ ようになる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.kobun.vi: I intend not to quit my job.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who has an intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the job that will or will not be quit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: やめない is the negative form placed before つもりです, creating the meaning of intending not to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.kobun.why: The object of the intention is marked by を, while the negative verb comes directly before つもりだ. Therefore, the sentence clearly expresses the speaker's plan not to quit the job.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes a decision that has been made, not just a plan or intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.kobun.tip: For an intention not to do something, やめないつもりです must be used; do not use つもりじゃない when you mean “intend not to quit.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ つもりだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.vi: Anyone with an opinion, please speak up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of ある in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ある comes before 方 to modify the person who has an opinion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase 意見がある comes before 方 to identify the person being discussed; は introduces that person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: おっしゃって is the て form of the honorific おっしゃる, used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after the て form to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.why: The clause 意見がある comes before 方 to create the phrase “a person with an opinion.” After that topic, the て form combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this, the meaning is still “please say,” but the level of politeness is lower おっしゃってください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.tip: When speaking politely to the listener, do not replace おっしゃってください with the direct translation of “please say,” 言ってください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.tokens.3.m: person; polite counter for a person
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.kobun.cn: Vて + ください; おっしゃる → おっしゃって
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.vi: Because my grandchild told me to, I decided to quit smoking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 言われた is the past passive form, while ので connects the reason to the decision in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: は identifies the person who makes the decision being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the action やめる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary form やめる modifies こと, turning the action of quitting smoking into the content of the decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: ことに in the pattern ことにする indicates the content that was decided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: した completes the pattern ことにした and expresses that the decision was made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.why: 孫に言われたので is placed first to state the reason for the decision. やめることにした turns quitting smoking into the content that わたし decided for himself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことにした is replaced with ことになった, the sentence says that the decision was already arranged or was made by circumstances or another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used instead of ので, the reason stays the same, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand 孫に as the person being spoken to, but in this passive sentence に indicates the person who spoke to or affected the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.kobun.cn: V受身形: Vれる・Vられる; V普通形 + ので; V辞書形 + ことにする
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.vi: She passed the exam, so she has a bright expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に goes with 合格する to indicate the exam that the speaker passed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects an action or reason to the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The phrase 明るい顔を serves as the description before している in the pattern 顔をしている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: しています expresses a current state or facial expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.why: 彼女は is the topic, while 試験に合格して shows the reason for the later state. The phrase 明るい顔をしている uses を to combine the description of the expression with する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced here, the sentence focuses more on intentionally making an expression and does not emphasize a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 顔がしている, but the correct pattern is 顔をしている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.vi: He does not seem well these days. I wonder what is wrong with him.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は gives the time period as the background for the comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes him the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure 元気がない expresses an unhealthy condition or a lack of energy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: みたいだ comes at the end of the sentence to give a judgment based on observation or feeling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: どうした combines with ん to state what the speaker is wondering about, while だろう expresses mild self-questioning and guessing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.why: このごろは sets the time background, and then 彼は元気がない states the content being commented on. みたいだ turns this statement into a judgment that is not completely certain; だろう in the next sentence creates a self-questioning tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうだ is used, the sentence is usually based more directly on appearance or a clear sign being seen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If らしい is used, the sentence leans more toward information heard from others or a judgment based on objective evidence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.tip: Do not place みたいだ directly after a verb in the polite conjugated form, such as 元気がありませんみたいだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな+みたいだ／N+みたいだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.kobun.vi: It is not only the people in my country who are suffering because the air is getting worse.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause before 空気 modifies the air, while てくる emphasizes a change continuing up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the problem or cause that makes people 困っている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の nominalizes the clause 困っている, while は makes it the topic for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: だけではない denies the limiting meaning, saying that this group is not the only one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.kobun.why: The clause 悪くなってきた comes before 空気 to describe the air. The whole phrase 空気に困っている is nominalized with のは, and then だけではない is used to say that the scope is not limited to the people in my country.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ていく, the change is viewed from the present and continues toward the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the direction of change: てくる moves toward the present, while ていく moves away from the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.tokens.0.n: the い form of an adjective
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.vi: Yesterday, Mr. Suzuki invited me to a party, and I had a good time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to set the time for the whole event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は identifies the person who experiences the event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the person who performs the action affecting the subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle へ indicates the direction or place to which someone is invited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: 誘われて is the passive form in the て form, connecting being invited with the result of having a good time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The く form of the adjective ending in い modifies the verb 過ごした.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb is in the affirmative past form and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.cn: Group I: Vう→Vあれる／Group II: Vる→Vられる／する→される／来る→来られる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.why: わたしは is the person affected, so the passive form 誘われる is used; 鈴木さんに indicates the person who invited, while パーティーへ indicates the direction toward the party. The form て connects being invited with the result of having a good time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 誘う is used, わたし becomes the person who invites someone else, changing the subject of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 誘って is used, the subject performs the inviting and no longer has the meaning of being invited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake に for the person receiving the invitation, but in the passive sentence に indicates the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.vi: There are only three days left. I wonder whether I can finish writing the report.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.sk: あと + Quantity しか + ないのに、 + N は + potential verb + でしょうか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: あと adds the meaning of the remaining time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: しか limits the remaining time and combines with the negative form ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ない negates the amount of time remaining, while のに connects an unfavorable situation to the following question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes writing the report the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.4.vi: will it be possible to write it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: 書ける is the potential form, while でしょうか turns the sentence into a polite question expressing doubt or concern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.cn: V可能形＋でしょうか; Group I: final u sound→e＋る／Group II: remove る＋られる／する→できる／来る→来られる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.why: あと三日間しかないのに presents the very limited time as the premise for the question. 書ける uses the potential form to ask whether there is enough ability to complete the report, while でしょうか expresses polite concern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書きますか is used, the sentence only asks whether someone will write it or not, without emphasizing the ability to complete it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書けそうですか is used, the question depends more on feelings or signs that suggest writing it seems possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.kobun.tip: Do not translate 書ける as a definite action; it is the potential form, meaning “can write.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.vi: When I have not prepared for class, I am often made to answer the teacher’s questions, so I struggle.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks what is being prepared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern ていない describes a state in which an action has not been carried out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the time when the speaker is forced to answer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle の connects the owner to the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle に indicates the object that the act of answering is directed toward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.ch.7.n: The causative-passive form shows that the speaker is forced by someone else to do something; て connects with 困る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.why: The time clause comes first to give the situation, followed by the object of the question and the forced action. The form させられて connects the cause of discomfort with the result 困る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active causative form were used, it would mean that the speaker makes someone else answer, not that the speaker is forced to answer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If only the passive form were used, the sentence would only state that someone is answered or affected, without clearly showing that the person is forced to act.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may confuse させられる with させる and lose the meaning of being forced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.kobun.cn: Vさせられる・Vていない・Vて ＋ 困る
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.vi: If I keep watching TV for a long time, my eyes will hurt.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the period during which the action takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being watched.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 続ける is attached after the stem form ます to show a continuing action; と connects a condition with a usual result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the body part that undergoes the change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective い changes to the form く and then connects with なる to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.why: The period of time and the object come before the main verb. 見続ける expresses that the watching continues, while と connects this situation with the natural result that the eyes hurt.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 見ると is used, the sentence only states the condition of watching and does not emphasize that the watching continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: 見ていると emphasizes the state of watching, while 見続ける emphasizes that it continues for a long time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may forget that 続ける must connect with the stem form ます of the verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.tokens.10.n: adjective ending in い, continuative form
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.kobun.cn: Vます形＋続ける／Aい－い＋くなる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.vi: Because that game does not seem interesting, I do not want to play it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it does not seem interesting
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes to く and then connects with なさそう to say that something appears not to have that quality; から gives the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: たい changes to たくない to express the speaker’s negative desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.why: The topic is evaluated first, followed by the reason, and then the speaker’s desire. なさそう comes after the く form of the adjective い to create the meaning “seems not to be.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If おもしろそうだ is used, the meaning changes to “seems interesting,” which is opposite to the reason in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If おもしろくない is used, the sentence states that it is not interesting, without the guess based on appearance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may use おもしろそうではない instead of the natural form おもしろくなさそうだ in this structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.kobun.cn: Aい－い＋く＋なさそうだ／Vます形＋たい＋くない／普通形＋から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.vi: No matter what other people say, I do not intend to give up that plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the agent in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content of the quoted speech after 何.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The passive form 言われる combines with ても to create the concessive meaning “even if someone says something.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the object being given up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies つもり, creating the meaning “the intention to give up.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.7.n: つもり expresses a personal intention, while は emphasizes that the intention is negated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.8.n: ない completes the pattern つもりはない, meaning “do not intend to do it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.why: The concessive clause comes first to say that outside opinions do not change the decision. The dictionary-form verb comes before つもり because it modifies the noun meaning intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 予定はない, the sentence would refer to a schedule or planned event that does not exist, with less emphasis on personal will.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If つもりだ is used, the meaning changes to having the intention to give up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may mistake つもり for an objective plan, while this pattern emphasizes the speaker’s own intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.kobun.cn: Vて形＋も／V辞書形＋つもりはない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.vi: You must not say such rude things to anyone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person receiving the words, while でも expands the meaning to anyone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: そんな modifies the noun phrase that follows and points to the type of speech being criticized.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 失礼な is the な adjective that modifies こと.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content being said.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 言っては is the て form combined with は to introduce the prohibition pattern てはいけない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: いけません completes the pattern てはいけません, while よ emphasizes a reminder or warning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.why: だれにでも expands the listener receiving the words to anyone. The pattern 言ってはいけません comes after the object to prohibit saying something rude.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だれかに, the sentence only means speaking to someone, not just anyone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: だれにも is usually used in negative sentences to mean no one at all, while だれにでも emphasizes every person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use でも alone, but when showing the target of an action, they must keep に in だれにでも.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 + にでも; Vて + はいけない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.vi: When I say that I want to eat cake, my younger sister also shows that she wants to eat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the food that someone wants to eat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.2.vi: say that someone wants to eat
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the desired content quoted after the verb 言う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: と connects the speaking action with the reaction that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: も means “also” and marks the subject who has a similar desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.5.vi: shows that she wants to eat
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: たがる attaches to the form without ます to show another person’s desire through an observable sign.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.why: My desire is placed in the quoted content after と. After hearing that content, 妹 has a similar reaction, so たがる is used to talk about another person’s desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 妹も食べたい is used, the speaker directly states the younger sister’s desire, while 食べたがる only describes an observable sign.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べたそうだ is used, it means that the younger sister seems to want to eat at that moment. It does not stress the tendency to want to do something as たがる does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use たい for every subject, but when talking about another person’s desire, たがる is usually needed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q20.kobun.cn: Vます形 + たい / Vます形 + たがる / 普通形 + と + 言う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.vi: I was very troubled because I had lost an important notebook.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective な directly modifies the noun 手帳.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing that was lost.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the event that caused the trouble with the state of 困っていた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 困っていた describes a state of being troubled at a certain time in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to describe the notebook. Then を marks the thing that was lost. The form て connects the cause, なくす, with the result: a troubled state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If なくなって is used, the sentence says that the notebook was lost or disappeared by itself, without stating who lost it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If なくしたので困っていた is used, the cause-and-effect relationship stays the same, but the reason is stated clearly with ので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake なくす for “be lost.” It is a transitive verb meaning to lose something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.kobun.cn: Vて + 困る / Vている・Vていた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.vi: The teacher often tells interesting stories and makes everyone laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content that the teacher tells.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: して is the て form of する. It connects the storytelling action with the result of making everyone laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the person affected by the causative action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: 笑わせます is the causative form. It describes making everyone laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.why: 先生は states who performs the storytelling action. After the content marked by を, して connects the storytelling action with its result; みんなを is the object made to laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 笑う is used, it means that everyone laughs by themselves, without the meaning that the teacher makes them laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes receiving help or permission for someone to laugh, unlike the meaning of actively making them laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget を before the person affected in a causative sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q22.kobun.cn: Vる → Vさせる・Vす → Vせる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.vi: A beautiful flower was sent from Yamada to Satou.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.sk: N から + 人 に + N が + past passive verb
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source or starting point of the sending.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who receives the sent object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 送られた is the past passive form. It shows that the flower received the action of sending.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.cn: Vる → Vられる（group 2）・Vう → Vあれる（group 1）・する → される・来る → 来られる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.why: The sentence chooses the flower as the subject, so it uses が and places it before the passive verb. から states the sender, while に states the receiver.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 送った is used, the subject is the sender and the sentence has the active meaning “sent.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This structure makes Satou the sender, completely changing the roles of the sentence elements.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に for the performer, but in a passive sentence に usually indicates the agent or the receiver, depending on the verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.vi: The number of vehicles has been increasing, and it will probably continue to increase from now on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object whose amount tends to increase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 増えてきた describes a change that has continued from the past to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds the meaning of continuing during a future period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 続けていく combines the meaning of continuation with the direction of change from the present toward the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: だろう is placed at the end of a sentence to express an uncertain prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.why: 増えてきた looks back at the trend from the past to the present. In the next sentence, 増え続けていく directs the continuation from the present toward the future, while だろう turns the statement into a prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern directs the continuation from the past to the present, so it is less suitable when talking about the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This form still says that the increase will continue, but it does not stress the direction of change from the present onward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mix up てくる and ていく without considering the time direction of the change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q24.kobun.cn: Vて + くる・Vます + 続ける → Vます + 続けていく・普通形 + だろう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.vi: My friend sent me a Japanese souvenir.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action of sending.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に refers to the person who receives the benefit of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being sent; 日本の modifies お土産.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 送ってくれた describes another person doing something that benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる（ past tense: くれた）
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.why: 友だちが is the person who performs the action, わたしに is the person who receives the benefit, and the gift is marked by を. てくれた shows that your action benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the subject is usually the person receiving help. It emphasizes that I asked for or received the sending.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern puts the speaker or subject in the position of doing a favor for someone else, which is opposite to the direction of benefit in the current sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に for the person doing the action, but with てくれる, に is usually the person receiving the benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.vi: Those who view the paintings should buy their tickets early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.sk: Nを + ご覧になる + Nは + 副詞に + Nを + おVます removeますください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the painting as the object viewed in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ご覧になる is a respectful way to describe the viewing action of the person mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 絵をご覧になる modifies 方, while は makes those people the main topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 早めに modifies the action of buying and requires it to be done before the usual time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the ticket as the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: お買いください is a polite request used to guide the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.cn: ご覧になる: ご + Vます形 removeます + になる; お + Vます形 removeます + ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.why: 絵をご覧になる comes before 方 to identify the people viewing the paintings and form the topic of the instruction. お買いください comes at the end of the sentence to make a polite request to buy tickets early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ご覧ください is used, the sentence asks the listener to view the painting instead of describing people who view it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 拝見する is used, it is humble language used by the speaker about their own viewing action, not respectful language that elevates the viewer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 方 as a word for direction, but in this sentence 方[かた] is a polite way to refer to a person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.vi: You must not think only about yourself. You must also think about other people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 自分 with こと, forming a phrase that modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: こと is what is being thought about, while ばかり emphasizes focusing only on this.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 考えて is the て form. It connects with はいけません to create a pattern meaning prohibition or “must not do.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: はいけません completes the pattern expressing that something is not allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 人 with こと, forming a phrase that modifies what is being thought about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: も replaces を to add object 人のこと alongside 自分のこと.
