default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: 考えなければ is the negative conditional form. It connects with ならない to create an obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: なければならない expresses an obligation: the action must definitely be performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.cn: Vて + はいけません; Vない remove い + ければならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.why: The phrase 自分のことばかり is the object of 考える and is limited by ばかり. The second clause uses も to add 人のこと, while なければならない expresses the obligation to think about other people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces the second clause, the meaning is still that something must be done, but this is another complete way to express obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it replaces てはいけません, the sentence becomes a gentler request meaning “please do not do it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake てはいけない for a gentle way to say something should not be done, while this pattern usually expresses prohibition or that something is not allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.vi: I am fed up because I am forced to eat nothing but fish every day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.sk: Frequency + N ばかり + Vさせられる + から、もう + Aな + になるわ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 indicates the time or frequency of an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 魚 is the object of 食べる, while ばかり emphasizes eating fish only.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I am forced to eat
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べさせられる is the passive-causative form, meaning that someone else forces the speaker to eat; から connects the reason to the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: もう modifies the state いやになる and shows that the feeling has reached the point of being fed up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: いやになる means to become bored or fed up; わ at the end of the sentence adds the speaker’s exclamatory feeling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.cn: Vさせられる: for group 1 verbs, change the final sound to the あ row + せられる; for group 2, remove る + させられる; する→させられる; 来る→来[こ]させられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.why: 魚ばかり is the limited object of the eating action. The passive-causative form puts the speaker in a forced position, and then から connects this reason with the feeling of being fed up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces the form in the sentence, the meaning is that the subject forces someone else to eat, not that the subject is forced to eat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is replaced by ので, the reason is presented more gently and objectively.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may accidentally omit ら in 食べさせられる, causing the sentence to change from being forced to eat to forcing someone else to eat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.vi: My father went to bed without eating dinner.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents 父 as the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 晩ご飯 as the object of the action 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べずに connects the action of not eating with the action of sleeping that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.cn: Vない remove ない + ずに; する→せずに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.why: 晩ご飯を is the object of the eating action, but this action is negated by ずに before 寝ました is performed. This order shows that sleeping happened without eating dinner first.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ずに is replaced by ないで, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the expression is more common and casual.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If なくて is used, the sentence may have a cause or state nuance, so it is less suitable than ずに for connecting two actions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use なくて to connect two actions, but the pattern for doing the later action without doing the earlier one is ずに or ないで.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.vi: The two people are talking happily.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.sk: N は + Aい remove い + そうに + N を + Vています
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents 二人 as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 楽しそうに modifies 話をしています and shows how the two people are talking based on their outward appearance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 話 as the content of the action しています.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ～ています describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます・Aい remove い・Aな + そうだ; adverbial form: そうに; noun-modifying form: そうな + N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.why: 楽しそうに comes before 話をしています to describe the outward state shown while talking. しています shows that the action is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used at the end of the sentence, it means “seem happy,” without directly describing the way of talking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is used before a noun, it modifies that noun, such as an atmosphere that seems happy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily write 楽しいそう, but with an adjective ending in い, い must be removed before adding そう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I had a headache and a fever as well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.sk: Time point は + N が + Aいかったし、N も + ありました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes yesterday the time point and topic of the conditions described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part that has the painful condition in the first clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 痛かった is the past form of the adjective, while し connects this reason or condition to the additional idea that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds another condition that existed together with the headache.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.why: きのうは sets the time context for the whole sentence. し connects the headache and fever to list things that happened together, while も emphasizes that the second condition is added.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If し is replaced with ので, the first clause becomes the direct cause of the second clause instead of simply listing another condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If the form て is used, the conditions are connected more closely, and the listing meaning and open-ended reason of し become weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically use も to mean “also”; here, も adds the fever to the list of conditions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい普通形・Aな + だし・N + だし
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.vi: Because I arrived 30 minutes early, there was no one at all in the hall.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.sk: Period of time も + Aく + Vすぎたから、N には + だれも + いませんでした
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: も attaches to a period of time to emphasize that it is more than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 早く modifies 来すぎた and describes arriving too early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 来すぎた combines with a verb and すぎる to indicate an excessive degree, while から connects a cause with its result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: には states the location and also creates the scope for talking about people's presence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: だれも acts as the subject and combines with a negative predicate to mean “no one.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: いませんでした is the negative past form of います, used for the existence of people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.cn: Question word + も + Vない; Vます omit ます + すぎる; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.why: ３０分も and 早く modify 来すぎた, clarifying that arriving early was excessive. After から comes the result at 会場, where だれも combines with the negative predicate いませんでした to express that there was absolutely no one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If だれも is replaced with だれか, the meaning changes to “someone,” which usually goes with an affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If だれでも is used, it means “anyone,” rather than the complete negation expressed by だれも～ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.vs.2.d: If すぎる is omitted, only the meaning “arrive early” remains, and the sense of arriving excessively early is lost.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use だれも in an affirmative sentence, but だれも means “no one” when used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vi: I am looking for someone who meets these conditions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the demonstrative word to the noun 条件 and modifies it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the standard that the person meets; the whole phrase modifies 人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being searched for.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 探しています uses the ている form to express an ongoing search.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.why: これらの modifies 条件, while 条件に合う is the preceding clause that modifies 人. Because 人 is the object of 探す, を is used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This connection makes 条件 directly modify 人 and does not clearly express the meaning of a person who meets the conditions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes a person who met the conditions at a certain time or according to a confirmed result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect 条件 to 人 with の, but the meaning of “meet” requires 条件に合う人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q1.kobun.cn: N1 の N2; N に合う + N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.vi: We can learn many things even from everyday life.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 毎日 with 生活 and forms a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 生活 with 中 and indicates the area within life.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the source or scope from which something is learned, while も means “also” or “even.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: いろいろ modifies the content being learned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 勉強する is in the dictionary form and modifies こと.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: こと turns the action 勉強する into a noun, while が marks that act as the subject that can be performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: できます expresses the ability to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.why: The phrase 毎日の生活の中からも comes first to state the source and scope of learning. 勉強すること changes the action of studying into a noun that acts as the subject with が before できます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 中 is omitted, から only directly indicates the starting source; Nの中から emphasizes choosing or taking something from inside a scope.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If を is used, the noun before it is the object of study, not the source or scope that provides something to learn.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after 生活, but here から is needed to indicate the source from which knowledge is taken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.vi: I do not intend to attend next week's party.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who has or does not have an intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 来週 with パーティー to modify the party.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the event that the speaker plans to attend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 出る is in the dictionary form and modifies つもり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: つもり is a noun meaning intention, and は makes that intention the topic of negation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: ありません denies the existence of the intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.why: The verb 出る in the dictionary form comes before つもり to create the intention phrase “intend to attend.” は in つもりはありません highlights that the intention is denied.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern expresses an intention not to do something, while Vるつもりはありません emphasizes having absolutely no intention of doing it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with はずだ changes the meaning to a judgment or something believed to be certain, rather than the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily divide 出る into 出ない before つもり, but 出るつもりはありません already negates the intention in the following part.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + つもりはありません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.vi: No matter how hard the work is, it must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.sk: いくら + N が + Aいくても、 + Vない omit い + ければなりません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら emphasizes the high degree of the hypothetical situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject with the condition つらい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective つらい changes to つらくても to connect with the concessive meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.3.vi: if one does not do it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: やらない omits い and changes to やらなければ to create the condition in the obligation pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: なりません completes the double-negative pattern, meaning that one must do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.cn: Aい omit い + くても; Vない omit い + ければなりません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.why: The いくら仕事がつらくても clause states the concessive situation, while the following clause states an obligation that does not change. やらなければなりません means “if one does not do it, it is not acceptable,” which naturally means “one must do it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the sentence would mean that it is acceptable not to do it, which is the opposite of the obligatory meaning here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern allows someone to do it and does not emphasize an obligation to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand なければ as simply meaning “not do,” but with なりません, the whole phrase means “must do.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.vi: Even during the hot summer, many Japanese people wear suits to work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time, while も emphasizes that it is even during summer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates clothing or the state in which an action is performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination, while など expands the meaning to the workplace and similar places.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 出て connects the action of going out with the following action of working.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the object of する in the phrase 仕事をする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: する in dictionary form modifies 日本人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks the subject that is said to be numerous.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.8.n: 多いです is the main predicate and comments on the number of Japanese people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.why: 背広で describes the clothing worn when going to work, not the object of the action. The phrase 職場などに出て仕事をする modifies 日本人, and then 日本人が多いです forms the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 背広を着て is used, the focus shifts to the action of putting on a suit, instead of the state of wearing a suit while working.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also modifies 日本人, but it describes a person who has put on a suit and does not emphasize the manner of the whole action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 背広, but で is more suitable when talking about clothing or the state during an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.vi: I heard that computers were created 50 years ago.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.sk: N が + passive V + のは、 + Nだった + そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the passive action 作り出された.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の nominalizes the clause, while は makes the creation of the computer the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: だった serves as a past noun predicate and identifies the time of the event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: そうだ appears at the end of the sentence to show information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.why: The clause コンピューターが作り出された is nominalized with の and then made the topic with は. The following part states the corresponding time, while そうだ shows that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a similar form used to emphasize the time or reason for an event that happened. It does not necessarily mean that the information was heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If そうだ is placed directly after Vた, the pattern usually means that an event happened, according to what was heard; the current structure emphasizes identifying the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の in のは, so the long clause is not nominalized to serve as the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + のは
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.vi: I want to eat an apple. Please give me one of the large ones.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.sk: N が + Vたい。 + Aい + ほう + を + quantity + ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object of the desire 食べたい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べたい is the desire form of 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きいほう indicates the type being chosen; the given sentence contains the sequence がを, which is not a standard particle connection.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 一つ indicates quantity, while ください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.why: The first sentence uses 食べたい to express a desire. In the second sentence, 大きいほう changes the quality “large” into “the large type”; in a natural structure, this phrase must go with を before ください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ほか, the meaning becomes “another type,” so it is no longer a choice of the large type.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression means “the type that seems large,” emphasizing a judgment based on appearance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake ほう for the independent meaning “more”; here, it follows an adjective to create the phrase “the type or side that is …”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.vi: Within a day, around 1 p.m. is the hottest time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: のうちで limits the comparison to the whole day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the selected time the topic of comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies 暑い and creates a superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 暑い comes before 時 to modify the noun 時.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 時です is the predicate and identifies that time as the hottest time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.why: The phrase のうちで sets the range first. Then は states the selected time within that range. いちばん comes before the adjective to identify the highest degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: It can be replaced to say “among N,” with a nearly similar meaning but a more direct sense of range.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: まで only marks a limit up to a point; it is not used to choose the most prominent object within a range.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q16.kobun.tip: Do not translate のうちで as “inside” in the location sense; here, it creates a range for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.vi: According to what I heard, Mr. Yamada will come here tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.sk: Nでは + time + N は + N に + Vるそうです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: では states the source or basis of the reported information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: あした indicates the time when the action occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the person performing the action the topic of the clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the destination of the verb 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.4.vi: I heard that he will come
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 来るそうです uses the plain form 来る before そうです to report information that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.why: 話では places the information source at the beginning of the sentence. Then the time, topic, and destination add information to the clause 来るそうです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is also “according to …,” but it emphasizes the basis or source of the information more strongly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 話なら, the sentence becomes the condition “if we talk about that matter,” so it is no longer an information source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.tip: Do not confuse そうです for reporting information with そうです for describing appearance; the plain form comes before the reporting pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.vi: My son wants to go to London to watch the Olympic Games.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.sk: N は + N に + Vて + N を + Vます omit ます + たいと思っています
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the person who has the desire the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 行って connects going to London with watching.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the event being watched.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 見たいと思っています indirectly expresses a current wish or intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます＋たいと思っています
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.why: に identifies the destination, while て connects two consecutive actions. The object of 見る goes with を, followed by 見たいと思っています as the predicate expressing a current wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence is more direct and simple: “want to watch,” with less indirect meaning of intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes a decided plan or intention, not only a wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.kobun.tip: After 行って, do not use 行いて; this is the irregular て form of 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.vi: Since he has said that he will come, Mr. Yamada certainly will come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the content being quoted.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: 言ってあります shows that something was said and is still valid; から connects it to the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the person being judged the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ないはずはありません negates the possibility of “not coming,” creating the meaning that he cannot fail to come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.why: The first clause gives the basis through a quotation with と and the reason with から. The second clause uses a double negative to strongly conclude that the possibility of “not coming” is impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: It means “should/probably will come,” giving a more direct statement without a double negative.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: It means “it is not completely the case that he will not come,” which is much weaker and does not express certainty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.tip: Read the whole phrase はずはありません together; do not separate はず as “intention” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.kobun.cn: Vない＋はずはありません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vi: Because I stood on the train the whole time, I was a little tired.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 電車 with 中 to form a phrase meaning the inside of the train.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the action of standing took place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 立っていた describes a standing state that continued in the past, while から connects the reason to the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: 疲れた is the result caused by standing on the train the whole time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.why: 電車の中で identifies the place, while ずっと emphasizes a continuing period. The clause 立っていたから comes first to state the cause, followed by the result 疲れた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern says that I am tired because I am standing now; it does not emphasize a state that continued in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This form only states standing as a completed action and does not clearly show a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may simply translate ていた as past tense, but here it also emphasizes a continuing standing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.vi: When it is as hot as this year, working is really hard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: みたいに turns 今年 into a comparison standard modifying 暑い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a natural condition with a result that usually occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: の nominalizes 働く, while が marks working as the thing that feels difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 本当に modifies つらい to emphasize the degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.why: 今年みたいに creates a comparison for the level of heat. 暑いと states the condition, while 働くのが本当につらい is the result, and の turns the verb into a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with のように, the meaning “like this year” remains, but the expression is more formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 暑そうに, the meaning becomes “looks hot,” not truly hot like this year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.tip: と is a conditional particle here, not と used for quotation; look at the result clause that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.kobun.cn: N＋みたいに＋V・Aい／Aな・N＋みたいに（な）
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.vi: If we are talking about someone to marry, someone kind like Mr. Tanaka would be good, right?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 結婚 with 相手 to modify the noun 相手.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: なら turns the noun phrase before it into a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: のような modifies 人 and describes a person with characteristics like Tanaka.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the person judged to be suitable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: いい is the predicate, while ね adds a gentle sense of agreement or confirmation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.why: The phrase 結婚の相手なら states the condition about the type of person chosen. Then, 田中さんのような優しい人 is the subject of the evaluation いい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, it means a person showing typical qualities of N, not necessarily someone similar to a specific person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This form modifies a verb or adjective and does not connect directly to the noun 人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse のような with のように; before a noun, use のような.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.vi: I came to Japan to learn Japanese that sounds truly Japanese.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: らしい comes after 日本語 to modify 日本語 that follows, showing typical characteristics.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of learning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ために connects the purpose 習う with the action 来た.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the destination of 来た.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: 来た is the main action, while のです is used to explain or emphasize information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.why: 日本語らしい日本語 creates a noun phrase in which the first word modifies the second. The phrase 習うために states the purpose of coming to Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning would focus on being similar to Japanese, rather than having typical Japanese characteristics.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If ように is used, the sentence usually emphasizes achieving a goal or being able to do something, not only a direct purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate every ために simply as “in order to”; look at the following verb to identify whether it expresses purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.kobun.cn: N＋らしい＋N; V辞書形・Nの＋ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.vi: Because he was ill, Mr. Yamada could not attend yesterday's meeting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N のために ＋ N の ＋ N に ＋ past negative potential verb
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: Nのために connects the cause to the result of being unable to attend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies 会議 and identifies the meeting held yesterday.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the event that 山田さん could not attend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: られる expresses ability, while なかった makes it negative in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.why: 病気のために comes first and gives the reason. 会議に出る means “attend the meeting,” and then 出られなかった shows that the action was not possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning of the cause is almost unchanged, but the conversational tone becomes softer and more natural.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence has a stronger tone of blame or negative judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle に in 会議に出る; for the meaning of attending, 出る must be used with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.vi: I did not think it would be this cold outside.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents outside as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: そんなに modifies 寒い and usually occurs with a negative idea or an evaluation of degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: とは marks the content thought about or judged in 思いませんでした.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 思いませんでした is the polite past negative form of 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.why: 外は gives the topic, while 寒いとは is the content that the speaker did not expect or think about. そんなに emphasizes that the coldness was beyond expectation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If とは is omitted, the sentence is still correct, but the emphasis on surprise becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes “it is not necessarily cold,” denying certainty rather than talking about a previous thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand とは as “then”; in this pattern, it marks the content being thought about or evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.kobun.cn: 普通形＋とは思いませんでした
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.vi: Because highways are easy to drive on, you can drive at high speed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Vます omit ます＋やすいので ＋ N を ＋ V辞書形ことができる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the highway as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is easy to drive on
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: しやすい creates the meaning “easy to do,” while ので connects the cause to the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of 出す in the phrase スピードを出す.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns 出す into a noun, while が marks it as something that can be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: できる expresses the ability to perform the nominalized action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます＋やすい; V辞書形＋ことができる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.why: 運転しやすいので gives the reason, with やすい attached to the verb stem 運転し. The phrase スピードを出すこと is nominalized and becomes the subject with が of できる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.vs.0.t: Vます omit ます＋にくい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence means that the highway is difficult to drive on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence describes something being decided or becoming a certain way, so it no longer means ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily attach やすい to the full verb form; ます must be omitted first, as in 運転し＋やすい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vi: Since I will throw it away later, you can leave the trash as it is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.sk: Time point に ＋ V辞書形 ので ＋ N は ＋ State ＋ Vておく ＋ いいですよ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the time when the action will happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I will throw it away
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause to the main clause; 捨てる is the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes ゴミ the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: そのまま modifies the action おいといて and shows that the state is kept unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: This is a shortened form of 置いておいて, expressing leaving something as it is until later.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: いいですよ expresses permission or acceptance of an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ おく; in spoken language, it can be shortened to Vとく, and Vておいて to Vといて
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and is connected with ので. After the topic ゴミは, そのまま modifies the action of leaving something as it is, while いいですよ ends the sentence with permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vている, the sentence only describes the state of leaving the trash that way, without emphasizing keeping it unchanged for later handling.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vないでください, the sentence becomes a request not to do an action, and no longer means leaving an object as it is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake おいといて for a separate verb, but it is a shortened form of 置いておいて.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vi: Good jobs are not that easy to find.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents いい仕事 as the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: そう簡単に modifies 見つからない and shows that the degree is not as easy as people might think.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 見つからない is the negative predicate; のよ adds an explanatory and emphatic tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.cn: そう ＋ Aな ＋ に ＋ Vない; with an adjective Aい, use the basic form before に as an adverb
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, and then そう簡単に shows the degree of finding it. The negative predicate combines with のよ to explain and emphasize that it is not easy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If とても～ない is used, the meaning will be closer to completely impossible or extremely difficult, which is stronger than the current sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If そう is omitted and the affirmative form is used, the sentence only says that it can be found easily, without denying the expectation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate そう here as “seems”; そう簡単に～ない means “not that easy.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vi: I am currently collecting postcards from many different countries.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.sk: Time point ＋ N は ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Vております
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 indicates the time of an ongoing state or action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 国 with はがき and shows which countries the postcards belong to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the action 集める.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 集めております is the polite, humble form of 集めている and describes an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ おります; ～ております is the humble, polite form of ～ている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.why: 今 puts the time at the beginning of the sentence, and then わたしは gives the subject. The phrase 国のはがきを identifies the object, and then 集めております serves as the predicate and shows that the action is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vています, the basic meaning is still “be doing,” but the level of humility and formality is lower.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vてあります, the sentence describes a state prepared or carried out by someone, so it does not fit the speaker's collecting action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically use ～ております for every subject; this form is usually used to speak humbly about one's own action or state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vi: Anyone can play such a simple game.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.sk: そんな ＋ Aい ＋ N は ＋ どんなN でも ＋ potential verb
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the game as the topic; そんなやさしい modifies ゲーム.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: どんな人でも makes the subject mean “everyone,” without limiting the group.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: できます is the potential form of できます and expresses the ability to perform the action; よ emphasizes the information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 ＋ N ＋ でも; for example, どんな人でも, だれでも, 何でも
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.why: The phrase そんなやさしいゲームは makes the object the topic. どんな人でも comes before the potential predicate to say that no one is excluded from the range, so the meaning is that everyone can do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だれか, the sentence means that someone can play, without the meaning “everyone.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If だれも～ない is used, the sentence changes to mean that no one can play.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.kobun.tip: どんな人でも does not mean “someone”; でも after a question word creates a general meaning such as “anyone”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.tokens.4.m: what kind of person, any kind
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q6.tokens.6.m: even if it is..., any... also
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vi: I did not expect the work to go so smoothly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets the work as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: こんなに modifies うまくいく and shows a degree higher than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: とは marks the content being thought about or predicted and serves as the complement of 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 思いませんでした is a past negative predicate, showing that the speaker had not expected this beforehand.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.cn: こんなに + Aい／Aな + に／V; こんなに comes before an adjective or verb to show degree
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.why: 仕事は is the topic, while the content “progressing this smoothly” is introduced by とは. 思いませんでした is past negative, creating the meaning of being surprised compared with the earlier expectation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If そんなに is used, the degree is viewed from the listener’s side or from a psychological distance, instead of emphasizing the degree currently felt by the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If こんな is used, this word must come before a noun such as こんな仕事 and cannot directly modify うまくいく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.kobun.tip: こんなに modifies a verb or adjective, while こんな must come before a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.vi: Stop watching only TV and do your homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: ばかり limits the object of 見る and carries a critical meaning: doing only that one thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ないで connects a request not to continue the previous action with the action that should be done next.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 宿題 as the object of the action しなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: しなさい is a softer command than the direct imperative form; な makes the tone gentler.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.why: テレビばかり states the criticized action of only watching TV. 見ていないで connects it to the opposite action, while 宿題をしなさいな gives a gentle command that should be followed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vなくて, the sentence can easily mean a cause or a state of not doing something, and does not create a transition to another action like ないで.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vないでください is used, the sentence becomes a polite request not to do that action, without emphasizing doing homework instead.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.tip: Vていないで is formed from Vている + ないで, so い must not be omitted and changed into an incorrect form when saying “do not keep doing it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.kobun.cn: Vない形 + で; Vている + ないで → Vていないで
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.vi: While he was in Japan, I met him once.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the clause 彼が日本にいる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the place where 彼 exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: いる describes an ongoing state of existence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: あいだに turns the time period of a state into a point in time when another action occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: 一度 shows the number of times the action 会いました is performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: 会いました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.why: The clause 彼が日本にいる modifies あいだ and identifies the time period when the meeting occurred. あいだに emphasizes one action that happened during that period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If あいだ is used, the two states or actions are usually understood to continue together during the same period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse あいだに with あいだ and forget に when they want to say that an action happened during that period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q9.kobun.cn: Vている・Nの + あいだに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: I bought a ticket for the exhibition to be held at the department store from next month.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.sk: 時点 から + 場所 で + passive V + N + の + N を + Vました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the starting point of the exhibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the event takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The passive form comes before てんらんかい to modify the exhibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the exhibition with チケット, forming the phrase “the exhibition ticket.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: 買いました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: the う form changes to the あ row + れる; Group 2 verbs: remove る + られる; 来る→来られる; する→される
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 開かれるてんらんかい is a relative clause in which the exhibition is the thing being held. This whole phrase modifies チケット before を marks the object of 買いました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 開く is used, it means that the exhibition opens by itself or that the organizer is stated actively.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 開かれている is used, the sentence emphasizes the state of being held or currently taking place, not only a planned event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: When learners meet a clause before a noun, they may confuse the agent; here, 展覧会 is the object of 開かれる, so the passive form is needed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vi: This book must be returned by tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.sk: Nは + Deadlineまでに + Vない+なければならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before 本 to identify the book being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the book is the object that must be returned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: までに shows the deadline by which returning the book must be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative conditional form なければ creates the conditional clause for the obligation pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: なければならない expresses a duty or something that must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: は states what must be done with the book, while までに sets the deadline. The phrase なければならない turns returning the book into an obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with なくてもいい, the meaning changes to not needing to return it by the deadline or not being required to do so.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If べきだ is used, the sentence focuses on advice or what should be done, which is weaker than an obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: までに is the deadline by which something must be completed, unlike まで, which only shows a time that continues up to that point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q10.kobun.cn: Nまでに; Vない + なければならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vi: There is absolutely no food at home, so let’s go buy something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows where the food exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing being discussed as existing or not existing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぜん modifies ない and creates the meaning “not at all.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ないから connects the reason with the result, meaning “because there is none.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 何か is the indefinite object of the action of buying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The continuative form 買い+に combines with 行く to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: 行こう is the volitional form, used to invite or suggest going together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the subject 食べ物が, and then ぜんぜんないから states the reason. 買いに行こう expresses the purpose of going to buy something and invites the listener to do it together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence is more formal and emphasizes the purpose more.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the invitation is more polite than 行こう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.tip: English learners may incorrectly use に after the plain verb form; before に, the stem ます, such as 買い, must be used to show purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q11.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ に ＋ 行く・来る・帰る; ぜんぜん ＋ Vない; Vよう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vi: This cake costs as much as 800 yen per piece.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.sk: N は ＋ quantity ＋ amount of money も ＋ する
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this cake the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 一つ shows the number of cakes being priced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: も is placed after an amount of money to emphasize that the price is higher than expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: します means costs or amounts to in expressions about prices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.cn: quantity・amount of money ＋ も ＋ する
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.why: は states the cake as the topic, while 一つ８００円も combines the counting unit and the amount of money. も adds a feeling of surprise and emphasizes that 800 yen is expensive.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only reports a price of 800 yen. It does not emphasize that the price is expensive or surprising.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the price is only 800 yen, usually suggesting that it is cheap.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q12.kobun.tip: Do not understand も here as also; after a quantity or amount of money, も usually means as much as or up to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vi: How many kilograms does this luggage weigh?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.sk: N の N は ＋ 何＋unit ですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun にもつ with 重さ, forming the phrase this luggage's weight.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 重さ the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 何キロ asks for the number of kilograms, while ですか makes the question polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.why: の creates a modifying relationship between the luggage and its weight. は marks the weight as the information being asked about, while 何キロですか asks for the value in kilograms.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the question directly asks how heavy the luggage is, which sounds more natural in conversation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used, the weight becomes identified information rather than the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q13.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit の between two nouns; in this sentence, の is the necessary link for saying the luggage's weight.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vi: This dish is simple, so even children can make it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aなですから ＋ Nでも ＋ potential V ますよ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this dish the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects the quality of the dish with the result that it can be made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: でも is attached to a noun to emphasize that even a less likely or surprising case can do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 作れます is the potential form of 作る, while よ emphasizes the information the speaker wants the listener to note.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason with ですから, and the second clause gives the special subject with 子どもでも. The potential form 作れます describes the ability to make the dish, not just the act of making it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead, the sentence only says that children can make it, losing the meaning that even children can make it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If にも is used instead, the meaning is closer to children can also make it for someone or children are also allowed to have it made for them, so it is less suitable than でも.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.tip: Do not translate 作れます as make; it is the potential form, meaning can make or be able to make.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q14.kobun.cn: N・Aな ＋ でも; V可能形; Aな ＋ ですから
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.vi: Sorry, I have something to do, so I will go home first.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと reduces the degree of 用事, making the expression softer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks 用事 as something that exists or is happening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason with going home first, creating a soft and polite tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the order or time when going home takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: 帰ります is the main predicate and politely expresses the decision to go home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.why: 用事があるので gives the reason first, followed by the main action 帰ります. ので makes the explanation gentle and polite, which is suitable when asking to leave first.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead, the reason is more direct and conversational, and less gentle than ので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If あって is used instead, the sentence sounds natural in conversation, but the connection between the cause and result is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.tip: With a noun, you must use Nな＋ので, as in 用事があるので; do not connect a noun directly to ので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.vi: According to this morning's weather forecast, a strong typhoon is said to be coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.sk: N の N によると ＋ Aい ＋ N が ＋ plain-form V そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今朝 with 天気よほう, forming the phrase this morning's weather forecast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: によると indicates the source of information supporting the statement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きい comes before 台風 to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks 台風 as the subject of the action of coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: そうだ comes after the plain form of 来る to report information that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.why: The phrase によると gives the information source before the forecast content. 大きい modifies 台風, 台風が marks the subject, and 来るそうだ reports that the typhoon is coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 来そうだ is used instead, it means that it seems to be coming soon based on the speaker's judgment, not on information heard from a source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 来るらしい is used instead, the tone of guessing or uncertainty is clearer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse 来るそうだ with 来そうだ; そうだ after the plain form means it is said that, while after the stem ます it means it seems.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ; N ＋ によると
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.vi: When I was young, I broke a camera and was scolded by my father.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.sk: N のとき ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ N に ＋ past passive V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: とき indicates the time when the main event occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object affected by the act of breaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects breaking the camera with the result of being scolded.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the past passive form and describes the speaker being affected by the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence. Then the cause is connected with て, followed by the result in the passive form. The particle に identifies the person who scolded the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that breaking it happened accidentally or caused regret.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q17.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget に before the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.vi: The children have become quiet, haven't they? It seems they have gone to sleep.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.sk: N ＋ Aな に ＋ なる ＋ ね。 ＋ V short past form ＋ ようだ ＋ ね
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase introduces the topic being discussed; the comma creates a natural pause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: なりました describes a change to a quiet state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.ch.2.vi: seem to have gone to sleep
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ようです comes after the short form to make an inference based on observed signs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.why: The first sentence states the children's current condition, while the second guesses the reason for their quietness. ようだ connects with 寝た in the short form to express a guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～そうだ is used, the sentence usually relies more on appearance or direct signs, without emphasizing a situational guess as ようだ does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may directly attach ようだ after a noun or adjective な and forget の or な.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の ＋ ようだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.vi: Since the beginning of this month, the weather has suddenly been getting colder; are you well?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the point when this month begins.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: てから connects the starting point with the event that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 急に modifies the unexpected change in temperature.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to the form く to connect with なる, and then て is used to continue the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: てくる describes a change continuing up to the present; が connects to the following question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: ですか creates a polite question about someone's health.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる; Aい omit い ＋ くなる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.why: てから sets the time point, while てくる shows that the change toward colder weather has continued up to the present. が gently shifts from weather information to a polite inquiry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～ていく, the change would be viewed as continuing from the present into the future.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ようになる is used, the sentence describes the beginning of a state or ability, not just a change in temperature.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the time direction of てくる and ていく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: I will put the wallet in the bag in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.sk: N place に ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ おく
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place that receives the object being put in.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being put into the bag.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 入れて in the て form connects with おきます to create the meaning of preparing an action in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ておく describes doing something beforehand and keeping the result as preparation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.cn: N place＋に＋transitive V; Vて＋おく／Vないで＋おく
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: かばんに is the place where something is put, while さいふを is the object moved there. 入れておく combines putting something in with the idea of preparing beforehand.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入れてある is used, the sentence emphasizes that the wallet is already in place, without emphasizing the speaker's intention to prepare.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 入れている is used, the sentence usually only describes an action in progress or an object being kept inside, without the clear meaning of doing it beforehand as in ておく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use で after かばん when saying that an object is put inside; に marks the destination of 入れる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.vi: About what time will the company president return?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ごろ ＋ お＋Vます-stem＋になる ＋ でしょうか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the company president as the person whose return time is being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: ごろ indicates an approximate time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: お＋the form without ます＋になる is a respectful way to describe a superior's action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: でしょうか makes the question more polite and softer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by an approximate time and then the company president's action. Honorific language is used because the person performing the action deserves respect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If お～ください is used, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to perform an action, rather than a question about the company president.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use this honorific for their own actions instead of for the actions of someone who deserves respect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.vi: Sitting continuously for a long time is not good for the body.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.sk: Aい ＋ N ＋ Vます-stem＋つづける＋ている＋のは ＋ N に ＋ negative Aい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the action of sitting continuously and shows the duration.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.1.vi: the act of continuing to sit
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: つづける connects with the verb stem to show a continuing action; のは turns the whole phrase into the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the object affected by whether something is good or bad.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: よくない is the negative form of よい and forms the evaluative predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.why: The whole action phrase is nominalized with のは to make it the topic, and is then judged to be bad for the body. ている emphasizes that the state of sitting continuously is still continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～ながら, the sentence describes two actions happening at the same time, without emphasizing the continuation of one action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse つづける with ている; つづける emphasizes continuing to do something, while ている emphasizes an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q22.kobun.vi: The train has stopped because of an accident.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: ために indicates the cause that made the train stop.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the train as the subject in a stopped state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ている describes the current state resulting from the train having stopped.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q22.kobun.why: The cause phrase comes first, followed by the subject and the resulting state. ために connects a noun with the meaning “because of.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～ので, the sentence still gives a cause, but the tone is softer and more naturally explanatory.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～によって is used, the cause is presented in a more objective or formal way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ために as a purpose; in this sentence, Nのために means the cause, “because of.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.vi: My older brother studied abroad in the UK, but his English is not good.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the older brother as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates where the study abroad took place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: のに connects two contrasting clauses: he studied abroad, but the result was not as expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks English as the subject being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: うまくない is the predicate and describes poor English ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the action clause, and then のに creates a contrast with the result in the following clause. 英語が is the subject of the comment うまくない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with けれども, the sentence still means “but,” with a more neutral tone and less emphasis on being contrary to expectations than のに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ても, the meaning changes to “even if one studies in the UK, one is still not good at English,” with more emphasis on the assumed condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget な before のに when the preceding part is an adjective な or a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.vi: It may rain, so take an umbrella and go outside.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the phenomenon predicted to occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: かもしれない expresses an uncertain possibility, while から connects the reason to the suggestion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being carried.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects 持つ with the action 出かける in consecutive order.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The volitional form よう gives an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋かもしれない; plain clause＋から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.why: The weather prediction clause gives the reason, and から connects that reason to the suggestion. The two actions, 持って and 出かけよう, are connected by the て form to show that one is done and then the other.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If でしょう is used, the prediction “it will probably rain” shows that the speaker considers this possibility more likely.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q24.kobun.tip: Do not connect かもしれない with a noun or a verb in the polite form; use the plain form before this pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.vi: Since we leave at 9:00, please gather before 8:50.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the departure time as the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects information about the departure time with the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: までに indicates the deadline by which gathering must be completed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the verb 集まる with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください is a pattern used to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.why: The departure time is given first as the reason, and then the deadline is placed directly before the verb “gather.” までに emphasizes that the action must be completed before a certain time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is used instead of までに, the meaning is “gather until 8:50,” without clearly emphasizing completion before the deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If うちに is used, the sentence emphasizes doing something while the time or situation still exists, not a fixed deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse までに with まで; までに is used for something that must be completed before a certain time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q25.kobun.cn: N＋までに; Vて＋ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: Cold days like those in winter continue to last.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: のように creates a comparison and modifies 寒い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 寒い comes before 日 to modify “days.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: つづいて in the て form connects with います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ている describes the state of the cold days continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: 冬のように compares the degree of coldness with winter, and then 寒い modifies 日. 日がつづいています creates a predicate showing that such days are continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 冬らしく is used, the sentence means that something has winter-like features rather than directly comparing it with winter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 冬みたいに is used, the meaning is similar, but the expression is more casual than ように.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: ように after a noun must be followed by の; do not say 冬ように directly in this comparison structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q3.tokens.7.m: be; be in the process of
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi: Since I came by car, I cannot drink alcohol today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.sk: N で ＋ Vた ＋ ので、N は ＋ N は ＋ negative potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means of transportation used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason with the result and sounds softer and more explanatory than から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: は states the time and sets the background for what follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: は marks alcohol as the item being contrasted or limited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 飲めません is the negative potential form, showing that the speaker cannot drink alcohol.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: 車で来たので gives the reason for not being able to drink. 今日 は limits the time, while おさけは uses は a second time to emphasize that alcohol specifically is what the speaker cannot drink.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence only states that alcohol is what cannot be drunk, without a clear contrast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If を飲みません is used, it means that the speaker does not drink alcohol by choice or habit, not necessarily that the speaker cannot drink it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を in every sentence with the verb “drink,” but は here contrasts and limits the topic: alcohol specifically is what the speaker cannot drink.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな＋ので; N＋は＋Vない／Vません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: Since I am hungry, let's eat some bread or an onigiri.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.sk: State が ＋ Vたから ＋ Nか ＋ Nでも ＋ V意向形
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that is in the hungry state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: でも follows a noun to give a representative suggestion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: よう is the volitional form, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before から, followed by foods offered as suggested choices. The よう form at the end of the sentence turns the action of eating into an invitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone becomes softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ましょう is used, the invitation is more polite than よう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand でも to mean “but,” but in this structure it means “for example.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q5.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aな・Nだ ＋ から; N ＋ でも; V意向形
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: I accidentally ate too much breakfast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the food affected by the action of eating.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べ removes ます and connects to すぎる to show an action beyond the proper limit; て connects to しまう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: てしまった describes a completed action, often with regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: The object of eating takes を. The verb 食べ connects with すぎる to create the meaning “too much,” and then the form てしまった adds the feeling of having done it accidentally and regretting it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 食べすぎた is used, the sentence only emphasizes eating too much, without emphasizing the feeling of accidentally doing it or regretting it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 食べておいた, the meaning becomes eating beforehand or preparing by eating in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: Do not connect 食べる directly with すぎる; remove ます from the form ます to make 食べすぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q6.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ すぎる; Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: Every morning, I make boxed lunches for my younger brother and younger sister.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.sk: Nは ＋ Time ＋ NやNの ＋ Nを ＋ Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person who performs the main action of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.vi: of the younger brother and younger sister
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: や lists some, but not all, objects, while の connects this phrase with おべんとう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the boxed lunch as the thing being made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 作って is the て form, connecting the verb 作る with います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: Vている describes an ongoing action or a repeated habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: は introduces the person performing the action, while 毎朝 shows when it is repeated. The phrase 弟や妹の modifies おべんとう, and 作っています shows that this is a habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this structure is used, the sentence lists several typical actions instead of emphasizing a habit that continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If ています is replaced with てあります, the meaning becomes a state in which something has already been prepared by someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: や does not mean listing everything; it usually implies that there are other objects as well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q7.kobun.cn: N ＋ や ＋ N; N ＋ の ＋ N; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: This is the supermarket I often stop at before going home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the place being introduced the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the action 帰る in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: A clause in the dictionary form comes before and modifies the noun スーパー.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: Vる＋まえに indicates the time when an action occurs before another action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: よる comes before スーパー to modify the supermarket that is often visited.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: です ends the introductory sentence and identifies the place as a supermarket.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: The phrase わたしが家へ帰るまえに states the time, while よくよる modifies スーパー. Everything before スーパー helps identify which supermarket it is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If まえに is replaced with あとで, the meaning changes to often stopping by after going home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If とき is used, the sentence only says that it happens when going home; it does not necessarily emphasize that stopping by happens first.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: With まえに, the verb must use the dictionary form 帰る, not the past form 帰った.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q8.kobun.cn: Nへ ＋ 帰る; Vる ＋ まえに; Vる ＋ N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: There was a loud sound in the next room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects となり with へや to form the phrase “the next room”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the sound occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな directly modifies the noun 音.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the sound that is heard or sensed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: する combines with 音が to express that a sound was produced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: で identifies where the event occurs, while 音がする is the structure used to describe a sound being heard. 大きな comes directly before 音 to describe the sound.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 音が聞こえる is used, the focus is on the listener being able to hear the sound, not only on the sound being produced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 音が鳴る is used, the meaning is closer to a sound ringing or being made by an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: With smells, sounds, or sensations, learners may easily use をする; the correct structure is Nがする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: He only eats the food I cook, and he has never cooked for himself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that he is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who performs the cooking action in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 作る comes before 料理 to modify it and show that it is food cooked by me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the food that he eats.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: だけ limits the action to eating, while で connects to the contrasting situation in the next clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: で indicates how the action is performed: by himself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: Vたことがない denies the experience of having done something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: The clause わたしが作る comes before 料理 to modify the food. だけで limits his action to eating, and then ことがない states that he has never cooked by himself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べるしかない is used, the meaning becomes “there is no choice but to eat,” with a sense that there is no other option.
