default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 作ったことはない is used, the sentence only denies the experience and may create a contrastive tone that is softer than the current expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use ことがない with the plain verb form to say “have never”; experience is expressed with Vたことがある, or its negative form is Vたことがない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.tokens.8.m: word to fill in, possibly だけ: only, merely
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q1.kobun.cn: Vる＋だけ（で）; Vた＋ことがある／ことがない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vi: Because I want to study abroad, I decided to quit my current job.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.0.vi: because I want to study abroad
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 今 with the noun 仕事 to modify the job.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the job as the object of the action of quitting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ことに combines with する to turn the action やめる into the speaker’s decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: しました is the polite past form of する, completing the pattern ことにしました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with ので, followed by the object 仕事を and then the action やめる. ことにする expresses a decision made by the subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means that quitting the job was decided because of circumstances or by someone else, without emphasizing the speaker’s decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ことにする, a personal decision, with ことになる, a decision that was already set or made by someone outside.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vi: My younger brother is going to take an exam soon, but he does nothing except play games every day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 時 point に ＋ N が ＋ あるのに ＋ Time ＋ N ばかり ＋ Vて ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the younger brother is the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the exam as the subject of ある.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: のに connects a situation that is contrary to what is expected in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: ばかり limits the object and emphasizes that he only plays games without doing anything else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: して is the て form of する, connecting to the verb あそんでいます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: ています describes an action in progress or a repeated habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.why: あるのに creates a contrast between an exam coming soon and playing games every day. ばかり comes after ゲーム to limit what the younger brother does, while て connects two consecutive actions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ばかり is replaced with だけ, the sentence only states the limited range of playing games, so the critical tone is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If しか〜ない is used, the sentence emphasizes that he does absolutely nothing else besides playing games.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that Vて＋ばかりいる requires いる and often expresses a complaint about doing only one thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka is cheerful and kind to everyone, so he has many friends.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Mr. Tanaka is the topic of the listed characteristics.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: し connects the first characteristic with the following reason or characteristic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the object toward which the adjective 親切 is directed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: だから connects the reason with the result 友だちが多い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks 友だち as the subject described by 多い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.why: し is used to list positive characteristics, while だから states the direct reason for the result of having many friends. に marks the object of the adjective 親切.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If し is replaced with そして, the sentence sounds more like joining two sentences and does not clearly show a list of reasons.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If だから is replaced with ので, the reason stays the same, but the expression sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use し as a simple connector, but in this sentence し also suggests that the speaker is listing several reasons or characteristics.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形＋し／Aい＋し／Aな＋だし／N＋だし
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q13.kobun.sk: Greeting ＋ どうぞ ＋ お＋Vます-remove＋ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: お＋the ます form of a verb＋ください creates a polite invitation or request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q13.kobun.why: どうぞ comes before an invitation to make the sentence more natural and polite. お入りください uses a polite honorific request structure, suitable for an employee speaking to a customer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is substituted, the sentence still means “please come in,” but the level of politeness is lower お入りください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily add ます after ください, but this pattern uses the verb stem in the ます form with ます removed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.vi: If you cannot read Chinese characters, you cannot do this work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks 漢字 as the object read in the ability 読める.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition with the inevitable result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that this work is the topic of the ability to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: できません is a polite negative form, stating that the work cannot be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.why: The condition 読めないと comes before the result できません, following the order of condition and then result. が marks the object of reading, while は shifts the focus to the work that needs to be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ないと is replaced with なければ, the sentence still means if one cannot read, but the tone is more formal and the condition is clearer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If ても is used, the sentence means that even if one can read Chinese characters, one still cannot do the work, changing the relationship to concession.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate と as and, but in this structure と means if...then and usually expresses an inevitable result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.vi: Please come in wearing your shoes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.sk: どうぞ ＋ N を ＋ Vたまま ＋ お＋Vます-remove＋ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks shoes as the object being worn.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: Vたまま describes keeping the state of wearing shoes while performing the following action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: お入りください is a polite invitation and serves as the final predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.why: くつを はいたまま describes a state that is kept unchanged, then connects directly to the action of entering. This pattern shows that the following action happens without changing the previous state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If たまま is replaced with ながら, the sentence emphasizes two actions happening at the same time rather than keeping a state unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If ないで is used, the sentence means entering without doing a certain action, so it no longer means keeping one's shoes on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand まま as still, but it must follow Vた to emphasize that a completed state is being maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: This is an exclamation showing that the speaker realizes the situation is not good.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: また modifies the following action and shows that the event happened one more time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content of the action that was accidentally performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてしまった describes a completed action with a sense of regret or against one's wishes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q16.kobun.why: また comes before the verb phrase to emphasize repetition. ねぼうをする is a verb phrase with を marking the content of the action, followed by てしまった, which shows that the event happened unintentionally and the speaker regrets it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～ておく, it means doing something in advance or preparing beforehand, without the meaning of accidentally doing it and regretting it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that てしまう does not only mean completing something, but often also expresses regret or an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q17.kobun.vi: No matter how much I am asked, I will not lend this camera.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら begins the concessive part and emphasizes that no degree of something will change the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: Vても connects to the main clause to mean that even if this happens, the result will not change.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that this camera is the topic being refused for lending.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 貸してあげる describes doing something for another person, while ない negates that action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q17.kobun.why: いくら～ても creates the concessive part before the main clause. このカメラは is the topic, while 貸してあげない places the refusal at the end of the sentence and negates doing something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～てくれない is used, the speaker requests or complains that another person does not do something for them, which is different from the speaker doing something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use あげる from the receiver's point of view; in this sentence, the speaker is the person lending, and another person receives the benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.vi: My stomach has hurt since this morning. It seems I ate too much last night.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows when the stomach pain began.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ゆうべ adds the time when the action of eating too much happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べすぎる is formed from the stem 食べ of 食べます and すぎる. It shows an action that goes beyond the normal amount; the past form shows that it already happened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: ようだ is placed at the end of the clause to make a guess based on the current situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.why: The first sentence states the starting time and the current state. The second sentence puts the time of the event first, uses 食べすぎた to state the suspected cause, and ends with ようだ to make the statement less certain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～そうだ is used, it usually describes an appearance or a sign that something is about to happen. It does not stress a guess based on a situation as ようだ does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～らしい is used, the meaning is closer to information heard from someone or a more objective judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may connect 食べる directly to すぎる. They need to omit る and use the stem 食べ before すぎる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q18.kobun.cn: Vます形のますを取る・Aいのいを取る・Aな語幹＋すぎる; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の＋ようだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.vi: Students who did not take the exam must write a report.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the exam as the object of the action of taking it in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The short-form clause comes before 学生 to modify “students who did not take the exam.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase 試験をうけなかった学生 forms the topic, while は states the group being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the report as the thing that must be written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: The conditional negative form 書かない changes into 書かなければ and combines with ならない to express obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.why: The clause 試験をうけなかった comes before 学生 to identify which students are meant. After the topic comes the object レポートを, and the obligation pattern at the end states what must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～なくてもいい, it means that the action is not necessary, which is the opposite of the obligation in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～べきだ is used, the meaning is that the speaker thinks someone should do it or has a duty to do it. It is less direct than a required rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the order and put 学生 before the modifying clause. In Japanese, the description always comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q19.kobun.cn: Vない（いを取る）＋ければならない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: This knife is used to cut bread.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the knife is the topic whose use is being explained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing being cut.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: Vるのに shows the purpose for which the knife is used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 使います is the predicate. It says what purpose the knife is used for.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: パンを is the object of the cutting action, while 切るのに turns that action into a purpose. The purpose phrase comes before 使います to state the use of the knife.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If パンを切るために使います is used, the meaning is still “used to cut bread,” but the expression is more formal and direct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: ように usually goes with a goal or a state that should be reached. It is less natural than のに when talking about the use of a tool.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: In the pattern for showing purpose, のに here does not mean “although.” Understand it as “for what purpose” or “to do what.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q2.kobun.cn: Vる＋のに＋使う; N＋に＋使う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.vi: The cake is finished baking. Please try eating it to see whether it is tasty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the cake as the object that has completed the baking process.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: かどうか turns the content おいしい into something to check, then adds it to the action of trying to eat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてみる describes trying to do something, while ください turns the statement into a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.why: The first sentence reports the cake's state. In the second sentence, おいしいかどうか is the content to confirm. It comes before 食べてみてください, asking the listener to try eating it to check that point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If only ～か is used, it still creates an indirect question, but it does not clearly stress the two possibilities of yes or no as ～かどうか does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If かどうか is omitted and only 食べてみてください is used, the meaning remains “try eating,” but it does not clearly state the purpose of checking whether it is tasty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put かどうか at the end of the whole sentence. This pattern must come immediately after the content to be confirmed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N＋かどうか; Vて＋みる; Vて＋ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.vi: Because the roads are crowded, I think taking the train will be better than taking a taxi.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the road as the subject that is in a crowded or congested state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the conclusion in the following clause; こんでいる shows the state of being crowded.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: より marks the taxi as the standard for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: のほうが marks the option chosen as better in the comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the judgment being quoted before 思います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.why: The clause with から comes first to state the reason. Then より gives the comparison standard, のほうが selects the better option, and とと思います frames the speaker's judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ほど～ない is used, the meaning becomes “not as good as a taxi,” instead of stating that the train is better than a taxi.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the complete comparison pattern. If より is omitted, it is still possible to say that one option is better, but the comparison standard is less clear.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may reverse the positions of the two means of transport. In this pattern, the standard of comparison comes before より, while the option being judged comes before のほうが.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q21.kobun.cn: N1より＋N2のほうが＋Aい・Aな; V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nだ＋と思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.vi: I plan to stay in Japan until March next year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states Japan as the place being discussed, while に shows a place of existence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 来年 with the specific time point that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: まで marks the ending time of staying in Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: いる in the dictionary form comes before つもり to show an intention to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: つもりです creates a polite way to express the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.why: The place is stated first with は, followed by the ending time with まで. The verb いる in the dictionary form connects directly to つもりです to express an intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 予定だ makes the sentence focus more on a plan that has already been arranged and less on personal intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse まで with a starting time, but まで always shows an ending limit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q22.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ つもりだ; Nの ＋ つもりだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.vi: I think I may be able to go home early today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Adv ＋ potential V ＋ と ＋ 思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic and the time setting for the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 早く is the adverb form of 早い and modifies the action of returning home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.ch.2.vi: that it is possible to return home
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content being thought; 帰れる is the potential form, meaning that it is possible to return home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 思います is the main verb and takes the entire clause before と as the content of the thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.why: Today’s context comes at the beginning of the sentence, and the adverb 早く modifies 帰れる. The content of the thought must come before と, followed by the main verb 思います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with と思っています gives the feeling of a thought or plan that has already been formed and is still being kept.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use the polite form 帰れます directly before と in this basic pattern; use the short form 帰れる instead.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + と思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.vi: Do you have any questions about this problem?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the question or problem being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: について indicates the topic or object being mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 何か expresses an unspecified thing and modifies 質問.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes 質問 the topic in order to ask whether there are any questions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: ありませんか is a polite way to ask whether any questions exist.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.why: について limits the topic to this problem. 何か comes before 質問 to ask openly about any question, while は makes 質問 the object to be confirmed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with に関して gives almost the same meaning as について, but it sounds more formal and written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.tip: Do not translate について as a place particle; in this pattern, it means about or related to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q24.kobun.cn: N + について; N + についての + N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.vi: That room is being used by someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before へや to identify the room being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the room as the topic, with a slight contrast to other places.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ほかの modifies 人 and identifies the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject who is using the room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 使って is the て form and connects the verb with います in a pattern that expresses an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: います completes the Vている pattern and shows that the action is continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.why: The room is presented as the topic, while the user is the subject, so it takes が. 使っている describes an action happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 使われています changes the sentence to the passive voice and emphasizes that the room is being used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out が before the subject of an action in a clause, but here 人が is required to identify who is using the room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vi: At home, I make the children do cleaning and laundry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: では gives the context and location where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who is made or allowed to do the work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: や connects nouns in an incomplete list.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the tasks assigned to be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: させています is the causative form combined with ています, expressing the repeated action of letting or making someone do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: では sets the family context, に indicates the person acting under the causative form, and や lists typical tasks. The causative form shows that the children do these tasks.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうじとせんたく is used, the sentence lists exactly two tasks and does not have the feeling of “and similar tasks.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 子どもにそうじやせんたくをしてもらっています is used, it means that I have the children help me, emphasizing the speaker’s benefit rather than the act of making them do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: With a causative verb, the person who performs the action usually takes に; do not confuse this に with を, which marks the task.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vi: At this company, everyone speaks English, so it is fine even if you do not know Japanese.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: では gives the context, meaning within this company.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject who performs the action of speaking English.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the language used in the action of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason clause to the result and gives a softer explanatory tone than から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the ability or object mentioned in できる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.5.vi: even if you do not know
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: できない changes to できなくて and then adds も to express “even if you do not know Japanese.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: かまわない is the main predicate and expresses that there is no problem or no need to worry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with ので, followed by the concessive condition できなくても before the conclusion かまわない. The particle が marks the subject or object of ability, while を marks the language being spoken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes that it is permitted not to know Japanese, while かまわない emphasizes that it is not a problem.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ても as only “also,” but in this sentence it has the concessive meaning “even if...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q4.kobun.cn: Vて形・Aいく・Aな・N＋ても／でも
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: Sometimes I dream that I become a bird and fly in the sky.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the result of a change, while て connects the action of becoming a bird with the next action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the space where the action of flying takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: とぶ comes before ゆめ to modify it and show that it is a dream about flying in the sky.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the dream being seen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 見る is the main verb and combines with ゆめを to express dreaming about something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: こと turns an event into a noun, while がある expresses that the event happens sometimes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: 鳥になって connects two successive states or actions, while とぶ comes before ゆめ as a clause that modifies a noun. The phrase ゆめを見る is the content, and then ことがある adds the meaning that it happens sometimes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence says that the speaker has had the experience of dreaming this way, not that it happens sometimes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ことがある with the meaning of experience; when used with V辞書形, this pattern usually expresses something that happens sometimes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vi: When I return to my country, I think I will work as a Japanese teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the destination of the action of returning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a condition or assumed time with the intention in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being taught.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 教える comes before 仕事 to modify it and identify the type of work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the work that will be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: しよう is the volitional form and combines with と思います to express the speaker’s plan or intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.why: 帰ったら sets a time or condition at the beginning of the sentence. 教える modifies 仕事, then 仕事を is the object of しよう; the volitional form combines with と思います to express the speaker’s intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence shows a clearer plan or determination, while と思います is softer and suggests a thought or intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use the plain form before と思います when expressing an intention; change the verb to the volitional form, such as しよう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q6.kobun.cn: V意向形＋と思う／と思います
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vi: This pen is easy to write with, isn't it? Let's just buy one more.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.sk: N ＋ Vます-removeます＋やすい ＋ Nだね。もう ＋ quantity ＋ V意向形
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: これ makes the item being discussed the topic of the comment or question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 書き is the removed ます of 書く, joined to やすい to form an adjective expressing ease of action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: だね concludes the statement and confirms the comment about the pen with the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: もう adds the idea of buying another one in addition to the pen already mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: １本 indicates the number of long objects being bought, and 本 is the counter for pens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: 買おう is the volitional form, expressing a gentle invitation or decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.why: 書きやすい comes before ペン to describe the pen's feature. もう１本 is a phrase giving an additional quantity, while 買おう uses the volitional form for a suggestion or decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with にくい, the sentence means that the pen is difficult to write with.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with this pattern, the speaker only guesses that the pen seems easy to write with.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q7.kobun.tip: Do not connect やすい directly to the dictionary form; remove ます from the verb before adding やすい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vi: When I was confused because I did not know the way, a person nearby showed me the way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that is known or unknown in わかる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: わからない changes to the なくて form to connect the reason with the state of being in difficulty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ていた expresses an ongoing state, while たら creates the point in time when someone appeared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the location of the person being mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: いた comes before 人 to modify and identify the person who was nearby.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the person who gave directions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: 教えてくれた expresses that another person performed the action for the speaker's benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.why: わからなくて states the reason, while こまっていたら sets the background of an ongoing situation before the main event. The nearby person becomes the new subject, performs 教えて, and くれる shows that the action benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with てもらう, the sentence focuses on the speaker receiving help or asking someone else to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with てあげる, the viewpoint shifts to the person who performs the action for someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q8.kobun.tip: Learners may easily omit the subject of くれる; with てくれる, another person performs the action, while the benefit goes to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vi: The red umbrella? If it is the red umbrella, there is one here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 赤い comes before かさ to modify it and identify the umbrella's color.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ですか forms a confirmation question about the information just mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.2.vi: if it is the red umbrella
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: なら takes the noun 赤いかさ as a condition or topic and gives the corresponding information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates where the umbrella exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses the existence of an object, while よ is used to inform the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.why: The first sentence confirms the noun 赤いかさ. In the second sentence, なら takes that same noun as a condition or topic, and ここにあります states where the object exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If だったら is used, the condition is assumed more clearly; なら is often used when receiving and responding to information just mentioned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with は, the sentence only introduces the topic “as for the red umbrella...,” without the clear conditional meaning of なら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t4-q9.kobun.tip: なら attaches directly after the noun, without adding だ before なら in the Nなら structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vi: I received a watch as a gift to celebrate entering school.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the event of entering school with おいわい, creating the meaning of a gift or congratulations for entering school.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the purpose or occasion for receiving the gift.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: もらいました is the predicate and expresses that the speaker received something from someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: The event of entering school is connected to おいわい by の. に states the occasion or purpose, を marks the gift, and もらいました expresses the act of receiving.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with として emphasizes that the gift is given as a gift to celebrate entering school.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に in this sentence with the giver; the giver usually goes with から or に, depending on the expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vi: Because the weather is nice today, I will do the laundry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that today is the time and topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the adjective いい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason いい with the action します in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the verb します.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: します is the main predicate and expresses the action that will be performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.why: 天気がいい is a clause describing a situation, in which が marks the subject of the adjective. から comes after the reason and before the main action せんたくをします.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ので, the meaning is still “because... therefore...,” but the explanation sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If ために is used, the sentence can sound more objective or written, and is less natural here than から.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use を after 天気, but with a state-describing adjective such as いい, they need to use が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vi: Don't just keep reading books. Why don't you go outside sometimes?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: ばかり limits the object and creates the sense of doing only one thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 読んで is the て form, connecting the action of reading with the following negative pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ～ていないで asks someone not to continue maintaining the action they are doing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: たまには states the frequency, and は creates a contrast with only reading books.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: へ indicates the direction of the movement in 出る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 出ませんか uses a negative question form to make a gentle invitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.why: 本ばかり modifies the action 読んで and emphasizes only reading books. ～ていないで asks the listener to stop or not continue that action, and then 出ませんか gives an invitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ばかり is replaced with だけ, the sentence only states the neutral limitation “only reading books” and reduces the complaining tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If only 読まないで is used, the meaning is “don't read books,” without the sense of “don't keep reading continuously” expressed by ～ていないで.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.tip: Learners may understand ばかり as “only” in every case, but with repeated activities it often implies a complaint.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q11.kobun.cn: N＋ばかり; Vて＋ばかり＋いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the window as the subject of the intransitive verb あく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: あいて is the て form of あく, and it connects to います to express a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: います in ～ている is an auxiliary verb showing that the current state is still continuing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q12.kobun.why: The window itself is in the open state, so が is used with the intransitive verb あく. Here, ～ている does not stress an action in progress; it stresses that the state still remains.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If をあけています is used, it means that someone is opening the window or leaving it in a state that they opened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If あきました is used, the sentence only reports that the window opened. It does not stress that the state is continuing now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with あく, but the intransitive verb あく goes with が; を is used only with the transitive verb あける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vi: I am interested in Japanese history.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本 with れきし to modify it and identify what kind of history is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object that the speaker is interested in.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks きょうみ as the object of 持つ in the fixed phrase 興味を持つ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: もって is the て form of 持つ, and it connects to います to express an existing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: います in ～ている shows that the state of being interested continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.why: 日本のれきし creates a noun phrase in which the history is identified as Japan's history. に marks the object of interest, while 興味を持っている expresses that the state of being interested continues.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 興味がある is used, the meaning is still “be interested,” but the structure uses が with 興味 as an existing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with を勉強しています, the meaning changes to studying Japanese history, not simply being interested in it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the object of interest, but the pattern 興味を持つ uses に for the object and を for 興味.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q13.kobun.cn: N＋に＋興味を持つ; Vて＋いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vi: Because I studied hard, the exam was quite easy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: よく modifies 勉強した and shows the level of studying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 勉強した is the plain past form, and it connects to ので to give the reason for the statement that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents the exam as the topic evaluated in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: かんたんでした is the polite past adjective predicate な, giving an evaluation of the exam.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.why: The clause 勉強したので comes first to state the reason, and then 試験は puts the topic before the evaluation. ので creates a mild, objective cause-and-effect relationship between studying hard and the evaluation of the exam.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので replaces から, the basic meaning does not change, but the explanation becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If ために is used, the sentence may express a more objective and formal reason, and it sounds less natural in simple conversation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect ので directly after な or a noun, but な must be added: 簡単なので, 学生なので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.vi: No matter how much I work, my salary does not increase.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら states how high the degree of the action in the conditional clause is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: Vて＋も connects a concessive clause and expresses that the result remains unchanged no matter how much one works.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 給料 the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 上がりません is the main predicate in the polite negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.cn: Vて・Aくて・Aなで・Nで ＋ も; usually used in the form いくら～ても
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.why: The clause はたらいても states a concessive condition, while the main clause shows that the result does not change. は emphasizes that 給料 is the object being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Without いくら, the sentence only means that the salary does not increase even if one works; it does not stress the degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～たら is used, the sentence becomes an ordinary condition and no longer has the meaning “no matter what happens.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget も after the て form and say only いくら働いて, making the sentence incomplete.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.vi: Eating in such a hurry is not good for your body.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: そんなに modifies the manner or degree of hurrying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of いそぐ connects to 食べる and shows how the action of eating is carried out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: V辞書形＋と connects a condition with a natural or usual result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the object affected by the adjective よくない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: よくない is the negative form of よい, while ですよ adds a tone of informing and reminding.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.why: いそいで adds the manner to 食べる, and then 食べると creates a condition leading to a natural result. 体に comes before よくない to show the affected object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～たら is used, the sentence only states a specific condition and does not stress a natural result like ～と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～なら is used, the sentence means “if it is true that you eat in such a hurry…,” usually based on existing information or an assumption.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use によくない instead of 体によくない, but に is enough here to show the affected object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q16.kobun.cn: V辞書形＋と; Aい＋と; N・Aな＋だと
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.vi: I read the newspaper every morning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes わたし the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎朝 shows the time when the action of reading the newspaper is repeated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being read.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 読みます is the polite present predicate and expresses a habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.why: 毎朝 comes before the object and predicate to state the repeated time. 新聞を combines with 読みます in the pattern for a verb reading an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: This connection is incorrect because が marks the subject, while 新聞 is the thing being read.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding に after 毎朝 is unnatural in a sentence that states a repeated time like this one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を because Vietnamese has no separate particle for marking the object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.vi: My father can speak both Chinese and English.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with 父 and shows possession or a family relationship.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 父 the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: も replaces を and adds 中国語 to the list of languages spoken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: も after 英語 shows that English is also within the same object range.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 話します is the main predicate and takes the two objects listed with も.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.cn: N ＋ も; when listing: Nも ＋ Nも
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.why: わたしの identifies the father, while 父は is the topic of the sentence. Both languages are objects of 話します and are connected by も to express that both are included.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence simply lists two languages that are spoken and does not stress “both Chinese and English.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If だけ is used, the sentence means speaking only Chinese or only English, depending on its position, and removes the meaning that both are included.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after both nouns, but in this listing pattern も replaces を and is repeated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.vi: This is bread made by me from rice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the item being introduced the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who performs the action 作った in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the material or source from which a product is made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: A past-tense clause comes before and modifies パン.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: です ends the sentence introducing and identifying the item.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.why: The clause わたしが米から作った comes directly before パン to modify that noun. から indicates the original material, while これは…です creates the framework for introducing the item being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: で emphasizes the means or material used to make something, while から emphasizes the original source material.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: を turns 米 into the object being made, so the meaning becomes growing or producing rice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q19.kobun.tip: Do not put the modifying clause after パン as in English; in Japanese, the modifying part always comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vi: Please let me do that work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before 仕事 to identify a known task.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the work the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person who is allowed or made to perform the action in a causative sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: やらせて is the て form of the causative form やらせる. It connects with ください to make a request for permission or a proposal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to make the request polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: The work mentioned first is the topic, and the person who will do it is marked by わたしに. The causative form combined with ください expresses the wish to be allowed to do that work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks for permission more gently and suggests a wish for the listener to give the speaker a chance to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: The causative form やらせる here does not mean “make me do it”; it means “please let me do it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q2.kobun.cn: N に ＋ V使役形て ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.vi: I heard that a boy's face usually looks more like his mother than his father.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 男の子 with 顔 and identifies the face as belonging to the boy.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 顔 the topic of what was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: より indicates the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: に goes with the verb にる and indicates the person whom the face resembles.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: という marks the content that is said or heard and connects the preceding clause to 話.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the content or story that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.6.n: 聞いた is the main predicate in the plain past tense.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.why: 父親より母親に creates the comparison: more like the mother than the father. The whole clause before という is nominalized as the content of 話, and then 話を聞いた expresses hearing that story.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If NよりNのほうが is used, the sentence directly says that the mother is more similar than the father, so the comparison is clearer and more complete.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If Nと同じ is used, the sentence only says that someone is similar or exactly alike, without showing that the person is more similar than the father.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.vs.2.d: If ～そうだ is used, the sentence may mean “I hear that” or “it seems,” but its connection and nuance differ from quoting content with という.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the person being compared, but に is the particle that goes with verbs expressing resemblance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q20.kobun.cn: Nに似る; V普通形＋という＋N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.vi: My younger sister talks a lot. She is quiet only when she eats.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the younger sister is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: おしゃべりだ is the predicate and uses だ after the noun おしゃべり.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the adjective 静かな into a noun, while は makes being quiet the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 食事 with とき to modify the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: だけ limits the time, while だ completes the final predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.why: The first sentence states a general characteristic of the younger sister. In the second sentence, のは turns the state 静かな into the topic, and then ときだけ limits the time when the younger sister is quiet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか～ない is used instead, the meaning is still “only,” but it requires a negative form and has stronger emphasis.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put だけ before the noun in the wrong position; with a time expression, say 食事のときだけだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.vi: This watermelon is too large to fit in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the watermelon the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きい removes い and connects with すぎる to form 大きすぎる; the て form connects the cause to the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the watermelon should be put.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: 入らない is the negative form and expresses that the watermelon cannot fit inside the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹・Aい remove い・Aな ＋ すぎる; すぎる ＋ て when connecting clauses
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.why: The characteristic 大きすぎて comes first to state the cause. The place receiving the action uses に, while 入らない negates the possibility of the watermelon fitting into the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If あまり～ない is used, it means “not too...,” which is weaker and does not emphasize exceeding the limit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q22.kobun.tip: When connecting すぎる to the following clause, use すぎて, not すぎるて directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.vi: There are many manga on my bookshelf that I bought but still have not read.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: には indicates where something exists and also highlights that location.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 買ったまま describes the state remaining unchanged after buying and connects with the unread state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause meaning not yet read comes before and modifies まんが.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the manga as what exists on the shelf.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: たくさん modifies the quantity of まんが.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: あります is the predicate showing the existence of an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ まま; Vていない expresses a state in which an action has not been completed
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.why: The location 本だなには comes before the existence verb あります. The phrase 買ったまま読んでいない successively modifies まんが, showing that the manga was bought but remains unread.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If けれども is used, the sentence only states the contrast “bought but not read” and does not emphasize the unchanged state as まま does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q23.kobun.tip: Do not understand まま as simply meaning “while”; this pattern emphasizes that the state after the action remains unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.vi: I think Japanese is more difficult than English.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Japanese is the object being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the object used as the standard for comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: と quotes the content of the opinion before 思います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 思います is the main verb and takes the entire opinion before と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.why: より sets English as the standard, while the adjective 難しい describes Japanese. と acts as a quotation marker that connects this opinion to 思います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern directly states which side is greater, so it sounds more certain than the “I think” expression in the current sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means “not as … as …,” so it reverses the direction of comparison from the current sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.tip: After と, a plain form such as 難しい must be used to quote a thought; 難しいです cannot be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q24.kobun.cn: N ＋ より; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ と思う
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.vi: Japanese food is not that delicious.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Japanese food is the object being evaluated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: それほど indicates the level being considered and is usually used with a negative sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: おいしい changes to おいしくない to make the adjective い negative, and です is then added to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.why: それほど comes before an adjective to state the degree, while the negative form おいしくない denies reaching that degree. は keeps 日本料理 as the topic of the evaluation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: あまり～ない also means “not very,” and is often milder and more neutral than それほど～ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: そんなに～ない also denies a degree, but it is often used when responding to a degree that has just been mentioned or observed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use それほど with a positive adjective in this meaning; the pattern normally requires a negative form after it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q25.kobun.cn: N＋ほど＋Vない／Aいくない／Aなではない; それほど＋Vない／Aいくない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vi: I will show Lee the way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person who is guided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb あんないする with あげる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: I will do it for you
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: あげましょう expresses an offer by the speaker to do something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.why: The person performing the action uses が, and the person being guided uses を. The verb あんないする changes to the て form to connect with あげる and express doing something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～てくれる, the meaning changes to another person doing something for the speaker or the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ～てもらう, the focus is on the speaker receiving help from another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse あげる and もらう because both may be translated simply as doing or receiving help, so you need to identify who gives the benefit and who receives it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vi: I had Mr. Tanaka repair this letter for me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies 手紙 and refers to the letter near the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the letter the topic and also the object being repaired.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who performs the helpful action for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the repair action with the pattern of receiving help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: もらいました shows that the speaker received help from Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.why: The letter is made the topic by は. The helper uses に, while the repair action in the て form comes before もらう to show that the speaker received help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～てあげる, the speaker actively does something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ～てくれる, the focus is on another person actively doing something for the speaker or the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use を directly before もらう to indicate the helper; in this pattern, the helper usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q4.kobun.cn: N に ＋ Vて ＋ もらう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vi: Since there is no time, let’s hurry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks what is being discussed as existing or not existing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ない combines with ので to give the reason for the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do an action together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and is connected with ので, followed by the suggestion. ない is the negative form of ある, which fits the meaning that there is no time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～から is used, the reason is usually more direct and stronger than the softer tone of ～ので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～のに is used, the sentence has a contrasting meaning, such as doing something even though there is no time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may forget that with nouns and な adjectives, なので must be used, not ので directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ ので ／ Aな・N ＋ なので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vi: That store is open from 8:30 in the morning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies 店 and refers to a store far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the store is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 朝 indicates the general time of opening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: から marks the starting point of the open state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects あく with いる to create a pattern that describes a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: います combines with the て form to describe the store as being open.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.why: The store is made the topic, followed by the time and the starting point. あいています does not only describe the action of opening; it emphasizes that the store is open and remains open.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に開きます is used, it only says that the store will open at 8:30 and does not emphasize a continuing open state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If まで is used, the point in time is understood as the end of the open state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may translate あいています as “is opening” in the sense of an action, but here it describes the state of the store having opened and still being open.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.tokens.8.m: open; be in an open state
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q6.kobun.cn: N ＋ から ／ Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vi: I heard about Mr. Tanaka from many different people.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: いろいろな modifies 人 and requires な before a noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the source of the information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 田中さん with こと and creates a phrase about matters concerning Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ことを marks the content that the speaker heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.why: The source of the information comes before から, the content heard comes before を, and the verb 聞きました comes last. The structure Nのこと refers to all the matters or information related to that person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If に聞きました is used, it means asking or hearing directly from one specific person, without emphasizing a broad source of information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If について is used, it emphasizes the topic of Mr. Tanaka rather than matters related to him.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may leave out の in 田中さんのこと, making the noun phrase sound unnatural and disconnected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vi: I came to Japan to study computers.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects コンピューター with 勉強 and indicates the subject of study.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content carried out together with する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ために connects a verb in dictionary form to the main clause to state a purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.why: The purpose is placed before するために, while the destination goes with へ and comes before 来ました. 勉強をする is a verb phrase in which を marks the activity of studying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: When ～ように is used, the sentence usually refers to a goal or a state that needs to be reached, not simply the purpose of an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: When ～ので is used, the sentence states the reason for coming to Japan, so it no longer emphasizes the purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the ます form before ために, but with this purpose pattern, the verb must be in dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ために ／ Nの ＋ ために
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vi: Although I went early in the morning, I still could not buy a ticket.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 朝 indicates the time when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 早く is the adverbial form of the adjective 早い and modifies 行った.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 行った is the past plain form, which connects with のに to create a contrast with the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the ticket the topic commented on in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 買えませんでした is the negative past form of the potential form, expressing that it was not possible to buy it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.why: The clause 行ったのに states a condition contrary to the expected result. Then きっぷは shifts to the topic and states the actual result. The form 買えませんでした shows that buying the ticket was not possible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with けれども, the sentence still has a contrastive meaning, but the connection sounds more ordinary and does not emphasize the unexpected result as のに does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ても is used, the meaning is closer to “even if I went early, I still could not buy it,” with more emphasis on a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that のに connects directly after the plain form, while adjectives な and nouns need な added.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t5-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: Because I have just arrived in Japan, I am still not used to it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the destination of the verb 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 来たばかり expresses something that has just been completed, while なので connects the reason to the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ modifies 慣れていません and emphasizes that the state has not changed up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 慣れていません uses ている in the negative form to express the current state of not being used to something yet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: 日本に indicates the destination, and then 来たばかりなので gives the reason. The main clause combines まだ with 慣れていません to express a state that still continues up to now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたところ is used, the focus is on something just being completed at the time of speaking. It does not necessarily emphasize the feeling of “recently” as ばかり does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてから is used, the sentence only means “after coming to Japan” and does not clearly show that the reason is having just arrived.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: ばかり always follows a verb in the た form in this pattern; do not say 来るばかり to express “have just arrived.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q1.kobun.cn: Vた＋ばかり; V普通形・Aい＋ので／Aな・N＋なので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi: Because I took a full week off, my illness got better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.sk: Duration も ＋ Vた ので、 ＋ N が ＋ Aく ＋ なる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: も emphasizes a period that is longer than usual or expected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause before it with the result after it; 休んだ is the past form of 休む.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject whose condition improves.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: よく is the adverbial form of よい and modifies なった.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: なった expresses a change to a new state and is used in the past form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. The duration with も adds emphasis, while よくなった shows that the illness changed to a better state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and conversational, while ので sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: ために usually sounds formal and emphasizes the reason in a more written style.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: When saying that an illness has improved or a condition has become better, use よくなる. Do not use よくする unless someone actively makes it better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi: If you do not understand, try looking it up in a reference book, for example.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: 分からない is the present negative plain form, which connects with と to state a condition leading to the advice in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: でも suggests one possible means, meaning that you can look it up in a reference book, for example.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 調べてください uses the て＋ください form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: The condition clause comes first to identify when action is needed. 参考書でも gives a specific method without limiting it to the only method, and then 調べてください gives advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with たら, the condition is more clearly hypothetical and sounds more natural when talking about a situation that may occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with で, the sentence only says to look it up using a reference book and no longer has the meaning of “for example.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand でも as “also,” but in 参考書でも it suggests “a reference book, for example.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形＋と; N＋でも; Vて＋ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vi: If I make an effort, the chance of failing the exam will probably be low.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: すれば is the ば form of する and is used to state a condition for the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に goes with 落ちる to mark the exam that the speaker may fail.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 落ちる in dictionary form comes before 可能性 to modify the possibility of failing the exam.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject judged to be 少ない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 少ない states a low level, while だろう expresses a guess or an opinion that is not absolute.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: The condition 努力すれば is placed at the beginning to provide the basis for the opinion. The phrase 試験に落ちる modifies 可能性, and then 可能性が少ない expresses a low chance of failing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 少ない is replaced with 低い, the meaning is still that the possibility is low, but the expression is more direct and more commonly used with 可能性.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 落ちないだろう, the sentence more strongly states the guess that the person will not fail, rather than simply saying that the possibility is low.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 可能性が少ない as “little possibility,” but natural Vietnamese would say “low possibility.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q12.kobun.cn: Vば; N＋に＋落ちる; V辞書形＋N; Nが＋Aい; 普通形＋だろう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: そんなに is an adverb of degree that modifies the degree of anger.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: な follows a verb in dictionary form to create a negative command, meaning “do not” or “stop doing.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: そんなに comes before the verb to limit the degree of the action. 怒るな uses a negative command pattern, so the sentence directly tells someone to stop.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a more polite request: please do not get angry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the tone is softer, close to “there is no need to get that angry.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse な in 怒るな with a sentence-final particle, but here な marks a prohibition after a verb in dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vi: I will prepare in advance the things I will use tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.sk: Time ＋ V辞書形 ＋ N を ＋ Vておく
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates the time for the preparation action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in dictionary form modifies もの, creating the meaning “the things that will be used.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: もの is the object being prepared, and を marks the object of 用意する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 用意する changes to the て form and connects with おく to express doing something in advance for a later action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: The clause 明日使う comes before もの to identify which things they are. The object ものを comes before 用意しておきます, where ～ておく emphasizes preparation in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～ている, the sentence only describes a state of preparing or having prepared something and does not emphasize doing it in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～てある is used, the sentence emphasizes the resulting state of something having already been prepared by someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that おく must connect to a verb in the て form and cannot connect directly to the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vi: I want you to tell Mr. Suzuki to come and visit my home next year without fail.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.sk: N に + Time + Adverb + N に + Vてください と + Vてほしい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person who receives the message being conveyed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: This part states the time of the invitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies the invitation and shows a strong wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination of the action 遊ぶ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the whole quoted invitation that is being conveyed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: 伝えてほしい expresses the wish for the listener to convey that invitation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.why: 鈴木さんに is the recipient of the message, while the message content comes before と. The pattern ～てほしい comes after 伝えて to express the wish for someone else to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～てもらいたい, the meaning leans more toward wanting to receive help from that person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～てください is used, it becomes a direct request to the listener, rather than a wish for someone else to convey.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.tip: English learners may mistake に in NにVてほしい for a place; here, it indicates the person who is expected to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or an older person
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q15.kobun.cn: N に + Vて + ほしい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.vi: Because it was spicy food, I did not eat it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective ending in い modifies 料理.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the cause to the result; the noun 料理 comes before なので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べませんでした is the polite past negative form of 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.why: 辛い modifies 料理 to form the noun phrase “spicy food.” The cause phrase comes before なので, followed by the result 食べませんでした.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with から, the reason is usually more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～のに is used, the meaning changes to contrast, such as “although it was spicy food, I still did not eat it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.tip: English learners may connect a noun directly to ので; な must be used after a noun or the adjective な.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい + ので; Aな・N + な + ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.vi: If it is alcohol, it is better not to drink much.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: だと changes 酒 into a hypothetical condition: if it is alcohol.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: あまり is used with a negative predicate to show a small amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.ch.2.vi: it is better not to drink
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 飲まないほうが states the choice that is judged to be better.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: いいですよ completes the advice and よ emphasizes the information the listener should note.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.why: 酒だと places the condition at the beginning of the sentence, followed by advice using the structure Vないほうがいい. あまり combines with 飲まない to limit the amount of drinking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～なら, the condition is based on information or an assumption being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～たほうがいい is used, it recommends doing an action instead of recommending not drinking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.tip: English learners may translate 飲まないほうがいい as “it is better not to drink,” but forget that this is advice not to drink.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q17.kobun.cn: N + だと; V普通形・Aい + と; Aな・N + だと
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.vi: For your sake, it is okay even if I am scolded.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.sk: N のために、 + passive Vて + もいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: ために indicates the purpose or the person who benefits from the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 叱られる is the passive form “be scolded,” and it combines with ても to create a concessive meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: いい completes the pattern ～てもいい and expresses acceptance or permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.why: あなたのために states the reason or purpose for enduring something. 叱られてもいい uses the passive form to say “be scolded,” and combines with てもいい to show that this is still acceptable.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～てもかまわない, the meaning is still “it is okay,” but the tone is more formal and objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～てはいけない is used, the meaning changes to “it is not allowed.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.tip: English learners may use 叱ってもいい to mean “it is okay to be scolded,” but the passive form 叱られてもいい must be used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q18.kobun.cn: Vて・Vないで・Aいくて・Aなで・Nで + もいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.vi: Please believe me; I will definitely become a respectable person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: 信じてください is a polite request in the first clause.
