default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the speaker is the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な modifies 人間 and keeps な before the noun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the result of the change in 人間になる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: なってみせる consists of the て form of なる and みせる, emphasizing the determination to achieve it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the request 信じてください, then states the speaker’s topic and goal for change. に marks the result of なる, while ～てみせる expresses strong determination.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～てみる, it only means trying to do something and does not show determination to prove it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～つもりだ is used, it only states an intention, with weaker determination than ～てみせる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q19.kobun.tip: English learners may understand みせる as “show” in its usual meaning, but in ～てみせる it emphasizes the idea of achieving something no matter what.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi: If it is cheap, I will buy it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q2.kobun.sk: Aい remove い + ければ + Vます
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 安い changes into the conditional form ～ければ to connect with the result clause that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q2.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + ければ; Vる + えば
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first and is connected with ～ければ. The main clause uses 買います to state the result that will occur if the condition is met.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～たら, the sentence still means “if it is cheap,” but the tone is more conversational and the condition is more specific.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse ～ければ with ～れば and forget that an adjective ending in い must change い into ければ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q20.kobun.vi: You must not lose valuable things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of losing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb なくす changes into the て form, なくして, and combines with は to create a prohibition pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: いけません completes the pattern てはいけません and expresses something that is not allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q20.kobun.why: The object phrase comes first, followed by the action changed into the て form to connect with はいけません. This pattern gives a prohibition or a rule against doing something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the sentence has a polite-request tone: please do not lose valuable things.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may think that てはいけません only means “should not,” but this pattern usually clearly expresses a prohibition or something that is not allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.vi: Because the homework is not finished yet, do not play video games.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject in an unfinished state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies 終っていない and emphasizes that the state is still unfinished.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 終る in the ている negative form becomes 終っていない, then connects with から to state the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object involved in the action of playing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 遊ぶ in the dictionary form combines with な to create a strong negative command: do not or must not do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.why: The clause with から comes first to state the reason, while the main clause ends with Vるな to give a prohibition. まだ combines with the negative form of ている to express that something is still unfinished.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the reminder becomes more polite and means “please do not play video games.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, the sentence emphasizes a rule against playing rather than a direct command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may use な after every negative form, but this prohibition pattern must follow a verb in the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.vi: I believe that he will definitely come back.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of returning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: きっと modifies 戻ってくる and shows the speaker's certainty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 戻る changes to the て form, becoming 戻って, and combines with くる to express movement back toward the speaker; と marks the content that is believed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 信じています uses the ている form to express a continuing state of belief.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.why: The content being believed comes before と, followed by the verb 信じています as the main predicate. てくる shows movement back toward the speaker or reference point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the action will mean moving away from the point of speech or toward another place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence only expresses a thought or judgment, with a weaker sense of belief.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate てくる simply as “come,” but in this sentence it emphasizes movement back toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q22.kobun.cn: Vて + くる; V普通形 + と + 信じる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.vi: I am currently unsure whether to go or not.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: か comes after 行く to create one possibility in a pair of choices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 行かないか creates the opposite possibility to 行くか, and together they form the matter being considered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: は identifies the person who is unsure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 今 indicates the time when the uncertainty is happening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 迷う changes to the ている form to express an ongoing state of uncertainty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: ところだ comes after 迷っている to emphasize that the person is currently in exactly that state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.why: The pair Vるか Vないか presents two opposite possibilities and forms the matter being considered. The topic わたしは comes before the time expression 今, and the predicate 迷っているところだ identifies the current state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only asks whether someone will do it, without emphasizing two choices presented in parallel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes being in the middle of an action or process rather than being unsure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the second か, but the complete choice structure is usually Vるか、Vないか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.vi: Because I neither read books nor do my homework, I do not pass.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: も replaces を and adds the meaning that I also do not read books.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 読まないし gives one reason and also opens the way for the next reason in the list.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: も marks homework as the second item listed together with 本.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.ch.3.vi: because I also do not do
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: しない is the negative form of する and combines with ので to connect the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main result clause, using the polite negative form of 合格する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.why: し is used to list several causes, while ので connects the whole cause section to the result at the end of the sentence. も is repeated after each noun to emphasize that neither activity is done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence lists typical actions rather than necessarily giving reasons.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect し directly to a noun and forget that the noun needs だし, while a negative verb directly uses ないし.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形＋し／Aい＋し／Aな＋だし／N＋だし; V普通形＋ので／Aい＋ので／Aな＋な＋ので／N＋な＋ので
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.vi: The whole thesis has been completely written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the grammatical subject of the writing action in the given sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 全部 modifies the action 書いてしまった and shows that the action covers the entire thesis.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 書く changes to the て form, becoming 書いて, and combines with しまった to express a completed action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.why: 全部 comes before the predicate to limit the scope of the action, while てしまった is placed at the end to emphasize that the writing is complete. With the use of が in the given sentence, 論文 is made the grammatical subject of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes doing something beforehand to prepare for a later purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence only states that the action is completed, with less of a feeling of regret or something happening against one's wishes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand しまった as only past tense, but this pattern also emphasizes completion or a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q25.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; Vてしまった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi: My house is near the school.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies 家 as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object used as the reference point for comparison with the adjective 近い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 近い is an adjective describing the distance of 家 from 学校.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: 家は is the topic, while 学校に is the reference point toward which the distance is measured. 近い directly acts as the predicate and uses に to express “near” which object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 学校の近くにある, the sentence emphasizes that the house is located in an area near the school instead of using the adjective 近い.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use を after 学校; the pattern 近い goes with に to indicate the object being compared.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the action 言った in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 言った modifies こと and forms the noun phrase “what you said.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: なの is placed at the end of the sentence to ask about or confirm information in a casual way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: あなたが言った comes before こと to identify the specific content being discussed. 本当なの at the end of the sentence performs the confirmation question, with な following the noun 本当 before の.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 本当ですか, the sentence becomes more polite and direct and loses the casual feeling of なの.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: After a noun or an adjective ending in な, な must come before の in the pattern なの.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q4.kobun.cn: N／Aな ＋ な ＋ の; V普通形・Aい ＋ の
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi: If you do not understand something, please ask at any time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The plain-form clause 分からない modifies 時, meaning “when you do not understand.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 時 as an event assumed to occur.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: あったら is the ～たら form and connects the condition to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: でも combines with the question word いつ to create an unlimited meaning about time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞いて uses the て form to connect with ください and create a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to express a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: The conditional part comes first to state the situation in which help is needed. いつでも modifies 聞いて and shows that the learner can ask at any time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with いつも, the meaning is “always,” so it no longer has the sense of allowing something at any time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: いつでも means “whenever,” while いつも means “always”; these two patterns should not be confused.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 ＋ でも; Vたら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: You do not even do your homework, so do not play video games.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: も marks 宿題 as something that is also not done, with the meaning “even the homework.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: even though you do not do it
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects a situation that goes against what is expected in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks ゲーム as the object mentioned in the action 遊ぶ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: な comes after a verb in the dictionary form to create a strong prohibition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: のに connects not doing homework with playing video games as a criticism and an unexpected situation. 遊ぶな places the prohibition at the end of the sentence to state the action that is not allowed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 遊んではいけない, the prohibition keeps the same meaning, but the wording is more objective and softer than 遊ぶな.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Vる＋な is a strong prohibition, so avoid using it with older people or in polite situations.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: Vる ＋ な; V普通形 ＋ のに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: It is not good to use only honorific language.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks 敬語 as the object of the action 使う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The phrase 使ってばかりいる is nominalized with の, and は makes this whole action the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: よくないです is the predicate that comments on and evaluates the action mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: 敬語を is the object of 使う, while てばかりいる emphasizes repetition or doing only one thing. のは turns the whole verb phrase into a topic for the comment よくないです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～だけだ, the sentence only states the limit “only,” so the complaining tone about repetition becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: ばかり follows the て form in this pattern; it is not placed directly after a noun when expressing “doing only one thing.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q7.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ばかり ＋ いる; V普通形 ＋ のは
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 早く is an adverb that modifies the action 食べなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: なさい follows the verb stem in the ます form to create a request or instruction that is softer than a command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: よ is used at the end of a sentence to emphasize the statement and convey it to the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: 早く comes before the verb to show the manner or degree of the action. 食べなさい creates an urging expression, while よ emphasizes the reminder for the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes a more polite request: please eat.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence has a stronger and more direct command tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 早く with an adjective used independently, but in this sentence 早く is an adverb modifying 食べなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q8.kobun.cn: Vます語幹＋なさい; 文＋よ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: Even cooking a simple meal takes about an hour.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.sk: Aなに ＋ Nを ＋ Vる＋だけでも ＋ Duration＋ぐらいも ＋ Vでしょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 簡単な changes into 簡単に to modify how the cooking is done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb する in the phrase 料理をする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: だけ limits the action to simple cooking, while でも emphasizes that even just this is enough to lead to the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ぐらい shows an approximate duration, while も emphasizes that this number is large or significant.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: かかる shows the time needed, while でしょう gives the statement a speculative tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: The phrase するだけでも describes a minimal action that still produces a large result. The duration comes before かかる because かかる takes the period of time as the necessary amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だけなら, the sentence only states the condition “if doing only that,” and no longer has the meaning “even just that is enough.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If さえ is used, the emphasis is stronger and it usually means “even,” so it does not keep the limiting meaning of だけ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit も after だけで, but だけでも clearly expresses the meaning “even just ...”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t6-q9.kobun.cn: Vる・N＋だけでも; N＋ぐらい／くらい; 文普通形＋でしょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi: Whenever it rains, traffic becomes congested.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the phenomenon that causes the following result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the dictionary form of a verb with an inevitable result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that changes into a congested state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: になる shows a change into the state 渋滞.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, and the result comes after it. The particle が marks the phenomenon that causes the change and the object that undergoes it, respectively.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with たら, the sentence focuses more on a specific condition and does not necessarily express an always-true rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ば, the sentence emphasizes the condition-result relationship more logically.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate と as “and,” but in this sentence と connects a condition with an inevitable result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vi: She is the kind of person who wants to know everything.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Nでも ＋ Vたい omit い ＋ たがる ＋ N です
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that she is the person whose personality is being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 何でも refers to every object she wants to know about, with でも meaning “any.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 知りたがる comes before and modifies 人, describing that person’s characteristic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 人です is the main predicate, and です connects the description to the topic 彼女.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.cn: Vます形 omit ます ＋ たがる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.why: 何でも is the object of 知る, while 知りたがる is placed before 人 to create a clause that modifies a noun. たがる is used because the sentence describes a desire shown by another person, not the speaker’s direct desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 知りたい is used, the sentence expresses the subject’s direct desire, usually the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: ほしがる is used to show that someone appears to want an object; it cannot directly replace the desire to know something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use たい when talking about another person’s desire; when observing another person wanting to do something, たがる is usually used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vi: If you want to master Japanese, you must study very seriously.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object to be mastered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content of the intention quoted before 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: なら turns the previous intention or opinion into a condition for the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に turns the adjective な into an adverb, modifying 勉強する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: なければ creates a negative condition and connects with なりません to express obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: なりません completes the double-negative pattern, creating the meaning “cannot avoid doing it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と ＋ 思う；Vない形 omit い ＋ ければ ＋ なりません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.why: The intended content comes before と 思う, and then 思うなら turns the whole intention into a condition. The following clause uses 真面目に to modify studying and the pattern なければなりません to express obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If つもりなら is used, it emphasizes an existing plan or intention instead of the thought or determination expressed by と思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If なくてもいい is used, the meaning changes to “there is no need to study seriously.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget と between 身につけよう and 思う; と is the particle that quotes the content of a thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vi: Because I have lived in Tokyo before, I know the place quite well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose experience and knowledge are being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place connected with living.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I have lived there before
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: Vたことがある describes past experience, while から connects that experience to the reason in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the object that the adjective 詳しい refers to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 詳しい is the adjective used as the predicate, stating the result or state of knowing Tokyo well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.why: The experience of living in Tokyo is stated first and connected with から to give the reason. 詳しい goes with に to indicate the field or object that someone knows well; を is not used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If から replaces ので, the reason stays the same, but the statement sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 住んでいたから is used, the sentence only describes the state of having lived somewhere for a period of time and does not emphasize past experience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may say 東京を詳しい; the adjective 詳しい usually combines with に to indicate what someone knows well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q12.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ことがある；普通形 ＋ から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.vi: If the illness does not get better, I cannot travel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Vない と ＋ N へ ＋ negative potential form of V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が states the event that serves as the condition for the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.1.vi: if it does not get better
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: Vない＋と creates a conditional clause, meaning that if it does not get better, the following result will happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the destination of the movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 行けない is the negative potential form, expressing that the action of going cannot be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, and the result, being unable to go, comes after it. The particle が marks the event that the illness does not get better, while へ indicates the destination.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this still gives a negative conditional meaning, but the tone is more formal and rigid: ～ないと.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ～ないと with directly joining clauses using と in Vietnamese; remember that the verb must be in the ない form before と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.vi: This place is dangerous, so be careful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aい から ＋ N を ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ なさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this place the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the reminder in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: Vます remove ます＋なさい creates a light request or reminder.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ＋から; Vます remove ます＋なさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.why: The sentence gives the reason first and then the reminder at the end. を marks 気をつける as the action that should be taken, while なさい makes the reminder softer than a direct command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～てください, the request becomes more polite and sounds less like the speaker is in a guiding position.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use なさい with everyone; this pattern is usually used when the speaker reminds someone of lower status or someone close to them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.vi: Just as I was about to go out, the phone rang unexpectedly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.sk: V intention ＋ としたとき ＋ N が ＋ Vてしまった
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.ch.0.vi: when I was about to go out
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: V intention＋としたとき indicates exactly the time when someone is about to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that produces the sound in the unexpected event.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: てしまった expresses an event that has happened, often with a feeling of regret or against one's wishes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first and sets the background for the main event that happens at that moment. が marks the phone as the subject of ringing, while てしまった emphasizes that the event happened unexpectedly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern refers to the time when someone is about to try to do something or has just started doing it, while ～ようとしたとき focuses on the intention that formed just before that moment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand としたとき as meaning “be doing”; in fact, ようとする mainly indicates an intention or a preparatory action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.vi: If I stay in the United States for as long as two years, I will be able to speak English.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.sk: N に ＋ Time も ＋ Vば ＋ N を ＋ potential V ＋ ようになる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where someone exists or stays during this period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: も emphasizes a period that is longer than expected or significant.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: いれば is the ば form of いる and creates a hypothetical condition for the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the language being spoken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 話せるようになる expresses a change that leads to the ability to speak English.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.why: The condition about living in the United States comes first, and the result about language ability comes after it. を marks English as the content being spoken, while ようになる shows the development of ability over time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with ～ことができる only states the ability at that time and does not emphasize the process of becoming able to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 話すようになる to mean “be able to speak”; to emphasize ability, use the potential form 話せる＋ようになる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.vi: If you do not want to go, you do not have to go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.sk: Vたい negative ＋ なら ＋ Vなくてもいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.ch.0.vi: if you do not want to go
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: なら takes the 行きたくない clause as the condition or premise for giving advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.ch.1.vi: you do not have to go
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: Vなくてもいい expresses that it is permitted not to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形＋なら; Vない remove い＋くてもいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.why: The clause stating the listener's wish comes first, followed by the permitted choice. 行かなくてもいい negates the action of going but keeps the meaning that it is permitted.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to “must go.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This also expresses obligation, but the tone is “if you do not do it, it is not acceptable.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate なくてもいい as “do not need to”; remember that it gives permission not to do something, rather than forbidding the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q18.kobun.vi: Do not get angry with me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the target of the anger.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: Vないで＋くれ creates an informal request asking the other person not to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q18.kobun.why: The target of the emotion is stated first with に, while the request is placed at the end of the sentence. ないで negates the action of getting angry, and くれ shows an informal, direct way of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～ないでください, the request becomes more polite and suits someone who is not close or someone of higher status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after 怒る; this verb usually uses 怒る＋対象に to indicate the person who is angry with someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka gave a gift to Mr. Lee.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who performs the action for someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being given.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: あげた is the past form of あげる, meaning to give.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.why: The giver is the topic, the recipient goes with に, and the thing given goes with を. あげる expresses giving from the speaker or someone connected to the speaker to another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with くれた, the meaning changes to Mr. Lee giving a gift to Mr. Tanaka or someone on Mr. Tanaka's side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If 李さんは田中さんからプレゼントをもらった is used, the focus shifts to Mr. Lee receiving the gift.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake に for a place, but in this pattern に indicates the recipient.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q19.kobun.cn: N に ＋ N を ＋ あげる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: No matter how cold it is, I must go.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: どんなに modifies the degree of coldness in the concessive clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes to くても to connect with the concessive meaning “even if...”.“
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 行かない changes to 行かなくてはいけない to express obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: どんなに寒くても creates a contrasting situation without changing the conclusion. The negative pattern combined with いけません creates the meaning “if you do not do it, it is not acceptable,” meaning that you must do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Using only ～ても still means “even if...”, but it does not emphasize the degree as much as どんなに～ても.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with this pattern gives a similar obligation meaning, but the tone is more formal and rigid.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate 行かなくてはいけません mechanically as “if I do not go, it is not acceptable”; in natural English, understand it as “I must go.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q2.kobun.cn: どんなに＋Aいくても／Aなでも; Vない＋くてはいけない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.vi: This is the book I received from the department manager.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the item being introduced the topic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the person or source from which the item was received.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: いただいた is a clause modifying 本 and shows the humble way the recipient speaks.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the sentence politely and identifies it as the book.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.why: The clause いただいた comes directly before 本 to modify the book. から states the source of the gift, while いただく shows the recipient's humility toward a superior.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with もらった, the sentence still means that the speaker received the book, but the humble tone is weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 部長がくれた本 is used, the focus shifts to the department manager giving the book.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate から as meaning a place, but here it indicates the person giving the item or its source.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q20.kobun.cn: N から ＋ いただく; Vた ＋ N
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.vi: Teacher, could you please write a leave application for me?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: 先生 is the form of address for the person being asked, placed alone before the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item that the listener is asked to write.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 書いて is the て form, connecting the verb 書く to the polite request pattern that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: Vていただけませんか is a very polite way to ask someone to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.why: The person being asked is called first, the item to be written takes を, and the verb in the て form connects to the request pattern. The negative question form makes the request softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 書いてくれませんか, the request is still polite but less formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書いてください is used, the sentence becomes a more direct request and does not emphasize respect for the person being asked.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.tip: Learners may easily omit て before いただけませんか, but the verb must be in the て form to connect the pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q21.kobun.cn: Vて + いただけませんか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.vi: Lee, could you collect the documents for me?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: 李さん is the person being called and the person being asked to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks what needs to be collected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 集めて is the て form, connecting the requested action to くれないか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてくれないか is a familiar request used when asking the listener to do something for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.why: The person being asked is called at the beginning, the item to be handled takes を, and the て form then connects to くれないか. The negative question form makes the request softer than a direct command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 集めてください, the request is clearer and more polite but less familiar.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If 集めてもらえないか is used, the speaker emphasizes wanting to receive the listener's help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q22.kobun.tip: Learners may easily understand くれないか as an ordinary question, but in this pattern it is a request for someone to do something for them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.vi: I would like to ask permission to present first.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: に changes 先 into an adverb showing the order of actions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: させて is the て form of the causative, connecting to いただく to express asking for permission to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.2.vi: I would like to ask permission
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: たい expresses a wish, while んですが softens the statement and leaves room for the listener to respond.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.why: 先に is placed before the verb to state the order of presentation. The causative structure combined with いただきたい expresses a humble wish to be allowed to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 発表してもいいですか, the sentence simply asks for permission and does not have the clear humble tone of いただきたい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If 発表させてください is used, the request for permission is more direct and less formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.tip: Learners may easily mistake させて for doing something oneself, but it includes the idea of asking someone with authority to allow the speaker to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q23.kobun.cn: V使役て + いただく/いただきたい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: 兄さん is the person being called and the person being asked for help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 手伝って is the て form, connecting the verb to ちょうだい to make a request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてちょうだい is a soft, familiar request, usually used with someone close to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q24.kobun.why: The person being asked is called first, and then the verb in the て form connects to ちょうだい. This pattern keeps a familiar tone and is softer than a direct command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 手伝ってください, the sentence is more polite and neutral, suitable for someone who is not very close.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 手伝ってくれる？ is used, the sentence becomes a familiar question asking whether the other person will help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q24.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use ちょうだい with everyone, but this pattern is suitable only for familiar relationships.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.vi: The food I bought for the cat is here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the animal for which the food was bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: This clause modifies 餌, while てやった indicates doing something for the benefit of an animal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 餌 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the food exists.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate showing the existence of an object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.why: The clause 買ってやった comes before 餌 to modify this noun. The particle に marks the recipient of the benefit, while は makes 餌 the topic; ここにあります states its location.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the tone is more polite and neutral, and it is often used for someone of equal or lower status.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q25.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use に as a direct object, but here に indicates the animal for which something is done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: If you try opening the window, the room will become cooler.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the window as the object of opening.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 開けてみる shows trying to do something, and と connects that action to the result that is noticed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the room as the subject that becomes cooler.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to しくなります to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.cn: Vて＋みる; V辞書形＋と; Aい remove い＋くなる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: 窓を開けてみると describes trying an action first and then noticing the result. 部屋が涼しくなる uses が for the changing subject and くなる for the change of state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: ～てみたら can also mean “when you try doing it,” but it often suggests a specific result after the attempt.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: ～なら means “if the matter is opening the window” and does not clearly show the sequence of trying and then getting a result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use 涼しいになる; the adjective い must change to 涼しく before connecting to なる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: I hear that he is a famous soccer player in Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that he is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the range or place in which his fame is considered.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 有名な modifies the noun サッカー選手 that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.vi: hear that he is a soccer player
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: だそうです is attached after a noun to convey information that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: は places the topic first, while 日本で limits the range of 有名. 有名な comes directly before the noun to modify it, and then だそうです ends the sentence with the meaning “I hear that.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: With adjectives or verbs in an appearance-based form, そうです expresses the speaker's judgment, not information that was heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also conveys information, but it has a clearer explanatory or concluding tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: Before そうだ, nouns and な adjectives need to keep だ: 選手だそうです, not 選手そうです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい＋そうだ; Aな・N＋だそうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: You do not look well. Are you sick?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the state 元気 that is judged not to appear complete.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ない changes to なさそう to describe the appearance of lacking that state, and then で connects it to the next sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 病気する is put into the polite past form and か is added to make a question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: Vない remove い＋さそうだ; そうだ＋で
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: 元気がない is the state of “not being well,” while なさそうで turns that state into an observation based on appearance and connects it to the question. The subject of 病気しましたか is omitted because it is understood to be the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: ～ようです also expresses a judgment, but it is based on more evidence rather than appearance alone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: ～みたいです has a similar meaning but is more familiar than なさそうです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: With 元気がない, do not mechanically say 元気じゃなさそう; the common form of this pattern is 元気がなさそう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vi: From now on, I have no idea what I should do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the starting point for deciding what to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: どうしたらいい creates an indirect question, while か marks the content that is unknown.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぜん modifies 分かりません and is used with the negative form to emphasize the degree of not knowing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 分かりません is the main predicate, negating knowledge of the answer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.why: これから sets the time reference, followed by the indirect question content that functions as the meaning object of 分かりません. ぜんぜん comes before the negative predicate to emphasize not knowing at all.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: どうすればいいか also means “what one should do,” but it focuses more on suitable conditions or methods.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: どうしたらいいのか emphasizes uncertainty or the need for an explanation more strongly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.tip: ぜんぜん is normally used with a negative predicate, so one must say ぜんぜん分かりません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q6.kobun.cn: Vた＋らいい; 疑問詞＋Vたらいい＋か; ぜんぜん＋Vない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vi: According to Wang, it seems that he is waiting for someone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: によると indicates the source of the information used as the basis for what follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the waiting action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 誰かを is the person being waited for, and を marks the object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 待っている uses the ている form to express an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: そう at the end of the sentence indicates information that was heard or passed on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.why: The phrase によると puts the information source at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the subject and object of the action. Vている describes an ongoing action, while そうだ turns all the preceding content into reported information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing そうだ with らしい still gives indirect information, but the sense of guessing or hearing from an unspecified source is less emphasized.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: ようだ usually expresses a judgment based on signs, rather than simply reporting what someone else said.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうだ, meaning “it is said that,” with そうだ, which describes appearance and connects to the verb or adjective stem to mean “seems.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vi: Beijing is known by people around the world as the capital of China.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents Beijing as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: として indicates the status or role in which Beijing is viewed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the people who perform the action of knowing or recognizing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 知られている is a passive form combined with ている, expressing a state of currently being known.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.why: The topic 北京 comes first, followed by the role 中国の首都として. Because the sentence emphasizes Beijing's state of being known by others, it uses the passive form, and に marks the agent.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If によって is used, the person or cause producing the passive action is presented in a more formal and objective way.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If としては is used, the meaning changes to considering Beijing specifically as the capital, often creating a contrastive or limiting nuance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate に in a passive sentence as a place; here, に indicates the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vi: When I was in elementary school, my father made me write a diary every day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.0.vi: when I was in elementary school
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: のとき indicates the time or period when an event occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎日 modifies 書かされた and indicates the frequency of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: In the passive causative, に indicates the person who makes or forces the subject to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being written.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 書かされた is the passive causative form, expressing that the speaker was forced by their father to write.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning, followed by the frequency and the person causing the force. 父に and 日記を identify the person who forces the action and the thing being written, respectively, while 書かされた ends the forced-action content.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書かせた is used, it means that the father made or allowed someone to write, without emphasizing that the writer was forced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書いた is used, it only says that someone wrote a diary, with no longer any meaning that the father forced them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 父を instead of 父に; in the passive causative, the person forcing the action usually takes に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t7-q9.kobun.cn: V五段：ない形のない→あ ＋ せられる；V一段・する・来る ＋ させられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vi: It is too expensive, isn't it? I would like you to make it a little cheaper.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: ですね is used to express an impression and seek agreement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 安く is the linking form of the adjective 安い with する, and then て connects the action with もらいたい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: もらいたい expresses the desire to receive a price reduction from someone else.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q1.kobun.why: 高いですね gives an opinion first, and then もう少し安くして describes what the speaker wants the seller to do. 安くして connects with もらいたい to create the meaning of wanting someone to do something for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the desire for someone else to do the action is expressed more directly, with less emphasis on receiving the benefit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q1.kobun.tip: Do not say 安いして; the adjective ending in い must change to 安く before combining with する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q1.kobun.cn: Vて＋もらいたいです；Aい→Aく＋する
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the language being spoken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 話すこと turns the action of speaking into a noun, and が marks that action as the object of ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: できる is the predicate expressing the ability to perform an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q10.kobun.why: 日本語を is the object of 話す. The dictionary-form verb 話す is nominalized with こと and then combines with ができる to create the ability structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If the potential form 話せる is used, the sentence still means “can speak,” but it is shorter and more direct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place を before できる; in this pattern, the action has already been nominalized with こと, so it takes が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vi: It can be said that all the success is thanks to the teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.sk: N は ＋ すべて ＋ Nのおかげだと ＋ potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes 成功 the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: すべて modifies 成功 and shows that all the success is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content being judged or stated, while の connects 先生 with おかげ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 言える is the potential form of 言う. It functions as the main predicate and expresses the ability to make a judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.cn: Nの ＋ おかげだ; Plain sentence ＋ と ＋ potential V
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.why: 成功は gives the topic, while すべて limits the scope to all the success. The judged content comes before と, and then 言える shows that the speaker can make that judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If と思う replaces it, the sentence changes from “can say” to “I think,” emphasizing personal opinion more strongly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If と言われている replaces it, the meaning becomes that the judgment is said by many people or is commonly reported.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit と before 言える; と is required to mark the complete content being stated.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vi: I wish winter vacation would come soon.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes winter vacation the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 早い changes into 早く to modify 来る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb 来る connects with と to create the wish pattern ～といい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: いいね expresses a wish and a gentle sense of shared feeling at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.why: 冬休みは is the topic, while 早く modifies 来る to say that it comes early. 来るといい expresses the wish for something to happen, and ね makes the sentence softer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead tends to express advice or a wish in the form “it would be good to do that.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Using this instead usually has the sense “just do ..., and it will be fine,” and it is less natural than ～といい when expressing a wish.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse 早く with 早い and forget to change the adjective ending in い to く when it modifies a verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + といい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q13.kobun.vi: I am about to go out now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the time when an action is about to begin.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 出かける in the dictionary form comes before ところです to indicate an action that has not started but is about to happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q13.kobun.why: これから identifies the present time, while 出かけるところです shows that the action is just before starting. Therefore, this pattern means “about to do,” not “doing.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were replaced in this sentence, it would mean going out or being in the middle of the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were used instead, it would mean having just finished going out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 出かけているところ when they want to say “about to leave,” but the form for “about to do” must be V辞書形 + ところだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.vi: While everyone is sleeping, I plan to leave the house.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks everyone as the topic in the time clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 寝ている describes the state of sleeping and connects with あいだに to identify the period when the main action occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the place connected with the outward direction of the verb 出る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 出る in the dictionary form connects with つもりです to express the speaker’s plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.why: The clause 寝ているあいだに comes first to set the time frame for the action 出る. 出るつもりです places the plan at the end of the sentence, while に is connected to the starting place mentioned in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing に with は emphasizes a state continuing throughout that period rather than an event occurring during it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing つもりです with 予定です gives more of a schedule or an arranged plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse あいだに with あいだは; に focuses on an event occurring during the period, while は focuses on a continuing state.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q14.kobun.cn: Vている・Aい・Aなな・Nの + あいだに; V辞書形・Vない形 + つもりだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.vi: Since it may rain, it is better to take an umbrella.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the natural phenomenon that is the subject of 降る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: かもしれない comes after the plain form to express possibility, and から connects this clause to the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object carried by 持っていた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 持っていたほうがいいです gives advice; the form 持っていた emphasizes having an umbrella with you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.why: The clause about possible rain comes first and is connected with から to give the reason. Then, 傘を is the object of the carrying action, while ほうがいい places the advice at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing かもしれない with でしょう makes the prediction seem more certain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing ほうがいい with べきです makes the advice stronger and more like an obligation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit を before the object being carried or use から as a separate word instead of attaching it to the reason clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + かもしれない; Vた形 + ほうがいい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.sk: Frequency + N で + N を + V辞書形 + ことがあります
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: 時々 modifies the whole action and shows how often it happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the action 食事をする takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks 食事 as the content carried out with する.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: する in the dictionary form connects with ことがあります to say that something happens occasionally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.why: 時々 comes at the beginning to modify the frequency, 外で identifies where the action happens, and 食事をする is the verb phrase. ことがあります turns the action into an event that sometimes occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form were used, it would mean having had the experience of doing it, not still doing it occasionally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with よく食事をします emphasizes doing it more often than 時々.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand ことがある as meaning only “there is an event,” but with V辞書形 + ことがある, it describes something that happens occasionally.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q16.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことがある
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.vi: I have still never met Mr. and Mrs. Cao, but I often hear about them.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object of meeting, while は creates a contrast with the information in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies the whole negative phrase to emphasize that it has still not happened up to now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: あったことがありません expresses never having had the experience of meeting someone, and が connects it to the contrasting clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes お噂 the topic of the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: よく modifies 聞いています to show how often the speaker hears it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: 聞いています describes a state or habit of hearing that continues up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ことがない; clause + が + clause
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.why: The first clause states that the speaker has never met the person; に marks the object of 会う, and は creates a contrast. The second clause shifts the topic to お噂 and uses よく聞いています to say that the information is still often heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If the negative form were replaced with the affirmative form, it would mean having met someone or having had the experience of doing something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing が with けれども still creates a contrast, but the tone is fuller and more polite.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with a person they meet, but the verb 会う goes with に; を is used here only for information that is heard.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q17.tokens.8.m: do not have; there is not
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.vi: When learners cannot attend class, they are required to contact the teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the activity or situation in which participation is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: とき turns the preceding clause into a time point for the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who receives the contact.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: しなければならない expresses an obligation to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ことになっている shows that this is an established rule or decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.why: The time clause comes first and connects with とき to state the condition. Then, に marks the person to contact; the obligation is expressed by なければならない and placed within the rule framework ことになっている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were replaced with ことにする, the sentence would describe the speaker’s decision, not an established rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were replaced with はずだ, it would mean a prediction or something believed to be certain, without emphasizing a rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that なければならない must use the negative form ない before connecting, even though the whole sentence means that something must be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q18.kobun.cn: Vない + なければならない; Vる・Vない + ことになっている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.vi: After graduating, I plan to start a company.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: たら connects graduation with the event that will happen afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that will be established.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 作る in the dictionary form modifies つもり and shows what the speaker plans to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: つもりです places the content 作る within the speaker’s intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.why: たら sets the point after graduation, while 作る comes before つもり to clarify the content of the plan. を marks the company as the object of the action 作る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were replaced with 予定です, the meaning would be more like an expected plan or schedule than a personal intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were replaced with ことにする, it would emphasize a decision that has been made, not just a plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use つもりです directly after a noun, but when talking about planning to do or not do something, it must connect with Vる or Vない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q19.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない＋つもりだ; Vた＋ら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vi: If I do not understand, I will ask someone to explain it to me.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person who carries out the condition and the main action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: たら attaches to the past negative form to create the condition “if I do not understand.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb 教える with いただきます in a pattern for receiving help.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: いただきます is a humble expression showing that the speaker receives help from a superior.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.why: The 分からなかったら clause gives the condition first, and then the 教えていただきます clause states that the speaker will ask someone else for help. て connects 教えて with the humble verb いただく.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning of receiving help remains, but the level of respect is lower いただきます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.tip: The conditional form たら uses the past form, so it must be 分からなかったら, not 分からないたら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q2.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aい・Aな・Nだ ＋ ら；Vて＋いただく
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.vi: When my older brother gets married, I decided to return to my country.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 上 with 兄 to identify the older brother in the family.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject who gets married.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a natural condition or time with the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction of movement toward 国.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 帰る is in the dictionary form and becomes a noun phrase through こと.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: ことに turns the action 帰る into the content of the decision in the pattern ことにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.6.n: ことにした expresses that the decision has been made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.why: と connects the marriage with the following action as its result or next time. 帰る is nominalized with こと and then combined with にした to express the speaker’s decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: ことになった indicates a decision or result determined by circumstances or another person, without emphasizing the speaker’s will.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If たら is used instead, the sentence only states a hypothetical condition or time, and the natural-law meaning of と becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use the past form before ことにした when stating a decision; the action that has been decided usually uses the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と、／V辞書形 ＋ ことにする・した
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.vi: If it rains tomorrow, everyone may still come to the practice session.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: 明日 states when the condition occurs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 雨 as the phenomenon occurring in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 降れば is the conditional form ば of 降る, connecting the condition with the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes みんな the topic of the prediction in the main clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the place or activity that everyone will come to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: 来る is the main predicate, placed before the expression of possibility.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: かもしれない lowers the certainty of the prediction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない・Vた＋かもしれない; Vば expresses a condition
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.why: The clause beginning with 降れば states the condition. In the main clause, は gives the predicted subject, に indicates the destination, and かもしれない shows that the speaker is not certain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If でしょう is used instead, the prediction sounds more confident かもしれない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If なら is used instead, the condition is usually based on information or an assumption stated earlier.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake に in 練習に来る for “with,” but here it indicates the place or activity that the speaker is going to.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.vi: When I was a child, I was often told, “Eat quickly.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子供 with 時 to create a time expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: 時 indicates the time when something usually happens.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies 言われた and indicates how often the speaker was told this.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 早く is an adverb and modifies the command 食べなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: なさい attaches to the stem of ます to create a request or a mild command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks all the preceding words as quoted speech.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: 言われた is the past passive form, showing that the speaker received the words.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹＋なさい; direct speech ＋ と ＋ 言われる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.why: The time phrase 子供の時 comes first, followed by よく, which adds frequency. The command is placed in quotation marks and connected with と as the content of the passive verb 言われた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べなさい is replaced with 食べてください, the request becomes more polite and softer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If 言われた is replaced with と言われていた, it emphasizes that the speaker was repeatedly told this during a past period.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may connect なさい with the dictionary form, but the correct form is the stem of ます, such as 食べます → 食べなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.vi: It seems that the students did not understand my words.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.sk: N には ＋ Nの ＋ N が ＋ Vない past ＋ と ＋ 見える
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: には identifies the subject being considered and adds a mild contrast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 私 with 言葉 to show that the words belong to the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks 言葉 as the object that is or is not understood.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 分からなかった is the past negative form of 分かる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the preceding clause as the content of an inference or judgment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: と見える expresses a judgment based on observable signs or circumstances.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.why: には identifies the object being judged, while 言葉が is the subject in the structure 分かる. The past negative clause is quoted with と and ends with 見える to express an inference.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If と見える is replaced with ようだ, it also expresses an inference, but ようだ may be based on a wider range of evidence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with そうだ, it usually describes an appearance or heard information, without emphasizing an inference from signs as と見える does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate 学生には as the main subject, but here it is the object being considered; the grammatical subject of 分からない is 言葉.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nだ＋と見える
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q24.kobun.vi: This motorcycle is difficult to ride.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies this motorcycle as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 乗り is the verb stem 乗る after removing ます, and it connects with にくい to show that an action is difficult to perform.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q24.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, and the predicate then describes how easy or difficult the action is. にくい follows the verb stem and changes the action of riding into the meaning “difficult to ride.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～やすい, the meaning changes to “easy to ride.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly connect にくい with the dictionary form, but they must use the verb stem after removing ます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.vi: Although he is 50 years old, he looks only 30.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: だが connects two contrasting ideas: the actual age is high, but the appearance is young.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に identifies only the object being viewed, while しか is used with a negative form to limit the meaning to 30 years old.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 見えない is the negative form of 見える. It combines with しか to mean “only looks like.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.why: だが places two contrasting parts side by side. に見える describes how the object is seen, while しか must be used with a negative form to emphasize that it reaches only that level.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ように見える is used, the meaning is still “looks like,” but the description sounds more cautious and less direct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～だけ見える is used, it only refers to the visible range and does not create the limited meaning “only looks like.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use しか with an affirmative sentence, but しか always needs to be used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q25.kobun.cn: N ＋ に見える; N ＋ にしか ＋ Vない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vi: Teacher, I will take you to the airport.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 先生 is used to address the listener directly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates the destination where the escorting ends.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 送って is the て form and connects the main verb with さしあげる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: さしあげましょう expresses a humble offer to do something beneficial for a superior.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q3.kobun.why: 先生 is the form of address, and 空港まで identifies the destination. 送ってさしあげましょう combines the て form with a humble verb to make a polite offer.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the offer still means “I will help,” but it does not clearly show respect toward the teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use さしあげる with someone of lower status; it is a humble expression used when the person receiving the action is respected.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vi: It is not such a big deal, so please do not get angry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 大きな comes before the noun こと and directly modifies it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ではない negates the noun こと, while よ emphasizes the information the speaker wants to convey.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ないで creates a request not to perform an action and connects with ちょうだい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ちょうだい makes the request softer and more familiar.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q4.kobun.why: そんな大きなことではない denies the seriousness of the situation. Then 怒らないでちょうだい uses the negative form ないで to ask the listener not to get angry.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the request sounds more polite and formal than ちょうだい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q4.kobun.tip: 大きな is used before a noun. It does not inflect like 大きい in this position.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vi: Do not worry; I will show you.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: ないで connects a request not to do something with the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects 教える with やる in a pattern meaning to do something for another person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: やる comes after the て form and shows that the speaker does something beneficial for the other person.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: から gives the reason for the advice 心配しないで.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q5.kobun.why: 心配しないで is the reassurance given first. The part 教えてやるから gives a reason to help the listener feel at ease. In it, て connects 教える with やる, and から marks the reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the tone is softer and more neutral, while 教えてやる can sound familiar or slightly superior.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q5.kobun.tip: から at the end of the sentence still expresses a reason, so the conclusion “do not worry” or “please feel at ease” is understood.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vi: Please allow me to study here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the person affected by the causative action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle で indicates the place where the studying takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The causative form combines with ください to make a request for permission to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q6.kobun.why: The person asking for permission is marked by を, while the place of the action is used with で. The verb 勉強する is changed into the causative form and then connected to てください to express a polite request for permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, it directly asks for permission and sounds less like asking someone else to grant permission.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake を in a causative sentence for the subject; here, 私を is the person who is allowed to perform the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q6.kobun.cn: V使役形のて形 ＋ ください
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vi: It is thanks to your help that I have become who I am today.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause 助けてくれた modifies おかげ. At the same time, くれた shows that the action was done for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: おかげで indicates a cause that brings a good result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 今の modifies 私 and refers to the speaker as they are now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle が marks the subject that exists in the result あります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses the existence of 今の私.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.why: The clause 助けてくれた comes before おかげで to state the specific reason. Then, 今の私が あります describes the present result formed thanks to that reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the subject of the action will be the speaker doing something for another person, which is the opposite direction of benefit from くれた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used here, the cause usually leads to a bad result or expresses blame.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand くれた as only meaning “gave,” but in this pattern it emphasizes that someone did something beneficial for the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q7.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くれた; Nの・V普通形 ＋ おかげで
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vi: I want to go out, but since it is raining, I plan not to go.
