default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: のですが connects the desire in the first part with the obstacle in the second part, creating a soft shift in meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the subject of the phenomenon 降っています.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ～ています describes a situation in progress, while から connects the reason with the decision in the following part.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative verb 出かけない comes before つもり to state a plan not to do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.why: The sentence begins with a desire and then uses のですが to shift to an obstacle. The reason is connected with から, and the sentence ends with つもりです to state the plan not to go out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予定だ is used instead, the sentence focuses more on a planned schedule than on a personal intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used here, the tone emphasizes a deliberate decision not to go, rather than simply stating a plan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place から at the beginning of the sentence; in this structure, から comes after the reason clause and before the conclusion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q8.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ つもりだ; V普通形 ＋ のですが; Vている ＋ から
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vi: In Japan, there is a rule that you must take off your shoes when entering a house.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: では limits the scope of the rule to Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the destination of the action 入る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 入る is placed in the dictionary form before 時 to indicate the time when the following action takes place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle を marks the item being taken off.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: Vることになっている describes a rule or a state that has been decided and is currently in effect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.why: では states the scope of the rule, while に identifies the place entered. The clause 入る時 comes first to indicate the time, and then the main rule is stated with 脱ぐことになっている.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, it means that the subject decides personally what to do, not that it is a general rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used here, the sentence only describes something that was decided and does not emphasize that the rule is currently maintained.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ことになっている as “has become”; in this sentence, understand it as a rule that is currently in effect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.tokens.11.m: become, be established as a rule
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t8-q9.kobun.cn: Vる ＋ ことになっている; Vる ＋ 時
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: じゃなくて negates a noun and connects it to the contrasting choice that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 牛肉 as the object being bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 買うんじゃないですか consists of the plain form of the verb, ん states an assumption, and じゃないですか asks for confirmation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q1.kobun.why: じゃなくて rules out the first choice and connects it to the correct choice. 牛肉を comes before 買う because を marks the object of the buying action; at the end of the sentence, んじゃないですか is used to confirm an assumption.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～でしょうか, the question is more polite and neutral, without suggesting that the speaker already has an assumption.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～わけではない is used, it mainly means partial negation, not a question confirming a choice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate んじゃないですか as simple negation, but here it usually means a confirmation question: "isn't it...?"
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい普通形 ＋ んじゃないですか／Aな・N ＋ なんじゃないですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vi: Because I do not have enough money, I will choose this bag.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject being evaluated as 足りない.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the decision to choose the bag in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に connects a noun with する in the pattern にする, expressing a choice or decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the polite form of する and completes the decision このかばんにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q10.kobun.why: The clause containing から explains the reason before giving the choice. The noun このかばん combines with にする to turn that choice into the speaker's decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with it, the sentence still means choosing the bag, but it emphasizes the act of choosing more than the decision to choose it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with する in this pattern, but a noun showing a choice must go with に.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vi: Because I do not understand this passage myself either, it is difficult to explain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states which passage is being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: にも emphasizes that even the speaker does not understand it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 説明し＋にくい creates an adjective meaning that something is difficult to do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.why: The clause before から gives the reason, while 説明しにくい is the result. The particle にも highlights the scope of “even I” not understanding it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing にくい with づらい still means that something is difficult to do, but it usually emphasizes difficulty caused by feelings or real conditions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with がたい makes the expression more formal and usually refers to something very difficult to accept or do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use にくい directly after the dictionary-form verb, but they must use the verb stem form ます, such as 説明しにくい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q11.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 ＋ にくい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.vi: I have decided to return to my hometown during the winter vacation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time に ＋ N へ ＋ Vる ＋ ことにする
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates a point in time and adds emphasis to the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction of the action 帰る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 帰ることにする expresses a decision made by the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, the destination is used with へ, and then the action is nominalized with こと before the decision pattern. The past form しました shows that the decision has already been made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことになる is used, it means that the matter was decided by circumstances or someone else, without emphasizing the speaker's decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If ようにする is used, it means trying to create a habit or arrange to do something, not simply deciding to do it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.tip: Do not mistake ことにする for “become”; this pattern expresses the speaker's decision to do or not do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q12.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ ことにする
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.vi: Do you know what time the meeting will start?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the meeting is the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the question part into a clause containing information that is known or unknown.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 知っていますか is the main question, asking whether the listener knows that information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.why: 何時に始めるか is the question clause inside the larger question 知っていますか. The particle に indicates the time, while か comes at the end of the subordinate clause to mark the information that needs to be known.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with かどうか, the question asks “whether or not,” rather than asking for specific information such as the time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If と思います is used, the sentence states the speaker's thought or guess and no longer asks whether the listener knows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.tip: When か comes in the middle of a sentence to introduce an indirect question, do not use the polite form before か; use the plain form, such as 始めるか.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q13.kobun.cn: 疑問詞を含む普通形の文 ＋ か
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.vi: What is that? I have never seen it before.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 何ですか。＋ Time まで ＋ Vた ＋ ことが ＋ ありません
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the object being asked about.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ですか creates a polite question about the identity or characteristics of the object.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: まで indicates a time limit extending to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 見たこと expresses the experience of having seen something, while が marks the content of that experience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません negates the experience mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.why: The first sentence asks what the object is, and the second talks about experience up to the present. Vたこと is used as a noun meaning an experience, and then ありません negates that experience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ありません is replaced with あります, the meaning changes to “have seen it” at least once.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見ない is used, it only says that someone does not watch or see something, without emphasizing experience up to the present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate こと as a separate “thing”; in this pattern, 見たことがない must be understood as a whole meaning “have never seen it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being cleaned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: きれいに indicates the desired state or result of the cleaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 掃除しなさい uses the verb stem form ます with なさい to give a request or instruction.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q15.kobun.why: 教室を is the object, きれいに describes the result to be achieved, and 掃除しなさい is the main command. The adjective な changes into an adverb with に before the verb.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If なさい is replaced with てください, the speech becomes more polite and softer, like a request or suggestion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: Using なければならない expresses an obligation, without directly ordering the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q15.kobun.tip: なさい connects to the verb stem ます, so it is 掃除しなさい, not 掃除するなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q15.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + なさい
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vi: This violin makes a strange sound.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the violin as the source of the sound.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the sound that is perceived or produced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: します combines with the noun 音 to express that a sound exists or is produced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q16.kobun.why: The violin is the topic, while the strange sound is what is heard, so it goes with が. The pattern 音がする describes the perception of a sound being produced, without emphasizing who intentionally made it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 音がします is replaced with 音を出します, the meaning is that the subject actively creates or produces the sound.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Changing 音 to 匂い keeps the same structure, but changes the meaning from perceiving a sound to perceiving a smell.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q16.kobun.tip: With 音がする, do not use を after 音; が marks the sound being perceived.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.vi: It is already late, and I am tired too, so let us go straight home.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: し connects the first reason to the next one and gives a listing meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: から follows a plain-form clause to state a direct reason.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: まっすぐ modifies the action of going home and shows how the movement is made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the destination of the verb 帰る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: 帰ろう is the volitional form of 帰る, expressing an intention or an invitation to do something together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.why: The first two clauses give reasons in order. し lists the reasons, while から states the reason leading to the decision. After the reasons come the manner of movement, the destination, and the volitional verb at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone becomes softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is used to list typical actions or states, so it is not suitable for connecting the reasons in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use し as a simple connector and forget that it usually lists several reasons.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + し
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.vi: Which do you like better, apples or oranges?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects the first noun in the pair of compared choices.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the second noun to the structure for choosing between two objects.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: どちらが asks which of the two objects is the subject of the preference.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 好きですか creates a polite question about preference.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.why: The two nouns are connected by と and placed together as two choices. どちらが is the subject of 好き, so the question focuses on choosing one of the two.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this pattern clearly states that one side is preferred instead of asking which one to choose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: どれ is used when choosing among several objects, without clearly limiting the choice to two.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put を after the item they like, but 好き usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q18.kobun.cn: N + と + N + と + どちらが + 好きですか
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.vi: I was surprised by how light that mobile phone was.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.sk: N の + Aい remove い+さ に + Vた
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies the noun that follows and identifies the phone that has been mentioned or is near the listener.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun 携帯電話 with the noun かるさ, creating the relationship “the lightness of the phone.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: かるさ is a noun showing a degree formed from an adjective, while に shows the cause of the emotion 驚いた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 驚いた is a past-tense verb that states an emotion that occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.why: その携帯電話の modifies the noun かるさ. This noun showing a degree combines with に to state the cause, and then 驚いた expresses the resulting emotion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 軽い is used, the sentence simply describes the phone as light, without focusing on “lightness” as かるさ does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: み also turns an adjective into a noun, but it usually refers to a quality or feeling, so it is less natural than さ when talking about lightness.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q19.kobun.tip: When forming a noun with ～さ, remove い from the い-ending adjective.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vi: Because that class does not take attendance, it is easy to skip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes that class the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 出席 as the object of the verb 取る.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 取らない is the negative form, while から connects the reason to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: サボり is the verb stem サボる, which connects with やすい to show that an action is easy to perform.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason with から, and the second clause describes how easily the action occurs. やすい connects to the verb stem サボり to express that skipping class is easy in this situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～にくい, the meaning changes to “difficult to skip class.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ～がちだ emphasizes a tendency to happen often, not how easy the action is to perform.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect やすい after the dictionary form, but they must use the verb stem after removing ます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.vi: Because I was woken up by a prank call, I could not fall asleep for a long time afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the agent or cause of the passive action 起こされる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 起こされて is the passive form, connected by て to what happened afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: そのあと indicates the time of the action 眠れなかった.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.3.vi: for a long time, with difficulty
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: なかなか is used with a negative form to emphasize that the action is difficult to achieve.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 眠れなかった is the past negative potential form, expressing that the person could not sleep.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.cn: 五段動詞: 語尾う段→あ段＋れる; 一段動詞: remove る＋られる; する→される; 来る→こられる
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.why: The sentence begins with a reason in the passive form, then uses て to connect it to the result. The time adverb and なかなか add circumstances before the negative potential predicate appears at the end.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 起こした is used, the subject is the person who wakes someone else, so the meaning “be woken up” is lost.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means being unable to wake up by oneself, which is different from being awakened by an outside agent.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in a passive sentence with に, which indicates a place; here, it indicates the agent causing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q20.tokens.5.m: for a long time without, with difficulty
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.vi: As soon as my younger brother got home, he suddenly started crying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 弟 the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of the verb 着く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a dictionary-form verb with a result that occurs immediately or naturally after that condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 急に modifies 泣きだした and shows that the event happened unexpectedly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 泣きだした consists of the verb stem 泣き and だす, expressing the sudden start of crying.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます + だす
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.why: The clause 着くと sets a condition or time first, while the main action 泣きだした happens immediately afterward. だす attaches to the verb stem to emphasize that the action begins suddenly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 泣き始めた, the sentence only says that the person starts crying, with less emphasis on the suddenness.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means continuing to do something, which is completely different from beginning an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q21.kobun.tip: Do not attach だす directly to the dictionary-form verb; use the verb stem, as in 泣き＋だす.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.vi: If you follow that road to the left, you will see a station.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: を indicates the route or space that the subject passes through, not an object affected by the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction of movement of 行く.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a verb in the dictionary form with a result or something that naturally happens after the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject that exists in a sentence using あります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is a predicate that indicates the existence of an object or place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.why: その道を gives the route, 左へ gives the direction, and 行くと creates a condition leading to a result. In the following clause, 駅が is the existing thing, and あります is the existence predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行くと is replaced with 行ったら, the sentence sounds more hypothetical and conditional. It does not emphasize a natural result as と does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: で indicates the means or method of going, while を in その道を indicates the route taken.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand を as marking only a required object, but with movement verbs, を can indicate the road or space passed through.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q22.kobun.cn: Nを（経路）＋ 方向へ ＋ V辞書形 ＋ と
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.vi: At first glance, it looks simple, but it is actually difficult.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects a verb in the dictionary form with something noticed immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: そう describes outward appearance; けれども connects it to a contrasting idea in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents a point of comparison with the appearance mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.why: The clause with と describes what is noticed at first glance. けれども creates a contrast between the simple appearance and the difficult reality.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ようだ, the sentence expresses an inference or judgment based on evidence, not just appearance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used instead of けれども, the contrast remains, but the expression is shorter and more neutral.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand と here as an ordinary condition, but this sentence emphasizes what is noticed immediately after looking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹 ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.vi: The concert is about to begin, so please enjoy it until the end.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point in time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that begins to take place.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it is about to begin
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects a reason clause with a request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: まで indicates the ending limit of the time period for enjoying something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: お comes before the verb stem to create a polite invitation or request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.why: から gives the reason for the invitation that follows. まで defines the time range, while お楽しみ is a shortened polite way to invite someone to enjoy something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use it in this sentence, the invitation becomes more direct and no longer has a polite nuance in the form お＋the verb stem.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If までに is used, it means completing something before a deadline, not continuing an activity until the end.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse まで with までに; まで indicates a continuing period, while までに indicates a deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.vi: My father went to the company without eating a meal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ Vない without ない ＋ ずに ＋ N へ ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person who performs the main action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food that is the object of 食べる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ずに connects a negated action with the next action. It means doing the later action without doing the earlier one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ました marks an action that happened and uses polite speech.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.cn: Vない without ない ＋ ずに; する → せずに; 来る → こずに
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.why: 食べずに places the action of not eating before the action of going, showing that the same subject performs both actions. へ identifies the destination of the movement.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ないで, the meaning is almost the same, but the expression is more common and less formal.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: 食べないで can mean the command “do not eat” when used alone, so its tone differs from ずに in this narrative sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to remove ない before adding ずに: 食べないずに is incorrect; it must be 食べずに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vi: If you take time off because of illness or a similar reason, you are required to contact them in advance.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause or reason for taking time off.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 休む in the dictionary form modifies 場合, creating the meaning “the case of taking time off.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the case of taking time off the topic and condition being discussed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates when the contact must be made.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 連絡する modifies こと, turning the action of contacting into the content of the rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: こと turns an action into a noun, while に marks the result or content that has been decided.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.6.vi: has been established as a rule
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: なっている describes a rule that has been established and remains in effect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.why: The clause 休む modifies 場合 to create a specific condition. Then, 事前に indicates the time of the action, while Vることになっている expresses an established rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ことにする is used, the subject decides or arranges the matter independently.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ことになった is used, it emphasizes that the rule or decision was formed at a certain time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ことになっている as “has become,” but in a sentence about rules, it means “is established as a rule.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q3.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない ＋ ことになっている
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vi: For this company trip, let us choose the Hakone hot springs.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今度 with 社員旅行, creating the phrase “this time’s company trip.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the company trip as the item being chosen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the option chosen after the verb する in the pattern にする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form of する, turning a decision into a suggestion to do it together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.why: The phrase 今度の社員旅行 identifies the trip being discussed. に follows the place or option chosen, while しましょう expresses a suggestion to decide together.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～を選ぶ is used, it emphasizes choosing an option and sounds less like a shared suggestion.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～に決める is used, it emphasizes making a firm decision about one choice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を before the option, but the pattern にする uses に to mark the chosen item.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q4.kobun.cn: N ＋ にする; N ＋ にしましょう
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vi: After the doctor advised me to, I decided to quit drinking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who performs the speech action in a passive sentence 言われる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the reason or situation before it to the following clause.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb やめる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb やめる comes before ことにする to express the subject's decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する, completing the pattern ことにしました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.why: The person who speaks is placed after に in a passive sentence, and the て clause then connects to the speaker's decision. The verb やめる stays in the dictionary form before ことにする.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would mean that something was decided or became that way because of circumstances or another person's decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake にする for “make something become,” but in this pattern ことにする means deciding for oneself to do or not do something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q5.kobun.cn: Vる・Vない + ことにする
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vi: Because there is a test tomorrow, you should go to bed early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes tomorrow the time topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the existence of something in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects a reason clause to the advice that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: はやく modifies the action of sleeping and shows when it should be done.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb ねる takes the past form ねた before ほうがいい to give advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: いいです completes the polite expression of evaluation and advice.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.why: The clause with から gives the reason first, and then gives advice. は sets the time, while が marks what exists, namely 試験.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This form can be used to advise someone to do something, but Vたほうがいい is usually more direct and natural for giving advice about what someone should do.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before ほうがいい, but advice about what someone should do usually uses the past verb form Vた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q6.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ほうがいいです
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vi: I think you are more at fault in this matter.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は limits the topic of the comment to このこと.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ほうが marks the side being compared and emphasizes your side.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the whole statement 悪い as the content of the verb 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 思う is the main predicate and takes the quoted clause through と.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q7.kobun.why: このことは states the scope of the comment, while あなたのほうが identifies the side being compared. The statement 悪い is placed before と, followed by the thinking verb 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence means that the speaker holds or already has this thought, rather than simply stating an opinion at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit と before 思う, but と must connect the thought content to the verb 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The adverb form of 早い modifies the request to apologize.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 謝り is the stem ます of 謝ります, which connects to なさい to create a request or command.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q8.kobun.why: The adverb 早く comes first to urge when the action should be done. The verb 謝る changes to the stem ます 謝り and then connects to なさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the speech becomes more polite and softer, with less of a commanding tone than なさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect なさい to the dictionary form, but they must use the verb stem ます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vi: If you do not understand, you should ask the teacher.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This part forms a conditional clause connected to the advice; the standard form is usually 分からなかったら, while the given sentence keeps 分からないかったら unchanged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person whom the speaker will ask.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞く changes to 聞いた before ほうがいい to express advice to ask.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: いいです completes the advice pattern at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first to state a possible situation, followed by the person to ask and the advice. In the standard structure, the negative form of 分かる must change to 分からなかったら; the input sentence contains an extra い and is kept unchanged as requested.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence has the meaning “whenever you do not understand,” and usually describes a more certain result or rule.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily attach たら directly to 分からない; they need to change ない into なかった before connecting ら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t9-q9.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら; Vない形 → Vなかったら
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.vi: Because she was a middle school student 10 years ago, she should be about 25 years old now.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.sk: N は + time N に + N だったから + N は + quantity くらいの + はずだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the state occurred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.2.vi: because she was a middle school student
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: だった is the past form of だ, while から connects the reason clause to the result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: は states the time being compared with 10 years ago.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: くらい shows an approximate amount, while の connects this phrase to はずだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: はずだ is placed at the end of the sentence to express a well-supported guess.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and is connected by から, followed by a guessed result in the present. は at かのじょは states the topic, while 今は creates a contrast between the two times.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with でしょう, the sentence is still a guess, but the tone is softer and places less emphasis on logical evidence than はずだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with かもしれない, the sentence only means that she may be about 25 years old, with a lower level of certainty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use はずだ as a guess without evidence, while this pattern usually relies on clear information or reasoning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t17-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + の + はずだ
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vi: When will John travel to America?
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that John is the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: いつ asks when the action will happen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: に in 旅行に行く indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: いく is a dictionary-form verb, while の？ turns the sentence into a casual question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.why: The sentence puts the topic first, then asks about the time and states the destination and purpose of going. の？ comes at the end to ask a casual question, giving the sentence a light and friendly tone.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with いきますか, the sentence becomes a more polite and neutral question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Using いくんですか gives the sentence more of a meaning of asking clearly about the reason or confirming information.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that の？ must come after the short form and cannot connect directly to the ます form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t19-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋なの・N＋なの ＋ の？
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.vi: A pleasant smell comes from the kitchen.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source or place from which a smell comes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: いい modifies the noun におい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the smell as something perceived by the senses.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: します combines with a sensory noun to express perceiving a smell.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.why: から states where the sensation comes from, while においがする uses the smell as the subject of perception. The adjective いい comes before におい to describe that smell.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If におい is replaced with 音, the sentence talks about a sound that is heard, not a smell.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means actively smelling something, not a smell coming by itself and being perceived.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use を with においがする because におい is the content of the sensation being perceived.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.vi: Please submit this assignment by the 10th.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the assignment is the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: １０日 is a time point used as the completion deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: までに indicates the time by which an action must be completed, or no later than that time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 出して is the て form of 出す, connecting the action of submitting with the polite request ください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: ください is placed at the end of a sentence to make a polite request or favor.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.why: The sentence states the object to be dealt with first, followed by the deadline. The verb uses the て form to connect with ください and make a polite request.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If １０日まで is used, it only states the time limit and does not emphasize that the task must be completed before the deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If １０日のうちに is used, it means completing something during that period, without necessarily expressing a deadline.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse までに with まで: までに is used when something must be completed before a certain time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamashita said, “I will call again.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 「Sentence」 と ＋ Vて形 ＋ いる（past）
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the speaker and the action of speaking.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the entire content of the direct quotation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 言って is the て form of 言う, connecting the quoted content with いました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 言っていました describes a state or speaking action that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.why: The spoken content is placed before と, followed by 言う to describe the speaking action. The 言っていました form shows that the person said it in the past.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ～そうです, it usually reports information heard from someone else rather than directly quoting the speaker.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 言いました is used, it only reports that someone said something once and does not emphasize a state or an action being remembered, as 言っていました does.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.tip: と must come after the complete spoken content; do not place と between the subject and the quoted words.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.kobun.cn: 普通形 ＋ と ＋ 言う／言っている／言った
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.vi: I can swim, but I can only swim 100 meters.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ V可能形が、＋ Quantity しか ＋ V可能形ない
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being discussed in both clauses.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object of ability in the pattern できます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: できます states an ability, while が connects to the contrasting clause that follows.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: しか limits the range to 100 meters and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 泳げません is the negative potential form, expressing the inability to swim beyond the limit stated earlier.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.cn: N ＋ しか ＋ Vない／Aくない／Nではない; the verb can use the negative potential form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.why: The first clause talks about general ability and uses が to contrast it with the specific limit in the second clause. しか comes after 100メートル and combines with 泳げません to emphasize that the ability stops at that level.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか is replaced with だけ, the sentence still means only 100 meters, but the tone is more neutral and a negative form is not required.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If ばかり is used, the sentence may suggest focusing only on or repeating one range, rather than simply expressing a limit of ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use しか with an affirmative sentence, but しか must be used with a negative predicate such as 泳げません.
